# Changelog

## Unreleased

- **Perf: the grouped W4A8 qt44 expert GEMM picks its two-tile x two-fragment entry from 4096 grouped rows instead of 12288 (gfx1201; output bit-identical). Raon-1-mini-preview v2 on R9700: pp1024 5,636 -> 5,788 tok/s (+2.7%); prompts of about 640-2,000 tokens gain, 512 and >= 2048 take the same entry as before.** Node sweep 64..8192 tokens, uniform and skewed routing (`bench_moe_grouped_qt44_iu4`): routed gate/up `nt2r2` / `nt2r1` = 0.95 at 640 tokens, 0.91 at 768, 0.83 at 1024, 0.77 at 1536 (down 0.94 / 0.91 / 0.92 / 0.84); one-expert shared down and dense gate/up/down at 4096 rows 0.89-0.94; at 4048 grouped rows (512 tokens) the two tie, so no size regresses. End to end (3 fresh processes per arm alternating): pp512 4,782 / 4,832, pp2048 5,964 / 5,996, pp4096 5,784 / 5,731 (unchanged route, within noise); prefill ids identical. Decode and DFlash verify unchanged: decode step 13.087 / 13.076 ms, greedy ids identical, verify k = 1/4/8/16 13.33/19.20/22.88/28.12 vs 13.40/19.25/22.86/28.12 ms. Receipts `raon/pfx/ev/fp8/a8sel/`.
- **Perf: Raon-1-mini-preview routed experts run W4A8 by default on gfx1100 (RX 7900 XT/XTX) and gfx1151 (Strix Halo) too: 7900 XTX pp512 3,333 -> 3,534 (+6.0%), pp2048 +5.9%, pp8192 +5.3%, pp16384 +4.5%; Strix Halo +4.9..6.4%. `HIPFIRE_RAON_PREFILL_PRECISION=f16` (or `routed_gu=f16,routed_dn=f16`) is the kill switch, shared with gfx1201.** `kernels/src/moe_grouped_qt44_a8_sym.gfx11.hip` is the RDNA3 twin of the gfx12 grouped qt44 W4A8 kernel: same ABI and fold (`sum = fma(RN(sc * d), float(C), sum)` per K128), activations on the WMMA A operand with the CTA's slot tiles shared through LDS, each lane loading one epoch of its row's K256 group and taking the other with `v_permlanex16`, unsigned codes with the zero point in the int32 chain seed (`-8 * s`, exact). Its output is bit-identical to the gfx12 kernel's (equal live-output hashes on 7900 XTX, Strix Halo and R9700 at every node-bench cell; 200/200 sampled outputs equal a CPU recompute). Node (7900 XTX, 4096 tokens, uniform routing): gate/up 5.64 -> 4.09 ms, down 3.60 -> 2.77 ms incl. quantize vs the F16 PeaceMaker route; on the 512-row chunks the XTX admits, down 1.03 -> 0.82 ms and gate/up at parity (uniform) to faster (skewed routing). KLD vs the BF16 teacher, default vs f16: code24 0.013484 vs 0.013938, WT2 0.080887 vs 0.080848 (identical on both RDNA3 cards). The per-site policy gains an arch half (`grouped_sym_tier_admits`: grouped W4A8 on gfx1201/gfx1100/gfx1151, W4A4/FP8 and the tiered Q8_0 GEMM on gfx1201 only); the gfx11 default is A8 at the routed sites only (shared/dense FFN unmeasured there, Q8_0 attention class has no gfx11 int8 route). 7900 XT capacity emulation (`HIPFIRE_EMU=rx7900xt`) still admits and recalls a 195,782-token needle. Receipts `raon/pfx/ev/a8r3/`.
- **Perf: Raon-1-mini-preview prefill now runs int8 activations at every GEMM site on gfx1201 by default (W4A8 routed experts, shared expert and dense layer-0 FFN; W8A8 Q8_0 attention-class projections). R9700, shipped `mq4-xts-a8attn-s`: pp512 3,669 -> 4,881, pp4096 4,171 -> 5,832, pp16384 3,639 -> 4,855 tok/s over the previous routed-only W4A8 default (+33% / +40% / +33%; +47% / +64% / +53% over all-F16). BF16-teacher KLD: code24 0.01413 vs 0.01379 all-F16, WT2 0.08204 vs 0.08091 (+0.0003 / +0.0011, inside the +0.002 budget).** The tier of each prefill GEMM site is a typed per-site policy resolved once at load (`crates/hipfire-arch-raon/src/precision.rs`) and logged per site with the reason when a site cannot run its request. `HIPFIRE_RAON_PREFILL_PRECISION` takes `f16` (global kill switch), `a4|a8|fp8` (every site), or `[<base>,]<site>=<tier>,...` over the sites `routed_gu, routed_dn, shared, dense, mla_q, mla_kv, mla_go, rda_qkvg, rda_o`, where `<site>=f16` is that site's kill switch; it replaces the developer-only `HIPFIRE_MOE_GROUPED_TIERS`. Quantized tiers run only on gfx1201, at prefill chunks of >= 64 rows, outside graph capture and Redline recording (`prefill_quant_admitted`); decode, speculative verify and every other arch keep F16 and are unchanged.
  - **Tiers.** The grouped symmetric qt44 core (`execute_grouped_moe`) and the shared/dense gated FFN (`gated_ffn_from_basis`, one-expert tables, load-verified symmetric headers) take F16, A4, A8 or the new FP8 tier (`moe_grouped_qt44_fp8_sym`: nibble -> e4m3 weights, `block_fp8_128` e4m3 activations with `d = amax/448` from `quantize_fp8_mmq_ds128`, `wmma_f32_16x16x16_fp8_fp8`, bit-exact vs a CPU recompute). Q8_0 projections go through the generic `q8_0_prefill_gemm` (hipfire-dispatch), which runs W8A8 `gemm_q8_0_a8_batched` or the new W8-FP8 `gemm_q8_0_fp8_batched` (int8 weights -> e4m3 RNE at LDS staging, e4m3 activations per 32-K block, `wmma_f32_16x16x16_fp8_fp8`, within a WMMA-rounding tolerance of a CPU emulation). Node (R9700, median of 25): W8A8 2.2–2.6x the F16 `gemm_q8_0_batched_chunked` at N = 4096 on every attention shape, FP8 0.92–1.00x of A8; grouped FP8 within ±3% of grouped A8 at every expert shape. Accuracy vs F64: Q8 FP8 2.5–3.7e-2 relative vs A8 0.5–1.3e-2; grouped FP8 0.0257 rms vs F16 against A8 0.0065.

- **Fixed: Raon-1-mini-preview decode on gfx1201 is back to ~73 tok/s (it had dropped to ~39 since the tiled F32 GEMM landed).** `gemm_f32_tiled_rows` (mHC selector and MoE router) was admitted at every row count, including decode (n = 1) and speculative verify (n <= 16), where its few-block grid is far slower than `gemm_f32_batched`. On R9700 card E with the same binary, the Raon decode step took 25.5 ms with it and 13.8 ms without (pre-change build: 13.8 ms), and a 2-row verify 29.1 vs 17.3 ms. The tiled kernel now runs only for calls of 512 rows or more (`F32_TILED_ROWS_MIN_N`), the measured prefill region. Both kernels are bit-identical, so outputs are unchanged. Found by the DFlash2 cost run (`raon/dflash2/evidence/b12`); the prefill A/B that admitted the kernel measured pp512..16384 only.
- **Perf: Raon-1-mini-preview routed experts now run W4A8 on gfx1201 by default (symmetric-verified qt44 experts; `HIPFIRE_RAON_PREFILL_PRECISION=f16` is the all-F16 kill switch).** The grouped routed-expert GEMMs inside `execute_grouped_moe` take a capability route (`moe_grouped_qt44_iu4`, `grouped_moe_site_tiers`): symmetric qt44 weights (`zp == -8*sc`, verified per layer at load) against int8 `block_i8_128` activations on `wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu8`, F32 grouped output, so the SiTU activation, per-expert down AWQ, the K 1088->1280 pad, the FWHT256 rotate and the combine run unchanged. R9700 (gfx1201), shipped `mq4-xts-a8attn-s`, same binary, 3 fresh processes per arm alternating, median tok/s default vs `=f16`: pp512 3,724 vs 3,346 (+11.3%), pp2048 4,302 vs 3,629 (+18.5%), pp4096 4,193 vs 3,560 (+17.8%), pp16384 3,656 vs 3,171 (+15.3%) (one default and one f16 process each had a low outlier at pp4096; medians used, all runs in the receipts). Node (4096 rows, uniform routing): gate/up 6,679 -> 2,644 us (+73 us quantize), down 4,379 -> 1,633 us (+282 us); output error vs the F16 grouped route 0.65% rms. **Quality is unchanged:** mean KLD vs the BF16 teacher code24 0.01388 vs 0.01379 (f16), WT2 0.08090 vs 0.08091; top-1 0.9629 vs 0.9626 / 0.8966 vs 0.8972.
  - **W4A4 (`=a4`) stays opt-in and fails the KLD gate:** both sites A4 code24 0.02462 (+0.0108), WT2 0.14113 (+0.0602); per-site (now `HIPFIRE_RAON_PREFILL_PRECISION=f16,routed_gu=<tier>,routed_dn=<tier>`): gate/up only A4 code24 +0.0068 / WT2 +0.0373, down only A4 +0.0035 / +0.0211, mixed gate/up A4 + down A8 +0.0067 / +0.0385; A8 per site: gate/up only -0.0002 / -0.0001, down only +0.0003 / -0.0000. The int4 activation step (amax/7) injects about 10% rms per expert output across 24 layers x top-6; W4A4 is 2.0–2.9x faster per node than F16 but not usable on this artifact.
  - **Not covered (work items):** a BF16-output epilogue and a fused activation/AWQ/pad/FWHT256/quantize producer (about 1-2 days); gfx1100/gfx1151 W4A8: see the RDNA3 twin entry above. Receipts `raon/pfx/ev/moeiu4-default/` and `raon/pfx/ev/moeiu4/`.
- **Fixed: sampled DFlash2 decoding is distributed as the target again: the verify depth no longer depends on the drafted token's own probability.** A window verifies the draft prefix whose running product of selector confidences stays at or above 0.5. The confidence of a row was the temperature-1 mass of the token the selector had just drawn, so at temperature > 0 a likely draw was verified more often than an unlikely one, and a verified row was no longer distributed as the selector's `q` (CPU law test: `P(t2 = c | t1 = a)` 0.42 against the target's 0.30). The confidence is now the row's top-candidate mass, computed before the draw (`selector_row_confidence`), which depends on the earlier drafts only; greedy windows are unchanged byte for byte (greedy picks the top candidate). Affects every DFlash2 target (Raon-1-mini, Flash-Next). Seeding was audited too: the selector draws and the accept/resample draws are consecutive draws of one request stream, never the same draw, so there is no shared-seed bias.
  - **Evidence** (R9700, `raon-1-mini-preview.mq4-xts-a8attn-s`, F16 draft, new `raon_dflash_oracle sampled`: 2000 cold trials per arm, 8 tokens, T 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20 / presence 0; every emitted token is tested against the truncated law of the row it was drawn or verified from): prose (`explain_concept`, thinking off, md5 dca47b0d) and code (`code_python`, thinking on, 3874f31c) pass all 16 gating chi-square tests each (DFlash p 0.44-0.99), no token outside its row's support. AR-vs-DFlash homogeneity differs at a few positions (mean-law TV 0.03-0.04): batched verify rows round differently from single-row decode rows (the known non-row-exact verify), not the sampler. Serve battery with DFlash on (R9700, 38 cases incl. 4 sampled presence-0 requests on the DFlash route): 37 pass; the 27K needle ran out of device memory growing the MLA mirror on this build (fixed by the next entry).
- **Developer: `raon_dflash_oracle sampled` (sampled law gate above) and `costs` (device-synced decode, verify per row count, partial commit and draft ms; prints window cost in decode steps).**
- **Raon-1-mini DFlash2 needs 0.8-1.3 GB less device memory, so the F16 draft fits next to a long-context MLA mirror.** The shared DFlash2 drafter no longer keeps a window-high raw feature ring on the device (Raon: 2048 rows x 51200 F32 = 0.42 GB): an all-sliding draft fed from host feature rows streams the rows it projects through a 128-row staging buffer (26 MB) into `fc`, and only the projected rows stay resident (`DflashScratch::new_windowed_staged`); the MQ rotation scratch is sized for that stage instead of a 1024-row chunk of feature rows. On the target, `spec_advance` (prefill and forced advances) now runs the AR prefill launch sequence and downloads only the kept feature rows through a per-layer stream tap, so the device capture buffer is sized for a verify block (16 rows) instead of the admitted prefill chunk (4096 rows x 200 KB = 0.84 GB); prefill state is AR's bit for bit. Before this, a 27K-token request with DFlash on ran out of memory growing the expanded MLA mirror on a 32 GB R9700.
  - **Gates** (R9700, F16 draft): feature capture bit-identical to the oracle tap for prefill (22 and 8000 rows) and for the verify's device capture (16 rows); `verifygraph` PASS (48 windows); greedy DFlash vs AR PASS on code / math / prose (justified tie / near-tie / justified tie) and identical on an 8K needle prompt; recurrence rollback byte-equal to full replay for keep 2..7 (the oracle now judges keep 2..7 only: keep 1's replay arm takes the single-row decode route). Serve battery with DFlash on (R9700, F16 draft, `--max-seq 32768`): 38/38, the 27K needle recalled.
- **Perf: the mHC stream-mix selector GEMM and the grouped-MoE router GEMM run an x-stationary tiled F32 kernel (`gemm_f32_tiled_rows`), bit-identical to `gemm_f32_batched`; `HIPFIRE_F32_TILED_ROWS=0` restores it. Raon-1-mini-preview on R9700 (on top of the admitted 4096-row chunk): pp512 2,895 -> 2,996, pp4096 2,957 -> 3,202, pp16384 2,673 -> 2,851 tok/s (+3.5 / +8.3 / +6.7%).** The old kernel ran one 32-lane wave per output and re-read each activation row once per output: 17 times for the mHC selector `[17, 10240]` and 128 times for the router `[128, 2560]`, about 12.5% of pp4096. The new kernel stages 4 activation rows × 1024 K in LDS per 256-thread block, and its 8 waves split the outputs. Each output keeps the lane-strided FMA order and the width-32 shuffle tree. pp4096: 183 -> 75 ms.
  - **Evidence** (`raon_oracle`, shipped `mq4-xts-a8attn-s`, one binary 66dc2cd9, kill-switch arms, 3 fresh processes per arm alternating; receipts `raon/pfx/ev/l1d/`). code24 and WT2 BF16-teacher KLD identical to every digit. The `gemm_f32_tiled_rows_parity` GPU test is bit-exact against `gemm_f32_batched` at (17, 10240, {1, 7, 512, 4096}), (128, 2560, {1, 5, 512, 4096}) and ragged shapes.
  - **gfx1201 only.** 7900 XTX (gfx1100, `raon/pfx/ev/xtx2/`, 3 fresh processes per arm alternating, 1 Hz link watcher with no drop) measured it 2.3–2.9% slower (pp4096 3,236 -> 3,145), so other archs keep `gemm_f32_batched`. On the same XTX run, the admitted chunk picked 512 rows at the default reserved context (to keep the mirror budget), so it ran the identical route: pp4096 3,236 vs 3,234. code24 KLD is identical on gfx1100 (0.0139383).
- **New: Raon-1-mini-preview speculative decoding with the official DFlash2 draft (opt-in: `--spec dflash` + `developer.dflash_draft` or `--model-draft`; `speculation.dflash` default unchanged, off).** The shared DFlash2 drafter now takes multi-stream target features (`dflash_config.target_streams_per_layer`; feature row = layers x streams x hidden, 5 x 4 x 2560 for Raon) and refuses a draft whose stream count differs from the target's. Raon captures the post-FFN 4-stream mHC carrier of layers 1/6/11/16/21 on the device (bit-identical to the oracle tap), verifies 1..16 rows in one batched forward replayed from a per-row-count HIP graph (bit-identical to eager at K = 1..16), and rolls back a partial accept by restoring the RDA/conv snapshot and rerunning only the kept rows' recurrence from the verify's captured inputs (`HIPFIRE_RAON_DFLASH_ROLLBACK=replay` restores the full-forward replay; 0.4-1.1 ms vs 15-37 ms per partial commit). `dflash_convert` keeps a multi-stream draft's `fc` in F16 under MQ formats (the raw residual features have per-channel outliers in the hundreds; an all-4-bit draft accepted almost nothing). `hipfire bench --spec dflash` now honours `developer.dflash_draft` on a config-off load, as `run` does.
  - **Evidence (R9700, `mq4-xts-a8attn-s`, F16 draft, `hipfire bench --spec off|dflash`, 256 greedy tokens, 3 fresh processes per arm alternating):** code (mtp-bench `code_python`, md5 3874f31c) 73.4 -> 133.9 decode tok/s, tau 4.2; math (`stepwise_math`, e5277942) 73.1 -> 121.4, tau 3.25; prose (`explain_concept`, dca47b0d) 72.9 -> 48.3, tau 0.58 (slower than AR: prose drafts rarely survive and a 2-row verify costs more than a decode step, so the default stays off).
  - **Gates:** draft forward vs an independent CPU reference of the draft on hipfire-captured features: cosine 1.000000 on every row, selector tokens equal. Greedy DFlash vs AR (3 genres, R9700 and 7900 XTX): first divergences are AR near-ties onto AR's runner-up (top-2 margin <= 0.5 logit), not byte-identical, because batched-verify projections round differently from single-row decode. Recurrence rollback is byte-identical to the full-replay arm for keep 2..7 on both cards; keep 1 differs because the replay arm's single-row forward takes the decode GEMV route.
- **Quality + decode: Raon-1-mini-preview ships a Q8F16 shared-expert / dense layer-0 FFN (`raon-1-mini-preview-v2.mq4-xts`, +0.16 GB). BF16-teacher KLD WT2 0.0809 -> 0.0743, code24 0.0138 -> 0.0116; tg128 +5.5% (R9700) / +8.8% (RX 7900 XTX).** The 24 shared experts and the dense layer-0 MLP are read by every token; the previous file stored them as 4-bit (the 48 shared gate/up tensors as plain RTN). The new file re-quantizes exactly those 75 tensors to Q8F16 from the BF16 checkpoint and keeps every other tensor byte-identical (independent md5 of all 19,359 remaining tensors; shipped `mq4-xts` sha256 3828f980…, new sha256 e136b14c…). The loader takes Q8F16 or BF16 for these tensors (no AWQ sidecar: they read the plain activation); BF16 is resident as its exact F16 image for prefill plus a load-time Q8_0 copy for single-row decode, and a decode row over a Q8_0 FFN weight now uses the Q8 GEMV instead of a one-column WMMA tile.
  - **KLD vs the BF16 teacher** (same binary, batched prefill, R9700; serial decode-path code24 agrees): shipped 0.0809 / 0.0138 (WT2 / code24), Q8F16 0.0743 / 0.0116, source-exact BF16 0.0749 / 0.0118 (no better than Q8, so BF16 is not shipped). Attribution: shared experts alone (dense left 4-bit) 0.0744 / 0.0118, i.e. the shared experts carry the gain.
  - **Speed, 3 fresh processes x 3 reps, median tok/s, shipped -> Q8F16:** R9700 pp512/2048/8192/16384 3229/3384/3174/2934 -> 3204/3342/3141/2913 (-0.7..-1.2%), tg128 72.5 -> 76.5; RX 7900 XTX (shader clock capped at 2,400 MHz) 3344/3301/3097/2648 -> 3233/3194/3002/2318 (-3.0..-3.3% up to pp8192, -12.5% at pp16384), tg128 63.7 -> 69.3. The XTX pp16384 drop is capacity: the +0.16 GB of weights comes out of the fast-prefill MLA mirror budget (15,037 -> 12,185 rows of 16,448), the rest of the context runs the absorbed route; the 32 GB R9700 is fully mirrored. Under 7900 XT capacity emulation (20 GB) the file still admits the full 262,144-token window, recalls the 27K-token needle, and pp32000 is 1,566 -> 1,495 tok/s.
- **Developer: Raon-1-mini always-active FFN storage (shared-expert gate/up/down of every MoE layer and the dense layer-0 gate/up/down) is selectable as `q8f16` (qt3) or source-exact `bf16` (qt16) instead of symmetric qt44 + AWQ sidecar.** `HIPFIRE_RAON_SHARED_FFN=qt44|q8f16|bf16` selects it in a full conversion (default `qt44`, unchanged), and `hipfire-quantize --raon-shared-ffn <q8f16|bf16> --input <shipped.hfq> --raon-source <checkpoint dir> --output <out.hfq>` builds the same variant from a shipped artifact without re-running calibration: every other tensor is copied byte-for-byte, the replaced weights keep their index position, their sidecars are dropped, and the shared `down_proj` keeps physical K 1280 (zero-padded). `--raon-shared-ffn-verify <q8f16|bf16> --input <shipped.hfq> --output <variant.hfq>` is the read-only proof (tensor table, payload equality, metadata modulo the updated keys). The artifact records `hipfire_raon.shared_ffn`.

- **Perf: Raon-1-mini-preview batched prefill now runs admission-sized chunks up to 4096 rows instead of a fixed 512 (`HIPFIRE_RAON_PREFILL_CHUNK_ROWS=auto|512|1024|2048|4096`; `512` restores the previous route). R9700 (gfx1201), shipped `mq4-xts-a8attn-s`: pp2048 2,880 -> 3,040, pp4096 2,807 -> 2,960, pp16384 2,555 -> 2,694 tok/s (+5.4–5.6%); pp512 unchanged.** Each chunk streams the routed-expert weights once instead of once per 512 rows (pp4096 grouped MoE GEMM 403 -> 305 ms, 13,522 -> 3,448 dispatches). Auto takes the widest rung whose scratch + work fit the free VRAM without shrinking the expanded-MLA mirror budget below the 512-row policy's for the same reserved context. A 20 GB card or a very long reserved context keeps 512/1024 and never fails to load. The MLA decompression tile stays 512 rows, and wider chunks expand their new rows tile by tile.
  - **Evidence** (`raon_oracle bench --pp 512,2048,4096,16384 --tg 0`, 3 fresh processes per arm alternating, auto vs 512, same binary; receipts `raon/pfx/ev/chunk/`). Identity: code24 and WT2 BF16-teacher KLD equal to every digit (0.0137939 / 0.0809147). A 6,981-token greedy run (4096 chunk + 2,885-row tail) gives byte-identical text at 4096, 2048 and 512.
- **Added: W8A8 Q8_0 prefill GEMM for gfx12 (`gemm_q8_0_a8_batched`, `kernels/src/gemm_q8_0_mmq_i8.gfx12.hip`; wired as the `a8` tier of the Raon per-site prefill precision policy above).** Int8 Q8_0 weights read in place (34-byte blocks) times int8 activations quantized per row per 32-K block (`d = RN(amax/127)`, `q = clamp(rint(x/d), ±127)`), `v_wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu8`, F32 output, `K % 32 == 0` (K = 576 and 512 included), no environment variable. `Gpu::q8_a8_quantize_x` + `Gpu::gemm_q8_0_a8_gemm` split the producer from the GEMM so one quantization serves projections that share an activation. Three CTA tiles (128x128, 128x64, 64x64) picked by grid fill (`q8_a8_pick_tile`); a `_slow` variant covers K % 64 == 32 and a 2-byte aligned weight base. The GEMM is exact up to the F32 fold order: `tests/gemm_q8_0_a8_gfx12.rs` matches a CPU emulation bit for bit across tiles, tails, K = 576/512/96 and both weight paths. R9700 node bench (`examples/bench_q8_0_a8_gfx12.rs`, producer + GEMM vs `gemm_q8_0_batched_chunked` incl. its F32->F16 convert, median of 25): 2.4-2.6x at N = 4096 on the 2560x5120 / 5120x2560 / 7680x576 / 10240x512 sites, 2.1-2.5x at N = 512 (1.29x on the tiny M = 576 N = 512 site). Accuracy is not the F16 path's: relative error vs F64 is 5e-3 on Gaussian BF16 activations and 1.2e-2 with massive channels, against 2e-4 for F16 activations, so each site needs its own KLD gate before it is switched.

- **Developer: EP host barriers are tagged, so a rank-local divergence fails at once naming both ranks instead of timing out 30 s later, and a stalled barrier reports where every rank is.** Every row-gather crossing (`EpRowGather::exchange_layer`) carries call kind, buffer, layer, slot count and a per-rank gather sequence number; every tile-exchange crossing (both exchange barriers and the host rendezvous the EP reserve loan and the stage quiesce use, `EpTileExchange::host_barrier(rank, what, epoch)`) carries kind, layer/epoch, tiles and the rank's exchange or rendezvous count. All ranks' tags are compared right after the barrier (an atomic store plus `ranks` loads per call, no device work). A barrier wait past 5 s prints each rank's last entered / last crossed tag, how long ago it crossed and what its host thread is doing (recording, at the barrier, host-waiting for a peer's producer event, launching the copy); the 30 s timeout error carries the same line. Always on; no new switch.
- **Fixed: a failing EP rank now aborts every EP barrier, not only the row gather.** `RankPool::set_abort` kept the first callback only (a `OnceLock`), so the tile-exchange and trunk-split barriers installed later were never aborted on a rank failure and a peer blocked there waited out its own 30 s timeout. Every `set_abort` registration is now kept and every callback runs on each failure or mesh poison (callbacks are idempotent), so a peer parked in any barrier family is released at once; CPU fault-injection tests cover several families aborted by one abort, a crossing-tag mismatch aborting all, a missing participant failing within one timeout budget, and repeated aborts.
- **Perf: EP2 reserve decoupling is now the default for the admitted Flash-Next configuration; `HIPFIRE_EP_RESERVE_DECOUPLE=0` is the kill switch.** Measured on the C1 single-stream driver (Gate 3, `release-0.4.3/r9700x2-par/RESULT.md`, lever 3; 3 fresh EP2 servers per arm, alternating): +5.9% median, +7.4% to +8.5% paired (33 vs 28 resident layers per rank). Unset takes the route for an admitted load; a load that is not admitted, or whose capacity plan cannot be met, keeps the ordinary placement with a logged note (`=1` forces the route and fails such a load before any allocation; `=0` is today's path byte for byte). Original description: `HIPFIRE_EP_RESERVE_DECOUPLE` lets an EP2 Flash-Next load on exact gfx1201 stop sizing its forward scratch for the 4096-row prompt chunk, to keep more expert layers resident per rank (target at least 33; unset / `0` is today's path byte for byte).** The prompt chunk stays 4096. Calls of at most 512 rows use a small resident scratch bank, forwards of 513..=4096 rows use one borrowed 4096-row bank placed in a fixed suffix of whole-layer donors, and the 4096-row grouped-down exchange buffer is owned permanently at one address by both banks. Donor bytes are mirrored in pinned host memory and restored synchronously: once at outer prompt completion (or earlier, before a resident-bank or Full-table call), inside the prompt's elapsed time, never deferred to the second token. Every configuration outside discrete gfx1201 EP2 (other arches, other EP counts, single card, PP, tier / slab placement, DFlash, continuous batching, an explicit different chunk) keeps the ordinary path. **No measurement exists and no performance is claimed**: the experiment is killed by an id mismatch, a pp32K throughput ratio below 0.95 or restore-inclusive latency ratio above 1.05, a weighted sampled C1 gain below +8%, or fewer than 33 resident layers. `scripts/fn-ep-gate.sh --mode reserve` runs the same-binary off/on arms with per-rank plan / restore receipts, boundary and tail prompts and the id comparison; `scripts/fn_ep_compare.py reserve {arms,perf,c1,harvest}` evaluates the receipts and the kill rules (CPU fixtures in `tests/test_fn_ep_reserve_gate.py`). See [multi-gpu.md](docs/multi-gpu.md#flash-next-ep-ep-reserve-decoupling-opt-in-unmeasured).
- **Fixed: on gfx11 A8 prefill, `HIPFIRE_A8_FUSED_PROD=0` now runs the standalone A8 quantizer instead of handing the projections to IU4 (W4A4).** `Gpu::iu4_producer_sidecar_active` and `iu4_gfx11_producer_quant_fused_active` decline a shape A8 owns when the fused producers are off; with them on (the default) nothing changes. Qwen3.8-27B mq4-xts code24 on gfx1151 (`HIPFIRE_GFX11_A8_PREFILL=1`): the opt-out went from KLD 0.048487 (IU4 level) to 0.027297, and its `.kldseq` (`aec8f346`) is now bit-identical to the fused default, so the fused and unfused A8 producers agree.

## v0.4.5 — 2026-10-30

Highlights (details in the entries below):

- **7900 XTX Flash-Next:** native MTP on by default (host-mapped routed experts), and short prompts prefill on the hybrid SP slow-link route by default (TTFT at 1K rows about 8 s -> about 2 s).
- **Copy lane:** the native-MTP n-gram copy lane is on by default on Strix Halo and R9700 (single-file edits +11.6–14.6% decode on Halo).
- **MQ3 verify:** symmetric MQ3V2 (`mq3-xts`) speculative verify on R9700 runs fp16 WMMA tiles, and its base WMMA kernels split K across 8 waves.
- **GGUF-native (opt-in):** dense Qwen3.5 / 3.6 / 3.8 GGUF files load natively on gfx1201 behind `HIPFIRE_GGUF_NATIVE=1`.
- **UX:** live prefill progress, one `hipfire load summary:` line per load, `hipfire fit --kv-mode/--kv-k/--kv-v/--spec`, `hipfire config explain`, and refusals that name the expected file and the next command.
- **20 GB cards:** automatic `max_seq` no longer promises a context the card cannot hold, and an explicit `max_seq` that cannot fit is refused at load.
- **New architecture: Raon-1-mini-preview (KRAFTON, 28.8B / 4.3B active, arch 19)** — `hipfire pull raon-1-mini-preview` (Q8 attention + XTS experts, KLD WT2 0.081 / code24 0.0138 vs BF16). 7900 XTX pp512 3,327 / pp16384 2,652 / decode 64 tok/s; R9700 pp512 2,919 / decode 72; 20 GB cards hold about 195K tokens. The worked example for adding a new architecture. Thanks to u/Queasy_Asparagus69 (Hugging Face: datayoda) for the original community port and bug reports.
- **Multi-GPU Flash-Next:** sampled requests now run in continuous batching (EP2 C8 73.8 -> 82.5 tok/s, PP2 56.1 -> 107.3; TTFT p50 24 s -> 0.66 s), and PP2 serves sampled requests with native MTP (C1 56 -> 103 tok/s).

- **Perf: Flash-Next continuous batching (`serve.vmm_batch` under `topology.ep` / `topology.pp`) now admits sampled requests instead of serializing them on the singleton route (`HIPFIRE_SERVE_BATCH_SAMPLED=0` / `serve.batch_sampled = false` restores the previous behaviour).** Lanes with neutral repeat/presence/frequency penalties draw on the host per lane from the same sampler as singleton AR, so each request's tokens are byte-identical to singleton AR at the same seed; penalized requests keep the singleton route. MTP lanes verify sampled windows naively. 2x R9700 Flash-Next, C8 sampled serve: EP2 mq4 73.8 -> 82.5 tok/s, PP2 mq3 56.1 -> 107.3 tok/s, TTFT p50 24.1 s -> 0.66 s.
- **Perf: Flash-Next under `topology.pp` serves sampled requests with native MTP via speculative rejection sampling (Leviathan), as the single-card route already did (`HIPFIRE_MTP_SAMPLED=0` sends sampled requests to AR).** Requests with neutral penalties only; naive and penalized requests stay AR. Output matches AR in distribution, not byte for byte: the sampled MTP distribution oracle gains a PP2 arm and passes all 4 arms (n=2000, min p 0.137). 2x R9700 PP2 mq3, weighted sampled C1: 55.99 -> 102.87 tok/s (+84%).
- **Fixed: Raon-1-mini-preview (arch 19) decode no longer drops to about half speed on R9700 (gfx1201) when its decode queue shares the card with another queue or process.** Decode alternated between about 73 tok/s and about 39 tok/s from process to process (and inside one process); prefill was unaffected, and memory/shader/fabric clocks were identical in both states (memory clock at its top level, board power 265 W fast vs 200 W slow). The slow state is a fixed ~25 ms per token regardless of model weights, so it is dispatch latency, not bandwidth. The cause was the per-token hop through the legacy null stream: the token id was staged with a blocking `hipMemcpy` and the logits were read with a blocking `hipMemcpy`, both on the null queue, while the graph replays on its own stream; every token made the runtime synchronize two hardware queues. The graph decode route now stages the token id with a stream-ordered `hipMemsetD32Async` on the decode stream (`Gpu::write_u32_stream_ordered`) and reads logits / the greedy token back ordered on that stream (`Gpu::download_f32_stream_ordered`, `RaonBundle::download_logits`, `tensor_ops::argmax_f32_host_stream_ordered`, used by the serving route's greedy step). With no decode stream the old calls are unchanged. Output is bit-identical (greedy ids md5 unchanged).

- **Perf: Flash-Next PP lane decode no longer blocks the host thread on each band edge: the receiver band's stream waits on the sender's group event on the device (`hipStreamWaitEvent`), so every micro-batch's launches are enqueued ahead of the edge. Measured on 2x R9700 (gfx1201), mq3-xts 25/23, C8 steady: 123.3 -> 125.4 tok/s (+1.7%, about -1.1 ms of the 64.9 ms step); BetterBench shape: 105.6 -> 108.2 out tok/s (+2.4%); C1 unchanged (57.1 vs 57.1 steady tok/s).** The step's critical path is `b0g0 + b0g1 + b1g1`. The old loop enqueued the output band's group only after the host saw the sender's event complete; now every launch is enqueued within the first 11 ms of the step (the overlap loop's host time drops from 46 ms to 11 ms, `HIPFIRE_PROF_DIAG` build) and the output band's group sits queued behind the device fence. Edge events are created with `HIP_EVENT_RELEASE_TO_SYSTEM` (they gate a device -> pinned host -> device hop). The mesh MTP protocol path (bounded polls against a transport deadline) is unchanged. `HIPFIRE_PP_LANE_EDGE_HOST_WAIT=1` (developer) restores the host `hipEventSynchronize` per edge.
  - **Evidence** (base = beta 4282a57ea0 binary, new = this change, `hipfire bench --concurrency 8 --backend batch`, fresh process per run, alternating base/new, cards C,B): steady shape (16 x 192 greedy tokens), 6 pairs: base 122.61 / 123.46 / 123.18 / 123.48 / 123.34 / 123.37 steady tok/s, new 124.79 / 125.62 / 125.41 / 125.44 / 125.01 / 125.87 (every new run above every base run). BB shape (24 requests, sampled lanes), 3 pairs: base 104.68 / 106.12 / 105.96 out tok/s, new 108.22 / 108.22 / 108.07. C1 (`--concurrency 1`), 4 pairs: base 57.06 / 57.18 / 57.10 / 57.11, new 57.06 / 57.14 / 57.02 / 56.92 steady tok/s (within noise).

- **Added: Raon-1-mini-preview (arch 19) expanded MLA K/V mirror in Q8 when the BF16 mirror cannot cover the reserved context (`HIPFIRE_RAON_MIRROR_Q8=0` always keeps BF16).** The fast-prefill decompressed K_nope/V mirror is stored as INT8 codes with one F16 scale per (row, head, plane): 72,800 B/token instead of 143,360, so a 20 GB-class card keeps the fast route for about twice the rows before the absorbed route takes over (7900 XTX max_seq 16,448: 15,037 vs 7,636 mirror rows; HIPFIRE_EMU=rx7900xt pp32000 1,376 vs 1,311 tok/s). The tiled prefill and split-KV decode kernels dequantize in-kernel (the K tile once per block into LDS); the format is chosen once at load from free VRAM (BF16 when its budget covers the whole reserved context, since it is 1-2% faster; Q8 otherwise) and the budget uses that format's row size. KLD vs the BF16 teacher is unchanged within noise (code24 0.01392 vs 0.01379, WT2 0.08062 vs 0.08092).
