Credit: **u/Queasy_Asparagus69 (Hugging Face: datayoda)** wrote the original community port and reported the bugs that shaped the route: the stream refusing generations (`stream must begin with gen_start`), thinking never closing, the broken `enable_thinking: false` frame, and needle-probe prompt-echo at greedy. See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md), [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md), [docs/QUANTIZATION.md](docs/QUANTIZATION.md).
- **Added: Raon-1-mini-preview (arch 19) decode is hipGraph-captured by default.** The whole decode step (embedding, all 25 layers, head, device-side `seq_len` advance) is recorded once per admitted context bucket and replayed per token; the token id and the slot's `seq_len` live in stable device buffers the recorded kernels read (the host refreshes the id before each replay; a generic `device_counter_add_i32` kernel inside the graph advances `seq_len`), so one recording is valid at every position of its bucket. Context admission (latent mapping, K/V mirror) runs outside capture, and a graph is re-recorded exactly when a baked address or extent changes. `HIPFIRE_GRAPH=0` selects the per-launch eager route; a failed capture is an error, not a silent fallback. `raon_oracle state --mode graph` gates eager vs graph over `--steps` greedy steps: every logit byte of every step, `seq_len`, every RDA state, conv plane and live latent row bitwise equal, across a mirror-growth re-record, a reset and a shorter request through the same recording; `raon_oracle bench` records `decode_mode` and graph capture/replay counts per rep. On gfx1201 (R9700) decode is intermittently 2x slower per step (40 vs 82 tok/s graph, 78 eager) in some processes or phases; the same dips appear in eager decode and in llama.cpp on that card.
- **Added: Raon-1-mini (arch 19) bench tooling and `hipfire bench --matrix` decode.** `raon_oracle bench` (`--pp`, `--tg`, `--reps`, `--warmup`, `--prompt-file`) runs pp/tg (prefill/decode throughput) through the production `RaonBundle::prefill`/`decode_step` on a committed fixed prompt (`benchmarks/prompts/raon/state.txt`, cyclic ids, per-N id-stream md5), and records the binary md5, model md5 (`<model>.md5` sidecar, computed once if absent), GPU arch, `HIPFIRE_*` controls and sysfs clocks. `--profile` attributes one pass per pp and one decode pass to kernel buckets (MoE grouped/indexed/route, trunk GEMM, RDA recurrence, conv/prepare, MLA attention/decompress, mHC, norms, head, launch gaps) and reconciles the bucket sum against the unprofiled wall; `--bucket-json` re-buckets a saved profile on the CPU. New in rdna-compute: launch-level timing (`profile::start_launches`/`stop_launches`) times every launch through the launch funnels, so kernels without a hand-placed `begin_timer` are covered; it is off (one thread-local read per launch) unless started. The daemon's `bench_decode` now serves arch 19 (`BenchDecodeRoute::Raon`, `RaonCarrier::bench_decode_prime`/`bench_decode_run` over `decode_step`), so `hipfire bench MODEL --matrix` reports both pp and tg rows for Raon.
- **Added: serving route `raon_ar` for KRAFTON Raon-1-mini-preview (arch 19), plus the `raon-1-mini-preview` registry card.** The route selects on arch 19 and runs the shared `generate_ar_with_forward` producer (think router, XML `<tool_call><function=..>` router, `stop`, explicit `max_think_tokens` budget, one correlated terminal), with `gen_start` emitted before any token/reasoning/progress event. Thinking-on renders `<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n` so the stream starts in reasoning; thinking-off renders the template's own `<think></think>\n\n`; no second opener is ever appended, and a `max_tokens` stop inside reasoning stays reasoning-only with `finish_reason: length`. Sampled requests that set nothing explicit take the checkpoint's `generation_config` defaults (`top_k` 20, presence 1.5); presence/frequency/repeat penalties see only generated tokens (new `penalty_generated_only` option on the shared AR body; the AR body's `eos_token` is now `eos_tokens`, so both `<|im_end|>` and `<|endoftext|>` end a turn). Greedy requests are never given a default penalty.
- **Added: a per-rank / per-band lane-store census (`lane::census`: `LaneSpecBudget`, `lane_spec_census`, `ar_lane_census`, `admit_and_stage`), and a pipeline band that owns target layers but not the MTP head can now size and hold its lanes' GDN capture rings.** Every figure is built from the allocators' own inventories (`row_capture_allocation_sizes_scoped`, `MtpGpuState::allocation_sizes`, `MtpAppendScratch::allocation_sizes`), overflow refuses before any allocation, and a head owner must be a band that runs the LM head, so a non-output pipeline band charges no head, logits or wide-hidden bytes. `Qwen4LaneStore::device_bytes_scoped` is now this census under the legacy `k + 1`-row budget (identical bytes for every store the constructor built before; a non-output band with `spec_k` answers its target-only bytes instead of `None`). No route changes: expert-parallel and pipeline-parallel stores still stage AR lanes.
- **Added: a default Flash-Next pipeline-parallel load (`topology.pp`) now fits a model that the uniform split at the default chunk refuses, with no `HIPFIRE_PP_LAYERS` or `HIPFIRE_PREFILL_CHUNK_ROWS`.** The load keeps the uniform split at the default prefill chunk whenever every card holds it (such loads are unchanged). When a card is short it runs the existing per-band census (pure arithmetic, no allocation) over the chunk rungs 2048, 1024, 512 and 256 below the default, picks the largest chunk at which some split fits (every split for `pp = 2`, a deterministic steepest-descent walk from the uniform split above that, band 0 always at least 2 layers) and the most balanced fitting split, then sizes the edge buffers, every band and the mesh from that one split and chunk. It logs `qwen4 PP auto-fit: layers a,b chunk C (uniform u,v at chunk R short by X MiB on rank r)`; when nothing fits the refusal keeps its text and adds the nearest candidate. An explicit `HIPFIRE_PP_LAYERS` is never searched and an explicit `HIPFIRE_PREFILL_CHUNK_ROWS` is never stepped down (only its split is searched). The chunk changes numerics (output equals a single card at the same chunk), the split does not. From the measured 2× R9700 mq3-xts loads (uniform 24,24 at 4096 short by 1.84 GB on rank 1; hand-tuned 25,23 at 1024 fits) the unit-tested fixture picks 25,23 at chunk 1024 for `max_seq` 16,384. No hardware run of the auto-fit itself yet.
- **Perf: the gfx1201 27B prefill gate/up GEMM (`gemm_mq4g256v2_gate_up_silu_mmq_iu4_b1s`) ships a re-paired f32 K128 fold. Output is bit-identical; 27B pp8192 prefill is about 1% faster.** The fold's math is unchanged per element (`float(C) - magic`, `RN(sc*d)`, fused `fma`, ascending K128 order). Only the VOPD packet partners, the register rotation and the issue priority change:
  - **Change** (`iu4_gemm::Tune` chain fold, selected only for this export by `shipped_gate_up_slab`):
    - Each fmac pairs with the next accumulator's stage-1 `subrev`, so stage 1 leads by one accumulator.
    - The unbiased values rotate between VGPR banks. Packets that read one bank twice drop from 64 to 20 per K128.
    - `s_setprio 2` covers each K128 block's WMMA groups and `s_setprio 1` the fold.
    - The `_v64` verify exports and every other export are byte-identical. Module SHA b952699f -> b351ce70; export code SHA c9f1efc5 -> 9d12e51e.
  - **How it was found:** PM-KRSI fold rounds F1–F3, an agent search on the f32 fold, after PmKrsi1100's IU4 roofline found it is 33% of the kernel's cycles. An exact op-count cut does not exist (proved during the search); fold cost on gfx1201 follows bank collisions within a packet.
  - **Node timing** (pm_loop ABBA vs the old shipped kernel, M=17408 K=5120 N=8192): 0.9745, and 0.9758 in a fresh process (sign test p <= 4.9e-4, A/A floor 0.027%).
  - **End to end** (R9700, `hipfire bench --matrix --spec off`, 6 fresh processes per arm, alternating order, base = beta 6c99bef7f8):
    - pp8192: median 5,168 -> 5,223 tok/s (+1.1%; land min 5,207 > base max 5,177).
    - pp16384: +0.4% (not separable).
  - **Identity:** greedy text (`-t 0 -n 400`, prompt md5 db6cbbd9, fresh HOME and kernel cache) is byte-identical base vs new. The gfx1201 `.kldseq` pins reproduce on the new build: WT2 ff88c499, code24 9b061631.
- **Added: long prompts now show prefill progress instead of silence: the daemon emits `prefill_progress` events, `hipfire run` prints a live `prefill 512/2048 tokens (25%), ETA 6s` line, the TUI chat shows `prefilling 512/2048 (25%) · ETA 6s`, and `hipfire serve` streams send a `: prefill 512/2048` SSE comment.** The daemon writes `{"type":"prefill_progress","id","attempt_id","done","total"}` (`done`/`total` count the prompt tokens this request prefills, a cache-hit prefix excluded) after each prompt-prefill chunk while `done < total` (no event for a single-chunk prompt or at `done == total`), ordered after `gen_start` and before the first token/reasoning event; the id is escaped through `serde_json` like every other event. Instrumented: the Qwen3.5-family AR prefill (no-eviction and eviction chunk loops), vision-language batched prefill, native-MTP and DFlash prompt prefill, dense TP2 and Qwen3.5 MoE EP prefill, Flash-Next (Qwen4) AR, native-MTP and continuous-batch lane prefill, and the Qwen3.5 VMM continuous-batch lanes; routes whose prompt prefill is one whole-prompt forward (the legacy Qwen3.5 batch lane, LFM, Gemma4, MiniMax, DS4 EP) and the experimental multi-slot engine emit nothing. Chunk loops in crates without the request writer report through a thread-local `hipfire_runtime::prefill_progress` scope that is live only during the request's prompt prefill (decode-time replays, forced advances and terminal repair stay silent); no extra GPU sync, one small line per chunk. The `hipfire_client` engine surfaces the event to `generate` callbacks (`OpenAiSseEvent::PrefillProgress` on the SSE side, `prefill_percent`/`prefill_eta_secs` helpers); `hipfire run` prints it to stderr on a TTY only (not `--json`, throttled to 500 ms, erased before the first token); `serve` drops the comment before the `200` commits (a stream never commits early because of it), counts it for keepalive, and never sends it after the final frame. `HIPFIRE_PREFILL_PROGRESS=0` suppresses the daemon event (and so every consumer). Measured on one R9700 (Qwen3.8-27B `.mq4r`, 77,092-token prompt, `hipfire run --stats` on a pty): 150 progress updates on each of `--spec off`, `mtp` and `dflash`; TTFT 118.0 s with progress vs 118.3 s with `HIPFIRE_PREFILL_PROGRESS=0` (no cost). `hipfire serve` on the same prompt committed at 15 s and then streamed `: prefill 4096/77906` and one comment per 512-token chunk until the first token. The ETA extrapolates the rate so far, so it reads low early in a long prompt whose later chunks attend over more context. See `docs/SERVE.md` (streaming), `docs/CLI.md` (`run`) and `docs/env-vars.md`.
- **Added: every model load prints one `hipfire load summary:` INFO line stating what is on or off and why (speculation route and the engine's reason when it is off, KV layout/backend, admitted context and what bound it, weight placement, load-time prefill decisions).** The loader, Qwen3.5/Qwen4/DeepSeek4 carriers and the daemon record their existing decisions through a new process-global `hipfire_config::load_summary` note store (reset per load, no policy re-derived); the daemon formats the line and adds the same facets to the `loaded` ack as a `load_summary` object, which `hipfire serve` publishes on the resident model's `/v1/models` entry. `hipfire run`/`serve` inherit the daemon stderr, so the line appears once; `bench` is unchanged. Observed on one R9700 with a config that turns every speculator off: `hipfire run qwen3.8:27b` prints `spec: off (DFlash off: speculation.dflash=off; MTP off: speculation.mtp=off; ngram off: speculation.ngram=off) | kv: fp8 (vmm backend, automatic) | context: 262144 (user-set; model 262144, card 504465; measured fit unchanged)`, and `--spec dflash` / `--spec mtp` / `--spec ngram` print `spec: dflash (draft qwen38-27b-dflash-mq4.hfq, block 16)` / `mtp K=3` / `ngram K=12 min=2`. See `docs/CLI.md` (Load summary) and `docs/SERVE.md`.
- **Added: `hipfire fit` takes `--kv-mode`, `--kv-k`, `--kv-v` and `--spec` (alias `--speculation`), so the dry-run admission answers for the exact load `hipfire run` would make, and its plan now says what it is based on and why it decodes the way it does.** Fit builds its load params through the same helper `run` now calls (`load_params_with_overrides`: config, `--kv-mode`, the `--kv-k`/`--kv-v` axes, the effective speculation selector, the DFlash draft it keeps), so a refused combination (`--kv-mode fp8` with `--kv-k q8`, `--spec mtp` on a Qwen4 profile with no MTP head, `--spec dflash` on an artifact with no declared draft) is the `admission` finding with the engine's exact text, and an invalid `--kv-mode`/`--kv-k` value gets the config schema's own message. `decode` reports every route the params select (`ar`, `dflash (draft <file>)`, `dspark`, `mtp`, `mtp (auto)`, `ngram`) with a second line naming the setting that armed it or kept AR (`--spec off`, `speculation.mode = off (config)`, MTP `auto` on an architecture with no measured AR floor or over host-mapped experts); a declared DFlash draft that is not installed is a new `draft` finding (`DOES NOT FIT` for an installed model, `UNDETERMINED` for a header-only tag; fix `hipfire pull <tag>`; the size is the registry's, fit never downloads it). The plan gets a `basis` line (`pre-load estimate from file headers + sysfs; the load re-measures free VRAM after weights, drafts and scratch (max_seq fit) and may admit less`) and `capacity` is tagged `(pre-load estimate: ...)`. JSON stays `hipfire-fit-1`, additively: `plan.basis`, `plan.decode_reason`, and top-level `overrides` (`input` stays the model-name string). When a GPU's free memory leaves no useful context (a busy card), the context finding says the model does not fit that GPU's currently free memory (free, total and held GiB) instead of suggesting a `memory.max_seq` of 0, and with several visible GPUs the plan, the per-GPU `this machine` rows and the quant-tier table use the best one (`plan.best_device`, per-device `capacity`, additive in JSON); every shown capacity is capped at the model's trained window with the raw KV room noted (`up to 262144 tokens (model limit; KV room for 1.68M)`; JSON keeps the raw `capacity` and adds `capacity_shown`). `run`'s behaviour is unchanged. See `docs/CLI.md` `### hipfire fit`.
- **Added: `hipfire config explain` with no key prints every effective setting with its source, and audits the `HIPFIRE_*` environment.** One row per schema key (grouped like `list`; `developer.*` only when set) with the layer that set it: `default`, `default · <arch>`, `registry <tag>`, `profile <name>`, `config.toml`, `<catalog file> [<model>]`, `env HIPFIRE_X` or `cli`; `--model <tag>` resolves in model scope like `hipfire config <tag> list`, and `-j` emits `settings` and `env` arrays. The `environment` section classifies each set `HIPFIRE_*` variable as `applies <key>`, `bootstrap`, `runtime`, `DEPRECATED since 0.4.0, removed in 0.5.0: <what to do instead>` (CASK/PFlash aliases, `HIPFIRE_DFLASH_WINDOW=0`, `HIPFIRE_DFLASH_CTX_CAP`) or `UNKNOWN` with a nearest-name suggestion (typos such as `HIPFIRE_KVMODE` no longer pass silently); secret-looking names print `(set)`. Classifier: `hipfire_config::env_audit`, known names from the `docs/env-vars.md` inventory. `config explain <key>` is unchanged.
- **Changed: the most common refusals now name the expected file and the exact next command.** `model not found` (`run`, `img`, `embed`, `bench`, `sidecar-gen`) names the file expected under the models dir and `hipfire pull <tag>` (or `place <file> in <models>` for a local-only entry; a path says `no such file` and points at `hipfire list -r`; an unknown tag keeps its did-you-mean list and adds `then: hipfire pull <closest>`). `daemon binary not found` (`run`, `img`, `embed`, `bench`, `profile`, `serve`, `emu`) repeats the `cargo build --release -p hipfire-daemon` hint and names the install path it probes and `HIPFIRE_DAEMON_BIN`. `DFlash draft not found`, `vision sidecar not found` (`run` and `serve`), `port N is in use by another process`, the `serve` `model not found locally` / `serve.allow_request_paths` refusals, the loader's `spec-decode target unsupported` / `spec emitter unsupported` (`--spec off`) and the Flash-Next `safetensors is a conversion input` refusal (`hipfire quantize <dir>`) each append the flag, config key or command that fixes them. Message prefixes are unchanged.
- **Fixed: Qwen4 slow-link prefill (S1) on a stacked-expert (aggregate F16 / symmetric IU4) artifact with a 1,537–3,113-row context now declines by name and runs the incumbent, instead of failing admission with a dispatch `degenerate route storage dimensions` error that looked like a HIP fault (and failed a forced `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SLOWLINK_PREFILL=1` load as a capacity refusal).** The window is `min(16,896, max_seq)` rows, but the aggregate routes charge a worst-case 48 K1 + 3,066 F32-tail cohort (3,114 rows) that the route layout needs inside it. Admission now refuses such a window before the census with `window too small for its cohort rows: rows {r} < k1 48 + tail 3066`, computed from the same `route_dims` the layout is built from. Every context that admitted before (aggregate from 3,114 rows, the slab route from 1,537) is untouched: the check only adds a refusal, so profiles, census and layouts are byte-identical.
- **Perf: 7900 XTX (exact gfx1100) Flash-Next native MTP is on by default with host-mapped routed experts (`--spec off` / `speculation.mtp = "off"` opts out).** `auto` previously declined the head there (`qwen4 native MTP: off by default with host-mapped experts`) and ran AR. XTX default A/B (OD 2400, `auto` before vs after): greedy 32K code 34.5 -> 45.6 tok/s (+31.7%), 32K prose +15.1%, 131K code +32.6%, 131K prose +48%; sampled (registry settings T1.0 / top-p 0.95 / top-k 20) 32K code +28%, 32K prose +38%, 131K prose +48%, no request retired to AR (n=2-3 per arm; 131K n=1-2). Greedy MTP ids are not byte-identical to AR on this route: they diverge near argmax ties (3 of 4 greedy cells, first difference at token 44-66; texts coherent; MTP repeats itself exactly), the same host-mapped divergence recorded in 0.4.0. Sampled MTP matches AR in distribution: the sampled-MTP oracle passes on the gfx1201 host-mapped route with the D2 split forced on (4 arms x 2000 trials, min p 0.068); it could not run on the XTX test host, whose PCIe link drops under that workload. The per-request AR floor still retires MTP to AR on any request where it loses. Other arches with host-mapped experts (gfx1151, unmeasured) still keep AR under `auto`.
- **Perf: exact gfx1201 symmetric/asymmetric MQ3V2 (qt49) base WMMA kernels (residual, gate/up, qkv, qkvza; the n<64 route speculative verify runs on) split K across 8 waves per block and load each 104 B group as 13 aligned u64 with packed fp16 dequant.** The old kernel ran one wave per 16 rows (320 waves on the m=5120 projections) with 48 single-byte loads per group. Kernel time on one R9700, cold weights, n=2..16: down/wo residual median 120 -> 68 us, m=17408 residual 88 -> 73 us, fused gate/up pair 206 -> 139 us; result matches a host reference to the fp16 limit (rel 2.5e-4, same as before). Qwen3.8-27B mq3-xts, 3 fresh processes: DFlash 155.8 -> 177.3 tok/s, MTP 73.4 -> 89.0 (tau and the 128-token greedy output unchanged on two prompts), pp4096/pp16384 unchanged (3,550/3,401 -> 3,552/3,408 tok/s).
- **Perf: symmetric MQ3V2 (qt49, `mq3-xts`) speculative verify on exact gfx1201 (MTP, DFlash block 16: n<=16 rows) runs the fp16 WMMA tiles instead of the W3A4 integer MMQ; A4 now starts at 17 rows.** The A4 consumer is a 128x128 tile with width-independent cost; at n<=16 the WMMA kernel is 1.3-1.7x faster on every 27B projection (gate/up 115 vs 77 us, down 160 vs 101 us at n=8) and also drops the per-projection activation quantize. Qwen3.8-27B mq3-xts, one R9700, same prompt, 3 fresh processes: DFlash 113.8 -> 154.8 tok/s median (+36%; tau 8.77 -> 9.58), MTP 53.8 -> 70.9 (+32%; tau 2.63 -> 2.74; one run at 49.2 under host noise); the 128-token greedy output is byte-identical before and after and to AR. Prefill (n>=64) and gfx1100 are unchanged.
- **Fixed: the direct HFQ weight loader now refuses stale cross-row HFQ4-G128 payloads instead of returning NaN logits.** The weight_store manifest paths already rejected files quantized before `b4846285e` (groups packed across rows when `K % 128 != 0`), but `hfq::load_weights_hfq` and the other `decode_raw_codec` callers uploaded them and produced all-NaN logits (stale `smollm2-360m-instruct.mq4`: 49152/49152 NaN). `decode_raw_codec` now applies the same per-row `validate_payload_extent` check, so the load fails with `source payload has N bytes, expected M for HFQ4G128 [rows, K]`. Re-quantized files load unchanged.
- **Fixed: the llama-family AR route (`llama::forward_scratch` decode, e.g. Qwen3-8B) streamed the end-of-turn token as text and sent no `finish_reason` (HIPF-191).** Qwen3-8B AR emitted a trailing `<|im_end|>` token event that DFlash/DSpark never emit, and its `done` had no `finish_reason`, so serve reported `stop` for `max_tokens`-truncated replies. The terminator is still committed to KV but no longer streamed, and `done` carries `stop` or `length`. gfx1151 qwen3-8b.mq4 greedy: AR text now byte-identical to DFlash.
- **Perf: Flash-Next native MTP n-gram copy lane is on by default on Strix Halo (gfx1151) and R9700 (gfx1201): single-file edits +11.6–14.6% decode on Halo (whole-file edit 92.6 -> 106.1 tok/s), +5.6–7.2% on R9700; `HIPFIRE_MTP_NGRAM_COPY=off` / `speculation.mtp_ngram_copy = "off"` is the kill switch.** `speculation.mtp_ngram_copy = "auto"` now arms the copy lane (verbatim-copy matcher, triple 5/1/63, take cap 7) for native Qwen4 MTP (arch 16) on gfx1151 and gfx1201, the two GPUs whose n-gram source `auto` already arms; every other GPU keeps the 5/3/3 pool, and `on`/`off` are unchanged. It had stayed off since it landed because its Oct 17 re-gate (Halo, monolithic GPTQ3 + q4 PLE, before the fixed-row-tile verify kernels) measured no gain once the fill-shift head fix had raised native acceptance (sampled f11 −0.5%, agentic −4.5%, two processes per arm). Re-measured on beta 3e79fc400 with the canonical registry layout (split base + arch PLE + trunk overlay + expert hot set, native K=7, take cap 7), one binary per card, the switch set by env only, a fresh `hipfire serve` per process, ABBA-interleaved; decode tok/s is the token-weighted server rate, median over processes (receipts `release-0.4.3/copylane/runs/{E,halo}`, kit `copylane/kit`, prompts md5-pinned in `kit/PROMPTS.MD5`). Greedy output was byte-identical copy-lane on vs off on every request (Halo 48/48, R9700 96/96), takeovers accepted 96–99% of drafted tokens on edits, TTFT and load placement unchanged, sampled outputs sane (edit correctness 9/9 per arm on the whole-file edit).
  | Workload (decode tok/s, off -> on) | Strix Halo, 3 processes/arm | R9700, 6 processes/arm |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | Edit, greedy (whole-file rename edit, signature edit, list copy) | 93.08 -> 103.85 (+11.6%) | 69.19 -> 74.15 (+7.2%) |
  | Edit, sampled T0.7 top-p 0.95 top-k 20 | 92.20 -> 104.73 (+13.6%) | 69.57 -> 74.50 (+7.1%) |
  | Edit, greedy, thinking on | 89.20 -> 96.90 (+8.6%) | 66.60 -> 70.35 (+5.6%) |
  | Code, greedy (fresh function, HumanEval completion) | 77.38 -> 84.92 (+9.8%) | 85.31 -> 85.06 (−0.3%) |
  | Code, sampled / thinking on | +2.7% / +0.4% | +2.9% / −0.1% |
  | Prose, greedy / sampled | −0.4% / −1.8% | +0.7% / −0.3% |
  | Agentic code-edit chain (6 turns, 9–29K context, thinking on), greedy / sampled | 68.12 -> 69.04 (+1.4%) / −0.2% | −0.3% / −0.4% |

  Copy-free requests (prose, the agentic chain's mostly new text) take no or few copy windows and stay within noise; the R9700 ran on a shared host with whole-process slow modes in both arms (process spread up to 35% on single prompts, medians unaffected).
- **Fixed: Flash-Next DFlash2 keeps the live session after a turn that stops inside a verified window (HIPF-179).** `Dflash2Speculator` had no terminal-prefix repair, so an EOS or stop inside the accepted drafts took the unrepaired-terminal reset and the next turn could reuse only a session snapshot. The Qwen4 target now retains the window's pre-window snapshot after `commit_prefix` (as native MTP does); the new `SpecTarget::repair_committed_prefix` restores it and replays the consumed prefix, and the speculator trims its feature rows and `host_tokens` to match. gfx1151, HIPF-143 mt-bench (16 x 2 turns, greedy): turn-2 cached tokens 4493 -> 5335 (= warm AR), turn-2 text equal to warm AR on 16/16 rows (was 15/16); decode tok/s unchanged.
- **Developer (lab): `pm_loop` times the gfx1201 IU4 verify shapes cold (`--pool`, `--flush-l2`, `--flush`), adds a `qkvzaset` adapter and records a same-process null dispatch (`timing.null_dispatch`).** Hot pm_loop reads of the 40-272-workgroup verify GEMMs were up to 38% faster than the same kernels in-model, so verify candidates were mis-ranked. `--pool` rotates distinct seeded weight sets totalling more than 192 MiB (weights cold, activations and instructions warm) and matched the in-model rocprof node times of 27B DFlash verify within 5.6% (mean 3.0%) on all nine cells (gate_up, down, qkvzaset at n = 32 / 64 / 80; R9700, shipped `_v64` objects, identity held on every pool member); `--flush-l2` read 5-20% slow and `--flush` (2 x 96 MiB device copy between dispatches, shared with `hip_loop` via `examples/support/cold.rs`) 26-53% slow. Verify-shape candidates are judged with `--pool`.
- **Developer: Flash-Next EP ranks bind dispatch through the sealed plan (#861 slice 3).** Every Qwen4 EP MoE table (compact decode, full-peer chunk, balanced live, MTP head) now comes from `adapt_expert_execution_plan(plan, rank)` (real owner ranks, compact local slots, the owner-routed EP contract) instead of a rank-0-of-1 stand-in; dispatch admits such a rank on the None-mode decode/prefill path (`ExpertExecutionContract::is_owner_routed_ep`) and refuses before launch a rank without that contract, outside the sealed mesh or owning no expert, an EP decode without its row gather, and a tile exchange of another rank. The tile owner table and the static row gather read the seal's ownership. Emulated EP2/EP4 on gfx1151 stays byte-identical to single-device and to beta.
- **Flash-Next (Qwen4) EP: exact output-axis split of the replicated trunk projections (`HIPFIRE_EP_TRUNK_SPLIT=prefill|decode|on`, default off; #862).** Rank `r` of `N` projects only complete output rows `[r*m/N, (r+1)*m/N)` of the QSA q/k/v/indexer/output, GDN qkv/z/output, the Q8 decode copies of the HC input-mix down and the LM head (MTP head QSA included) on a row view of the resident weight, so every output element keeps its whole reduction; a copy-only band exchange (`EpRowGather::exchange_bands`, one pitched copy per rank, the row gather's publish/barrier/alternating-buffer protocol plus a cross-rank geometry tag) rebuilds the full output before any consumer, and the LM head is gathered whole before the unchanged full-vector argmax. The seam is shared (`hipfire_dispatch::pipeline::projection_split`, installed per rank thread by the mesh); prefill (chunk forwards) and decode (decode/verify of at most 8 rows) are gated separately; BF16 weights, the row-exact wide verify, the IU4 trunk and calls larger than the exchange buffer project whole. Attach refuses ranks whose banded-weight census or chunk rows differ. Every rank still keeps the whole trunk resident (no memory saving yet). Halo gfx1151, **EMULATED** EP2/EP4 (`HIPFIRE_EMULATE_GPUS`): logits, peer mirrors and state byte-identical to single for AR (6 prompts x 64 tokens, every mode, EP4 `on`) and native MTP greedy/sampled (verify, head, rollback), 48-layer chunk digests identical, flag-off EP2 == beta EP2. The long-prefill gain, decode cost and per-rank bytes need physical multi-GPU and are not measured. (#1010, @fivetide)
- **Perf: symmetric MQ3V2 (qt49, `mq3v2.symmetric`, the dense `mq3-xts` recipe) prefill runs W3A4 integer WMMA on exact gfx1201 by default: 27B pp4096 616 -> 3,559 tok/s, pp16384 607 -> 3,436 (5.7-5.8x, one R9700, 3 fresh processes per arm; decode unchanged at 49.3 tok/s). `HIPFIRE_MQ3V25_A4=0` (or `kernel.iu4_prefill=false`) restores the F16 route.** The loader validates every qt49 group's zero = f16(-4·d) before trusting the marker (a marked file with a bad group fails to load; unmarked/asymmetric qt49 files are unchanged). Dense qwen35 prefill on such artifacts admits the 8192-row chunk and the GDN chunk scan; the gfx1201 RMSNorm/SwiGLU A4 producers feed `gemm_mq3v25_residual_mmq_iu4` (SET/ADD) and its gate/up+SiLU twin, which widen the 3-bit codes to int4 in LDS and are bit-identical to the MQ4 IU4 kernels on equivalent weights. Quality on a 27B RTN symmetric qt49 fixture (AGENTS.md §5 method, fp8 K / q8 V, 24 chunks): WT2 KLD F16 0.165682, A8 0.166033, A4 0.192996; code24 0.116710 / 0.117199 / 0.139162. The A4 penalty over the 8-bit-activation route (+0.0270 WT2, +0.0220 code24) is within shipped MQ4 A4's penalty over native FP8 at the current pins (+0.0277 / +0.0223). gfx1100 (7900 XTX, full-tile V2C kernel) is opt-in `HIPFIRE_MQ3V25_A4=1` until its hardware proof; gfx1151 keeps the F16 route (its V2B kernel is bench-only). `HIPFIRE_MQ3V25_A8=1` (developer, exact gfx1201) selects a W3A8 route on the shared 136-byte `block_i8_128` activations.
- **Changed: `hipfire serve`, `run` and `bench` now warn loudly on stderr when GPU memory spills to system RAM (GTT growth with VRAM full), instead of silently running 2-3x slower.** On Linux/amdgpu a `SpillMonitor` (`crates/hipfire-cli/src/spill.rs`) baselines `mem_info_gtt_used` right after the model load on the card the bench's `power_device` resolution names, and after each finished request (each generation for `run`/`bench`) prints `WARNING: GPU memory is spilling to system RAM: GTT +N MiB since load while VRAM is full (U/T MiB)…` when GTT grew >= 256 MiB while VRAM used is within 512 MiB of total; it repeats only after another 256 MiB. `bench --json` adds a per-run `spill` object. Unreadable counters disable it silently; no-op off Linux. See `docs/CONFIG.md` § Spill warning.
- **Fixed: a single-card Qwen VMM load with automatic `max_seq` no longer promises a context it cannot hold, and an explicit `max_seq` that cannot fit is refused at load instead of failing mid-request.** Qwen3.8-27B MQ4-XTS + DFlash on a 20 GiB card (R9700 with 12 GiB held by another process; same result in 0.4.4) published `max_seq` 119,610 and then failed with `prefill: hipMalloc: out of memory` at ~40K tokens; AR failed at ~100K; an explicit 131,072 loaded and failed at ~38K. The carrier's `card_cap` is measured right after the weights upload, before the KV owners' prefix, DeltaNet state, scratch and the DFlash/MTP/DSpark drafts exist, and per-request owners were charged nowhere. `card_cap` now also subtracts the drafts' device reserve (one resolver shared with the placement capacity), and `finish_qwen35_load` re-measures after the speculator is built: the published context is the largest whose remaining KV mapping (`planned_mapped_growth_bytes`) plus a per-request reserve fits the free VRAM (`admission::qwen35_measured_fit`). The reserve is the minimum prefill reserve (512-row PBS, its 1 GiB headroom, 128 MiB rounding), one DeltaNet checkpoint per ring (AR ring, plus the speculator's; further checkpoints are taken only from memory the admitted context does not need, else the ring recycles its oldest), and with native MTP the per-request `MtpSpecState` and prompt-fill buffers. Below 512 tokens an automatic load is refused; an explicit `max_seq` above the fit is refused naming the largest fitting value (`memory.oom_guard = off`: warning only). One `max_seq fit: measured after full load: free=… transient=… (prefill … + checkpoints … + mtp …) … ; context A -> B` line reports it. Measured on a 20 GiB-equivalent R9700, every config filled to its published context (prompt = context - 768, then 512 generated tokens) without error: MQ4-XTS DFlash 36,578 (fp8 KV) / 34,695 (q8), MTP 69,092 (fp8) / 86,738 (fwht3); MQ3-XT MTP 136,854 (q8) / 181,187 (fwht3), DFlash 115,651 (q8). 16 GiB: MQ3-XT MTP 32,768 (q8) / 41,943 (fwht3); MQ4-XTS is refused at load. On a 32 GiB R9700 the automatic context stays 262,144 for AR, DFlash and MTP.
- **Fixed: Qwen3.5-family native MTP no longer allocates a whole-prompt hidden buffer per request (Qwen3.8-27B: 20 KiB per prompt token, 1.76 GiB at 90K tokens), which nothing charged and which made long prompts fail mid-prefill with `mtp prefill: hipMalloc: out of memory` well inside the admitted context.** The prompt-fill pairing buffer (`prefill_trunk_and_mtp_cache_parts`, `crates/hipfire-arch-qwen35/src/mtp_spec.rs`) now holds one outer prefill chunk plus its partner row; the chunk's last hidden is carried to row 0 between chunks and seeds `prev_hidden` after the last one. Pairing (token `p` with the trunk hidden of `p - 1`) is unchanged.
- **Fixed: a Qwen3.5-family prompt no longer picks a wide prefill PBS that its own later KV growth needs.** The AR, vision, native-MTP and DFlash prompt paths choose the prefill ceiling once per prompt from free VRAM; that choice now deducts the KV the same prompt will still map (`qwen35::prefill::request_kv_growth_deduction`), so a long prompt on a tight card runs narrower chunks instead of allocating ~1.8 GB of widened PBS early and failing its own KV mapping later. With no remaining KV growth (short prompts, warm cache, large cards) the choice is unchanged.
- **Fixed: a registry tag whose canonical local file is missing or a dangling symlink no longer loads a different tier.** `find_model_path` (hipfire-cli) fell through to a separator-insensitive substring scan, so `qwen3.8:27b-mq3` with a dangling `qwen3.8-27b.mq3` link silently loaded `qwen3.8-27b.mq3-xt` (first in directory order; `-pro` matched too). For a registry tag the fallback now accepts only a file whose name equals the entry's `file` ignoring `-`/`.`/`_`; otherwise the tag resolves to nothing and the existing sha-verified pull runs (it replaces a dangling link).
- **Fixed: Qwen2 (`qwen2_ar`) and MiniMax (`minimax_ar`) AR `done` carries `finish_reason` (`stop` on EOS, `length` on `max_tokens`).** Serve read the missing reason as `stop`, so a reply cut off by `max_tokens` reached clients as `stop` / Anthropic `end_turn` / Responses `completed`. Same rule as the generic llama loop (#1008).
- **Fixed: kernel objects no longer embed the build directory (`givens_rotate_to_g64_f32` changed bytes on every pack build), and `kernel_idproof` names modules the toolchain itself compiles nondeterministically instead of reporting them changed.** Device `assert` expands `__FILE__` into the object; the pack script compiles in a fresh `mktemp` tree, so the module (the only registered one with a live `assert`, `kernels/src/givens_rotate_to.hip`) carried `.../hipfire-kernel-pack.<random>/kernel-cache/<arch>/<module>.<key>.hip` and was reported changed between any two builds. `hipcc` now gets `-fmacro-prefix-map=<source dir>/=`, so the object names only `<module>.<key>.hip`. Argv only: no cache key, pack index or other module's bytes change, and a source in a directory containing `=` keeps the old behavior. The module's object changes once, at this commit; a unit test pins the argv. Separately, gfx1201 `qsa_bf16_scores` compiles to one of three equivalent code variants run to run (hipcc's post-RA scheduler; same source, flags and path; gfx1100/gfx1151 are stable), so two builds of one commit can still differ in that module: `kernel_idproof` now classifies a module whose index.json matches but for `object_sha256` (and whose `.hash` matches) yet whose object differs as `nondeterministic`, lists it by name, and does not fail `--require-identical` for it.
- **Perf: the Qwen4 S1 slow-link prefill window is sized from the load's actual free device memory (keeping 1 GiB free) and levelled per request.** `admit_grown` sizes the window at load, on a quote that holds 1 GiB back from the actual free device memory (so the load leaves at least that much free beyond every charge, the 512 MiB margin and the session cache's device snapshot slack). A context whose covering window (`max_seq` rounded up to a 768-row tile) is at most 64 tiles runs every request in one window, so the window outranks extra resident layers: the covering window is tried first, then a binary search down to the largest whole-tile window above the 22-tile (16,896-row) floor that admits, each with its own resident-layer verdict (the KV charge is that of the load's `max_seq`). A longer context (262,144, 131,072) runs several windows anyway: it keeps the floor admission's resident-layer count and grows the window only with the memory left at that count above the hold; nothing fitting keeps the floor admission unchanged. The one-layer trade for a 32K one-window is gone. The S1 load line reports the window rows/tiles, resident layers and remaining slack (free hold included). A request's rows are then spread evenly over the windows the greedy packing would run, so a prompt just past a window no longer pays a full expert sweep for a short tail (requests whose windows are closed by session cuts keep the transaction's window ends). Modeled on the XTX Flash-Next MQ4 load at max_seq 262,144: AR-loaded 6 -> 5 resident layers and a 33,024-row window (32K one sweep instead of two; modeled +1.6% at 32K because those windows are compute-bound, and fewer resident layers cost decode speed), MTP-loaded unchanged (no room for the trade); not yet measured on hardware. The daemon logs one `qwen4 S1 plan:` line per S1 request with its window rows (each window is one expert sweep) and one `S1 window grown` line at load.
- **Perf/Memory: 7900 XTX (exact gfx1100) Flash-Next QSA context state and the gather / split-KV decode workspace are demand-mapped VMM by default, byte-identical (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_VMM_GFX1100=0` restores the legacy arenas).** Automatic `kv_backend` now resolves to `vmm` on gfx1100 as on gfx1151/gfx1201 (certified platform and HIP VMM runtime required): pages commit as requests touch them instead of all of `max_seq` at load (96 MiB at the first tile vs 4224 MiB at 262144 tokens, q8), peak VRAM measured ~3.5 GiB lower (18.22 vs 21.75 GiB, 8K+32K cell), greedy 8K/32K outputs identical, decode and prefill speed unchanged. The gfx1100 VMM path is map-only (never unmaps or remaps a live VA); a CPU unit test pins it. An explicit `kv_backend=vmm` with the switch at `0` is refused naming it.
- **Perf: Flash-Next pipeline-parallel prefill on gfx1201 defaults to 4096-row chunks (4x R9700 PP4: 32K prefill 6,953 -> 16,657 tok/s, 2.4x; 8K +39%; decode unchanged), `HIPFIRE_PREFILL_CHUNK_ROWS=16384` restores the previous chunk.** The PP band pipeline fills only when several canonical chunks are in flight, and the gfx1201 compact default of 16384 rows left a 32K prompt two or three chunks. `qwen4_pp_prefill_chunk_requested` now sizes both the band loads and the PP mesh planner (bands refuse a chunk that differs from the mesh chunk); an explicit `HIPFIRE_PREFILL_CHUNK_ROWS` still wins, and single card, EP and other arches are unchanged. PP output equals a single-card run at the same chunk; the first 32 greedy tokens were identical to single card at 8K/32K/64K/131K (byte identity evidence pending). Measured 2026-10-28, 4x R9700, packed mq4-xts, beta c7c44097cc + explicit chunk env, greedy, one fresh process per arm (decode ~54 tok/s in every arm):
  | Prefill tok/s | 16384 rows (old default) | 8192 rows | 4096 rows (new default) |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | 8K | 4,838 | 6,039 | 6,709 |
  | 32K | 6,953 | 14,026 | 16,657 |
  | 64K | 13,445 | 16,735 | 18,260 |
  | 131K | 15,194 | 17,444 | 17,885 |
- **Fixed (lab): `qwen4_kld`'s `auto` expert placement now leaves its own all-row logits buffer free, so a 24 GB card no longer places experts into the memory that buffer needs.** `eval` allocates `n_ctx` x vocab F32 logits (1940 MiB at 2048 rows) after the placement, which the product loader never holds and the `incumbent_auto_resident_layers` reserve did not charge: on the 7900 XTX at `n_ctx` 2048 `auto` kept layers 0..10 (210 MiB over reserve + margin) and the first prefill hit `hipMalloc: out of memory`; it now keeps 0..8. `incumbent_auto_resident_layers` takes the extra bytes (`all_row_logits_bytes`); the product loader, `qwen4_greedy_ids`, `qwen4_cpu_split_parity` and the S1 fallback pass 0 and are unchanged. The symmetric-IU4 MoE route's own scratch was already charged by the product placement (`int4_xq`, `moe_group`, `down_i4q` census terms, equal to the `reserve_qwen4_moe_sym` allocations except the down sidecar's 2.6 MiB expert pad, inside the 512 MiB safety margin).
- **Added (developer knob, now default ON on exact gfx1100; see above): SP, a short-prompt per-window mode of the S1 slow-link prefill on the 7900 XTX (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SP=1`, typed `developer.qwen4_sp`).** After each host layer's single count barrier the planner (`sp_plan` cost model, exact argmin over k) picks the top-k* experts by exact routed-token count and streams only those (one ring page set per layer, no prefetch); every other active expert runs on the CPU (the D2 F32/BF16-boundary engine on the widened F16 activations the GPU arm reads, rounded BF16 RNE into a compact pinned row table); one unchanged `slowlink_combine_panel` over the hybrid row table applies every slot in canonical expert-id order, so the result is a function of the route ids alone. It also opens S1 to single-tile requests of 5..=768 rows (all-or-incumbent: S1 admits them only when their window is SP-qualified) (S1 now levels a multi-window request's rows across its windows, so no short last window of SP's size remains to open). Everything is gated: exact gfx1100, the `Aggregate` window route (on a symmetric-IU4 profile, the gfx1100 default, SP-qualified windows run the F16 `Aggregate` route through a per-window override of the tile scope's MoE arm, carved from the same route region (SP row cap 4,507 there), while non-SP windows keep SymIu4; `sp: f16 route` names a profile that cannot host it), 512 experts, CPU quants for the host layers, a splice pool, the route-region fit, the pinned-host fit and `serve.prefix_cache` off; a failed rule is a sticky named `sp: <reason>` decline (receipt `sp.decline`) and S1 is unchanged. Adds no VRAM (the hybrid table lives in the already-charged route region) and about 158 MiB of pinned host memory (`LoadOwner::SpHost`: x16 / sorted / CPU-rows / inverse buffers, the xfer stream, four events, the CPU scratch). An SP-armed process scopes its session snapshots with the `sp-e1v1` host-arithmetic identity, so it never shares a snapshot (disk tier included) with an SP-off lineage. A mid-window failure drains the ring and the xfer stream, quarantines the SP owners if that drain fails, restores the transaction and disables SP for the process (`sp_unavailable`). With the knob off no SP code path runs and receipts are unchanged (the `sp` receipt object exists only with the knob on). Lab builds add `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SP_FORCE_K=all|cpu|auto` (`all` selects the touched-only mode below) and `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SP_TRACE=1` (one JSON line per SP layer). The numerics differ from stream-all S1 only in the CPU slots' values (E1 vs WMMA) and in the K2-ized F32-tail tiles; the card gates (identity of the non-SP paths, exact mechanics, TTFT A/B, KLD, soak) had not run when this entry was written; they have since (see the two default-on Perf entries above), and the knob is now on by default on gfx1100. Design and gates: `screens/SP/HOOK-DESIGN.md`.
- **Perf: 7900 XTX (exact gfx1100) hybrid SP is the default short-prompt prefill: Flash-Next TTFT at 1K rows 8.05 s -> about 2.1 s, KLD-gated (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SP=0` is the kill switch; typed `developer.qwen4_sp`).** Unset now resolves to on for exact gfx1100 and off on every other arch (an explicit `1` elsewhere declines `sp: arch not calibrated`). On short single windows (5..=5,376 rows, no interior session cut) the hybrid mode streams each host layer's top-k\* experts and runs the rest on the CPU (D2 E1 engine), one canonical combine, SP windows on the F16 `Aggregate` route on the symmetric-IU4 profile. Quality gate (V4 KLD vs the BF16 teacher, S1 stream-all as the base): WT2 dKLD -0.0020, 95% CI [-0.0037, -0.0004]; code24 dKLD -0.0023, CI [-0.0067, +0.0007]. Where a load-time rule declines the hybrid mode (a small `max_seq` window whose route region fits fewer than 2,048 SP rows, no CPU quant, the pinned budget, `serve.prefix_cache` on, ...) the touched-only mode (default on, byte-identical to stream-all S1) runs instead and the load prints `qwen4 SP: hybrid mode declined, falling back to touched_only: <reason>`; `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SP_TOUCHED=0` removes the fallback and both knobs `0` is S1 as before. The hybrid mode adds about 158 MiB of pinned host memory and scopes session snapshots with the `sp-e1v1` identity token, so a gfx1100 process no longer shares session snapshots with one that ran without it (set `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SP=0` for that).
- **Perf: 7900 XTX (exact gfx1100) short-prompt prefill (5..=768 rows, one window) now runs on the S1 slow-link prefill with a selective expert schedule (SP touched-only mode), byte-identical to the stream-all S1 sweep, default ON on gfx1100 (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SP_TOUCHED=0` is the kill switch; typed `developer.qwen4_sp_touched`).** The card showed the hybrid SP at k = U (every touched expert streamed, no CPU expert) byte-identical to S1 at N = 1536 / 2048 / 2304 but not at N = 1024 (a 768-row WMMA tile plus a 256-row F32-tail tile), because the hybrid K2-izes F32-tail tiles (a range-masked tail cohort is unsafe over groups that skip CPU experts). With no CPU expert the masking is safe again, so the touched-only mode keeps S1's exact pipeline: on the same short windows as SP (single window of 5..=5,376 rows, no interior session cut, no one-row tile; below S1's 769-row floor all-or-incumbent) every tile keeps its S1 class (the F32-tail tile keeps the 0x80 route fill, the cohort counts and S1's own tail stages), the layer runs S1's per-panel `execute_panel` (K2 GEMMs, ordered per-panel combine, K1 / F32-tail cohort against the panel's binding), and only the weight schedule is selective: after each host layer's count barrier the experts holding a K2 grouped row or a cohort slot (read from the one barrier's padded and cohort counts, no `sorted` readback) are packed ascending into groups of at most 32, tight `[first, last + 1)` bindings, and the ring streams exactly those groups at once (nothing prefetched, resident layers never pump the sweep schedule). It serves both aggregate window routes, the F16 `Aggregate` and the symmetric IU4 `AggregateSymIu4` that is the gfx1100 default (the first card run found the mode declined silently on the IU4 route; the hybrid mode still serves `Aggregate` only and names `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_MOE_SYM_IU4=0` in its decline), and prints one `qwen4 SP:` line to stderr at load with the armed mode or the named decline plus a DEBUG `qwen4 SP window` line per window. No CPU quant, splice pool, pinned owner or VRAM is needed and `serve.prefix_cache` may stay on (the bytes are S1's, so the session-cache identity is unchanged). Equal to stream-all by construction: an expert's arithmetic does not depend on its binding and the ordered per-panel combine (ascending expert id across panels, F32-tail cohort accumulated in place binding by binding) is partition-invariant, a CPU model test (`slowlink_combine_touched_only_panels_equal_stream_all_panels`) proves it for touched versus 32-expert groups, and untouched experts hold no row or cohort slot so no id-range mask drops one. With `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SP=1` also set the hybrid mode wins, except that the lab placement `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SP_FORCE_K=all` now selects this mode. The receipt's `sp` object reports `mode` (`touched_only` / `hybrid`). Greedy-id identity with S1 was proven on the card (two fresh processes at N=1024 and 1536, d32k, `max_seq` 262144, ids equal to beta); unset follows the arch default (on for exact gfx1100, off elsewhere), an explicit `1` on another arch declines `sp: arch not calibrated`. The hybrid SP (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SP=1`, CPU experts, different numerics) stays default OFF pending its KLD gate; with both on, hybrid wins. With the default on, every S1 receipt on gfx1100 carries the `sp` object and the S1 load prints one `qwen4 SP: touched_only mode armed` line.
- **Perf: 7900 XTX Flash-Next native MTP decode +17.8% at 32K, +18.9% at 131K, +19.8% at 250K: the MTP head's routed experts now run on a rows=1 D2 CPU split executor by default whenever the trunk's D2 split is armed on the same load (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_MTP_HEAD_D2=0` is the kill switch), target token ids identical.** XTX qualification (256 greedy tokens, native MTP K=3, default D2 + S1, `max_seq` 262144, stock clocks, one fresh daemon per run, decoded text read): 32K `depth_32768`, ABBAAB, 3 runs per arm: MTP decode 35.5 / 32.7 / 35.4 tok/s with `0` vs 43.4 / 41.7 / 40.3 armed (median 35.4 -> 41.7, +17.8%; every armed run is faster than every `0` run), steady ms/token 28.4 -> 24.1, one token-id sequence across all six runs; accepted drafts per window 1.97 / 1.87 / 1.83 armed vs 1.97 / 1.97 for two `0` runs, while the third `0` run (the 32.7 tok/s one) retired MTP mid-request under the existing retire policy (97 AR windows, 0.59 accepted per window overall) and is kept in the median. 131K `depth_131072`, ABBA, 2 runs per arm: 33.8 / 34.0 -> 40.0 / 40.6 tok/s (+18.9%), steady 29.6 -> 24.8 ms, 1.97 accepted per window in all four, one id sequence. 250K `depth_250000`, 1 run per arm: 27.8 -> 33.3 tok/s (+19.8%), same ids; the `0` run retired MTP after 52 windows (131 AR windows), the armed run kept MTP throughout (1.48 accepted per window). The head's 512 host-mapped experts were read over the link by the GPU on every draft; armed (unset or `1`, trunk D2 armed, non-EP) the CPU reads them in place and the GPU keeps only the shared expert and the routed tail. `0`, or a load whose trunk D2 is off (e.g. a fast-link card), is byte-identical to before (typed boolean developer key `developer.qwen4_mtp_head_d2`). The head executor lives only in the MTP head, so the trunk's split layers, executor capacity rows (4), verify window and census are unchanged; cost is +40 B device and 112,760 B pinned host. The D2 arming decision is unchanged: the measured selector still prices the handoff with the copy-transport constant only (`CURRENT_COPY_TRANSPORT_HANDOFF_NS`). Evidence (7900 XTX, AR, 256 greedy tokens, default D2 + S1, `max_seq` 262144, stock clocks, one fresh daemon per run, decoded text read): 32K ABBAAB n=3 per arm (cells `competitive/depth-sb/cells/d0r1-32k-{1..6}-{copy,cpw}`): `copy`/`host` 33.3 tok/s (steady 29.94 ms/token) vs `mapped`/`cpwait` 34.6 tok/s (28.84 ms/token), every `cpwait` cell faster than every `copy` cell; 131K ABBA with the default build (`l3c-131k-*`): 29.1 / 29.7 -> 31.0 / 31.4 tok/s (steady 33.5 -> 31.9 ms); 250K ABBA (`l3c-250k-*`): 26.5 / 26.5 -> 28.7 / 28.7 tok/s (37.2 -> 34.8 ms); one token-id sequence per depth across both arms, prefill unchanged, and every default load reports 42 mapped / 42 cpwait layers. Request soak, one daemon per arm running 131K/256, 8K/64, 131K/256 (`l3s-*`): both 131K requests return the fresh-daemon 131K ids and the 8K ids match across arms; default 31.7 / 35.1 / 31.7 tok/s vs copy 30.4 / 33.4 / 30.3, no drift between the first and second long request. The CPU arm bytes are the same by construction and the existing D2 parity and canonical-join tests cover the route. The `qwen4_cpu_split_parity` lab drains the stream before the join, so a gfx1100 lab run sets `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_D2_JOIN=host`.
- **Fixed: the per-token PLE row upload no longer runs on the legacy NULL stream (removes the only bidirectional cross-stream dependency from decode; not the cause of the gfx1100 PCIe-link-drop hang).** `PleHostStage` kept its staging bytes in a pageable `Vec` and copied them with `hipMemcpyAsync(..., NULL)`, the only operation in default decode on a stream other than the blocking compute stream C and the token readback stream, so the runtime had to order C and the NULL stream against each other in both directions (the only bidirectional cross-stream pair in decode). The staging buffer is now pinned (`hipHostMalloc`, allocated once on first use, freed in `free_gpu`) and every upload (fenced, unfenced device-token, mesh token ids, blocking opt-out) is a stream-ordered `hipMemcpyAsync` on `gpu.active_stream`. Same bytes, same order on C. The fenced path's fence is now recorded on C; the device-token path stays unfenced (the readback sync of the previous forward's argmax event orders it). The drain rule is a `PleSequencer` unit-tested against a fake device.
- **Perf: exact gfx1201 slab IU4 launches of n ≤ 128 rows (the 64-row DFlash verify chunk, short batches) use per-shape schedules and skip the dead half of the 128-token tile, byte-identical, default ON (`HIPFIRE_VERIFY_V64=0` restores the shipped exports).** Four new `_v64` exports in the `_b1s` bundle (`gate_up_silu`, `full_add`, `full_set`, `qkvzaset`) carry the rendezvous-window schedule (paired W fetch except the fused projection) and the new `iu4_gemm::Tune::idle` knob: at 64 tokens or fewer the tile's token-half-1 waves only computed zeros whose stores are masked, so they skip their WMMA and fold work (the wave remap puts one dead and one live wave on every SIMD). Measured on the card (pm_loop, N = 64, identical to the shipped kernels): down 100.5 -> 62.6 us, wo 42.5 -> 29.2 us, qkv 53.1 -> 37.6 us, z 38.4 -> 27.7 us; the shipped exports are untouched and still serve n > 128 (and every n with the switch off). See `docs/env-vars.md`.
- **Perf: exact gfx1201 DFlash/MTP verify batches (n ≤ 128) run each GDN layer's input projection (QKV, Z, beta, alpha) as one launch instead of four, byte-identical, default ON (`HIPFIRE_GDN_ZBA_FOLD=0` restores the four separate launches).** The non-fused IU4 GDN input projection issued four SET GEMMs per layer; beta and alpha (M = 48) each ran as a single workgroup that was pure K-loop latency, and Z (M = 6144) left most of the GPU idle. The loader already appends beta and alpha to the Z weight buffer for the fused prefill kernel, so one `_b1s` launch (`gemm_mq4g256v2_residual_mmq_iu4_qkvzaset_b1s`, the fused GDN projection kernel without the GDN preparation) now covers the QKV weight and that `z_m + 128`-row fold: QKV tiles store every row like the plain SET kernel, Z tiles store Z, and the last tile stores beta and alpha straight to their outputs (the same rows the same kernel math produced, so all four outputs are bit-identical to the separate launches). When that launch is not admitted (non-slab activations, other shapes) the QKV SET plus the Z/beta/alpha fold SET + `split_mq4v2_z_betaalpha_g12` split, or the separate launches, run as before. Admission is exact gfx1201, the existing fold predicate, the fold weight buffer present, scratch and outputs large and 16-byte aligned; prefill-sized batches keep the previous launches. The new symbols ship in the gfx1201 kernel pack.
- **Perf: the exact VMM continuous-batch route now serves A3B (`qwen3_5_moe` `.mq4rs`) on exact gfx1201, byte-identical per request to the singleton route, default ON (`HIPFIRE_A3B_VMM_BATCH=0` restores the previous route: the batch stager refuses A3B and requests run on the singleton / multi-slot path).** `exact::supports` admitted only dense layers; it now also admits the certified A3B MoE layers (MQ4G256V2 attention/router/shared projections, MQ4G256V2 routed gate/up, MQ4G128V2 routed down, hidden 2048, 256 experts top-8), and every stage that was a per-row singleton launch is lane-batched with per-lane bytes equal to the singleton kernels (DeltaNet mixer, FullAttention mixer incl. the group-8 fp8 VMM flash tile, the MoE block with expert-deduplicated routed gate/up and down, the lm_head), documented in the entries below. C8 aggregate on the 32-request steady set (greedy, 256 tokens, 3 fresh processes, interleaved): 500.0 / 508.9 / 513.1 tok/s (median 508.9; TPOT p50 15 ms) against 235.6 for the previous route (sequential singleton) and 346.9 for the multi-slot route; C4 381 (previous 237.5); C1 unchanged (a lone request runs the singleton). Decoded text of all 32 steady requests is identical to the singleton in every run. Verified with `cb_vmm_state_oracle` (per-lane state, KV, logits byte compare vs the singleton at 1/2/4/8 lanes) and decoded-text identity on the committed prompts.
- **Perf: the exact VMM continuous-batch route reads each distinct routed expert's weights once per layer-step across lanes (A3B gate/up, routed down), byte-identical per lane to the singleton (`HIPFIRE_A3B_MOE_DEDUP=0` restores the lane twins; `HIPFIRE_A3B_MOE_DEDUP_DOWN=0` keeps the twin for the routed down alone).** On a C8 batch the 64 (lane, slot) picks of a layer-step hit only ~46 distinct experts, so ~28% of the routed weight bytes were re-reads. With 2+ lanes `gemv_mq4g256v2_moe_gate_up_k8_dedup_rows` and the routed-down pair `gemv_mq4g128v2_moe_down_dedup_rows` + `gemv_mq4g128v2_moe_down_combine_rows` (`kernels/src/moe_dedup_mq4rs.gfx1201.hip`, `Gpu::moe_decode_lanes_mq4rs`) make one wave per (row tile, lane, slot) read the id table, exit if an earlier pair picked the same expert, else compute every pair that picked it from one weight read, per column with the singleton kernel's arithmetic pinned with explicit fma (the gate and up streams contract differently in the singleton). The routed down is split into the per-pair slot parts (`MoeDecodeLanesArgs::down_expanded`, the existing `moe_down_expanded_batch` scratch) and the singleton's ascending-slot weighted fold. Lab gate `crates/rdna-compute/tests/moe_dedup.rs`: bit-identical to the real singleton launches and to the lane twins for N in {1,2,3,5,8} over same / rotated / partial / disjoint / random / heavy-collision / out-of-range routing and adversarial activations; gate/up at N=8 and 46/64 distinct experts 119 -> 58 us warm (124 -> 80 us at 64/64), the routed down is on par with the twin (compute/latency-bound, not weight-bandwidth-bound). C8 K=8 N=32 daemon smoke on the R9700: 420 -> 451 steady tok/s (gate/up dedup alone 448).
- **Perf: the exact VMM continuous-batch route runs the A3B final norm and lm_head lane-batched, byte-identical per row to the singleton head (`HIPFIRE_A3B_LANE_HEAD=0` restores the previous head).** With 2+ decode rows the 2N per-row `rmsnorm_f32` + `mq_rotate_x` launches and N row copies become one `rmsnorm_f32_rowsplit` launch (`grid.y = rows`, the singleton kernel) and one batched `mq_rotate_x`, and the PM multi-column lm_head becomes `gemv_mq4g256v2_head_lanes_n<N>` (`kernels/src/gemv_mq4g256v2_head_lanes.gfx1201.hip`, `Gpu::gemv_mq4g256v2_head_lanes`): one wave per 4-row tile reads each weight row once for up to 8 rows with the singleton R2 kernel's per-row dequant, accumulation and shuffle-tree order, and stores each row to its slot's logits (no consecutive-slot runs). Lab gate `crates/rdna-compute/tests/head_lanes.rs` proves it equal to the real singleton launch and the PM twin (100M logits, N 1..=8, permuted slots, adversarial activations, signed zeros).
- **Perf: lane-batched, byte-identical `wo` residual GEMV for the A3B exact VMM batch route on gfx1201 (`Gpu::gemv_mq4g256v2_residual_lanes`, `kernels/src/gemv_mq4g256v2_residual_lanes.gfx1201.hip`), default ON for 5..=8 decode lanes (`HIPFIRE_A3B_LANE_WO=0` restores the PM x-batch residual).** The attention-output projection of every DeltaNet-MoE and FullAttention-MoE layer (m 2048, K 4096, MQ4G256V2, no AWQ / Paro) ran `pm_xbatch::residual`. The new hipcc kernel splits the K range of four rows over the four waves of a workgroup (wave `w` runs accumulator chain `w` of every row; the finished chains are exchanged as raw f32 through LDS), streams each weight row once and decodes it once per group, and every lane's column runs the singleton `gemv_mq4g256v2_residual`'s exact arithmetic (the four group-interleaved accumulators, the per-row-parity contraction form of the first two products the compiler gives the singleton, the `(acc0 + acc1) + (acc2 + acc3)` combine, the 32-lane lower-lane-left reduction tree and the `y + acc` residual add), so lane bytes equal the singleton's and the PM x-batch's: the lab gate `crates/rdna-compute/tests/a3b_lane_wo.rs` (2630 cases, N 1..=8, random + zero / +-large / overflow / denormal / tie activations and residuals, extreme headers, partial tiles, negative control) and the full-model byte oracle `cb_vmm_state_oracle` pass. With the instruction / last-level caches and TLB cold, as between the two `wo` launches of a decode step (`LANE_WO_FLUSH=1`), it is 6.3..8.7 us per launch faster than the PM x-batch launch at 5..=8 lanes but only level with it (+-0.4 us) at 1, 2 and 4 lanes, so only 5..=8 lanes take it; in the C8 A3B run (K=8, N=32 requests, 3 fresh processes per arm) it decodes 519.8 tok/s vs 507.7 tok/s (+2.4%) for the previous lanes kernel (two rows per wave), texts identical. Dense models' `wo` / `w_down` stay on the PM x-batch residual. The gain is bounded by the exact arithmetic: the per-column FMA chains cannot be shortened without changing bytes, so the K-split only shortens each wave's dependent chain and the live accumulator state.
- **Perf: the exact VMM continuous-batch route runs the A3B (`qwen3.5-moe` `.mq4rs`) projection groups as one lane-batched multi-weight GEMV per group instead of one `pm_xbatch` launch per weight, byte-identical per lane (`HIPFIRE_A3B_LANE_PROJ=0` restores the per-weight launches).** On exact gfx1201 the DeltaNet QKVZA group (wqkv + wz + w_beta + w_alpha), the FullAttention QKV group (wq + wk + wv) and the MoE router + selector + shared gate/up quartet each ran 3-4 `gemv_mq4g256v2_xbatch_pm` launches per layer (an ~8.7 us floor each, even for the 1-row selector and the 32-row beta/alpha). `gemv_mq4g256v2_lane_proj_k2048_gfx1201` (`rdna-compute/src/lane_proj.rs`, `kernels/src/gemv_mq4g256v2_lane_proj_k2048.gfx1201.hip`, wave64) computes up to four weight segments and 1..=8 decode columns in one launch: every weight row is streamed once, its dequantised values are reused for all columns, the activation columns are staged once per workgroup in LDS, and each (row, column) keeps the singleton `fused_qkvza_mq4g256v2` / `fused_qkv_mq4g256v2` arithmetic term for term (accumulator ownership, FMA contraction, reduction tree), so the bytes equal the singleton launch on that lane alone. The lab gate `crates/rdna-compute/tests/lane_proj.rs` compares every output word against the real singleton launches and the x-batch loop for 1/2/3/5/8 lanes on random, zero, +-large, denormal, tied, outlier and non-finite activations and sane / large / fully random-header weights, plus the norm-fold chain and a one-bit negative control. Groups the launch does not admit (non-gfx1201, AWQ / ParoQuant / non-MQ4G256V2 weights, K != 2048) and the dense 27B layers keep the `pm_xbatch` loop.
- **Added: lane-batched, byte-identical twins of the A3B (`qwen3_5_moe` `.mq4rs`) decode MoE block for the exact VMM continuous-batching route on gfx1201 (`Gpu::moe_decode_lanes_mq4rs`, `kernels/src/moe_decode_lanes_mq4rs.gfx1201.hip`).** One launch each of the router top-k, shared-expert down (+ sigmoid-gated residual), routed gate/up and routed down + combine (+ residual) now covers 1..=8 decode lanes instead of one launch per lane; the shared silu+rotate reuses the batched launch of the same kernel. Every twin is the singleton kernel's own body behind a lane-indexed entry (same reduction order, FMA contraction and compiler flags), so per-lane bytes equal the singleton launches by construction; `tests/moe_decode_lanes.rs` proves it against the real singleton launches (560 random/adversarial lanes with forced top-k ties and shared experts, N in {1,2,3,8}, negative controls) and also proves the `pm_xbatch::plain` router/selector/shared-gate/shared-up projections, the batched norm and the norm fold per-lane identical to the singleton 1281-row chain.

Every twin runs the singleton kernel's own body per row (`blockIdx.z` = row), proven bitwise against the real singleton launches in `cb_a3b_fa_lanes_gate` (N in {1, 2, 3, 8}, tile-boundary lengths, shuffled row-slot maps, row-group-split partials) and by the exact byte oracle at ks 1, 2, 4, 8. The VMM flash-decode plan is now admitted for A3B, so the opt-in non-exact VMM route (`serve.vmm_batch` with `nonexact`) is also admitted for A3B and sizes its flash partials like every other model; the group-6 (H24/KV4) route and its module sources are unchanged.

There is one predicate, `Gpu::qwen4_moe_sym_iu4_requested`: the S1 slow-link window route (`SymIu4RouteFacts::of_gpu` -> `aggregate-sym-iu4`) and the regular prefill (>= 512 rows) both read it, so they cannot disagree; the config effective-value rule (`developer.qwen4_moe_sym_iu4`, unset) says on for gfx1100 too. Layers whose routed-expert headers fail the load-time symmetry check (asymmetric artifacts), decode, MTP and prefill under 512 rows keep the incumbent route; any `-DIU4_A4_CANDIDATES` other than `2` withdraws the request. The two grouped IU4 GEMMs are the PM-KRSI round-2 objects of this release (kernel-level IU4 PM chain 0.518 of the F16 hipcc chain over one S1 window's route sweep: gate/up 26.7 -> 12.7 ms, down 11.4 -> 7.1 ms; the round-2 generator wins stack on top at 0.821 and 0.937 node time). Not bit-exact against the F16 WMMA route: it trades quality for speed, and the numeric acceptance is the S1 slow-link context-mean KL bound (16K <= 0.03948458079446915, 4K <= 0.027284316982763658, `scripts/slowlink-gap/quality_campaign.py`) plus the BF16-teacher KLD deltas the gfx1151 / gfx1201 defaults were taken on.

The reference is the frozen Q1a gfx1100 chunk-major baseline (4096-row tiles, F16 MoE), not the BF16 teacher, so the lower 4K mean is "no further from the reference" (`off`'s 4K bootstrap interval is 0.0093-0.0502, a few divergent rows), not an accuracy gain.     |---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---:|
    | WikiText-2 24 x 2048 | 0.061196 | 0.090530 | +0.0293 [+0.0261, +0.0329], IU4 worse in 24/24 chunks | 0.9135 -> 0.8960 | 3.6973 -> 3.7122 | +0.0306 |

Identity: decoded-text sha256, token counts and speculative window counters (cycles, accepted, verified rows, tau) identical for every request across all A/B runs (C1 12, C4 32, C8 32 steady requests per run) and for three committed prompts (humaneval_0, fiction_lighthouse, the 2K ds4 prompt) at C1/C4/C8; `cb_vmm_state_oracle --spec dflash --dflash-block 8 --max-lanes 8 --phase probe --aggregates 63,64,65,96,128` passes (every lane byte-equals its isolated singleton window; the C8 64-row aggregate is one 64-row chunk, `rows_per_chunk [64]`, against `[56, 8]` with the switch at 0).
- **Perf: gfx1201 TP4 decode runs as a whole-token graph by default (Qwen3.8-27B mq4-xts on 4x R9700: 54.0 -> 77.5 tok/s, +43%, median of per-process medians over 4 fresh interleaved processes per arm: eager 49.6-54.5, graph 77.4-77.6; greedy token IDs identical to the eager route on 3 prompts).** The eager route spent 1,650 kernels per token per rank, five per collective (`tp_pack16_bf16`, three peer copies, `tp_fold16_bf16`) plus cross-device events, with about 40% of the token idle between launches, and the events cannot be captured. Each collective is now one `tp_peer_pushn_reduce_bf16_gfx1201` kernel per rank: the rank packs its partial to bf16, writes it as 16-byte granules `{w0, g, w1, g}` (four bf16 values and the generation tag twice) into its slot of every peer's fine-grained VRAM mailbox (`hipDeviceMallocFinegrained`, allocated before peer access is enabled; system-scope write-through b128 stores), waits (bounded, new wait site 10) for the three other slots in its own mailbox and folds `x + (r(p0) + r(p1) + r(p2) + r(p3))` in rank order, the arithmetic of `tp_pack16_bf16` + `tp_fold16_bf16`, so the residual is bit-identical. Two banks alternate with a device-resident per-rank generation, so replay needs no host reset or event. The pushes go to ONE peer at a time (release fence and barrier between destinations): a GPU writing write-through stores to two or three peers concurrently collapses to about 1.5 GB/s per sender, which made the first all-peers-at-once draft 50 us per collective (lab `tp_peer_pushn_probe`, 128-collective dependent chain, graph-captured) against 6.5 us for the serialized form. The load qualifies the mailboxes with 64 eager exchanges compared bit for bit with a host replay and falls back to the eager route (with a message) on any difference; a bounded-wait timeout fails the request with the device wait error, restarts the generations and mailboxes after every rank drained, and clears the late timeout records of the stalled rank (a timeout consumed by rank 0's logits download now also triggers that reset: `Gpu::take_unreported_device_wait_timeouts`), so the next request in the same daemon runs normally; the developer-only `HIPFIRE_TP_PEER_PUSH_FAULT=rank:replay[:ms]` stalls one rank to exercise it (daemon test: stalled rank 2 on graph launch 20 -> request 1 errors in 1.9 s, requests 2 and 3 in the same daemon complete with the eager token IDs). Kill switches: `HIPFIRE_TP_FULL_GRAPH=0` (graph) and `HIPFIRE_TP_PEER_PUSH=0` (peer push, hence the graph); both restore the eager route, as does `HIPFIRE_TP_EXCHANGE=f32|f16`. Persistent/fusion ideas from LithosAI's 2026-10-27 MI355X post.
- **Added (opt-in on TP2, default off): `HIPFIRE_TP_PEER_PUSH=1` reduces the gfx1201 TP2 whole-token decode graph's residual through tagged peer-VRAM granules; bit-identical, but only +0.6% decode, so it is not the default there (TP4 uses the same mechanism by default, previous entry).** Each rank pushes its f32 partial into the peer's fine-grained VRAM mailbox (`hipDeviceMallocFinegrained`, new `HipRuntime::malloc_peer_finegrained`, allocated before peer access is enabled) as 16-byte granules that carry the generation tag in both 8-byte halves, and polls only its own mailbox: one `tp2_peer_push_reduce_gfx1201` kernel per rank per collective, no fence, no flag, no cross-device read or read-modify-write, two alternating banks, bounded wait (new wait site 9). The loader qualifies the mailboxes with 64 eager exchanges compared bit for bit with a host replay and falls back to the coherent-shadow reduction (with a message) if any value differs.
  - **Lab (`tp_peer_push_probe`, 2x R9700, 128-collective dependent chain, graph-captured, 3 fresh processes):** incumbent `tp_graph_signal_reduce_gfx1100` 9.03-9.35 us per collective over the producer-only floor; fence + release flag push 5.7-5.8 us; tagged-granule push 4.23 us. 10,000 replays x 128 collectives (1.28M generations) per arm per process: zero mismatches against a host replay of the exact arithmetic, canaries intact, random per-replay rank delays and launch order, pipelined and synchronized, and a missing-peer injection exits through the bounded wait in 500 ms.
  - **End to end (Qwen3.8-27B mq4-xts, TP2, 3 fresh processes per arm, interleaved):** 54.4 / 54.6 / 54.6 tok/s off vs 54.7 / 55.0 / 54.9 on (+0.6%); committed token IDs identical on 3 prompts (173, 256 and 256 tokens, fresh daemon per run, decoded text read). The saving does not reach the wall clock because the ranks' work is imbalanced (the head rank runs `lm_head` and the other rank waits in the next collective), so a faster collective mostly shortens the wait.
- **Fixed: every gfx1100 PeaceMaker object now declares at least 16 user+system SGPRs (LLVM `FeatureUserSGPRInit16Bug`, set for gfx1100/gfx1102 wave32 compute).** The builder declared 2 user SGPRs plus the workgroup-id SGPRs (3-5 in total) on gfx1100, below the hardware's 16-SGPR initialisation minimum that LLVM satisfies in `SITargetLowering::allocateSystemSGPRs` by padding the user SGPRs until `user + workgroup id X/Y/Z/info >= 16`. `Arch::declared_user_sgprs` / `KernelSpec::declared_user_sgprs` now pad the same way (`.amdhsa_user_sgpr_count` 14 with X and Y enabled, 13 with Z, 15 with X only), the workgroup ids follow the padding (`s14`/`s15` instead of `s2`/`s3`), `native::assemble` and M7 refuse a gfx1100 descriptor below 16, and `tests/gfx1100_user_sgpr16.rs` lifts every committed `kernels/*_pm_gfx1100*.hxaco`. The generators moved the kernarg blocks that sat on `s14`/`s15` and are otherwise unchanged: each new object's instruction stream equals the previous one under a pure SGPR renaming and the kernel descriptors differ only in `user_sgpr_count` (and `next_free_sgpr`), with M7 obligation-free and old-vs-new emulator output byte-identical where the emulator models the kernel. Regenerated: `gemm_mq4g256v2_residual_iu4_pm_gfx1100` (iu4_v2c SET/ADD/gate-up, the default dense MQ4V2 prefill GEMM), `gemm_mq6g256v2_residual_pm_gfx1100`, `qwen4_moe_iu4_sym{,_e8p}_pm_gfx1100`, `mq_i4_moe_gemv_mq4only_pm_gfx1100`, `e8p_i4_moe_gemv_pm_gfx1100`, `mq_i4_a4_pm_gfx1100`, `qwen4_lane_rows_pm_gfx1100`, `mq4_rows_x4_pm_gfx1100`, `bf16_rows_wide_pm_gfx1100`, `qwen4_slab_union_plan_t8_pm_gfx1100`, `ep_tile_mask_pm_gfx1100` and the two `ep_gather_grouped_rows_by_tile_owner*_pm_gfx1100` objects. gfx1151/gfx1201 objects are byte-identical.
- **Fixed: the gfx1201 row-local A4 producer `mq_i4_a4_pm_gfx1201` (`mq_i4_a4_r128_k640`) no longer computes a wrong 64-bit `xq` address once the record index `g*L + slot` exceeds ~828,505.** The prologue passed the record index in `T0` to `mad64`, which writes the low product into `T0` before `s_mul_hi_u32` reads the index, so the high dword came from `72 * (72 * x mod 2^32)` instead of `72 * x`; records were stored in whole 4 GiB multiples out of bounds. The index now goes to a dead SGPR (`ROWS5`), as `moe_rotate_i4_pm` already does, and `mad64_reg` refuses an index in the `T0`/`T1` scratch pair. This producer is not dispatched by the runtime (the gfx1201 slab route uses `moe_rotate_i4_pm_gfx1201`, which was already correct), so no shipped model output changes. Records below the old threshold are bitwise identical; the regenerated `kernels/mq_i4_a4_pm_gfx1201.hxaco` differs only in the one prologue register. New `tests/mq_i4_a4_emu.rs` runs the kernel on the emulator on sparse 64-bit buffers at L = 70M (record indices up to 350M) and grid-extreme rows (workgroup index 20,000,001, `h` offsets above 4 GiB), bitwise against the CPU reference; the byte-oracle harness gains `bigl_*` cases (L = 1M and 13M).

Tests run under the new `ci` Cargo profile (`cargo test --profile ci`): `opt-level = 3` for every external dependency and for the crates that host the exhaustive CPU oracle/emulator tests (`peacemaker-*`, `hipfire-dispatch`, `hipfire-quantize`, `hipfire-runtime`, `rdna-compute`), `opt-level = 0` elsewhere, and `debug-assertions` / `overflow-checks` on. The release build job builds every lib and bin plus the shipped daemon and the dark NPU stack; every other target (examples, benches, GPU-only tests) is type-checked by a separate `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` instead of a second full release build (everything that ships is still built in release, everything CI runs is built and linked by the test shards).

- **Fixed: the automatic Flash-Next D2 default no longer refuses D2 at load because of one outlier CPU probe sample (a ~5 tok/s load).** The selector priced D2 on the *slowest* of the 5 CPU arm samples, so one preempted batch (hipx `xb-splitkv0-2`: slowest 7,316 µs against a 410 µs median) turned worst-case D2 into 8,122 µs against PCIe 3,691 µs and the load stayed on PCIe, although the median D2 was 1,216 µs. D2 is now priced on the **median** CPU arm sample (the upper median, over every pass) plus the handoff, against the unchanged optimistic PCIe (fastest link sample, minimum launch floor), with the unchanged 85% margin. A CPU arm pass whose slowest sample is more than 200% of its median is re-probed once and the two passes are pooled (10 samples), so a minority of slow samples (fewer than 3 of 5, fewer than 5 of 10) is ignored while a uniformly or majority-slow CPU still ends on PCIe. The load line now reports the statistic (`median CPU arm of N samples`, plus `first pass was dispersed, re-probed once and pooled` when it re-probed), the slowest sample, the D2 the single slowest sample would have given, and both max/min and max/median spreads. Unit tests inject the reported samples (one 7,316 µs outlier among ~410 µs: D2; uniformly slow: PCIe; the 85% boundary and the dispersion threshold are exact). `docs/CONFIG.md` carries the new selector semantics.

- **Developer: the pre-card emulator gates (`hip_loop --emu`, `pm_loop --emu`, `emu_race_gate SPEC.json`) now run every kernel under the gate model `Emulator::hw_model()`.** In-flight memory (a load's destination registers are written only when its `s_waitcnt`/`s_wait_*` retires it, with the M7 retire rules: in-order `vmcnt`/`lgkmcnt`, `vscnt`/`kmcnt` only at 0, SMEM blocks a positive `lgkmcnt`; touching a register a pending load still owes is `[in-flight]`), LDS happens-before race detection (`[race]`: a cross-wave access pair must be separated by a retired access and a barrier epoch; atomics on one dword are exempt from each other), and schedule exploration (round-robin, one-wave-runs-ahead for every wave, seeded random; stores must be bit-identical, `[schedule]`). `Memory::set_strict_read` makes an unwritten byte of a workspace region an `[uninit]` read, and LDS addresses wrap at 32 bits. gfx12 LDS store sources are locked until `dscnt` retires them; gfx11 stores read their data at issue (stock hipcc relies on it), so `hw_model_strict_store_sources()` is opt-in and used by no gate. `R3Mq6Wp-02-lag-w4n128` (the candidate that dropped the XTX) passes the gate model: its fault has no ordering/race/address mechanism (`gpu/rounds/r3/fault-0952/ROOT-CAUSE.md`), so the gate cannot predict it.
- **Fixed: the gfx1100 K3 down producer `mq_i4_a4_r128_k640_gfx1100` (`mq_i4_a4_pm_gfx1100`) stored its A4 records 4 GiB past the sidecar once the record index `g*L + slot` reached 828,505, which `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_MOE_SYM_IU4=1` on a 16,896-row S1 window (L = 168,960 slots, group 4, slot >= 152,665) hits.** `mad64(XQ_PTR, ARG_XQ, T0, 72)` passed the scratch `T0` as `x`, and the generator emitted `s_mul_i32 T0, T0, 72` before `s_mul_hi_u32 T1, T0, 72`, so the high word was computed from the clobbered low product (`floor(low * 72 / 2^32) << 32` added to the pointer; 0 below the threshold, which is why every small-shape gate passed). The route judge faulted the card with `HipError(700)`. The high word is now computed first (3 reordered instruction pairs, nothing else in the object changes) and `kernels/mq_i4_a4_pm_gfx1100.hxaco` is regenerated (sha256 `bff74331...`, was `c4090d3f...`); `crates/peacemaker-isa/tests/mq_i4_a4_gfx1100_xq_extent.rs` replays the real kernargs at `p = 320, g = 4` on the emulator (records bit-equal the CPU reference, exact-size `xq`) and proves the old instruction order faults. The emulator gains `v_maxmin_f32` / `v_minmax_f32` (legacy three-operand min/max) for it.

The committed twin writes the six loads as `rip_fragments` and still emits the shipped bytes (assembly, proof and linked object) for every dense variant; Rust `blocks::fragments` stays the generator's step and the independent reference.
