Confirmed on the 7900 XTX (OLD `2b66f6c5a1` vs NEW `a09d589f65`, default D2 route, n=3 fresh daemons per arm, one long request each, ABBAAB; binary sha256 prefixes OLD `93c7f428…`, NEW `b8b22d27…`; prompts `depth_8192` md5 `d96cd608e165a708383df0e8c6f06de1`, `depth_32768` md5 `6632ac3121107d60cfece0de64552d72`): 32K AR 30.2 -> 33.3 tok/s (+10.3%), 8K AR 30.4 -> 33.9 tok/s (+11.5%); CPU arm R1 median 342.9 -> 300.1 us (-12.5%); 256 greedy IDs byte-identical across all cells (32K sha16 `41c77f2fcbde9b82`, 8K `167858d95c73824d`). - **Developer: `iu4_gemm` ring depth 3 (`Tune { ring: RingDepth::Three }`, `pm_loop --ring 3`, `.rip` `const RING = 3`).** The dense K128 variants (every epilogue but the fused GDN projection; both tiles) publish two slabs ahead: the A/W payload rings are three LDS slabs deep (27B gate/up kernel 20480 -> 28672 B per workgroup: the launch keeps the shipped 20480-byte dynamic LDS and the object declares the extra slab as static LDS, `group_segment_fixed_size` 8192, so the product launcher is right for it), a second prefetch register set holds each next block's slab 1 (it takes the eight VGPRs `magic8` held: each block's first WMMA group seeds its accumulators from `cacc[3][1]`, so the kernel stays at 187 VGPRs), and a block fetches the block after next. LDS addresses stay immediates through a `K/256 - 1 = 3q + r` entry branch (typed `wg_if_else`, rings `starting_at` slot `(3 - r) % 3`), a three-group loop body counted by `q` and the peeled tail group (code 14084 -> 32192 bytes for the 27B gate/up kernel). Depth 3 is scheduling only: result bits equal depth 2's on the CPU emulator at K = 256/512/768/1024/5120, every candidate is M7-certified, the depth-2 digests are unchanged, and the fine `.rip` twin with `const RING = 3` emits exactly the generator's depth-3 bytes for every wait placement (new fine natives `iu4::publish_slab_set`, `fetch_ahead`, `fetch_slab`, `setup`, `split_trips`, `ring_cmp`, `group_end`). `Spec::validate` refuses the rest (sparse blocks, the GDN projection, a budget that does not fit) with the numbers; `pm-census tune` stops pruning ring 3 where the generator accepts it. Product defaults, digests and the shipped objects are unchanged; no GPU measurement yet.

Result bits equal depth 2 (checked on the interpreter against the exact reference at K = 256..3840 covering r = 0, 1, 2 and q = 0..4); depth-2 bytes, digests, register and LDS maps are unchanged (the half-1 refetch settles its store-source hazard through `Builder::settle_defs`, a no-op at depth 2). The depth-3 object keeps the depth-2 dynamic launch size and declares the third slab as `group_segment_fixed_size`. `pm-census tune` lists the legal ring-3 points of the MQ6 domain, records the pruned ones with the reason, and takes `PM_CENSUS_RIP_DIR` scripts as MQ6 candidates (ring read from the script's `const RING`; `pm_loop --rip` does the same).

Scripts get `Ring::new(a, b[, c[, d]])`, `ring.depth()`, `ring.starting_at(k)`, `advance(ring)` and `wg.wg_if_else(..)`. Depth-2 emission is unchanged (every shipped variant's bytes and digest pins are identical); the `tests/ui/halo_verify_attn_race.stderr` snippet renders the new `rotate<R, const D: usize>` signature. No kernel uses depth 3 yet.

Ring depth 3 is still refused (two-buffer `Ring`/`RingBuf`, immediate slot addresses, single prefetch set).
- **Developer: the 2:4-sparse `iu4_gemm` K128 blocks (`s24x64`, `s24x32`) are split into the same fine typed `.rip` natives as the dense one (cookbook 17).** `iu4::sparse_block_begin`, `sparse_fragments`, `sparse_wmma`, `sparse_scale_loads` and `sparse_scale_tail` are the steps that differ from dense (the publishes, waits, fetches, `d_loads` and `fold_scale` are shared); `kloop::sparse_block_with` is now their composition and `iu4::sparse_block` / `sparse_block_stepping` keep working over it. A dense step on a sparse spec (and the reverse), an `s24x64` second sub-block or `_s1` scale tail, and a read or SWMMAC group of an unpublished slot are build errors. `iu4_gemm_fine.rip`'s sparse arm (`fine_sparse_block`) uses only fine natives and emits the shipped bytes and proof for all four sparse variants; product bytes and the sparse digest pins are unchanged.
- **Developer: `pm-census tune` enumerates the Flash-Next MQ6 prefill GEMM (`gemm_mq6g256v2_mmq_i8_pm_set_gfx1201`) with the runtime-selected tile as the incumbent** (`mq6_i8_pm_token_tile`, 128x256 at the FN M=10240/N=4096 node) via `pm_loop --base-shipped 128x256`, which an A/A null control now also accepts. gfx1201 run: control 1.0002 (not separable), every other tile/raster 3.3-13.6% slower; the shipped selection stays.
- **Developer: retained-PM4 dispatch ledger (`HIPFIRE_REDLINE_LEDGER=<file>`, optional perturbing `HIPFIRE_REDLINE_LEDGER_TIMING=1`, both default off) and `pm-census ledger`.** Retained Redline decode dispatches never reach rocprofv3, so the PM census refused every AR cell. With the ledger on, `prepare_pm4_prefix` writes one JSONL row per retained dispatch at retain time (kernel symbol, code-object origin/module, image SHA-256 and length, grid, block, shared memory, grid binding); replay only bumps two per-program counters (replay count and the whole-program span the tape's bracketing timestamps already return), and a cumulative `replay_summary` is flushed at controller shutdown and daemon exit. `pm-census ledger --ledger F --model M --arch A --phase P` joins the image SHA-256 to the PM object inventory (pm / hipcc / unknown) and emits a `CensusV1` cell for `pm-census census matrix`. The default tape is unchanged, so the cell is **count-weighted** (exact dispatch counts per kernel, no per-kernel time; the matrix reports `pm_share_of_dispatches` and leaves the time shares unset). `HIPFIRE_REDLINE_LEDGER_TIMING=1` prepares the per-dispatch-timestamp tape (the `HIPFIRE_REDLINE_DISPATCH_PROFILE` instrument) in a separate run and yields a time-weighted cell labelled perturbing. `CensusV1` gains an optional `measurement` record (absent in every rocprof census, so existing census files and matrices are byte-identical). Unset, no product code path changes beyond `Option::None` checks.
- **Developer: `iu4_gemm` generator knobs `Spec::tune` (`ring`, `wait`, `fold_op`), `pm_loop --ring/--wait/--fold-op`, and the tuner's (ring x wait) space for the dense 27B prefill gate/up GEMM.** `wait` (`after` default, `mid`, `before`) moves the K-loop block's next-slab publish (the `flip_weights` + LDS stores that carry the vector-memory wait for the slab's global fetch) before the slab's WMMA bundles, between its two 32-K sub-block bundles, or after them; the stores target the ring's free next buffer, so every placement is legal for the typed rings and bit-identical (CPU-emulator tested for set/add, token/slab). `ring 3` (prefetch two slabs ahead) is generated for the dense variants (see the ring-depth-3 bullet above). `fold_op muladd` is a deliberately NUMERIC twin (non-fused `v_mul_f32` + `v_add_f32` stage-2 accumulate, the hipcc DAG): `pm_loop` declares `numeric_contract.relation = "numeric"`, checks set/add against the `muladd` CPU reference (silu has none: finite and NaN-pattern-equal to the baseline, the KLD/state gate decides) and reports `identical_to_baseline` honestly. Every default-`Tune` spec emits the same bytes as before (digest tests unchanged); the symbol and ABI of a tuned kernel are the incumbent's. `pm-census tune plan|run` enumerates the legal points (`wait` mid/before) with the pruned `ring=3` points recorded in the derivation; `PM_CENSUS_IU4_NUMERIC=1` adds the `muladd` candidate (never in the default space). Product defaults are unchanged.
- **Fixed: Flash-Next long-prompt prefill on slow-link loads with the automatic D2 CPU split (default config, e.g. 7900 XTX on PCIe 4.0 x4) runs layer-major (S1) again instead of re-streaming host experts per chunk.** With `memory.offload_exec` unset, the per-load D2 default armed a CPU split on the host layers, and S1's guards (`slowlink_forward_blocker`, `s1_layer_check`) refused any CPU split, after S1 was already admitted and charged at load, so every prompt over one tile ran the chunk-major route: a 19,848-token prompt prefilled at 59.7 tok/s (332 s) on v0.4.4. The automatic D2 split never runs host arithmetic on prefill rows (`host_arith_call`), so the guards no longer refuse it; decode keeps the D2 split. The MTP prompt fill's capture-buffer check compared against the 1536-row legal maximum instead of the admitted tile (768 rows on this load), so MTP never took S1; it now uses the admitted tile and logs the bypass reason at DEBUG. The automatic S1 floor is now one row past the admitted tile (769 rows on a 768-row tile; was a fixed 1,537), so 769..1,536-row prompts no longer pay two incumbent chunks. Greedy ids are unchanged.
- Add an opt-in host-mapped direct-read placement for Qwen3.5/3.8-VL vision matrices, preserving resident and streamed execution and their F16/padded layouts.

- **Fixed: Flash-Next long-prompt prefill on slow-link loads with the automatic D2 CPU split (default config, e.g. 7900 XTX on PCIe 4.0 x4) runs layer-major (S1) again instead of re-streaming host experts per chunk.** With `memory.offload_exec` unset, the per-load D2 default armed a CPU split on the host layers, and S1's guards (`slowlink_forward_blocker`, `s1_layer_check`) refused any CPU split, after S1 was already admitted and charged at load, so every prompt over one tile ran the chunk-major route: a 19,848-token prompt prefilled at 59.7 tok/s (332 s) on v0.4.4. The automatic D2 split never runs host arithmetic on prefill rows (`host_arith_call`), so the guards now refuse only loads that can (D1 splice or explicit `memory.offload_exec=cpu`, `host_arith_every_call`); decode keeps the D2 split. The MTP prompt fill's capture-buffer check compared against the 1536-row legal maximum instead of the admitted tile (768 rows on this load), so MTP never took S1; it now uses the admitted tile and logs the bypass reason at DEBUG. The automatic S1 floor is now one row past the admitted tile (769 rows on a 768-row tile; was a fixed 1,537), so 769..1,536-row prompts no longer pay two incumbent chunks. Explicit `memory.offload_exec=cpu` still prefills on the incumbent route. Greedy ids are unchanged.
- **Fixed: release kernel packs now carry every module the flagship gfx1201 routes load, so pack-only hosts no longer need hipcc for Qwen3.8 27B AR/MTP.** Measured on the published v0.4.4 gfx1201 binaries with a clean home and kernel cache, 27B AR and 27B MTP compiled 7 and 8 modules with hipcc at first request (and failed outright without a compiler): the fp8 VMM tile/reduce/KV-write set, the `*_rows` GDN / qknorm / FA-prep / gated-norm twins and `attention_fp8_e4m3_kv_batched_segs`. They are now registered in `kernel_registry::entries` (gfx1201 only; their sources and launchers are gfx1201-gated) from the same source helpers the launchers use. New CPU test `flagship_pack_coverage` pins the complete measured module set of six gfx1201 routes (27B AR / DFlash / MTP, flash-next AR / MTP, A3B mq4rs AR; `fixtures/flagship-pack-gfx1201.tsv`) with exact symbol, flags, scheduler profile and source SHA-256, and the portable subset on gfx1201, gfx1100 and gfx1151 (`fixtures/flagship-pack-shared.tsv`). Measured gfx1151 (27B AR / DFlash / MTP) and gfx1100 (27B AR / DFlash / MTP, flash-next AR / MTP) module sets are pinned the same way (`fixtures/flagship-pack-gfx1151.tsv`, `fixtures/flagship-pack-gfx1100.tsv`); the gfx1151 strict-after run exposed `select_regrid` and `topk_values_fixup_f32` as pack gaps, now registered for gfx1151 as well as gfx1201.
- **Developer: `pm_loop` is tri-arch (`--arch gfx1201|gfx1151|gfx1100`) for `qwen4_moe_sym`, and times complete chains: `--kernel qwen4_moe_verify` (Flash-Next few-row routed experts).** `qwen4_moe_sym` emits, M7-certifies (for the selected arch), launches through the R1 `KernelAbiV1` contract and ABBA-times against each arch's shipped object (gfx1151 NT4 / streamed NT8 / NT4 rr1 down from `QWEN4_MOE_IU4_SYM_PM_GFX1151`, gfx1100 NT1 from `QWEN4_MOE_IU4_SYM_PM_GFX1100`; entries absent on an arch are refused by name); every other kernel refuses a non-gfx1201 `--arch`, and a device of another arch is refused. `qwen4_moe_verify` (H2560/I640/E512/top10, `T=1|2|3|4|7|8`, `res=resident|mapped` with the experts in host-mapped memory) runs, as its baseline arm, the chain the shipped selector issues at that T/arch through the public `Gpu` launchers (T>=2: input FWHT256, fused scatter, grouped F32 gate/up (gfx1151 `_inverse`), unscatter+SwiGLU+FWHT128, indexed down, top-10 combine; T=1: the decode route), with every selector predicate and its source line in the record and re-checked on the live device. `--candidate iu4_sym` forces the shipped PM symmetric-IU4 grouped chain (A4 producers, sym gate/up and down, grouped combine) below its 512-row policy floor; `--null-control aa` runs the baseline chain in both arms. Each arm is checked against its own CPU recipe (`cpu_f64_chain`; `cpu_iu4_chain`, exact A4 producer/fold/combine arithmetic), bit-for-bit on a repeat over the other arm's buffers, and timed with events around the whole chain. Chain arms swap buffer sets every ABBA round (`timing.crossover`): with a fixed binding, buffer placement alone made a gfx1201 A/A separable by up to 0.9%; with the crossover no A/A run was separable (gfx1201 0/36, gfx1151 0/12, gfx1100 0/12). The stale gfx1201 source anchors in `qwen4_moe_sym`'s baseline provenance now point at the current lines. Product code is unchanged.
- **Dense Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 TP: the row-parallel all-reduce exchanges 16-bit partials (`HIPFIRE_TP_EXCHANGE=auto` default: bf16 for multi-row exchanges at any TP degree and for single-row decode at TP>=3, f32 for single-row decode at TP2; `bf16`, `f16` or `f32` force one format; developer A/B knob). NUMERIC, not byte-identical to f32.** Each rank converts its f32 partial to bf16 once; every rank sums the rounded, rank-ordered partials in f32 into its f32 residual (`x + (r(p0) + r(p1) + …)`). The residual stream, the sums and the rooted route's residual broadcast stay f32. It covers the TP2 direct-peer read, the TP2 whole-token graph (`tp_graph_signal_reduce16_*`) and the TP>2 rooted/all-pull folds of both the hand and the generic dense-TP routes, which stay byte-identical to each other (`tp_prefill_decode_matches_hand_route`, TP2 and TP4). Peer transport between distinct devices, 2-4 ranks; host-staged, same-device emulation, EP and the no-target `AllReduce` stay f32. Judged by paired prefill KLD vs the f32 exchange (24 chunks, 27B mq4-xts, R9700): bf16 - f32 = -0.00222 [-0.00443, -0.00001] / +0.00029 [-0.00220, +0.00277] (WT2/code24, TP2), +0.00092 [-0.00033, +0.00216] / +0.00193 [-0.00202, +0.00588] (TP4): within noise; f16 likewise, with max |partial| 436.5 (WT2) / 412.9 (code24). `eval_hipfire` gains `--tp N` (hand dense-TP prefill, q8 KV). See `docs/multi-gpu.md#dense-tp-partial-exchange-16-bit-developer`. **`auto` policy measured** (R9700 gfx1201, Qwen3.8-27B mq4-xts, 3 fresh processes per arm, ABBAAB, auto vs `HIPFIRE_TP_EXCHANGE=f32`): TP2 pp2048 3328.6 -> 3585.2 tok/s (+7.7%), TP2 decode 54.9 -> 54.9 (-0.1%, auto keeps f32 there; forced bf16 measured -1.4%), TP4 pp2048 2114.2 -> 2593.2 (+22.7%), TP4 decode 48.8 -> 54.5 (+11.8%; f32 arm noisy 44.9-50.9, forced bf16 vs f32 earlier +7.0%).

- **Release: prebuilt Linux ROCm binary archives (`hipfire-<tag>-linux-rocm-<arch>-x64.tar.gz` + `.sha256`, gfx1151 / gfx1201 / gfx1100) are attached to the release.** `scripts/build-binary-archive.sh` builds the CLI and daemon once from the tag in the release image (same toolchain as the kernel packs), strips both binaries (`strip --strip-unneeded` on the staged copies), and packs `bin/hipfire`, `bin/daemon`, `bin/kernels/compiled/<arch>/` (the pack's kernels, SHA-256 checked), `LICENSE` and `NOTICE` into a reproducible tarball. The HIP runtime is not bundled; the host needs ROCm.
- **Fixed: the CLI now finds a daemon sitting beside its own executable.** `find_daemon` probed only `HIPFIRE_DAEMON_BIN`, `$HIPFIRE_HOME/bin` (default `~/.hipfire/bin`) and the source tree, so an extracted `bin/hipfire` + `bin/daemon` pair outside an install needed `HIPFIRE_DAEMON_BIN`. The order is now `HIPFIRE_DAEMON_BIN`, `<dir of the running hipfire>/daemon` (`daemon.exe` first on Windows), the hipfire home's `bin/`, then the source-tree `target/`. The daemon found is still checked by the same doctor/version checks as any other.
- **Fixed: release kernel packs now carry the modules the shared launchers request on every arch, so hosts without hipcc no longer fail on first use.** The registry that `scripts/compile-kernels.sh` / `build-kernel-pack.sh` package had `gemv_q8_0_wide` (the plain Q8_0 GEMV for K <= 1536) only for gfx1201, and no entry at all for the generic `rope`, the LFM2 `conv1d_gated_decode`, `sample_top_p` and `sample_rows_pf` modules; a pack-only host (no hipcc) then failed the first LFM2 decode, or any Q8_0 GEMV on gfx1100/gfx1151, at kernel load. All five are now registered for gfx1100, gfx1151 and gfx1201. New CPU test `pack_carries_every_shared_launcher_module_on_every_arch` checks each against the launcher's own `ensure_kernel` call and every arch's registry; it is a table of the modules known to be hit on supported models, not a blanket scrape (about 470 modules the runtime can request, in lab, vision and older-family paths, are deliberately JIT-only).
- **Developer: one typed kernel ABI contract for the MQ6 int8 GEMM and the grouped symmetric-IU4 MoE GEMMs (`hipfire-kernel-abi`, `KernelAbiV1`).** Each contract states the explicit kernarg fields and hidden words (offset/width/kind), the kernarg segment, every operand's format/access/alignment/byte extent over the launch params, the admitted domain, the numeric contract and, per export, arch, pinned object SHA-256, block, dynamic/static LDS and grid. The MQ6 launchers (`gemm_mq6g256v2_i8_prequant`, `_norm_rope`; PM and hipcc twins) and the grouped MoE launchers (`qwen4_moe_sym_gemm`, `qwen4_moe_sym_nt1_gemm`: MQ4, sealed-slab E8P and W3 NT1) now build both the `kernelParams` array and the `KernargBlob` from one validated image, and refuse a wrong arch/export/format/alignment/extent/domain/grid/block/LDS before enqueue. Kernarg bytes, grids, blocks and LDS of admitted launches are unchanged (byte-equality tests against the removed packing). `pm_loop`'s `mq6_i8_gemm` / `qwen4_moe_sym` adapters encode through the same contracts and refuse a candidate whose generator kernarg layout drifts; `railgun::contract` builds `LaunchRecord`s from validated invocations and checks authored nodes against the contract. `crates/rdna-compute/tests/kernel_abi_drift.rs` checks every contract against the generator `KernelSpec`/`KernargLayout` and the committed object metadata, with deliberately broken fixtures (pre-widening 60-byte MoE ABI, swapped fields, wrong LDS, wrong object hash, recipe interchange). Also corrects the stale SHA-256 in the doc comment of `kernels::GEMM_MQ6G256V2_MMQ_I8_PM_GFX1201`.
- **Developer: `pm-census` (workload corpus, PM/hipcc census, noise harness) and `hipfire_atlas::workload::WorkloadCaseV1`.** `pm-census census` attributes a rocprofv3 trace's ROI kernel time to PM / hipcc / unknown by joining each dispatch's code object (device-ELF size + symbol) to the repo's embedded PM objects at a given commit, reports kernel busy/sum, copy busy and overlap, idle, exclusive time per origin/dispatch path/ABI contract, and `census matrix` lays out the 27 model x arch x phase cells with unmeasured cells explicit (never zero). `pm-census extract` turns Redline captures, railgun program manifests, rocprofv3 traces and `pm_loop` records into a content-addressed `WorkloadCaseV1` corpus (contract-decoded kernarg params where a `KernelAbiV1` export matches). `pm_loop` gains `timing.noise` (per-round ABBA ratios and dispersion, block-median dispersion and drift), `--null-control aa` (the baseline object as both arms, separately loaded) and `--noise-floor FILE`; `pm-census noise` aggregates fresh-process records into A/A false-positive rates, a q95 noise floor and cross-process sign tests.
- **Developer: `pm-census tune` — first bounded PM autotuner loop (R4 search, R5 evidence-keyed store/table, R6 promotion gates); `pm_loop --offline`.** `pm-census tune plan|run` enumerates the legal generator-knob domain of one `WorkloadCaseV1` node (today `qwen4_moe_sym` gfx1201 gate/up NT1/4/8 and down NT1/4/8 + gp NT4/8; the shape is derived from the node's `M`/`m_total` and refused on mismatch), screens every candidate offline (`pm_loop --offline`: emit + M7 + baseline resolution, no device; pruned on any failure or when the resolved baseline is not the corpus node's incumbent), marks code-identical negative controls and duplicates by the launched function's `code_sha256`, measures an A/A noise floor of the incumbent in 3 fresh processes, then discovery (ABBA, sign test p <= 1e-3, material >= 0.5%, above the floor) and a held-out fresh-process confirmation, with process/wall budgets and a resumable ledger. `tune export` turns the append-only store (key: arch, kernel, shape, numeric contract, mode, incumbent and candidate code/object sha256, commit, `pm_loop` sha256) into a deterministic table with exact-key `lookup`; only promoted rows are selectable (the KLD/state stage and the product reader are described below). First gfx1201 runs (A3B prefill T=8192): the gate/up incumbent NT8 beats NT4 (1.073x slower) and NT1 (1.554x slower); down gp NT8 is 1.006x slower than the gp NT4 incumbent; no winner; code-identical controls not material (A/A floors 0.066% / 0.074%).
- **Developer: `pm-census tune` KLD/state promotion gate, product tune-table reader (`HIPFIRE_PM_TUNE_TABLE`, unset by default), and `.rip` candidates for the dense 27B prefill gate/up GEMM.** The R6 `kld_state` stage is no longer a stub: a bit-identical candidate (every attempt `identical_to_baseline`) passes on that exact-output proof (attached model evidence must then be byte-identical); a numeric candidate is admitted past correctness only to require promotion-grade `eval_hipfire --scoring-mode prefill` evidence — incumbent and table-selected candidate runs on the same reference/model/evaluator/KV flags, `HIPFIRE_GRAPH=0 HIPFIRE_NORMALIZE_PROMPT=0`, fresh HOME, >= 24 chunks, candidate run bound to the discovered code object — and a paired per-chunk Student-t 95% upper bound on the KLD increase <= 0.0005 (`pm-census tune kld`, `tune promote`, `tune trial-table`; screening-grade evidence never promotes). `tune export --out` writes a product block (symbol, arch, M, K, incumbent image sha256, content-addressed code object). `rdna-compute` reads such a table only when `HIPFIRE_PM_TUNE_TABLE` names one: exact key (arch, symbol, M, K) for `gemm_mq4g256v2_gate_up_silu_mmq_iu4_b1s`; stale rows (incumbent image sha256 differs from this build's), code-object sha mismatch, unreadable objects and duplicate keys are refused to the incumbent; the 27B gfx1201 route planner moves only that export into a `pm_tune:<sha16>` module so the preloaded route binds the variant. Unset: no file I/O, no hashing, unchanged route plan (unit-tested). `tune plan|run` enumerates that node (`dense-27b` preset M=17408 K=5120, `.rip` scripts from `PM_CENSUS_RIP_DIR` as `rip` candidates); a resumed `.rip` record is reused only if its script sha256 is unchanged. Measured on gfx1201: 9 script-level candidates (s_setprio level/placement, trip-end order, K-loop unroll x2), all bit-identical at N=255/256/8192; none separable+material faster (best: peeled-group priority 0, 0.998x, below the 0.5% material bar); ring depth, wait placement and in-block prefetch order are fixed by the typed generator and not `.rip`-expressible. A table-selected variant reproduces the gfx1201 WT2 pin `.kldseq` (`ff88c499…`) byte for byte.

## v0.4.4 — 2026-10-27

- **Developer: Qwen3.5 AR hipGraph / Redline replay refuses int8, int8c and hfq4 KV caches (HIPF-192).** `attention_int8c_f16_kv` / `attention_int8_kv` / `attention_hfq4_kv` size their block and LDS (`scores[seq_len]`) from the host `seq_len`, which a replay freezes at the capture position, so per-token decode past ~256-511 positions went degenerate (one argmax every position). `ar_graph_eligible_for_kv` now refuses those tiers, which then decode eagerly. No `KvMode` builds these tiers, so production routes are unaffected; contributor-measured on gfx1151 qwen3.5-9b.mq4 int8c/int8 at 600 rows: logits bitwise equal to `HIPFIRE_GRAPH=0 HIPFIRE_AR_GRAPH=0`. (#1004, @fivetide)
- **Fixed: the pre-compiled kernel probe honors `HIPFIRE_HOME`.** Its home fallback read `$HOME/.hipfire` directly, so with `HIPFIRE_HOME` pointing at an install without a kernel dir the loader picked up another install's objects and every load failed `packaged object rejected (index mismatch)`. The probe order (beside the executable, `kernels/compiled` under the CWD, then the hipfire home) is unchanged; with `HIPFIRE_HOME` unset the home is still `~/.hipfire`. (#1001, @amittell)
- **Registry: Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B entries no longer default to `presence_penalty 1.5` (now 0.0 in `recommended_settings` and the `general` / `instruct` sampling profiles; 14 tags).** Serve and `run` inject the registry penalty into every request that sends none, and a greedy request with a non-neutral penalty runs AR (entry below), so these models never used DFlash for greedy requests by default, `hipfire run --tp N` was refused (`presence_penalty is not supported at tp>1`), and serve applied a penalty the user never asked for. An explicit `presence_penalty` (request, CLI or `generation.presence_penalty`) is unchanged. Qwen3.8 entries never carried it; `nex-n2:mini` keeps its card's value.
- **Qwen DFlash: a greedy request demoted to AR by a non-neutral penalty now says so in the serve log.** `qwen3.5:9b`'s registry general profile carries `presence_penalty 1.5`, `serve` injects it into every tp<=1 request that does not send one, and `select_generation_route` sends any penalized greedy request to AR because the DFlash verifiers apply no penalties; with the registry 9B DFlash draft loaded that meant `drafter=dflash` never appeared and decode ran at AR speed (R9700 gfx1201, `qwen3.5-9b.mq4` + `qwen35-9b-dflash-mq4.hfq`, greedy chain: 78-110 tok/s AR vs 203-413 tok/s DFlash at tau 5.2-8.3 with `generation.presence_penalty 0`) with no line explaining why. Behaviour is unchanged and identical to v0.4.3.1 (byte-identical text, same route); the daemon now logs `DFlash spec disabled -> AR (non-neutral repeat/presence/frequency penalty ...)` per request (previously only temp>0 requests got the warning).
- **`--tp N`: repeat, presence and frequency penalties now work on Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 dense TP (mesh and hand routes) and Qwen3.5-MoE EP; `hipfire run qwen3.5:4b --tp 2` and serve requests carrying registry sampling are no longer refused (`presence_penalty is not supported at tp>1` / HTTP 400).** The tp>1 loops sample on the host over rank 0's logits (the LM head runs on rank 0 only), and the daemon guard (`request_guards.rs`) existed because that sampler had no penalty stage while the single-GPU path penalizes on its own. The Qwen tp>1 loops now apply `sampler::apply_logit_policy_cpu` (the penalty stage of the single-GPU host sampler) to rank 0's logits before the existing sampler, over the tokens generated so far (never the prompt, the single-GPU Qwen AR scope) with the single-GPU window (`repeat_window` of at least 1, at most 2048). DeepSeek4 and MiniMax EP still refuse a non-neutral penalty (their loops have no penalty stage); `serve` now forwards configured penalty defaults at tp>1 for Qwen archs, as at tp=1. **Greedy output, with and without penalties, is byte-identical to single-GPU:** 2x R9700 (gfx1201), serve battery of 5 committed prompts (`benchmarks/prompts/hw-gate/serve-battery.json`), TP2 vs one card. `qwen3.5-4b.mq4`, mesh and hand routes: no penalty, registry presence 1.5, and presence 1.5 + repeat 1.05 are each 5/5 prompts identical; `qwen3.8-27b.mq4-xts`, mesh route: no penalty and presence 1.5 + repeat 1.05, 5/5. The penalties change the text on the single card and on TP2 alike (e.g. the 4B code answer is 142 tokens without and 192 with), so the match is not vacuous. Registry sampling (temperature 1.0, seeded): 4B 5/5 identical, 27B 4/5 (the TP sampler draws from the full distribution, the single-card kernel from its top-K, so sampled text is not byte-identical in general). MoE EP (`qwen3.5-35b-a3b.mq4`, TP2) accepts and applies penalties, but its text already differs from single-GPU without any penalty (EP numerics), so no byte-identity is claimed there.
- **Fixed: gfx1030 (RDNA2) + any MQ6/HFQ6 model (e.g. `qwen3.5:9b-mq6`) crashed the daemon at pre-warm with `no implementation for GemvMq6G256Prerotated` (#478).** The MQ6/HFQ6 GEMV rows (plain, pre-rotated, residual, SwiGLU-residual) were arch-gated `HasMmq` (gfx906/RDNA3/RDNA4), but their kernels are generic wave32 scalar kernels with no WMMA/MMQ dependence (the prefill GEMM and fused QKV/gate-up HFQ6 keys were already `Always`). The gate is now `HasHfq6Gemv` = `HasMmq` plus wave32, which admits RDNA1/RDNA2 and leaves gfx906/RDNA3/RDNA4 routing and CDNA exclusion unchanged. **Resolve-tested on CPU only (gfx1010/1030/1031/1032 and the prior archs); not validated on RDNA2 hardware**, so the load-time "UNVALIDATED on RDNA2" warning stays. Workaround until verified: use an `.mq4` SKU.
- **Fixed: DDTree combined with CASK/TriAttention eviction panicked mid-run (`target_hidden_host size mismatches position`) (#272).** The combination is now refused at load before any allocation (`DDTree ... cannot be combined with CASK/TriAttention eviction`), and `dflash_spec_demo` exits with the same message. CASK is deprecated since 0.4.0, so no host-shadow compaction was added; drop the CASK sidecar or set `ddtree_budget = 0`.
- **Fixed: DFlash serve with `--kv bf16` failed every request at the first verify-graph capture (`HipError(906): hipMemcpy D2D at offset: operation would make the legacy stream depend on a capturing blocking stream`; capture since afba4a9adc, default-on since 213df925c7; v0.4.3 and beta).** bf16 KV is not a batched-attention tier (`fa_layers_batched_ok`), so each full-attention layer of the captured verify forward ran `batch_chunk_full_attn_fallback` (`qwen35/prefill.rs`), whose per-row decode loop copied the residual row with blocking legacy-stream `hipMemcpy` (the 906) and uploaded the row position from a host slice (under capture an async upload from a stack temporary, so a graph that got past the copies would have replayed the first cycle's positions). The fallback now uses the stream-ordered `memcpy_dtod_at_auto` and copies the row position device-to-device from `pbs.positions` (uploaded outside capture by every caller) into `s.pos_buf`, which the decode kernels read on the device, so one captured graph is valid at every window position; eager behaviour is unchanged (same copies, same values). Evidence, R9700 gfx1201, Qwen3.8-27B mq4-xts + registry DFlash draft, `--kv bf16`, greedy `serve_harness.py` battery and chain (400 tokens, fresh serve process per arm): beta `085dd189b5` fails all five battery requests with the 906 above; the fix captures B=16 (4,162 blobs) and completes, and the decoded text is byte-identical across 2 fresh processes, to `HIPFIRE_VERIFY_GRAPH=0` on the fix, to `HIPFIRE_VERIFY_GRAPH=0` on beta, and (DFlash off) to beta's AR run; the default fp8 KV DFlash battery is byte-identical to beta (that tier takes the batched path and never reaches the fallback). On gfx1100 (XTX) `--kv bf16` is refused at load (`native KV bf16 requires exact gfx1201 H24/Hkv4/D256`), so the bf16 repro is not reachable there; the XTX default q8 DFlash battery is byte-identical to beta.
- **`qwen3_dspark_bench` (lab example) sizes KV from the prompt (HIPF-172).** A >4096-token prompt overran the hard-coded `max_seq = 4096` KV and page-faulted; the prompt is now tokenized before load and `max_seq = max(prompt + max(max, warmup) + 256, 4096)`. Lab example only, no default-path change. (#996, @fivetide)
- **gfx1100 (7900 XTX): compressed MTP draft vocabulary for Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 MTP heads that ship without a sidecar (the 27B), default ON for exact gfx1100 (`HIPFIRE_GFX1100_DRAFT_VOCAB=0` keeps the full-vocab draft).** At load, the rows of a fixed 65,536-token subset are copied out of the trunk lm_head (178 MiB on the 27B) and the existing compressed-draft paths run over it; verify, the accept rule and the bonus token are unchanged, so the target distribution is the trunk's (sampled mode stays distribution-exact). **NUMERIC, not byte-identical:** the draft changes which tokens are accepted per window, so verify row shapes shift and greedy MTP text can diverge from beta at a near-tie (MTP already differs from AR the same way; `HIPFIRE_GFX1100_DRAFT_VOCAB=0` is bit-identical to beta). KLD/eval paths never load the draft: standard WT2/code24 kldseq pins unchanged. The subset is built only from public files in this repo (`examples/mtp_draft_vocab.rs`, rebuilt byte-for-byte by `tests/draft_vocab_rebuild.rs`). 27B mq4-xts, MTP K=3: decode +7.5% at 9K, +1.7% at 39K, +2.4% at 100K, +3% on short prompts.
- **Explicit native MQ6 railgun programs on gfx1151.** A fixed-binding prepare/replay API authors the single/x4 lane-row kernels from their real A1/G8 corpus receipt, plans allocation-wide dependencies and executes a retained PM4 program with conservative system visibility. Shapes, actual HIP allocation bounds and the loaded ABI are checked; a standalone oracle covers changing-input replay and a two-node RAW chain against incumbent HIP rows. Model capture integration and existing Redline defaults are unchanged. See `docs/MQ6-RAILGUN.md`.
- **G12 slice 1: one assistant-turn cache publication seam (#666).** Qwen AR, Qwen spec (MTP/DFlash), DS4 (AR/EP/spec), the continuous batch and the Qwen4 lane batch each carried an identical cache-action struct plus store function. All now publish through `hipfire_engine::turn_cache` (`TurnCacheAction`, `apply_turn_cache_action`, `asst_turn_fingerprint`); DS4's empty-payload skip moves into its action builder. No behaviour change: gfx1151 multi-turn AR (Qwen3.5-9B), MTP (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) and DS4 (V4-Flash mq2r) runs are byte-identical to beta, including `cached_tokens` and every cache store.
- **gfx1201 packed-Q8 split-KV DFlash verification accepts up to 64 KV splits** (`HIPFIRE_GFX12_FA2_SPLIT_COUNT=2|4|8|16|32|64`; default still 8, still opt-in behind `HIPFIRE_GFX12_FA2_SPLIT_VERIFY=1`). The LSE partial entry already derives each split's tile range from the live context and the merge loops over the split count, so only the guards (kernel partial + merge, launcher, env parse) limited it. At 8 splits a long context runs on 32 workgroups. R9700, Qwen3.8-27B MQ4-XTS + DFlash2, Q8 KV, eager verify, B=8, 64K prompt, `dflash_spec_demo`, 200 tokens, identical text in every arm: VerifyAttn 74.9 / S8 95.5 / **S16 109.9** / S32 109.6 / S64 107.8 tok/s (single runs). (#921, @paleluna82-del)
- **gfx1201 (R9700): native-fp8 split-KV FA2 verifier for the fp8 verify attend, default ON at 16 splits from 8,192 tokens of LIVE context, for verify blocks of at most 16 rows (`HIPFIRE_GFX12_FA2_SPLIT_VERIFY_FP8=0` restores VerifyAttn; `=<2..=64>` picks the split count with no context floor and admits 2..=32 rows). NUMERIC, not byte-identical above the floor (byte-identical to VerifyAttn below it).** The earlier default-on attempt failed an independent regate on the stock config (27B MQ4-XTS + DFlash, fp8 KV, DFlash block 16, verify graph on): the route bound kernels and grew its Q scratch at launch inside verify-graph capture (`hipMalloc: operation not permitted when stream is capturing` on every singleton request), measured its context floor against the graph's `physical_cap` grid, and the lane-batched CB verify did not take it (`lane_fa_oracle` 9/18 FAIL). Now (1) capture-time admission: a capture takes the route only when the caller names the window's live context and `Gpu::fp8_fa2_split_verify_capture_ready` holds (module, merge and pre-convert loaded, Q scratch already grown), otherwise it keeps VerifyAttn; the DFlash verify graph loads and grows those assets right before it captures a window the route serves, and tags each captured graph with its route class (route on/off at the window's live `start_pos + B`), dropping and re-capturing a graph when a later window's class differs (a long request followed by a short one, or a decode crossing 8,192), so the floor is always the live context; (2) the lane-batched CB DFlash verify keeps the singleton launch for every lane the singleton serves with the split route (`Gpu::attention_verify_fp8_lanes_routed`; the other lanes still share one VerifyAttn tile + reduce), so batched == singleton at every context; (3) the default admits 2..=16 rows only (the kernel oracles cover B = 2, 4, 8, 16), so 17..=32-row prefill tails keep VerifyAttn. The fp8 verify attend (`attention_flash_fp8_e4m3_tile_batched`: DFlash chain verify, MTP/ngram verify blocks, prefill tails of up to 16 rows; eager and under the DFlash verify-graph capture) runs the FA2 GQA body with the native-fp8 KV fill and the packed-Q8 verifier's LSE + normalized-Oacc split records before VerifyAttn. Exact gfx1201 dense H24/KV4/D256, non-tree, not Redline-recording, partials large enough; everything else keeps VerifyAttn. A `HIPFIRE_FA2_SPLIT_LSE_FP8` build of the FA2 module enables the LSE entries with KMODE=8 under distinct `_lse_` symbols (the KMODE=8 Q0 module's objects and symbols are unchanged); its fill decodes E4M3 with `v_cvt_pk_f32_fp8` (equal to the software decode for every non-NaN code) from up-front 8-byte loads. The module is now in the gfx1201 kernel inventory (`attention_fp8_e4m3_fa2_gqa_partial_lse_gfx1201` with the merge, pre-convert and direct `_f16_` entries; trace row in `kernel-trace-qwen35.tsv`) and the launcher resolves partial, merge and pre-convert from that one module, so it compiles before ready: the first-request JIT (two hipcc compiles after ready, first fp8 DFlash turn 154 -> 57 tok/s) is gone. The DFlash route is an open predicted-fallback plan, so the module still logs one `unplanned kernel ... bound lazily (module already compiled)` line per symbol after ready, exactly like the other ~75 inventory modules on that route; no compile happens. (#922, @paleluna82-del; registration and capture/lane admission: maintainer)
  - **Speed, stock config, timing class** (unshared R9700 cards B and C under `fabric-run.sh --class timing`; Qwen3.8-27B MQ4-XTS + registry DFlash MQ4 draft, fp8 KV, DFlash block auto = 16, verify graph ON, greedy; `serve_harness battery`, three long turns per context, 1,024 max tokens; fresh serve process per sample, three per arm, order off def def off def off; off = `HIPFIRE_GFX12_FA2_SPLIT_VERIFY_FP8=0`, default = unset). Decode tok/s, per-process mean of the three turns, min / median / max, off -> default: 4K (3.7-4.0K live) 64.20 / 65.90 / 65.93 -> 64.00 / 64.33 / 65.73 (below the 8,192 floor, so no route: text md5 identical on all three turns, ranges overlap, the median gap is run-to-run noise), 16K 53.27 / 53.30 / 53.33 -> 59.57 / 59.60 / 59.67 (**+11.8%**), 32K 40.17 / 40.40 / 40.57 -> 51.20 / 51.40 / 51.40 (**+27.2%**), 64K 28.17 / 29.93 / 30.13 -> 42.60 / 43.37 / 43.57 (**+44.9%**), 128K 18.77 / 18.93 / 19.00 -> 33.53 / 33.70 / 33.80 (**+78.0%**); the ranges are disjoint at every context from 16K up; mean tau off -> default 1.91 -> 1.87 (16K), 1.72 -> 1.75 (32K), 1.74 -> 1.68 (64K), 1.67 -> 1.62 (128K), on different text. Kernel time per FullAttention layer (`verify_attn_oracle bench_serve`, eager, B=8, VerifyAttn / split ms): 512 0.039/0.063, 1K 0.037/0.046, 2K 0.058/0.055, 4K 0.101/0.070, 8K 0.186/0.101, 16K 0.366/0.161, 64K 1.468/0.609, 127K 2.946/1.115 (B=16 127K 5.84/2.13), which is why the default has a floor.
  - **Numerics.** Not byte-identical to VerifyAttn (f16 Q/K/V/P operands): `verify_attn_oracle oracle fp8` 63/63 PASS and `fa2_check fp8` at S=8/16/32 relative RMS error vs VerifyAttn max 4.23e-3 over B 2-16 x ctx 1-130,048 x eager/capture, no non-finite values. `eval_hipfire --scored-max-batch` does not reach this route (its 512/2048-token windows sit below the 4,096 scalar-kernel crossover, and DFlash `ChainVerify` is not set), so the end-to-end instrument is `verify_route_logits` (new example): teacher-forced DFlash `ChainVerify` blocks of 8 at 62.6-63.0K and 125.9-126.0K contexts, 256 rows x 3 prompts x 2 contexts, VerifyAttn logits vs default logits in separate fresh processes (VerifyAttn is bit-reproducible, two runs byte-identical). KL(VerifyAttn || split) per row: mean 3.4e-5 / 4.0e-4 / 4.9e-5 (64K prompts 1-3), 4.7e-5 / 3.6e-5 / 3.4e-5 (128K prompts 1-3), pooled 1.0e-4 nats, p99 <= 3.5e-3, max 9.2e-3; argmax agreement 98.0-99.6% (1524/1536 pooled), every flip at a top-1/top-2 margin <= 0.13 logits (median 0.01). For scale, the fp8 route's KLD against the source is 0.042 (WT2) / 0.030 (code24). Greedy DFlash text differs from VerifyAttn after 4-388 characters in all six long-context cells (per-prompt tau 1.42-1.82 vs 1.50-1.86 on the different text; neither direction dominates). Long-context retrieval, both arms: needle at 25/50/75% depth in real 62.6-63.0K and 125.9-126.0K-token prompts, 3/3 hit each; NIAH fixtures 16K/32K/64K/128K (10.9K/21.6K/43.3K/86.5K actual tokens) all hit.
  - **Stock-config gate** (branch `splitkv-fp8-default-v2`, R9700 cards B/C, Qwen3.8-27B MQ4-XTS + registry DFlash MQ4 draft, fp8 KV, DFlash block auto = 16, verify graph ON, greedy, fresh serve process per sample, off = `=0`, default = unset): `serve_harness battery` 5/5 `finish=stop`, runaway/empty/attractor 0, text md5 identical to off on every turn (the failing arm of the earlier attempt: 5/5 dead). 4K-class turns (3,730-3,999 tokens, below the floor, 4 turns): text md5 identical to off. Decode tok/s, order off def def off, two fresh processes per arm, no failures: 32K (three long turns) 41.07 / 41.20 -> 52.37 / 52.43 (**+27.4%**), 128K 19.10 / 19.27 -> 33.93 / 33.93 (**+76.9%**); the two default processes are bit-reproducible (identical per-turn md5 and tok/s). A 32K-class request followed by 4K-class requests in one process drops the route-on graph and re-captures at route off (`[verify-graph] ... route class changed`), and the 4K turns are md5-identical to off; a decode that crosses 8,192 mid-request (7.6K prompt) re-captures at route on, identical text up to the crossing. `lane_fa_oracle` 18/18 PASS with the route on (9 cases with split lanes) and 18/18 with `=0`; `verify_attn_oracle oracle fp8` 63/63 and `a3b_gqa8_oracle` 580/580 PASS (both pin the route off for their VerifyAttn reference). `verify_route_logits --block 16` (teacher-forced `ChainVerify`, 256 rows x 3 prompts x 62.6-63.0K and 125.9-126.0K contexts, VerifyAttn vs default in separate fresh processes; both bit-reproducible): KL(VerifyAttn || split) per-prompt mean 8.8e-5 / 3.8e-4 / 3.4e-5 (64K), 5.4e-5 / 2.8e-5 / 3.6e-5 (128K), pooled 1.0e-4 nats, p99 <= 3.5e-3, max 9.2e-3; argmax agreement 99.6% (1530/1536), every flip at a top-1/top-2 margin <= 0.11 logits.
  - **Routes that take it, rocprofv3 kernel trace** (default env, 27B fp8 KV, three ~9.3-10K-token turns of 192 tokens, daemon wrapped in `rocprofv3 --kernel-trace`; 16 full-attention layers per verify window, so dispatches / 16 = windows): DFlash 624 `attention_fp8_e4m3_fa2_gqa_partial_lse_gfx1201` + 624 merge (39 windows, verify graph), `--spec mtp` (K=3, eager) 368 + 368 (23 windows), `--spec ngram` 112 + 112 (7 windows with a drafted block of at least 2 rows; windows with no n-gram match are 1-row decode steps and never take it), and none with `=0` (DFlash off arm: 818 `attention_verify_gqa_fp8_gfx1201`, no split kernel). So MTP and ngram verify do take the route above 8,192 live context, like DFlash: eager `attention_flash_fp8_e4m3_tile_batched` routes on `max_ctx_len`; ngram reaches it through `ModelSlot::verify_block` -> `verify_dflash_block`, MTP through `forward_prefill_batch_with_pbs_opts` with `DflashFusionCtx::Off`. Ngram is opt-in on the 27B and drafts little there (tau 0.2-0.3), so its speed effect is not separately measured.
  - **Stock serve battery on the final binary** (card B, builtin 5-turn battery, default env): 5/5 `finish=stop`, runaway/empty/attractor 0, request md5 of every turn identical to the independent regate's default and `=0` arms; text read (merge-sort code, train-distance arithmetic reaching 210 miles, seasons, a coherent short story, a 5-item coding list).
- **Windows: `scripts/install.ps1` parameters bind again (#979).** Every release from v0.4.1 through v0.4.3.1 shipped the script with two UTF-8 byte-order marks, so PowerShell never saw its `param()` block and `-Tag`, `-Ref`, `-Branch`, `-Commit`, `-CompileKernels` and `-KernelPackUrl` were ignored. The script is now BOM-free ASCII, and the Windows CI job parses every `scripts/*.ps1` and fails on a doubled BOM or an unbound installer parameter. A branch or ref whose checked-out HEAD carries a release tag now also tries that release's prebuilt kernel pack.
- **Windows: release kernel packs are accepted on native Windows (untested on GPU hardware).** `kernel-pack install` and the runtime no longer reject a pack because the local HIP SDK's ROCm version or `hipcc` identity differs from the Linux build's; the format, arch, commit, cache ABI, extra flags, SHA-256 and every per-module index and object are still verified. Whether the Windows HIP runtime loads these code-object-v6 objects is unverified until a test report lands; `-CompileKernels` forces the local compile. Linux is unchanged.
- **Windows: the HIP runtime DLL is loaded so that the driver's System32 copy cannot shadow the HIP SDK's.** Absolute `amdhip64*.dll` candidates load with `LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR | LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS` (the DLL's own directory resolves its dependencies first), falling back to the previous load on failure; with no SDK root, hipfire's exe directory is tried before `~\.hipfire\runtime` and the standard search. The daemon logs `HIP runtime: <path> (runtime N, driver N)` at start, and `hipfire diag` / `diag --json` (`live_gpu.hip_runtime_library`, `hip_runtime_version_raw`, `hip_driver_version_raw`) report it.
- **Windows: unified-memory GPUs (Strix Halo) now release the model file mapping after the header, as on Linux; every later tensor read uses positioned reads.** Previously Windows kept the mapping, and its non-unix weight path read only from the mapping. Discrete GPUs keep the mapping on both OSes.
- **Windows CI builds and smokes the packaged binaries, and the job is now required (no longer `continue-on-error`):** the Windows MSVC job runs `daemon.exe --version`, `hipfire.exe --version` and `hipfire.exe diag --json` from the extracted ZIP with a System32-only `PATH`, and `scripts/check-pe-imports.ps1` fails the job if either binary imports a DLL outside the Windows system set, the MSVC runtime and the HIP SDK set. It is still compile/package coverage, not Windows GPU certification.
- **Docs: native Windows and WSL2 are both documented as untested on GPU hardware** (WSL2 was called the recommended route). New volunteer test kit `scripts/windows-check.ps1` (system/driver/HIP SDK/DLL resolution facts, smallest Qwen3.5 text model greedy run and short bench, optional 27B) and issue form `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/windows-test-report.yml`; see GETTING_STARTED "Help test Windows".
- **Dense Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 `serve --tp N` now loads the generic mesh executor by default (`HIPFIRE_DENSE_TP_ROUTE=auto`, developer; `hand` rolls back, `mesh` forces).** `auto` falls back to the hand route with `[loader] dense qwen TP route=auto -> hand: <reason>` for `speculation.mtp = on` or an uneven TP3/TP5 split; the mesh route supports every KV backend, VMM included, and is byte-identical to the hand route at TP2/TP4 (maintainer hwtest on the R9700s: logits fnv64 equal to the hand route at TP2 and TP4; a serve battery and chain also ran on TP2 and TP4 with the default route). On 4x R9700 (maintainer-measured on hiptrx), Qwen3.8-27B mq4-xts (`bench --matrix --spec off`, 3 fresh processes per arm, median of the run medians): TP2 pp512 3289.5 vs 2873.5 tok/s, pp2048 3355.2 vs 2753.8; TP4 pp512 2061.0 vs 1919.4, tg64@128 51.77 vs 43.96; TP2 tg was 0.5% behind the hand route (54.67 vs 54.94) and ties it after the LM-head change below (54.89 vs 54.95). (#927)
- **Generic dense TP: the LM head (final norm + output GEMV) runs on rank 0 only, as on the hand route (developer, byte-identical).** The Qwen3.5 mesh TP plan declared no weight for the `Head` op, so the splitter ran it replicated on every rank; `output_norm` and `lm_head` are now declared `Pin(Output)` in the plan, which places the op on rank 0 (the serve loop only reads rank 0's logits). `hw_tests::tp_prefill_decode_matches_hand_route` fingerprints are unchanged (TP2 27B rows 300 chunk 128 `62279ff57ec9bdeb`; TP4 rows 1100 chunk 512 `90ae89ad700fe986`) and serve-battery text is identical to the hand route and to before. 2x R9700, Qwen3.8-27B mq4-xts, `bench --matrix --spec off`, median of 3 fresh processes, TP2 generic vs hand: tg64@128 54.89 vs 54.95, tg64@4096 54.19 vs 54.24 (before: 54.75, 54.02).
- **`hipfire serve/bench --tp N` with speculation `auto` no longer fails on an auto-paired DFlash draft:** the daemon and `fit` drop the draft on tp>1 with a log line; explicit `on` is still refused. (#927)
- **Fixed a daemon panic (`assertion failed: size <= buf.size`) on reset when a VMM KV cache had grown past its first mapping** (`hipfire bench --tp 2 --matrix --ctx 4096` on the hand route): `KvCache::clear_gpu` now clears `t.buf.size()`. (#927)
- **Fixed: a LLaMA `.mq4` quantized before the row-padded HFQ4-G128 packer (`b4846285e`) with `K % 128 != 0` crashed the GPU on the first generate; it is now refused at load.** SmolLM2-360M (hidden 960) routes its K=960 projections to HFQ4-G128, which the old packer laid out across rows (540 B/row instead of 576), so the row-strided kernels read past the buffer (`Memory access fault … Page not present`). The single-device manifest load now checks every packed payload against its declared `[rows, K]` extent: HFQ4-G128 `[rows, K]` matrices must be row-padded and MQ4-G256 `[rows, K]` matrices need `K % 256 == 0` (higher-rank tensors such as the GDN conv1d `[C, 1, 4]` are packed flat and are not checked). Requantize such files.
- **Fix: railgun `KernelGuard` conditionals refuse a flag-writing body node that is more than one wave (`grid × block > 32`).** The guard runs once per wave, so a multi-wave writer's later waves could read the flag after its first wave cleared it and skip their work (HIPF-169 repro on gfx1151, `loki_cond --arm CP` under concurrent GPU load; such a program is now refused at `add_conditional`). `bounded_while` restores `conditionals` when a copy is refused, and `Gfx10Pm4CommandBuffer::ends_with_compute_idle` no longer counts a `CS_PARTIAL_FLUSH` that ends a `COND_EXEC` region (it may be skipped).
- **Developer: `scripts/serve-restart.sh` and the certify perf arm no longer kill other agents' serves and daemons (HIPF-176).** `serve-restart.sh` ran `kill -9` on every `pgrep -f "hipfire serve"` / `"target/release/daemon"` match and `fuser -k` on the port; it now runs `hipfire stop --force <port>`, which stops only this install's serve and daemons, and exits 1 if something else still holds the port. `autoresearch/ar/certify/serve_runner.py` freed the GPU with `pkill -9 -x daemon`, which hit every hipfire daemon on the host; it now kills only its own serve's process group. The two archived `cpu_exec_ab*.sh` A/B scripts keep their `pkill -f 'release/daemon'` and carry a warning. `scripts/serve-loop-gate.sh` likewise no longer kills other agents' daemons or leaves its own serve behind (HIPF-126, #953; #992): it tracks only its own `hipfire serve` PID and tears down that process group (TERM, then KILL after about 10 s; no more `pkill -f daemon` or `fuser -k`), starts the serve under `setpriv --pdeathsig TERM` so a SIGKILLed gate still takes it down, refuses to start (exit 2) when the port is already listening, and only accepts a `/health` whose pid is its own serve.
- **Fixed: MoE models whose hidden size is not a multiple of four 256-wide groups (K/256 % 4 != 0, e.g. MiniMax tiny, K = 512) silently produced all-zero MoE gate/up, so the routed experts added nothing (v0.4.3 regression).** The wave32 indexed HFQ4/MQ4 gate_up kernel is built without a tail and read only whole quads of groups. The three wave32 indexed launchers now send those shapes to the batched kernel with batch = 1, which handles the tail; K/256 % 4 == 0 shapes (K2048/3072/4096), K2816 and wave64 keep their kernels, so the hot decode shapes are unchanged (any other hidden size, e.g. 2560, now takes the batched kernel at batch 1; its speed is not measured). Output changes for the affected shapes by design (NUMERIC). On gfx1151 (author), tiny.mq4 gate/up L2 0 -> 78.9 / 79.5 and KL vs the HF f32 model 0.0719 -> 0.0385; the merge gate ran `moe_gate_up_tail_parity` 2/2 on gfx1201 and gfx1100 and MoE decode smokes (coherent). (#956)
- **Fixed: a ParoQuant safetensors directory (dense or MoE) under VMM KV was refused at admission with "automatic Qwen VMM context sizing requires an HFQ weight manifest" (v0.4.3 regression from 294c4ad9d).** Directory sources now skip automatic sizing and keep a fixed `max_seq` (default 4096 with a recorded reason when omitted), as before. On gfx1151 `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-PARO` loads under `kv=vmm` with the same decoded text sha as legacy KV; the merge gate loaded the same directory under VMM KV on gfx1201 with coherent text. (#955)
- **Fixed: a grammar violation on a retired DFlash request's AR step failed with a retryable gpu error ("terminal prefix repair failed: ... no completed window available") instead of a validation error (v0.4.3 #907 regression).** `spec_window_repair_attempt` no longer tries to repair a window on an AR step, so greedy Qwen3.5 DFlash requests carrying `tools` end with `class: validation, retryable: false`, as without retirement. Verified on gfx1151 (`qwen3.5-9b.mq4` + DFlash draft, forced `HIPFIRE_SPEC_RETIRE=100`); the gfx1201 serve smoke was coherent but did not exercise DFlash. `docs/env-vars.md` now says the retire policy compares committed tokens per cycle. (#950)
- **Batched ParoQuant MoE prefill (`HIPFIRE_PARO_BATCHED=1`, opt-in, default off) no longer produces prompt-ignoring text on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-PARO.** The shared gate/up overwrote the routed experts' rotated input before the routed GEMMs read it; the routed `InputBasis` stage now runs right before the routed tail, and the `gemm_f32_batched` guard accepts loaded `Raw` weights (beta errored with "F32 GEMM needs full-window F32 ... views"). On gfx1151 (`shisa-ai/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-PARO-packed`, greedy, legacy KV) the 48-token probes are byte-identical to per-token prefill (hidden rel-L2 at the worst layer 0.91 -> 0.032), but the flag-on route is NUMERIC: on the ~2K-token battery two of the prompts diverge from per-token at near-tie words after about 40 tokens. The merge gate noted that the gfx1201 batched Paro grouped WMMA hits a gfx11-only builtin (pre-existing, not this change). (#972)

- **`vision_mode` (`vision.mode`, `HIPFIRE_VISION_MODE`) now defaults to `auto` (was `off`): `run` / `serve` / `embed` load a present vision-tower sidecar and serve images without configuring anything.** Image prefill is fast enough to be a default (1024^2 image TTFT with the streamed tower: R9700 0.51 s, 7900 XTX 0.81 s on a PCIe 4.0 x4 host, Strix Halo 1.84 s; entry below). `hipfire config set vision_mode off` (or `HIPFIRE_VISION_MODE=off`) restores the pre-0.4.4 text-only load: the tower is never wired, even an explicit `--vision` is skipped, and an image request is refused with the error that names the knob. `auto` stays silently text-only when no sidecar is declared or on disk (no download, no message), so a model without a tower is unchanged. **The Qwen3.5/3.8-VL tower is no longer VRAM-resident under `auto`/`on`: it stays on disk/host and is streamed per block into two fixed VRAM staging slots during each image encode** (double-buffered on a private copy stream, pinned bounce buffers, parallel positional reads, the container pages pulled into the page cache in the background at load; same kernels, same weights, same order, so the tower embeddings are byte-identical to the resident path on gfx1201 (md5 of the dumped embeddings for every committed `benchmarks/vision/images` image plus a 1024^2 fixture), and greedy answers are identical). New value **`vision_mode=resident`** keeps today's whole-tower upload. Idle VRAM after a `qwen3.8-27b.mq4-xts` + `qwen3.8-27b-vision.hfq` load at `max_seq` 32768, vs `off`: `auto` +127.6 MiB (R9700) / +142.2 MiB (7900 XTX) — 2 x 45.0 MiB staging + 4.9 MiB small resident tensors + allocator overhead — and `resident` +958 MiB on both. The automatic `max_seq` also reserves the tower's activation scratch for the largest admitted image (327 MiB at the 2 MP / 7,812-patch budget, `vision_reserve=` in the `max_seq budget:` line) for any tower load: on the 24 GB XTX it is 223,323 (`off`) / 210,453 (`auto`) / 184,612 (`resident`); on a 32 GB R9700 the model's 262,144 in every mode (card capacity 514,414 / 500,846 / 473,603). Image TTFT at the HTTP level, streamed vs resident, median of fresh processes: R9700 1024^2 507 vs 504 ms first image (491 vs 482 repeat), Strix Halo 1841 vs 1826 ms (1805 vs 1788 repeat); see the vision tower section of `docs/CONFIG.md` for the XTX (PCIe 4.0 x4 on the measured host) and page-cache-dropped numbers. Only the Qwen3.5/3.8-VL tower streams; EmbeddingGemma 2, qwen35-embed, LFM2-VL and dots towers load as before for every non-`off` mode. The config TUI gains a Vision tower row (Memory & context). `hipfire bench` pins `vision_mode=off` in every arm (it has no media input), so bench loads, VRAM admission and numbers match earlier releases; the daemon and the CLI's admission/embed projections read the one schema default (`hipfire_config::vision_mode_default`) instead of hardcoding `off` for a load request without `vision_mode`. The EmbeddingGemma 2 scripts that check the tower-less refusals now pass `vision_mode=off` explicitly.

NUMERIC, KLD-gated, not byte-identical.** An MTP K=3 verify runs every MQ4G256V2 projection with 4 rows, which on exact gfx1100 went to the N<=16 f16 WMMA residual tiers (12 of 16 tile columns padding, the weight stream at about half of the card's bandwidth). These KLD and perf figures are the PR author's. *Maintainer gate (same 7900 XTX, `qwen3.8-27b.mq4-xts` and the AGENTS.md fixtures; ABBA with fresh processes, precompiled gfx1100 pack, 0 JIT lines; `hipfire bench --spec mtp`, committed `benchmarks/prompts/mtpfloor` prompts, 256 tokens, `HIPFIRE_VERIFY_GRAPH=0`):* decode code-1k 104.7 -> 127.4 tok/s (1.217x), prose-1k 106.7 -> 131.1 (1.229x), code-32k 81.8 -> 95.5 (1.168x), prose-32k 51.7 -> 58.9 (1.139x); prefill equal, tau equal except prose-32k 1.38 -> 1.32. - **Fixed: Flash-Next DFlash2 reuses the Qwen4 session cache on follow-up turns (HIPF-143).** The DFlash2 route (`--spec dflash` with a DFlash2 draft) prefilled every turn cold and reported `cached_tokens: 0`. It now plans and begins an AR-route session like the AR route does: it restores a snapshot or continues the live state, publishes its own snapshot boundaries, and prefills only the suffix. The draft keeps its feature rows below the restart point when it committed them for the same tokens and they still hold the 2048-row window its next forward reads. A suffix of at least one window restarts the draft with an empty context at that point instead, and any other hit prefills cold (`Speculator::can_resume_at`). Measured on Strix Halo with mt-bench turn 2 (16 prompts, greedy, 512 tokens): 4,493 tokens reused against 0 before, 2,228 prefilled against 6,721, prefill 511 → 349 ms mean, τ unchanged (1.55 → 1.56). Greedy text equals warm AR on every row where both reuse the same prefix and turn 1 took no think-budget realign (HIPF-194). Like AR, warm output is session-exact rather than cold-exact. A turn that stops partway through a verified window still drops the live state, because DFlash2 has no terminal-prefix repair; only snapshot hits the draft can resume remain for those turns.
- **DFlash 27B on gfx1201: the whole speculative window as one certified railgun program, opt-in (`HIPFIRE_DFLASH_RAILGUN_WINDOW=1` with `HIPFIRE_DFLASH_RAILGUN_CORPUS=<receipt corpus>`, developer; default off).** On exact gfx1201, dense 27B-class Qwen3.5, FP8 KV, the fixed-16 DFlash2 chain draft and greedy decoding, a warm window (draft, greedy selector, 16-row verify, hidden commit and head) is authored from the speculator's own launch plans as one typed railgun `KernelProgram` (`railgun::window::WindowPlan`, explicit Scalar32 / Interior64 / grid patch expressions over a finite shape topology), checked against the JIT receipt corpus (`railgun-cert whole16`, `railgun-jit-corpus --window-sequence`) and lowered to one retained PM4 indirect buffer; the KV writer `kv_cache_write_fp8_e4m3_batched` is admitted as `Conditional` with a sealed-positions bind witness (`railgun::index_bind`). Cold seeds, resets, lookup Copy/probe windows, unseen shapes and every builder refusal take the ordinary HIP route, counted per reason. A new shape is planned on the window thread (about 7.5 ms: plan, author, PM4 plan, artifact resolve) and lowered on a background thread while that window runs on HIP (`skeleton_building`; `HIPFIRE_DFLASH_RAILGUN_SYNC_BUILD=1` builds synchronously). Skeletons are keyed by shape family and draft attention `l_domain`; each records the Gpu scratch slots it binds and is replanned only when one of them is replaced (`rdna_compute::scratch::scratch_growth_epoch` gates the check), so a regrown scratch slot never leaves a skeleton bound to a freed buffer. Byte-identical to the HIP-graph route (drafted, accepted and committed tokens per window and the final text, prose and code, lookup off and default, background and synchronous builds). Measured on card A (R9700, 3 fresh daemons per arm, 7 warm requests each): prose window 40.64 -> 39.1 ms (51.4 -> 53.3 tok/s, +3.7%), code window 41.1 -> 40.1 ms (221.8 -> 226.4 tok/s in two of three processes; 221.0 in the third). The short-turn serve battery (5 turns of 243-668 tokens, about 50 distinct shapes per process) decodes 3-6% slower with the window on (130.1 / 139.1 vs 139.2 / 145.0 tok/s), because each new shape pays its window-thread planning; default-on needs that planning off the window thread. Developer diagnostics: `HIPFIRE_DFLASH_RAILGUN_DEBUG` (per-window line, per-skeleton build timings, and a pre-submit read-back of every kernarg buffer and decoded dispatch), `HIPFIRE_DFLASH_RAILGUN_TWIN` (bound images through HIP), `HIPFIRE_DFLASH_RAILGUN_MANIFEST` / `_SEQUENCE_OUT` (per-shape Whole16 manifests). Design: `docs/design/2026-10-25-dflash-railgun-window.md`.
- **railgun kernarg analysis: a guarded analysis and a `Conditional` status for kernels that index a direct pointer argument with a loaded `i32` (the DFlash Whole16 `kv_cache_write_fp8_e4m3_batched` writer, design A amendment 2026-10-25).** The reported `base-memory-derived` refusal of that writer is not the loaded position: the legacy lattice already drops it through the sign extension and multiply. It is the optional `slot_descs`/`row_slot` descriptor path (a 64-bit loaded `k_base` added into the row address). `peacemaker_ir::passes::kernargs::analyze_guarded(kernel, arch, &[Guard])` substitutes kernarg guards (HD256, B16, null `slot_descs`/`row_slot`) into the lifted ISA, fixes a branch's SCC when a scalar compare of constants decides it, and follows the CFG that remains; a guarded null is a constant with no provenance, never an allocation at address 0. Every access whose address depends on loaded data then needs a complete exact integer/address witness (new `passes/kernarg_ix.rs`: hash-consed bit-vector expressions through moves, sign/zero extension, constant shifts, add/sub/mul and matched 64-bit lo/hi/carry chains; unequal joins, EXEC-partial rewrites and unmodelled arithmetic give no witness) of the form `direct pointer argument + integer displacement` with a qualifying 32-bit index load; it is reported as `KernargFacts::indexed` (`IndexedArgEffect`: access pc, base argument, mode/class/path/cache bits, width, the checked 64-bit displacement `IdxExpr`, its `IndexLoad` records and the guards) and credited allocation-wide to its base argument. Pointer values in the offset, two loaded halves reassembled as a pointer, loaded 64-bit pointers, descriptor bases, mixed bases at a join, EXEC-stale bases, nested `P[Q[i]]` and any unmodelled operation keep `base-memory-derived`. `KernelStatus::Conditional` is new and distinct from `Proven` and `Unknown`; `IdxExpr` has a canonical s-expression `Display`/`FromStr` and a checked-wide evaluator (`eval_checked`) that refuses any wrap or sign change. The unguarded `analyze` is unchanged (the writer is still `Unknown`). Tests: synthetic ISA fixtures for SMEM/VMEM index loads, sign/zero extension, scalar and VCC carry chains, the negatives above, and the real gfx1201 writer object (`tests/kernarg_indexed.rs`).
- **gfx1100 (7900 XTX): WMMA split-K speculative-verify attention for 1..=8 rows, default ON for exact gfx1100 (`HIPFIRE_GFX1100_WMMA_VERIFY_ATTN=0` restores the incumbent verify attention; `HIPFIRE_VERIFY_ATTN=0` opts out too). NUMERIC, KLD-gated, not byte-identical.** Past the multi-row crossover (`HIPFIRE_FA_PERTOKEN_MIN_CTX`, 4096) an MTP K=3 verify (4 rows x 24 q heads over the Q8 KV of each of the 16 full-attention layers) ran the Q8 FA2 split-KV verifier (8 splits x 4 kv heads = 32 workgroups, ~105 GB/s of K/V) or the VerifyAttn rows twin (~160 GB/s), so verify time grew with the context. Eager only (HipGraph capture and Redline recording keep the incumbent routes); every other shape falls through unchanged. The module is in the gfx1100 kernel registry and pack (no first-request JIT). *Kernel (`bench_verify_attn_wmma --check`, 4 rows, cold K/V, f64 reference, RX 7900 XTX, ROCm 7.2.4):* 9K / 40K / 100K 194.5 / 777.0 / 2080.0 us (FA2 split verifier) and 135.2 / 519.9 / 1331.9 us (rows twin) -> 37.3 / 130.6 / 309.5 us (525-703 GB/s, 5.2-6.7x the split verifier); rel L2 vs f64 6.0e-4..6.3e-4 (the split verifier: 6.0e-4..6.2e-4). *KLD (canonical `qwen3.8-27b.mq4-xts` `3e38ccba…`, `--kv-mode q8 --kv-v q8`, `--max-chunks 24`, `eval_hipfire --scored-max-batch 4`, `HIPFIRE_FA_PERTOKEN_MIN_CTX=1` in both arms because the fixtures' 2048/512-token windows sit below the crossover; `=0` vs default, paired per-sequence 95% CI of default minus `=0`):* WT2 0.041110 -> 0.041106, -0.000004 [-0.000105, +0.000097]; code24 0.032749 -> 0.032974, +0.000225 [-0.000166, +0.000616]; both inside the bar (the PR author's batch-4 runs; the maintainer gate's verify-shaped KLD, ON minus OFF, was -0.000051 (WT2) / -0.000100 (code24) at batch 4 and +0.000593 / -0.000086 at batch 8, without paired CIs). The F32 projection arm now taps the calibration activation once (it was captured twice). `hipfire-arch-lfm2moe` no longer bypasses the dispatch registry (ledger row removed, 9 -> 0). The per-lane admission prefill (`Lfm2DecodeBatchState::prefill_lane`) is still its own loop.
- **VerifyAttn twins for fwht4 / fwht3 K (Q8_0 V) on gfx1201 and gfx1100: `attention_verify_gqa_fwht{4,3}_<arch>`.** GQA-shared split-K kernels (one KV scan per kv head for 8 rows x 6 q heads) that write the same `[row][head][max_tiles][2 + 256]` partials as `attention_flash_fwht{4,3}_tile_batched` (`v_mode` 8), reduced by `attention_verify_reduce_<arch>`; they take the K rotation's sign tables as two trailing kernel arguments and reproduce the reference tile's rotation, centroid products and fma order. `attention_flash_fwht{4,3}_batched_masked` intercepts non-tree, `v_mode` 8, descriptor-free (legacy slot) launches of up to 32 rows at head_dim 256, GQA 6, through `VerifyKv::{Fwht4, Fwht3}`; `Gpu::try_attention_verify_gqa` gains a trailing `signs` argument. `verify_attn_oracle` gains `fwht4` / `fwht3` kinds (`--kv fwht4`). Hardware byte-identity is gated by that oracle.

The fwht3 FA2 arm on gfx1201 also raises its `max_ctx_len <= 32768` ceiling to 262,144 and drops its `batch % 16` tail fallback (the body walks to `max(positions)+1` with 64-bit offsets and guards partial query tiles), so fwht3/fwht4 prompts past 32K and chunk tails stay on FA2.
- **fwht4 / fwht3 KV prompts now run the DeltaNet chunk-scan prefill on gfx1100 and gfx1201 (the admission also lets exact gfx1151 through; not measured there).** The scan never reads the KV cache, but its admission named only native fp8 and gfx11 Q8 KV, so `--kv-mode fwht4|fwht3` prefilled the 48 linear-attention layers token-serially (about +0.4 s per 8K tokens on the 7900 XTX by the scoping estimate). NUMERIC, KLD-gated: on WT2/code24 the paired 95% interval includes zero on both arches, but the `.kldseq` values are not byte-equal.

Outputs match `attention_q8_0_kv` and an f64 oracle within 1e-6 (`tests/attention_flash_q8_hd64_parity.rs`; the reference tile misses by 2.5). On gfx1151 SmolLM2-360M PARO decode goes 72.1 → 126.0 tok/s at 712 context, 24.7 → 121.9 at 3445 and 11.5 → 112.3 at 8196; the per-token prompt prefill is 1.3-5.6x faster too. Greedy text is identical across eager, hipGraph and redline, and equal to beta at 712, 3445 and 8196 tokens. At 7066 tokens it differs from beta after 35 characters: the f32 summation order is different. The merge gate ran other cards: gfx1201 SmolLM2-360M q8 decode 26.6 -> 265.5 tok/s at 1.1K context (text identical on 8 of 10 prompts, two near-tie flips at 4K); gfx1100 Llama-3.2-1B 153 -> 508 tok/s at 1.1K, text identical.

It now casts X to F16 and runs `gemm_f16_x_f16_wmma_lds_splitk` (gfx1201, the qwen35-embed tile policy) or `gemm_f16_x_f16_wmma_lds_auto_ld` (gfx11, fused bias); fc2's K = 4304 is zero-padded to 4352 at load (weight) and per call (`cast_f32_to_f16_pitched`). Image answers (shapes, colours, OCR) read correct on the fixed 448^2/1024^2 set.
