The draft's F16 weights with K % 2048 == 0 had a power-of-two row pitch that put every wave on the same DRAM channels (~50 GB/s); the loader now pads those rows by 128 halfs on gfx1151 and `gemm_mw16_residual_wmma_gfx1151_xlds` (the mw16 per-tile WMMA order, X panel staged in LDS) reads them at ~200 GB/s (per call 772 -> 250 us averaged over the draft; gate/up 2.17 -> 0.50 ms).
- **Qwen3-8B (head_dim 128) DFlash on gfx1151: the verify attention takes the VerifyAttn twin; 2K 12.1 -> 15.1 tok/s, 4K 9.7 -> 14.3 tok/s, 8K 23.2 -> 28.0 tok/s (`qwen3-8b.mq4` + `qwen3-8b-dflash.hfq`, AR 45.8 / 44.0 / 38.6), output bytes unchanged.** The gfx1151 VerifyAttn kernels (`attention_verify_wmma.gfx1151.hip`) now take head_dim as a template parameter and export `_hd128` entries next to the hd256 ones; `attention_verify_wmma_with` admits head_dim 128 and 256. Byte-identical to `attention_q8_0_flash_prefill_wmma` (`verify_attn_oracle oracle q8` with `VA_NH=16 VA_HD=128`, 139 cases; new `VA_HD` knob). Verify attention per layer at 7.7K context 3.79 ms -> 0.28 ms. DFlash stays slower than AR on this model at tau 0.2-0.8.
- **Fixed: `hipfire pull` verified a split base and its sidecars but never recorded the proof.** The pull's validity check (`existing_artifact_valid`) SHA-256-hashed an already-downloaded base, PLE sidecar, trunk overlay, expert hot set or head and discarded the result, and `download_verified` dropped the digest it had just computed while streaming. Only the retired-monolith migration wrote to the verified-artifact cache (`<home>/cache/verified-artifacts.json`), so a freshly pulled split base such as `qwen3.8:flash-next` had no proof: every repeat `hipfire pull` re-hashed the full base (about 70 GB for Flash-Next) and anything that needs a proof (e.g. the greedy MTP identity gate) refused it. A pull now records the proof (path, stat identity and digest, the same record the monolith path writes) for every artifact it downloads or finds valid, and a later validity check or pull of an unchanged file reads the proof instead of hashing. A file whose stat changed, or whose bytes do not match, still hashes and is never recorded. PLE sidecars the loader fetches on demand during a load are not recorded (no hipfire home in scope there); the next `hipfire pull` records them.
- **DeepSeek-V4 decode routed experts run through sealed MoE; `MoeSelectionBias` is the only biased-routing entry (HIPF-87, #666 G14).** The score layers' routed experts are a `SealedMoeCall` inside `Step::ExpertFfn` (`RoutedExpertsOp::Sealed`); `MoeFamily::run_bias_aware`, `MoeBiasAwareParams` and `run_moe_decode_bias_aware` are removed. Sealed decode gains `MoeSelectionBias::scores` (`MoeScores::Precomputed`: the model's `sqrt(softplus)` router scores feed the bias-aware selector, no router GEMV or sigmoid) and `MoeParams::mq2_lloyd` (`MoeMq2Lloyd`: SwiGLU clamp, atomic or expanded+combine down, native gfx1201/gfx942 backend and EP zero dummy; admits MQ2-Lloyd at any top-k up to 8). The kernel sequence is unchanged; heterogeneous `run_selected` shares the same MQ2-Lloyd helpers. DS4 seals each score layer's experts host-only from the uploaded pointer entries. Hash layers and batched prefill keep their entries. Score layers always take this path (no env switch). It landed without a DeepSeek-V4 hardware identity run on the merge side: no DS4 model was available, so only compile, unit tests (`hipfire-arch-deepseek4`, dispatch) and static review ran; the author's gfx1151 `ds4_rows_parity` rows (9 of 9 digests identical to beta) are contributor-measured, and the native gfx1201/gfx942 MQ2-Lloyd backend and EP shards were not run on hardware.
- **Flash-Next on gfx1201: decode-share lends the long-prefill scratch to the coldest resident experts' VRAM and uses the reclaimed reserve for more resident experts (default ON on admitted loads; `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_DECODE_SHARE=off` disables it).** Decode, verify and every prompt tile below 512 rows run on a dedicated 512-row scratch bank; a prompt tile of 512 rows or more runs on a scratch bank laid over a contiguous tail of cold resident experts (the donors), reading those experts through a byte-identical pinned host mirror while their device bytes are scratch. A prompt that ends leaves the tail dirty with no restore enqueued (the first token comes from the prefill head before any restore, and back-to-back prefills share one borrow); the next decode, verify, lane or sub-512-row call outside a prompt copies the whole dirtied prefix back from the mirror on the compute stream (up to 4,776 MiB on the R9700 plan; the design estimate assumes about 57 GB/s) and waits for it, so the restore is not part of time to first token but the second token pays it: after a 16K-token prompt the second token takes 65 ms instead of 23 ms (R9700, AR, measured), while TTFT matches decode-share off. `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_DECODE_SHARE_SYNC=1` restores at prompt end instead. The placement charges only the dedicated forward (resident bank, persistent token ids, speculative buffers) instead of the whole prefill scratch, so the hot-set budget grows by the difference and the plan keeps correspondingly more experts resident. A tile error takes a blocking drain-and-restore recovery, and a restore that cannot run poisons the loan so every later forward fails naming the reason. Scope: exact gfx1201, single device, the ranked hot-set tier, the compact scratch plan. It refuses (silently unless the knob was set explicitly) with expert parallelism, a `topology.pp` band, the NPU trunk, an S1 slow-link profile, a DFlash speculator, a CPU expert split (`memory.offload_exec=cpu`/`passback`, `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_D2_DEFAULT=1`), continuous batching, or a prefill chunk of 512 rows or fewer; an explicit `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_HOT_BUDGET_MIB` does not grow, so it turns `on` into `off` for that load. The measured D2 default stays off on a `fixed` / `on` decode-share load. On a sharing load the prefill chunk is final and a compact-plan symmetry refusal fails the load naming `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_DECODE_SHARE=off`. Modes for A/B work: `bind` (second expert view only), `bank` (owned test scratch), `fixed` (real donor tail, plain budget), `on` (default); developer knobs `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_DECODE_SHARE_VERIFY`, `_SYNC`, `_LOG`, `_SHADOWS`. The F16 weight shadows and the shared-expert INT8 shadows (about 1,477 MiB on Flash-Next), read only by prompt tiles of 512 rows or more, live in the start of the donor tail on `fixed` / `on` loads and are rebuilt in place at the first acquire of every borrow epoch (no resident copy, no reserve charge: under `on` that reserve becomes resident experts); `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_DECODE_SHARE_SHADOWS=0` keeps them resident. Under `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_DECODE_SHARE_VERIFY=1` the first rebuild is checked byte-for-byte against an ordinary rebuild.
  - A prompt tile reads the donors in VRAM wherever its scratch class did not overwrite them: the plan carries one BorrowPrefill expert view per prefill capacity class (1,024 rows up to the prompt chunk), the tile selects the view of the largest class its borrow epoch has used, and only the donors that class's scratch span overlaps are read through the host mirror. A short prompt therefore keeps almost the whole hot set in VRAM (on the R9700 plan, 184 of 1,918 donors for a 1,024-row class), and each class view adds one 393 KB pointer-table pair to the placement charge.
- **Fixed: greedy DDTree tree verify gave a different answer on each fresh run (HIPF-136).** After a tree verify, `move_rows_in_place` moves the accepted rows down into the committed slots (KV, GDN tape and other per-row buffers). It coalesces neighboring rows into one `(dst, src, n)` copy, and such a copy overlaps itself whenever the rows shift by less than the run length (`src - dst < n`). A device-to-device memcpy over overlapping ranges is undefined: the copy engine moves chunks in parallel, so which bytes ended up in the committed rows changed from run to run. Each run is now issued as ascending chunks of at most `src - dst` rows, which never overlap. Each chunk only overwrites rows an earlier chunk already read, so the result equals the per-row moves. On gfx1151 (`qwen3.6-35b-a3b.mq4r` + the z-lab Qwen3.6-35B-A3B DFlash draft, `HIPFIRE_DDTREE_BUDGET=16`, a 2,080-token prompt, 128 greedy tokens), 4 fresh beta processes gave 4 different outputs; with the fix, 6 of 6 match byte for byte (the PR author's run; the merge gate repeated it on gfx1201 with Qwen3.5-9B and its DFlash draft at budget 16: identical text across two fresh processes). The short prompts, chain verify and dense targets were already deterministic and stay unchanged.
- **gfx1151: sampled decode on a mixed-codec expert-slab model (`qwen3.8-flash-next-base.mq3-xts`) no longer idles the GPU for the slab layers' per-token host checks.** A sampled AR token builds its whole step program after the logits readback and the CPU sample, so the build is GPU idle time; greedy builds while the previous token still runs, which is why only sampled decode lost 6-9% against the MQ4 route. Each mixed MQ4 + W3 layer re-ran the codec admission (`expert_capabilities` table lookups) and the shape/dtype check for all 512 experts on every decode step. The admission now runs once per distinct codec (`layer_cold_codec`), and `ExpertTable` groups records by projection layout so the check covers the first record of each layout plus one dtype compare per record. On gfx1151 the idle gap before each sampled forward drops from 1.70 to 0.41 ms (MQ4 route: 0.35 ms), and the main thread's host CPU time per sampled token from 7.6 to 5.6 ms. The gap grew with host load (4.2 ms in a loaded run). Outputs are byte-identical.
- **Developer: Muse Glimmer dense tensor parallelism on the generic mesh executor, and the sandwich MLP ladders admit a TP split (#927 item 5).** The sandwich epilogue `x + post_norm(out)` cannot take a partial sum, so a TP rank now stops each sandwich sublayer at its output projection (`execute_sandwich_attention_partial`, `execute_sandwich_mlp_partial`), the splitter's `AllReduce` reduces the partial, and `execute_sandwich_epilogue` runs the single-card post-norm residual kernels on the reduced rows; the single-device ops and their launches are unchanged. `MlpLadder::SandwichWide` and the new `MlpLadder::SandwichSteps` (Glimmer's `SandwichMlpOp`, declarative only) are now `tp_shardable`. `muse_glimmer::mesh_tp` adds the plan, per-rank sharded loading (`GlimmerWeights::load_shard`) and `GlimmerTpBindings`; `muse-glimmer-30b` splits two ways (TP4 is refused: 2 KV heads). The loader still serves Glimmer on one device only. Oracle: `mesh_tp::hw_tests` (`HIPFIRE_GLIMMER_TP_MODEL`, `docs/multi-gpu.md`). Gate: physical gfx1201 TP2 on two cards, 481/481 argmax equal to the single-card run, the executor bitwise equal to the single-device rank-order oracle.
- **Strix Halo: a Flash-Next reload after the previous process exited is no longer refused for host RAM the exited process left parked in TTM's page pool.** Each daemon exit leaves its GTT pages (about 74 GiB after the stock 125 GB model, measured on gfx1151) in amdgpu's TTM page pool, outside `MemAvailable` (119.7 → 42.5 GiB) although the next GTT allocation takes them first and TTM's shrinker returns them under pressure. The pool estimate that the loader's host-RAM checks add (`expert_residency::ttm_pool_estimate`) only applied under `HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0`, which hip-bridge does not set on an APU, so the second load on the same boot failed with `MemAvailable - CMA is 28.5 GiB (plus 0.0 GiB estimated in TTM's page pool)`; it needed an `echo 2 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` between loads. The preload plan, the planned RAM/GTT upper bound and the CPU-window host check now use `ttm_pool_estimate_on(gpu)`, which counts the same estimate whenever the device is a GTT-backed unified-memory APU (`Gpu::is_gtt_backed_apu`: the device pool is larger than the carve-out). Discrete GPUs, carve-out APUs and the `hipfire fit` mirror (which already counted it) are unchanged. Three back-to-back loads without draining now load with identical placement, where the second and third were refused before.
- **`hipfire pull` no longer downloads the 305.5 MB Flash-Next trunk overlay on a host that will not apply it.** The loader applies the `.trunk-overlay` sidecar only on gfx1151 (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_TRUNK_OVERLAY=auto`), but every `hipfire pull qwen3.8:flash-next` on gfx1201 or gfx1100 fetched it anyway (wasted bandwidth and disk, no correctness effect; known issue of 0.4.3). The pull now plans and fetches it only when a detected GPU is a gfx1151 (a mixed host with one counts) or none is detected, or with `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_TRUNK_OVERLAY=1`; otherwise it prints one `Skipping Trunk overlay sidecar` line and the interactive summary omits the file. The PLE rows and the expert hot set are unchanged. Re-run `hipfire pull` after adding a gfx1151 card.
- **Swap snapshots now carry a real model fingerprint and a per-engine nonce.** `SnapshotStamp` v3 hashes the model file's length plus 64 KiB samples (start, quartiles, end) instead of using the file size as the model identity, and adds a random per-engine `instance_id`. A snapshot is only restorable by the engine that captured it; stale spill files from an older format are rejected and removed at start. `model_fingerprint` is public for tooling.
- **`/health` and `/stats` publish the multi-slot swap tier.** A `swap` object reports `tier` (`host+disk`/`host`/`disk`/`none`), live `evictions`/`restores`/`failures`, and `host_used`/`disk_used` against the effective budgets. It is configured from the resolved process policy at startup and refreshed from each `done` event (so the effective budgets replace the configured ones), so the endpoint still never waits on a model load; it is `null` on the standard route.
- **Abandoned parked sessions are swept, and the policy is configurable.** A swapped or cold session idle for `serve.multi_slot_session_ttl_secs` (default 3600; `0` disables) is closed by the next request or by the engine's idle timer (wakes at most every 30 s), and the non-resident table is capped at `serve.multi_slot_max_sessions` (default auto `max(64, 16 × slots)`), oldest first. Only a cold re-prefill can result; resident sessions are never swept. The daemon prunes pending-tool broker state for swept sessions.
- **Swap spills are written to a temp file and renamed; a failed write no longer flushes the cache.** The disk tier pre-checks evictable bytes, writes `<key>.snap.tmp`, evicts LRU entries only after that succeeds, and renames atomically. A failed unlink keeps its charge and warns instead of silently under-counting. Crash-left per-pid default swap directories are swept at startup (Linux), and an existing owned `serve.swap_dir` has group/other access removed.
- **`/metrics` publishes the swap tier.** `hipfire_swap_info{tier=...}`, `hipfire_swap_evictions`, `hipfire_swap_restores`, `hipfire_swap_failures`, and the host/disk used/budget byte gauges, from the same snapshot as `/health`.
- **`serve -d` says when swap flags were not applied.** Re-running `serve -d` against a live server prints a warning naming `--swap-host-bytes`/`--swap-disk-bytes`/`--swap-dir`, instead of silently accepting values that only a fresh daemon can use.
- **Multi-slot swap cleanup only touches spill files, and the directory is private to one daemon.** `serve.swap_dir` is operator-configurable, so the store no longer deletes the directory wholesale on start or shutdown: it removes `*.snap` files and leaves unrelated files and subdirectories untouched. The directory is created `0700`, must be owned by this user, is locked with `fs::File::try_lock` so two daemons cannot share it, and may not be a symlink; spill files are `0600` and created with `O_EXCL`, so a planted `<key>.snap` symlink is replaced rather than followed. A read-only directory warns and disables the disk tier instead of failing the load; a path that is a symlink or an existing non-directory fails the load with a clear error instead of being deleted. The default directory is now per process (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hipfire/swap/<pid>`, falling back to `$TMPDIR/hipfire-swap-<pid>`).
- **Multi-slot serve: swap host and disk budgets are configurable, and the disk tier is bounded.** `serve.swap_host_bytes`, `serve.swap_disk_bytes`, and `serve.swap_dir` add flag (`serve --swap-host-bytes`, `--swap-disk-bytes`, `--swap-dir`) and environment (`HIPFIRE_SWAP_HOST_BYTES`, `HIPFIRE_SWAP_DISK_BYTES`, `HIPFIRE_SWAP_DIR`) control. The 16 GiB host budget is now only the default; `0` disables a tier. `SwapStore` tracks disk bytes and evicts the least-recently-used spill snapshot at the ceiling; the affected session becomes Cold and re-prefills from its authoritative tokens. Defaults: 16 GiB host (unchanged) and 8 GiB disk (previously unbounded). A snapshot larger than the whole disk budget is refused *before* any eviction, so it cannot flush the cache on its way out. A session whose snapshot was evicted is re-prefilled into the same session id instead of minting a new `Cold` entry, and the resolved host/disk/dir policy plus the first park or restore failure are logged.
- **Strix Halo NPU: K = 5120 direct-BF16 stage for the qwen3.8-27b dense in-projections (kernel/program/transport level, no serving route yet; HIPF-161, #864).** The GDN in-projection (qkv 10240 + z 6144 + a 48 + b 48 = 16480 columns) and the FA in-projection (gated q 12288 + k 1024 + v 1024 = 14336) run on the existing G80 N512 program at K = 5120 (80 K64 chunks, B panel resident, one BF16 rounding after the whole K, no int32 partial combine): `gemm_g80_n512::build_panel_program_n512(rows_max, pitch, col0, k)` replaces the K6144-only `build_panel_program_out`. `npu_trunk_pack_a_bf16` gains a K5120 twin (`npu_trunk_pack_a_bf16_k5120`) and writes either A stream (`NpuBf16Layout::n512`: the N1280 four-segment 256-row-wave layout or the N512 eight-segment 512-row-wave layout); `NpuBf16Layout::validate` admits K <= 6336. `railgun::npu::trunk` gains `Shape::{DenseGdnIn, DenseFaIn}` (33 / 28 panels of 512) and sizes each A arena class and B panel from `Shape::k()`; the shipped Flash-Next pin grows by two 4 KiB placeholder pages (1,053,859,840 B, same memlock bound). Measured on gfx1151 by the contributor (the merge gate's own transport runs, 8 cases x 20 rounds all exact, were within 1-2%) (`npu-trunk-transport`, 8192 rows, exact vs whole-K int32 + `bf16_direct` every round, fclk not pinned): GDN 22.9 TOPS busy / 20.7 wall, FA 23.4 / 21.2; co-run with 16 GiB/round of GPU copies 17.8 / 15.1 and 19.5 / 16.6. Simulator: complete-arena exact on synthetic K5120 tiles at both pitches (the author also ran real qwen3.8-27b tiles; the merge gate did not). GPU emulate twin (pack + IU8 GEMM + `npu_trunk_epi_bf16`) bit-exact at K5120 at both 27B shapes (`npu_trunk_glue_check`).
- **CI repair:** refresh the settings golden, restrict native HSA diagnostic loading to Linux, and update TLS dependencies plus Tokio 1.53.3 to clear RustSec advisories. Prefill contract digest tests canonicalize JSON object keys under workspace feature unification; pinned kernel text, proofs and contract values are unchanged.
- **Fixed: the K1 MoE decode-GEMV byte oracle (`mq_i4_moe_gemv_byte_oracle`) reported FAILED on every narrow run with zero mismatches.** Since 4612a5d28 its verdict requires every row's `pass` to be true, but the narrow fixture and real-layer rows had no `pass` field. Narrow rows now carry `pass` = zero output and twin mismatches. On gfx1151 (the author's run; the merge gate ran only the oracle example tests) with the published `qwen3.8-flash-next-base.mq3-xts`, the narrow cases, real layers 0, 31 and 47, and the wide R=1–8 slab sweep (384 cells, `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SLAB_K1_C1` 0 and 1) all PASS with 0 mismatches. `docs/MODELS.md` now records the native gfx1151 quality and throughput of MQ3 XTS (W3 experts) against a trunk-matched MQ4 XTS reference (#866).
- **Flash-Next MQ6G256V2 trunk verify on gfx1201 and gfx1100: stream-split few-row kernels, byte-identical, default ON (`HIPFIRE_MQ6_ROWS_SPLIT=0` restores the incumbent rows kernels).** `gemm_mq6g256v2_f32_rows` / `_x4` at 3..=8 rows (and every 3..8-row group of a wider verify) ran one wave per weight row and re-fetched every activation row for each weight row (x traffic 5.12 R x the weight bytes). They now run `gemm_mq6g256v2_f32_rows[_x4]_split_r{R}_w{W}_s{S}`: a workgroup owns W weight rows sharing each x load, and S waves split the singleton's four accumulation streams, meeting in LDS for the unchanged `(a0 + a1) + (a2 + a3)` fold and `shfl_down` 16..1 tree; the arithmetic is the singleton DAG written with explicit `fmaf`, so every output word is bitwise the incumbent's and the one-row decode GEMV's (`mq6_rows_split_oracle`: 0 mismatches on gfx1201 and gfx1100). `(W, S)` comes from the measured table in `mq6_rows_split_config`; rows == 2 and gfx1151 keep their routes. Kernel GB/s, cold, incumbent -> split, gfx1201 (R9700): lm_head 248320x2560 N=4 350 -> 551, N=8 215 -> 343; GDN in x4 N=4 356 -> 519, N=8 187 -> 338; GDN out N=4 332 -> 481, N=8 161 -> 364; QSA in x4 N=4 351 -> 507, N=8 185 -> 330. gfx1100 (7900 XTX): GDN out N=4 370 -> 597, N=8 241 -> 456; lm_head N=4 516 -> 748, N=8 255 -> 442; GDN in N=4 511 -> 664, N=8 252 -> 412. The three gfx1201 Flash-Next route plans (`qwen3.8-flash-next`, `-base.mq4-xts`, `-base.mq2-xts`) were re-walked with the split kernels, so the native-MTP verify binds them as planned (18 `gemm_mq6g256v2_f32_rows_split_*` symbols per plan, sealed replays clean).
- **Fixed: generic (LLaMA-family) DFlash and DSpark on Qwen3 prefilled the prompt one token at a time through a stale decode body; the prompt now takes AR's batched prefill, and greedy spec output matches AR up to near-tie divergence.** `LlamaBundle::spec_advance` ran every prompt token through `forward_scratch_compute_capture`, the hand-written decode ladder (unfused GEMVs, single-block-per-head `attention_q8_0_kv`), because AR used to prefill per token. AR now prefills Qwen3 on gfx11/gfx1201 with Q8 KV through one `forward_prefill_batch` call and decodes through the lowered body (fused projections, tiled Q8 flash decode), so spec prefill matched neither AR's speed nor its KV. The spec prefill now shares AR's gate (`llama::llama_batched_prefill_eligible`, moved from `hipfire-generate`; widened to every LLaMA-family arch by the batched-prefill entry above) and takes `forward_prefill_batch_capture` there, and `forward_scratch_compute_capture` (the per-token spec path: other prompts, 1-3 row verify blocks, the one-token step after a spec retire) runs the lowered decode body unless `HIPFIRE_FORWARD_LOWERED=0`. Qwen3-8B mq4 on gfx1151, 7,741-token prompt, 512 greedy tokens: DFlash (`qwen3-8b-dflash.hfq`) prefill 538 s -> 13.1 s and decode 7.4 -> 20.8 tok/s (the spec-retire policy hands the request to AR after 32 low-acceptance cycles); DSpark sidecar prefill 537 s -> 13.4 s, decode 5.1 -> 11.8 tok/s; AR 14.5-15.3 s / 38 tok/s. On gfx1151 DFlash and DSpark text now equals AR's at 51 / 1,896 / 3,750 / 7,741-token prompts and on a cached second turn (beta diverged at 1,896 and 7,741); on gfx1201 (`qwen3-8b.hf4`, one 1,970-token prompt, 128 tokens) the merge gate saw byte-identical output, and on gfx1100 the answer still diverges from AR mid-answer at a near-tie (margin not measured; beta crashed there in prefill with HIP 700). The DFlash cycle itself still costs ~170 ms at 2K and ~280 ms at 8K context against a 22-26 ms AR token, so it stays slower than AR at this drafter's acceptance (tau 0.2-0.8 on these prompts).
- **Fixed: Gemma 4 EAGLE draft acceptance and `logprobs` depended on the previous request in the process (HIPF-129).** The draft head queries at the pending token's position and attends the target's last sliding/full cache slot through that position, but the target has not written that row yet, so the draft read a stale row: whatever the last verify or the previous request left there. The same greedy request reported τ 2.268 (56 rounds) as the first request after load and 2.442 (52 rounds) when repeated; tokens stayed equal, but sampled `logprobs` moved by up to 0.055 because the verify batch shapes changed. The draft head now attends that row only when the target's last forward wrote it (a verify row past the accepted prefix), as HF's `SinglePositionMultiTokenCandidateGenerator` does with the target K/V cut to the committed length; otherwise it attends through the position before (`SandwichAttentionOp::attend_through`). On gfx1151 (`gemma4-12b.mq4` + `gemma4-12b-assistant.q8f16.hfq`, `HIPFIRE_GEMMA4_EAGLE=1`) five repeats of a greedy request now report τ 2.268 / 56 rounds each, interleaved with another prompt, and three repeats of a seeded sampled request report identical τ, rounds and `logprobs`; committed tokens are unchanged. The merge gate re-checked repeat-request tau equality on gfx1201 and gfx1100 (2.953 both times).
- **Fixed: DeepSeek-V4 MQ2R prefill on gfx1151 left the O-LoRA `wo_a` output of half the prompt tokens unwritten, so prefill logits depended on what earlier work left in the scratch pool (HIPF-93).** The grouped E8-SoA WMMA launchers (`gemm_mfp4g32_e8_soa_grouped_wmma`, its `_b2` sibling, and the gfx1201 `_gfx1201_f16` variant) sized `grid.y` as `batch.div_ceil(64)` while their kernels cover 16 (B1, gfx1201) or 32 (B2) tokens per block, the same copy-paste 0e0ad47b4 fixed in the dense launchers. With the B2 route DeepSeek-V4 takes above 16 rows, tokens 32-63 of every 64 read stale `wo_a_out_batch`: zeros from fresh pool memory in the first prefill of a process, leftover decode/verify data afterwards. On gfx1151 (`deepseek-v4-flash-0731.mq2r`, 2,300-token prompt, B 1024) three prefills in one process gave logits digests `b193ad8b` / `c57d9cbf` / `c0a5bd65` (argmax 65 / 11910 / 35551); they now all give `63b0d515` (argmax 11), byte-identical across fresh processes. Prefill numerics change, and the grouped `wo_a` stage now does the full work its earlier timings skipped. `bench_e8_soa_correctness` checks both gfx1151 grouped variants at B=100 against NaN-poisoned output (`HIPFIRE_E8_GROUPED_PREFILL_ONLY=1`); the merge gate ran `bench_e8_soa_correctness` on gfx1201 (NaN-poisoned output, unwritten = 0 at B = 17 / 33 / 63 / 65 / 100 / 130; beta fails B = 100 with unwritten = 69632), but no DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end run was made on gfx1201.
- **Strix Halo (gfx1151) Qwen3.5-9B MQ4 DFlash: the 16-row verify and draft GEMMs over MQ4G256 (v1) / HFQ4G256 weights take the XLDS kernels, byte-identical, verify 52.5 → 38.9 ms per cycle, DFlash decode +27 % at 2K (HIPF-159; `HIPFIRE_GFX1151_XLDS=0` restores the base kernels).** The gfx1151 XLDS GEMMs (4 waves x 16 rows per block, the X slab staged in LDS once per block) covered only MQ4G256V2 and Q8_0, so `qwen3.5-9b.mq4` ran its verify gate_up / qkvza / qkv / residual (and the 4-bit batched lm_head) through the one-wave `gemm_*_hfq4g256_wmma{,_ldscoop_nosync,_k2}` kernels. The module `gemm_mq4g256v2_wmma_gfx1151_xlds` now also carries `gemm_{gate_up,qkvza,qkv}_hfq4g256_wmma_gfx1151_xlds` and `gemm_hfq4g256_residual_wmma_gfx1151_xlds`: the same main loop with the v1 header (one f32 (scale, zero) per group, cast to f16 as the base kernels do), taken by exact gfx1151 at 1..=16 rows and K % 256 == 0 (not when `HIPFIRE_GATE_UP_VARIANT` / `HIPFIRE_WO_WMMA_VARIANT` pins a kernel). Every output is the base kernel's WMMA chain, so outputs are bitwise the base's (`test_mq4v2_xlds_gfx1151`, now both formats at the 27B and 9B shapes). Other arches are unchanged.
  - Measured (Strix Halo, `qwen3.5-9b.mq4` + `qwen35-9b-dflash-mq4.hfq`, daemon protocol, greedy, 512 tokens, interleaved beta / this x2, shared box): DFlash 2K 45.5 → 57.9 tok/s (cycle 74.5 → 58.6 ms, AR 47.0), 4K 35.8 → 42.7 (cycle 94.1 → 78.9 ms, AR 46.1); every output hash is identical with the XLDS kernels on and off (2K and 4K); 9B DFlash output differs from AR on this box with or without XLDS (pre-existing on gfx1151). Kernel level (16 rows): gate_up 447 → 272 µs, qkvza 316 → 94, down 182 → 115, lm_head (248320 x 4096) 3.94 → 2.63 ms. At 4K DFlash still trails AR: the verify and draft attention costs (HIPF-123) remain.
- **Qwen3.5-9B DFlash on gfx1151: the verify attention takes the VerifyAttn twin and the draft attention a key-split kernel; 2K 45.7 -> 59.6 tok/s, 4K 36.0 -> 56.5 tok/s (`qwen3.5-9b.mq4` + `qwen35-9b-dflash-mq4.hfq`, AR 47), output bytes unchanged against the previous build.** The gfx1151 VerifyAttn twin (`attention_verify_wmma_with`) admitted only GQA 6 (27B, Flash-Next); its kernels now take the group as an argument and admit GQA 4 (16 q / 4 kv heads), byte-identical to `attention_q8_0_flash_prefill_wmma` (`verify_attn_oracle oracle q8` with `VA_NH=16`, 139 cases). Verify per cycle 52 -> 42 ms at 2K, 62 -> 42 ms at 4K. The draft's full-attention layers (`AttnFullF32`, B 16, head_dim 128) ran `attention_dflash_wmma_n64_f32`: one 2-wave workgroup per head (32 workgroups, the second wave idle at B 16) walking every key with each K/V load waited on alone, 1.4 ms per layer at 2K and 7.4 ms at 8K. On gfx1151 that tile now runs `attention_dflash_wmma_kvsplit_gfx1151`: 8 waves per (head, 16-row tile) split the keys, stage K and V^T through LDS with every load of a tile in flight, and merge their softmax states once; 50 us at 2K, 0.6 ms at 8K. It is not byte-identical to N64 (another f32 summation order; `test_attention_dflash` vs the CPU reference, max 3e-5); tau and output are unchanged on the 2K/4K prompts. Draft per cycle 20.4 -> 12.7 ms at 2K, 31.3 -> 15.1 ms at 4K. Other archs keep N64.
- **railgun: certified conditional nodes, IF and bounded WHILE on a device-written ControlWord (#867, gfx1151).** `KernelProgram::add_conditional` / `bounded_while` take two lowerings. `KernelGuard` keeps the tape unchanged: every body node is a guarded kernel whose no-op path railgun-cert certifies per code object (`railgun_cert::guard_flag`, new optional receipt field `guard_flag`: the entry block loads the flag through kernarg +0, compares it with zero and branches to a lone `s_endpgm`). `CpSkip` wraps the body in `COND_EXEC` (PM4 0x22, new `Gfx10Pm4CommandBuffer::begin_cond_exec` / `end_cond_exec`) behind `RELEASE_MEM` + `WAIT_REG_MEM`, and is admitted on gfx1151 only (`plan::cp_skip_admitted`); gfx12 compute `COND_EXEC` has no hardware receipt and is refused. The hazard planner treats a skipped body as executed, and coverage from boundaries inside a CP-skipped body does not outlive it. New PM module `kernels/railgun_guard_pm_gfx1151.co` (`railgun_guard_add_pm`, `railgun_guard_step_pm`, `railgun_flag_set_pm`; M7 clean). `railgun/examples/cond_probe.rs` checks flag set and flag clear byte for byte against the host-branched program on gfx1151 (2000 trials per arm, 0 mismatches; the ungated negative control differs on every clear trial). No runtime route builds conditionals yet; the recorded-tape (gfx12) lowering refuses CP-skip ops.
- **The NPU co-processor is a generic heterogeneous stage in `hipfire_runtime::coproc` (#864, slice 1); the Flash-Next NPU trunk runs on it, byte-identical.** The op-level stage map (per layer kind, which input-projection families the NPU may own; mixer core, recurrent/KV state, residual, FFN and head stay on the GPU), the EP-like ownership table over whole family groups, the `bf16_direct` stage numerics contract, the schema-4 calibration, the crossover planner with its live rate scales and max-window budget, and the layer-major chunk-pair schedule with its dependency edges moved out of the Qwen4 module into the runtime. Flash-Next declares `npu_trunk::FLASH_NEXT` (36 GDN + 12 QSA layers, K = 2560, groups qkv / zab / q / kvidx) and its pair executor iterates the shared schedule. Calibration files, planner goldens, plans and outputs are unchanged. At open the map is checked against the loaded model (layer count per kind, K = hidden size); a mismatch leaves the route off with that reason. `hipfire_runtime::coproc` replaces the `npu_trunk::{Calibration, plan, select_families, RateEstimator, ...}` re-exports for out-of-crate callers (`hipfire calibrate-npu-trunk`, `hipfire doctor --npu`).
- **A3B `.mq4rs` decode on gfx1201: the routed MQ4G128V2 down is one fused launch and the shared-expert k512 GEMV runs two rows per wave, both byte-identical, default ON (`HIPFIRE_MOE_NINEPATH=0` / `HIPFIRE_MQ4V2_K512_R2=0` restore the previous kernels).** The qwen3.5 MoE T=1 decode of a qt53 routed down (published `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-mq4rs`) ran four launches per layer (`silu_mul_f32`, `mq_rotate_x_128_v2`, `gemv_mq4g128v2_moe_down_top10_indexed_batched_expanded`, `moe_down_combine_k8_batched`). The new `gemv_mq4g128v2_moe_ninepath_d4` forms `silu(gate) * up`, the qt53 FWHT128 rotation (in registers, the lane that rotates elements 4l..4l+3 is the lane that dots them), the eight routed MQ4G128V2 down GEMVs, the ascending-slot weighted combine and the residual accumulate in one launch (single owner per output row, no atomics); the dispatch skips the Activation stage for it and keeps the four-launch sequence for T>1, other arches, a BF16 recipe, a specialized route, and `HIPFIRE_MOE_NINEPATH=0`. `HIPFIRE_MOE_NINEPATH=0` also turns off the existing d4 ninepath routes of the other routed dtypes. The shared-expert `gemv_mq4g256v2_residual_sigmoid_scaled_k512` (12.6 us/layer) gains a two-row-per-wave twin `..._k512_r2` (2.5 us/layer) with the geometry of the mq4r `gemv_hfq4g256_residual_sigmoid_scaled_gpu`. Both pin the FMA orientation of the kernels they replace explicitly and are verified bit-for-bit against them on randomized inputs (`cargo test -p rdna-compute --release --test mq4rs_decode_kernels_hw -- --ignored`).
- **gfx1201 MQ4G256V2 MLP gate+up verify GEMM loops over row tiles on a half-size grid, byte-identical, default ON (`HIPFIRE_GFX12_GATE_UP_TILE_LOOP=0` restores one block per row tile).** `gemm_gate_up_mq4g256v2_wmma_gfx12` (N 1..=16, the plain one-tile arm) now iterates `for (tile = blockIdx.x; tile < row_tiles; tile += gridDim.x)` with the body unchanged (same arithmetic, rounding, accumulation and reduction order); with grid x equal to the row-tile count it is exactly the old kernel. Both gfx1201 launchers of it, `gemm_gate_up_hfq4g256_mq4v2` and the F16-producer entry `gemm_gate_up_mq4g256v2_wmma_f16` (DFlash / MTP verify), size grid x as `ceil(row_tiles / t)`, `t = ceil(row_tiles / (CUs * 32))` (2 SIMD x 16 resident 76-VGPR waves per CU, R9700 64 CUs = 2048 slots); the other launch sites keep grid x = row tiles. The 27B MLP (17408 + 17408 rows, K 5120) had 2176 blocks for 2048 slots, so 128 tiles ran as a nearly empty second wave; it now runs 1088 blocks of two tiles. Kernel, cold on the R9700, median of 5 x 100 launches: 403 -> 575 GB/s at N=1, 405 -> 559 at N=2, 417 -> 555 at N=4, 464 -> 552 at N=8, 490 -> 535 at N=16. Qwen3.8-27B mq4-xts DFlash decode on the R9700 (`hipfire bench --spec dflash`, 128 tokens, 3 fresh processes per arm, interleaved, median): code 291.8 -> 314.7 tok/s (+7.8%), prose 58.7 -> 60.5 (+3.1%). `gate_up_tiles_oracle` (lab) compares ON vs OFF through both entries over 2 seeds, N in {1,2,3,4,5,8,16}, the 27B shape plus non-multiple-of-16 row totals, tiles == slots and slots + 1, 4097 tiles (t = 3) and K 256 / 512: 46966920 output words, 0 mismatches, NaN-sentinel guards and inputs intact; 27B serve AR and DFlash greedy transcripts are byte-identical to the incumbent.
- **The #666 device-mesh runner respects a fabric device reservation instead of escaping it (harness only, no product path).** `scripts/device_mesh_matrix.py` now maps a numeric device selector to the inherited `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` tokens (a `--devices 0,1` serving row no longer resolves `[hardware].devices="0,1"` to physical cards outside the reservation), probes each singleton device with its reserved ROCr token plus HIP 0 (the daemon no longer refuses the `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=pair requires HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES="0,1"` cardinality mismatch before GPU init), and substitutes the row env into negative probes so they go through the operator's launcher like the positives do. `git.dirty` ignores the in-tree `target-fi/` fault-inject build dir, and `pp_qwen35_reset_rolls_back_and_recovers` no longer overwrites the inherited ROCr UUIDs with numeric ordinals.
- **Device-mesh G5 fixture is now the canonical `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-mq4p` (harness-only; no production change).** `qwen3.6:35b-a3b` resolves to `qwen3.6-35b-a3b.mq4p` in `registry/v1.json`, so the G5 rows (`g5-production-sealed-moe-run`, `g5-production-sealed-moe-fault`), the `g1-route-oracles-nonllama` Qwen3.6 MoE fixture, the `matrix.json` `fixture_lock` and `route_oracle_single.rs` now pin that file (19757996288 bytes, sha256 `8eb3be6912aa9db2dcc89c3233b05ccdfe81a84a8d6ef43202f2098d7f2fc78f`, HF commit `04bc60b0a70ce4029cf963681836eab2e7027d6d`) instead of `qwen3.6-35b-a3b.mq4r` (`4685c140…`). The lock totals 9 files, 66.9 GB.
- **Flash-Next EP rank execution and the owner-routed row exchange are shared runtime infrastructure (#861 slice 2; numerics unchanged).** The per-rank worker pool that fans every replicated call out to the peer bundles — one worker thread + stream per rank, rank 0 on the caller's thread, first-failure poisoning, barrier abort and host-result agreement — moved out of `hipfire-arch-qwen4` into the generic `hipfire_runtime::rank_pool::RankPool`. The owner-routed exchange is now expressed as an explicit schedule from the sealed plans rather than an all-reduce: the owner-routed execution string turns each routed group's collective rows into a copy-only `OwnerRowGather` (never an `AllReduce{Ep}`), and `hipfire_runtime::sealed_moe::OwnerRoutedEpSchedule` derives the ranks/stride/hidden geometry the copy-only row gather needs, cross-checked against the load config before peer access. Kernels, route thresholds, quantization, state transactions and combine order are unchanged.
- **Flash-Next on gfx1201: the QSA prefill q / k RMSNorm + RoPE rides the int8 PM GEMM epilogue, byte-identical, default ON (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_NORM_EPI=0` restores the unfused launches).** The q (interleaved q-gate rows) and k projections that take the MQ6G256V2 int8 route now run the `gemm_mq6g256v2_mmq_i8_pm_set_nr_gfx1201_t256x128` entry, which writes the normed, weighted and rotated q / k heads (the gate half stays the plain GEMM output) from a per-call RoPE table (`indexed_attention_rope_table_f32`, built with the model's yarn from the chunk's start position); the two standalone `indexed_attention_norm_rope_f32_batched` launches of the prefill's batched branch are skipped for the projections that ran fused. Eager, F32 output, head_dim 256, rotary_dim 64, `M % 256 == 0` only; recording/capture, the NPU arena path and an installed QSA projection hook keep the unfused chain. The index-q norm is unchanged. New oracle `qsa_norm_epi_oracle`.
- **Flash-Next on gfx1201: the MoE shared expert prefill runs on INT8 (int8 x int8 WMMA) instead of F16 WMMA, default ON (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SHARED_INT8=0` restores the F16 route). NUMERIC, KLD-gated, not byte-identical.** At `route_rows >= 512` the shared expert's gate/up/down (BF16 weights, hidden 2560, intermediate 640) ran F16 WMMA through F16 shadows: gate/up GEMMs, `shared_expert_activation_bf16_f32` (F32 gate/up/hidden round trips), the hidden's F32 -> F16 conversion and the down GEMM, ~190 ms per 16384-token pass (the router and selector stay on their F16 group). Now: a model-lifetime INT8 shadow of the three weights built on first use (FWHT-rotated like the activations, A8 `block_i8_128` per 128 K, gate/up rows interleaved in groups of four so the SwiGLU is lane-local; 5.2 MB per layer, 239 MiB at 48 layers, freed with the other weight caches), the A8 blocks of the normalized activations emitted as a third output of the fused MoE front producer (`mq_rotate_x_i4_f16out_i8`: the F16 X and IU4 sidecar bytes are `mq_rotate_x_i4_f16out`'s, so no extra read of the F32 rows), one gate/up GEMM (`qwen4_shared_i8_gate_up_silu_bf16`, `kernels/src/qwen4_shared_i8_gemm.gfx12.hip`: the MQ6 INT8 GEMM's 128 x 128 tile with signed x signed `v_wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu8`, an exactly convertible int32 per K128 block folded as `fma(RN(d_w * d_x), C, acc)`, and the BF16-recipe SwiGLU `bf16(silu(bf16(g)) * bf16(u))` fused into its epilogue, so the F32 gate/up outputs and the activation launch are gone), one FWHT-128 + A8 producer for the hidden that also applies the selector sigmoid (`qwen4_shared_rot128_i8`), and the down GEMM (`qwen4_shared_i8_down_set_f32`) into the F32 rows the BF16 scaled add / HC row fold already consume. Operands per K are halved (A8 plus 6% scales vs F16) and the F16 conversion of the hidden, the F32 gate/up/hidden round trips and one launch are removed. Per layer at 16384 rows (hipEvent, card B, `examples/shared_i8_bench`): F16 chain 2480 us -> 1322 us with the A8 riding the front (gate/up GEMM 703 us at 153 TOPS, down 425 us at 127 TOPS, hidden producer 63 us, front +108 us), i.e. -1158 us/layer = -55.6 ms per 48-layer pass; DRAM-ideal traffic 545 -> 321 MB per layer (-10.8 GB per pass); the multiply-accumulate work (161 GFLOP per layer) now runs at the iu8 rate. *Accuracy.* GPU oracle (`examples/shared_i8_oracle`, receipts `fn-10k/shared-i8-receipts/`): every kernel is bit-identical to a host model (shadow planes vs the production rotations + the A8 quantizer contract, both GEMMs' F32/BF16 outputs vs the exact integer + fold model, the hidden producer and selector, the fused front's three outputs vs `mq_rotate_x_i4_f16out` and `mq6_i8_prepare_x`) at 512 to 4099 rows. The route error against an f64 model of the exact BF16 recipe is 1.5e-2 relative RMS of the shared-expert rows (gate/up alone 1.2e-2, down alone 9.0e-3) against 1.4e-3 for the F16 route, from per-128 int8 operands. *KLD (AGENTS.md section 5, prefill scoring, paired per-sequence 95% CI of candidate minus base).* code24: +0.0050 [-0.0005, +0.0106]; WT2: +0.0014 [-0.0051, +0.0080]; both pass the bar (`lo <= 0 or hi <= +0.010`); the base `.kldseq` hashes are the expected beta ones (`88038c3b...`, `22e45981...`). *Serve (greedy, long prompts).* NIAH (5,489-token prompt): transcripts identical to beta in AR and MTP; the ~11k-token prose prompt diverges from the first token (numeric lever) but stays coherent, AR and MTP agree, MTP tau 2.59 -> 2.49. *Perf.* pp16384 (16384 chunk, compact scratch, card B, 3 fresh processes per arm): 6459.1 -> 6604.5 tok/s (2536.6 -> 2480.7 ms/pass, -55.9 ms, +2.25%; 299 W median, sclk 2447 -> 2416 MHz); MTP `--spec auto` decode on the short committed prompts (route inactive below 512 rows) flat (prose 45.30 -> 45.20, code 67.70 -> 67.30 tok/s, within process spread); Redline shows only the pre-existing prefill128 instability. `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SHARED_INT8=0` restores the F16 route. *Admission.* The INT8 shadows (48 x 5.22 MB = 239 MiB) are their own VRAM reserve census term (`INT8 shared-expert shadows`, charged like the F16 weight shadows: exact gfx1201, route on, `route_rows >= 512`; 0 with `=0`), so expert placement cannot spend that memory.

## v0.4.3.1 — 2026-10-24

- **Fixed: Qwen3.8-27B native MTP on gfx1201 refused the MQ4 sidecar's fused kernels as outside the planned route.** The typed MTP layer program uses plain RMSNorm/SwiGLU rotation, fused QKV/gate-up and residual GEMV kernels independently of the trunk's AWQ scales; the sealed 27B native-MTP plan now includes that head closure. AR routing and the seal's rejection of unplanned kernels are unchanged.
- **A3B `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-mq4rs` decodes on retained Redline PM4 by default on gfx1201.** The symmetric-expert A3B file (`qwen3_5_moe`, `.mq4rs`) ran the HIP graph at 156 tok/s because `retained_redline_default` admitted only `.mq4r` and Qwen3.5 dense; it now takes the same retained PM4 default as `.mq4r` on exact gfx1201 with pp=tp=1 and no drafter (MTP-loaded requests, CPU offload, and `replay.backend = "hip"` are unchanged). Greedy ids are identical to the HIP route; tg128 ~232 tok/s at ctx 128, ~217 at 8K. Selection is by file extension, marked deprecated since 0.4.0 / removal 0.5.0 like the `.mq4r` route.
- **Registry: `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-mq4rs` now declares the `qwen3.6-35b-a3b.mtp` sidecar** every other `qwen3.6:35b-a3b*` entry carries, so `--spec mtp` finds the head. `speculation.mtp=auto` still resolves to AR for Qwen3.5.

## v0.4.2.1 — 2026-10-14

- **Strix Halo NPU trunk: the built-in calibration now applies on any Halo kernel and NPU firmware.** `npu_trunk=auto` armed only when the compiled-in Halo calibration matched the host exactly, including the kernel release, NPU firmware and GPU PCI address of the machine it was measured on, so every stock-kernel Halo logged `npu-trunk: off (calibration key mismatch: kernel.uname_release)` and served GPU-only. For the built-in calibration those three fields are now advisory: when any differs, it is used with its margin raised to 0.05 (the pipe must be predicted at least 5% faster than GPU-only, since the timings were measured on a different kernel/firmware), and the load logs `npu-trunk: built-in calibration measured on <kernel>/<fw>, this host <kernel>/<fw>; using it with margin 0.05`. Arch, build, model-index hash, epilogue and trunk route stay strict, and a user calibration file stays fully strict. Output is exact on either route; the calibration only chooses between them. First-load self-calibration is planned.
- **The NPU trunk calibration identity is pinned to `hipfire-0.4.2:npu-trunk-bf16-rowmajor-v1`.** It no longer derives from the crate version: it names the NPU serving numerics/transport, which a release bump does not change. Deriving it from the crate version would have orphaned the shipped Halo calibrations and left `npu_trunk=auto` GPU-only on 0.4.2.1.
- **Flash-Next: tool-call turns in the history replay the tokens the model emitted.** A follow-up turn whose history held an assistant tool call rendered that turn through the chat template. That stays a strict extension of the committed conversation only while the model's output is exactly the template's own canonical tokenization; a different BPE split of the emitted text, or spacing the template rewrites around `<tool_call>`, made the follow-up miss its live continuation and re-prefill the whole conversation. Qwen4 now replays a cached tool-call turn as the whole body the model emitted (reasoning, prose and every `<tool_call>` block), as it already did for plain turns, so the follow-up no longer depends on that. On Strix Halo with canonical model output both builds already continued in place: a 7-request tool chain and a 32K-context tool append reused every committed token before and after, with identical output. The cache key covers each call's name and arguments, and prose the client echoes with the calls must equal the emitted prose (empty content is accepted); an edited turn misses and falls back to the template render. Session-exact like every live continuation. Other model families keep the template render (`ToolTurnSplice::Envelopes`). `HIPFIRE_SESSION_CACHE_BYTES=0` turns reuse off.
- **Flash-Next session reuse is traceable per request.** With `HIPFIRE_QWEN_CACHE_TRACE=1`, every Qwen4 request (native MTP and AR) prints `[qwen4-session] route=… prompt=… prior=… lcp=… reused=… new=… source=live|snapshot|cold`: the previous turn's committed history, its common prefix with the new canonical prompt, and what the session cache reused. When the prompt diverges from that history, `[qwen4-session ids]` shows the token ids around the first difference. Host-side only; off by default.
- Changelog correction: the Flash-Next session cache's resident snapshot for deep appends past the pool budget (#847, HIPF-46, @fivetide; +512 tokens on a 256K prefix 4.7 → 197.5 tok/s on Strix Halo) shipped in v0.4.2 but was missing from its notes.

## v0.4.3 — 2026-10-24
- **Flash-Next on gfx1201: the default prefill chunk is 16384 rows under the compact forward scratch (4096 under the full plan).** Every chunk re-streams the host-tier routed experts, so the larger chunk raises long-prompt prefill; the compact phase-arena scratch at 16384 rows costs about as much VRAM as the full plan did at 4096, but fewer routed experts stay resident than at a 4096-row compact chunk, so decode is slower. `HIPFIRE_PREFILL_CHUNK_ROWS=4096` restores the previous chunk for decode-heavy use. Admission steps down 8192/4096/2048/1536 when the chunk does not fit. Prefill and decode are byte-identical either way.
- **The CPU-only launcher ABI gate resolves binding-free `match` selectors by their returned values, including tuple/enum patterns.** The dense-GDN v1/v2 producer selector introduced in `94a4e5ac3e` made the scanner mistake `DType` in a pattern for an unresolved kernel-name origin, failing closed despite the GDN launch being outside the MoE catalogue. Every returned arm remains checked; regression coverage rejects a bad ABI in each arm and an unresolved arm value. Value-binding matches retain conservative origin tracing; no launcher exemption or catalogue reduction was added.
- **Flash-Next on gfx1201: the compact forward scratch is the default for symmetric-IU4 packed artifacts too (the canonical `mq4-xts` split base and the `gptq3` monolith), at the unchanged 4096-row default chunk.** It was the default only for expert-slab artifacts (`mq3-xts`, `mq2-xts`); symmetric packed files needed `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_COMPACT_SCRATCH=1`. On the split base the forward scratch drops 4388 -> 1270 MiB and three more routed expert layers stay in VRAM (14 -> 17 on a 32 GB R9700). The GPU symmetry check at attach stays the authority: an asymmetric file is re-planned Full. `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_COMPACT_SCRATCH=0` keeps the full plan. Storage only: prefill and decode are byte-identical.
- **Fixed: Flash-Next failed to load on a narrow-link discrete card (gfx1100, 24 GB) with `qwen4: settled placement has no owning margin/stage charge`.** The shared placement owner added with the fixed-row-tile verify work requires every settled single-rank Flash-Next placement to carry the margin/stage charge that owns its bytes, but the admitted slow-link (S1) arm placed the profile's resident layers without recording any charge, so the load that selects S1 by default (a measured sub-16 GB/s host link, e.g. the 7900 XTX at 7.1 GB/s H2D) refused before allocating, with D2 on or off. The S1 profile now carries the placement charges it was admitted under (`SlowlinkProfile::charges`: the 512 MiB safety margin, no dedicated stage, and the S1 census) and the shared decision returns them for the admitted arm; the refusal for a settled placement no owner charged is unchanged. CPU test: `slowlink_admitted_gfx1100_placement_settles_with_the_profiles_own_charges`.
- **Registry: `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-mq4rs` (file `qwen3.6-35b-a3b-d53.mq4rs`, 18.70 GB / 17.42 GiB) is published in `hipfire-models/qwen3.6-35b-a3b`.** It is the symmetric-expert A3B file behind the 0.4.3 A3B prefill numbers: routed gate/up are symmetric MQ4G256V2 (qt44) and routed down is symmetric MQ4G128V2 (qt53), built with `hipfire-quantize --moe-expert-down mq4g128v2-symmetric`; SHA-256 `8806a742…1894` is pinned. It loads on gfx1201 only, where it takes the int4-activation expert prefill (pp16000 18,587.9 tok/s on one R9700; WT2 KLD vs the native-F32 parent 0.129 against 0.206 for `.mq4r`, 32 × 512 windows, q8 KV, prefill-whole); other GPUs refuse the load unless `HIPFIRE_MOE_SYM_IU4=0` accepts the qt53 F32 prefill fallback (about 5× slower than the IU4 route on gfx1201: 2,735 vs 543 ms at pp4096). No MTP sidecar is registered for it. `registry_gen.py` learns the `mq4rs` quant suffix; `.mq4r` entries are unchanged.
- **Flash-Next gfx1201 route plans (monolithic, split MQ4 XTS, base MQ2 XTS) re-walked for the default row-fold / GDN-i8 / MoE-front / grouped-down / int8 MQ6 routes.** The open plans listed kernels the new default-on levers replaced (`mq_rotate_x_i4`, `qwen4_moe_rotate128_i4`, `gemm_mq6g256v2_mmq_i8_gfx12`, `qwen4_mq6_x4_pm_gfx1201`, ...), so a sealed replay refused the real default route and an open load compiled the new kernels lazily after `ready`. The plans now carry `hc_row_fold`, `fn_gdn_dense_gate_i8`, `mq_rotate_x_i4_f16out` and the embedded `qwen4_moe_down_gp_pm_gfx1201`; the registry resolves that embedded image. `route_plan_build.py` leaves the fabric admission token and `HIPFIRE_TORCH_*` host paths out of its walk receipts. The base MQ2 XTS plan (`qwen3.8-flash-next-base.mq2-xts`, sha256 `e2ba7474…8e57`, re-pulled from `hipfire-models/qwen3.8-flash-next` after the original walk copy was removed) is re-walked the same way on the current beta (AR 637 + native MTP 230 requests, max_seq 131072, `HIPFIRE_ROUTE_PLAN=0`, empty private kernel cache) and now lists AR 51 HIP + 10 embedded modules (146 symbols) and native MTP 59 HIP + 10 embedded (175 symbols), with `hc_row_fold`, `fn_gdn_dense_gate_i8` and the embedded `moe_rotate_i4_pm_gfx1201` added (the registry's embedded-image table now resolves it) and the replaced kernels dropped.
- **Flash-Next on gfx1201: the load path no longer scans routed headers on the CPU; the GPU symmetry check decides the compact scratch plan, with a Full fallback.** The compact plan used to be chosen before expert placement from a CPU scan of every routed group header (~64 GB of mmap touches: 8 s warm, 229-310 s on a cold page cache). The aggregate route now selects compact optimistically (artifact assumed symmetric; device, flag and profile terms unchanged), and the exact proof that already ran at every load (`qwen4 symmetric IU4 MoE: V/N layers verified symmetric`) is the authority: when it verifies fewer than all routed layers, the compact attach returns `Qwen4GpuForwardError::CompactUnverified` after releasing its scratch and layers, and `attach_forward` re-plans the Full scratch at the largest chunk rung that fits the free device memory (`qwen4 forward scratch: compact plan refused by the GPU symmetry check (V/N layers verified); re-planned Full at R rows`). The S1 slow-link selector still uses the cached header verdict. Developer knob `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_COMPACT_FORCE_UNVERIFIED=1` forces the refusal for testing without changing per-layer routes.
- **Flash-Next on gfx1201: the routed-expert symmetry scan verdict is cached per model file, so the ~13 s scan is paid once per file (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SYM_VERDICT_CACHE=0` disables it).** The compact forward-scratch selector and the symmetric-IU4 window route read every routed trunk payload byte (`artifact::routed_headers_symmetric`) on each load, and one load could scan twice. The verdict now lives in `<HIPFIRE_HOME>/cache/qwen4-sym-verdicts.json`, keyed by canonical path and valid only while the file's stat key (device, inode, size, mtime), the scan version and a digest of the routed tensor names, shapes and byte ranges all match; an in-process memo makes a second scan in one load free. Only completed scans are stored (atomic, best-effort writes; a corrupt file is a miss; an overlay artifact always scans). The loader logs `qwen4 symmetric IU4 verdict: cached (<path>)` on a hit and `... scanned in X.X s, cached (<path>)` on a miss, and the `qwen4_symmetry_scan` load phase still wraps the call, so `load_phases` shows the saving.
- **Flash-Next gfx1201 compact forward scratch: step-local buffers of the GDN, QSA, HC, PLE, MoE and embedding steps share one phase arena; 16384-row scratch 8520 -> 5248 MiB, freeing VRAM for resident experts (byte-identical).**
- **PeaceMaker LDS bounds follow conditional early exits and independently derived epilogue addresses.** The checker mistook the gfx1151 Q8 lane-row tiles' post-refusal setup for K-loop redefinitions, then rejected an epilogue's reuse of a global-address register for a fresh thread-id-derived LDS address. Conditional branches directly to `s_endpgm` preserve entry-path evaluation, and local expressions are replayed without carrying loop state; unknown addresses and allocation bounds remain checked. Generated assembly and shipped kernels are unchanged.
- **`.rip` scripts can compose all of `qwen4_moe_sym` (MQ4, gfx1201), and `pm_loop --kernel qwen4_moe_sym --rip` times every entry.** `qwen4_moe_sym::blocks` (NT4/NT8) and `qwen4_moe_sym::nt1_blocks` (NT1) expose builder-level blocks (prologue runs, the run walk, a fold's head and per-tile body, the loads, descriptor steps, trip counter, epilogue runs, SwiGLU) and `Instruction`-returning compares and LDS accesses; the committed twin `peacemaker-isa/src/kernels/qwen4_moe_sym.rip` writes the exits, the run walk loop, each tile's liveness branch, **where every wait sits**, the K-loop and tail order, and the `gate_up` LDS hand-off (the gate waves' `ds_store`s, the up waves' `ds_load`s, `wg.handoff`) as script statements, and re-emits `qwen4_moe_sym::emit` / `emit_down_gp` byte for byte (`s_text` and proof) for `gate_up`, `down` at NT1/NT4/NT8 and `down_gp_nt4|nt8`. The Rust generators are rewritten over the same blocks and pinned to the digests recorded before the refactor (`peacemaker-isa/tests/qwen4_moe_sym_digests.rs`: every entry, the module texts and the `R4Spec` experiments). It replaces the down-only twin `qwen4_moe_down_gp.rip` and its `QDownGen` / `qdown::*` natives (typed-core blocks). Docs: REFERENCE section 16, cookbook 14.
- **Flash-Next gfx1201: the INT8 MQ6G256V2 prefill GEMM runs a 128 x 256 tile by default (-6 to -8 % kernel time on the large prefill shapes).** The `gemm_mq6g256v2_mmq_i8_pm_gfx1201` image now carries the banded `T128x256` entries (`..._set_gfx1201_t128x256`, `..._set_bf16_gfx1201_t128x256`; 16 waves, 512 threads, 55296 B LDS, same per-wave 32 x 64 tile) next to the four unchanged-byte 128 x 128 entries; `gemm_mq6g256v2_i8_prequant` picks the wide tile unless it would pad more tokens than the 128-token tile (`N % 256` in `1..=128`) or its grid loads the WGPs worse (`M=128, N=4096`: 16 CTAs, 1.34x slower than 128 x 128). Output is bitwise identical to the CPU reference and to the 128 x 128 entry (all 12 Flash-Next presets plus N=512 and ragged N tails and M tails, both epilogues). Measured on card B, 15 rounds x 30 launches, N=16384 shipped-old -> new: qkv M=10240 BF16 0.939, z (6144) 0.934, q (12288) 0.940, out (2560 x K6144) 0.919; M=512 0.940, M=128 0.951 (TOP/s 132 -> 142 on the 10240 shape, 36.6 % of the 389 TOPS peak). Measured on gfx1201 at A3B chunk shapes (N=4096, S=4096; N=8192; Q8_0 and fp8): bit-identical to the shipped kernels and at parity (ratios 0.9995-1.0009, no run separable).

It emits the bytes and proof of all twelve valid specs (`tests/fp8_gemm_twin.rs`). `pm_loop --kernel fp8_gemm [--scale row|k128|both] [--epi set|add|silu|silu-bf16|qkv|qkvza] [--rip fp8_gemm.rip]` launches as `fp8_f2_row_launch` does (the shipped repacker once in setup, then the GEMM) and reports the candidate against the shipped bundle bitwise; there is no CPU reference for this kernel, and `--emu` reports the emulator's refusal of dense FP8 WMMA.
- **`iu4_gemm`: 2:4-sparse SWMMAC K-loops (`Mma::S24X64`, `Mma::S24X32`), run end to end by the PeaceMaker emulator and timed by `pm_loop` on gfx1201.** *Kernel.* `Spec.mma` selects the matrix instruction; `dense` is the shipped WMMA K-loop and its variant names, symbols and emitted bytes are unchanged (digests pinned). The weights are the sparse SWMMAC operand A and live in the dense MQ4V2 container: `iu4_gemm::sparse24::pack_block` places the compressed codes and index words in the code bytes the unchanged staging routes into the registers the SWMMAC reads, so prologue, publish, LDS layout, fold and epilogue do not change (no weight bytes are saved; it measures the MMA-issue saving inside the production pipeline). `S24X64` issues one `v_swmmac_i32_16x16x64_iu4` per accumulator per 64-K slab, `S24X32` one `v_swmmac_i32_16x16x32_iu4` per sub-block with `index_key`; each accumulator is seeded with `magic8`. Valid for the 128x128x8 token-layout tile with `Epi::Set | Add`; every other axis is refused naming the axis. CLI `peacemaker-isa emit --kernel iu4_gemm --mma dense|s24x64|s24x32`; `.rip`: `Iu4Spec.mma`, `Mma::{Dense, S24X64, S24X32}`, `iu4::sparse_block` / `sparse_block_stepping`, and the twin's `-s24x64` / `-s24x32` variants, byte-identical to the Rust emit. *Emulator.* `peacemaker-ir` now runs the production `iu4_gemm` and `qwen4_moe_sym` kernels to completion (`s_setprio`, `ds_{load,store}_2addr_stride64`, the gfx1201 scalar udiv expansion, and the full `v_div_scale_f32` exponent domain, with numerics-probe receipt `gfx1201-div-r1`); `tests/iu4_gemm_sparse_emu.rs` shows the whole sparse kernel on random 2:4-pruned weights equal to the dense kernel and the CPU fold on the pruned weights bitwise, for both kinds. *`pm_loop`* (`rdna-compute` example, `--features lab`, through `fabric-run.sh --class timing`): `--mma dense|s24x64|s24x32` (also `--rip` and `--base-mma`) prunes the generated weights to 2:4 deterministically (`sparse-seed`; two pseudo-random K kept per group of four, pruned code 8), packs them with `pack_block` for the candidate, and times it against the shipped dense kernel on the pruned dense weights: `identical_to_baseline` is true and the CPU reference passes bit-exact, and the record gains `sparse: {mma, base_mma, groups_per_block: 32, kept_per_group: 2, seed}`. `--emu` now runs the dense and sparse candidates on the emulator at M=128, N=128, K=256 (SET and ADD) instead of refusing at `s_setprio`. `separable` is now an exact two-sided sign test over the per-round paired ratios (each ABBA round compares the candidate's two block medians of `--time` launches, default 50, with the baseline's two from that same round, so between-round clock and power drift cancels) with p <= 1e-3, ties counting against it (at least 11 rounds); `direction` is `faster`/`slower` from the majority sign, with `rounds_faster/slower/tied`, `sign_p`, `block_ratio` and `round_ratio_min/max`. The block-disjoint rule (every candidate block median on one side of every baseline block median, defeated by about 5% block-to-block drift) stays as `separable_block_disjoint`, and the twins' full-range rule, unchanged for `pm_decode_twins` and vetoed by a single hiccup launch, as `separable_full_range`. Until `separable`, ABBA rounds (default 6) are doubled up to `--max-rounds` (default 256) or `--time-budget-s` (default 240); `rounds_run`, `extended` and `stop` report it. Measured on gfx1201, gate shape M=17408, N=512, K=5120 (candidate vs the shipped dense kernel on the pruned weights, bit-identical output): `s24x64` 0.964 (12 of 12 paired rounds faster, sign p 5e-4, separable at the first 12 rounds), `s24x32` 1.084 (12 of 12 slower, p 5e-4); the dense-vs-dense control is 133 faster / 122 slower / 1 tied of 256 rounds, p 0.57, not separable.

At >= 128 rows (`HC_UP_V2_MIN_ROWS`), `low_rank == 320`, outside Redline recording and graph capture, `hyper_read_up_wmma_bf16_gfx1201_v2` (same module `hyper_read_up_wmma_gfx1201`, `kernels/src/hyper_read_up_wmma.gfx1201.hip`) runs instead: grid `[hidden/16, G]` with `G = ceil(rows/8192)` clamped to 1..4, 512 threads, the block's 64 weight rows staged into LDS once, X fragments fetched five K steps ahead, and the BF16-rounded gate read from a 16 KiB LDS table built at block start with the baseline's own expression; NaN or non-finite lanes recompute with the baseline epilogue so NaN payloads match. Every output u32 is bytewise `_t128`'s (`examples/hc_up_v2_oracle.rs`: random, adversarial, NaN-payload fuzz and an exhaustive sweep of all 65536 BF16 gate-input patterns per branch, rows 1 to 16384, plus an untouched-guard check; unit test `hyper_read_up_v2_is_bytewise_t128`). DRAM per row is unchanged (31,360 B); L2-to-LDS weight staging per row falls from 51,200 B to ~40,960 B * 160 / (rows per block). Kernel `_t128` 440-445 us -> `_v2` 283-286 us at 4096 rows and 1,765-1,785 us -> 1,190 us at 16,384 rows (`examples/hc_up_v2_bench.rs`, three fresh processes, R9700, per-call min; the DRAM traffic floor is ~0.85 ms at 16,384 rows); end-to-end pp8192 not measured. `scripts/route_plan_hc_up_digest.py` re-stamps the route-plan rows.

The new `fn_gdn_dense_producer_v2_{f32,bf16}` entries load a thread's 3 + 16 inputs before consuming any, drop the `bf()` re-roundings of values that are already BF16 widenings (a proven identity; the q/k final `bf(bf(x) * inv)` keeps both, since a NaN in both operands makes the payload follow the compiler's operand order), and take SiLU + BF16 rounding through hardware `exp2`/`rcp` only where that provably rounds to the same BF16 as the exact `expf`/division chain (|x| in [2^-20, 16], not within 64 ulps of a BF16 tie: 99.8% of that range; exhaustively verified over all 2^32 F32 inputs, 0 mismatches, max approximation error 17 ulp), else the exact chain. Every changed intermediate (the packed F16 q/k/v planes, g, beta, the conv history ring, the Q8 state codes/scales) and the scan's BF16 output are byte-identical to the v1 chain at rows {64, 65, 130, 777, 1024, 4096, 4160, 16384} on random inputs with NaN/inf/+-0/subnormal/tie values. Per GDN layer at 16384 rows (R9700, rocprofv3 medians): producer 2456 -> 1696 us (F32 qkv, at the DRAM floor), producer + KKT + scan 4.57 -> 3.78 ms (hipEvent). `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_GDN_QKV_BF16=1` additionally stores the qkv projection as BF16 bits on the exact-INT8 MQ6 route (the GEMM's BF16 entry, bitwise `RNE(F32 accumulator)`): the producer only consumes each qkv value through that rounding, so the GEMM write and the producer read halve (40 -> 20 KB per row each) and the producer drops to 1304 us (chain 3.4-3.45 ms), byte-identical. It is opt-in because the PeaceMaker INT8 GEMM's BF16 entry is still slower than its F32 entry at the qkv shape (16384 rows: 5.53 vs 4.96 ms), which outweighs the producer's gain until its epilogue is fixed.

Mixer tail (`hc_row_write_norm_gate_gfx1201`): a pregated GDN / attention HC write that is immediately followed by the next HC read of the same streams runs the write of the out projection's F32 `mixed` and that read's norm / F16 row / next-write gates as one kernel, and the read takes its prenormed route. Byte oracles (`cargo test -p rdna-compute --release --lib hc_row_fold_moe_gfx1201 hc_row_write_norm_gate_gfx1201 -- --test-threads=1`, GPU) compare every output byte (HC streams, F16 normalized row, next gate logits) against the unfused kernels run in sequence on clean data, NaN / inf / +-0 / subnormal / huge rows with NaN payloads of both signs, NaN / inf entries in the norm and gate weights, dead routes and unrouted experts, and isolated specials, at 16, 17, 4096 and 4097 rows: 100% byte-equal (NaN operand order is pinned to the unfused kernels' compiled order). hipEvent microbench on an R9700 (median of 3 fresh processes, `bench_hc_row_fold_gfx1201`), per sublayer: MoE tail 1397 -> 1242 us at 4096 rows and 5674 -> 4931 us at 16384; mixer tail 796 -> 590 us at 4096 and 3134 -> 2172 us at 16384. Idea from Gufo upstream (gufo-org/gufo @1071b361, MIT).
- **Flash-Next on gfx1201: the HC row folds retiled, fold time down 32% (MoE tail) and 8% (mixer tail) at 16384 rows, still byte-identical.** `hc_row_fold_moe_gfx1201` / `hc_row_write_norm_gate_gfx1201` ran at ~60% of DRAM bandwidth: one 256-thread block per token walked serialized phases (five dependent 4-byte gather rounds, five dependent stream load-store rounds behind the aliasing store, a `mixed` LDS round trip, twelve barriers). The block is now 320 threads, one per 8 columns of every branch: the ten gathered expert rows (16-byte loads), the shared / `mixed` row and the four stream chunks are all requested before the first use, the combine -> scaled add -> HC write chain stays in registers, and the norm's 256-partial reduction (same tree, same operand order) finishes its last five levels inside a wave: three barriers per token, LDS 29.7 -> 24.6 KB. Inside the combine every value is bf16-exact or the product / sum of two, so the reference NaN-splitting rounding is the three-op `(u + 0x7fff + bit16) & 0xffff0000` (a token whose route weights hold a NaN with payload bits below bit 16 runs the reference rounding verbatim); the NaN operand orders of the norm's partial sums and multiplies are pinned to the replaced kernels' compiled order. The MoE launch additionally needs a 16-byte aligned grouped-down tensor (its call-site gate checks it). Byte oracles (`cargo test -p rdna-compute --release --lib hc_row_fold_moe_gfx1201 hc_row_write_norm_gate_gfx1201 -- --test-threads=1`): 100% byte-equal on every case, NaN payloads included. hipEvent microbench on an R9700 (`bench_hc_row_fold_gfx1201`, median of 3 fresh processes, fold launch only): MoE fold 1239 -> 865 us at 4096 rows and 4924 -> 3369 us at 16384; mixer fold 592 -> 504 us at 4096 and 2181 -> 1999 us at 16384.

Neither the F32 gate output (rows x 6144 x 4 B) nor the F32 rotation reaches memory and the producer launch disappears: DRAM bytes per row 117,120 -> 43,392; on an R9700 the 4096-row pair 834 us (614 + 220) -> 311 us and the 16384-row pair 3,249 us -> 1,212 us (hipEvent medians, 3 fresh processes). One launch, `mq_rotate_x_i4_f16out` (the `mq_rotate_x_i4` source with the F16 cast of the loaded registers stored beside the sidecar), now emits the sidecar and the F16 X in the input-basis stage and the dead rotation is not run; the shared F16 scratch and the IU4 reservation are the ones the unfused chain used, the WMMA group launch simply skips its conversion (`gemm_bf16_xf32_f16_wmma_qwen4_groups_x16`). Byte-identical: `qwen4_moe_front_oracle` compares every byte of the F16 X and the sidecar against `convert_f32_to_f16` + `mq_rotate_x_i4` at 1, 16, 4096, 16384 and 4099 rows over random, wide-exponent, exact RNE-tie, special (±0, ±inf, quiet/signalling NaNs with payloads, F32 and F16 subnormals, F16 overflow/underflow ties) and mixed per-row data, and the router/selector/gate/up outputs of the WMMA group launch with and without the pre-converted X (28 cases, 0 mismatches). R9700 hipEvent, 3 fresh processes, inputs cycled over 256 MiB: 4096 rows 344 µs (`mq_rotate_x` 142 + `convert_f32_to_f16` 103 + `mq_rotate_x_i4` 82) → 114 µs, 16384 rows 1348 → 459 µs; 47,520 → 16,800 B/row of DRAM traffic (194 → 68 MB per sublayer at 4096 rows). Exact gfx1201 only, eager only; the S1 layer-major prepare/slowlink tiles, CPU split, recorder/capture and every other arch keep the unfused chain.
- **Flash-Next on gfx1201: fused HC down projection + activation, default ON (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_HC_DOWN_FUSED=0` restores the three-launch chain).** The F16 WMMA HC read's `input_mix_down` (M = 320, K = 10240) ran `gemm_bf16_xf16_f16_wmma` (split-K=4 tile + reducer) and then `hc_activation_fused_f32`; at >= 1536 rows, outside recording and graph capture, one launch (`qwen4_hc_down_fused_b64_k32`, `kernels/src/qwen4_hc_down_fused.hip`) now produces the packed BF16 activation the WMMA read consumes, byte-identical to the chain (every split partial is the incumbent tile's own zero-started ascending 16-wide K chain, the four partials are summed in the reducer's order in F32 registers, and the activation is `hc_activation_fused_f32`'s expression; the F32 `low` the chain also left is dead in this route and is not written). Per row it moves 21120 B instead of 33920 B (X in, BF16 out; no split scratch, no reducer pass, no F32 Y round trip). R9700, back-to-back, 3 fresh processes: 4096 rows 420-427 us -> 268-276 us (chain GEMM + reduce + activation), 16384 rows 1455-1465 -> 1037-1039 us, 2048 rows 206-210 -> 138 us; below 1536 rows the chain is as fast or faster and stays. The kernel is LDS- and issue-bound, not WMMA-bound: wave tile 80x32 (5x2 fragments, 80 accumulators plus 80 running-sum VGPRs), workgroup = all 320 rows x 64 B-rows, LDS planes laid out [kt, lane-half][row][8 halves] so fragment reads are conflict-free (the split-K tile's [kt][row][16] layout is 2-way conflicted), K staged 32 per barrier through a double-buffered tile with a split signal/wait barrier, and 128-byte (two-stage) global staging loads. New examples `hc_down_fused_oracle` (every output byte against the production chain, random + NaN/inf/zero/subnormal inputs, rows 1/16/1537/4096/4097/4099/16384) and `hc_down_fused_bench`.

Its `block_i8_128` blocks are bitwise equal to the two-pass chain on every Flash-Next shape at N=512 and 4000. The GEMM is the new builder family `mq6_i8_gemm` (`peacemaker-isa emit --kernel mq6_i8_gemm`, image `kernels/gemm_mq6g256v2_mmq_i8_pm_gfx1201.hxaco`, entries `gemm_mq6g256v2_mmq_i8_pm_set_gfx1201` / `_set_bf16_gfx1201`): the bitwise twin of the hipcc `gemm_mq6g256v2_mmq_i8_set{,_bf16}_gfx12` (F32 and BF16, every shape and N checked over the whole output; CPU-emulator tests cover M/N tails and K = 256..1024), 192 VGPRs, 36864 B LDS. It runs wherever its preconditions hold (`K % 256 == 0`, `M % 4 == 0`, 4-byte aligned output, output and weight extents under 2^31 bytes) and falls back to the hipcc kernel otherwise. At the kernel it is 1-3% faster than hipcc at N=4096 (131.7 vs 128.3 TF/s on 12288x2560) and up to 1.3x at N=128. Flash-Next pp16384 on the R9700 (3 fresh processes per arm): F16 PM route (`HIPFIRE_MQ6_I8=0`) 4690.0 tok/s; int8 hipcc + one-pass producer 4848.2 (+3.4%); int8 PM + one-pass producer 4873.5 (+3.9%). The route plans of the three gfx1201 Flash-Next artifacts list the one-pass producer and the PM image (the hipcc GEMM rows stay as the fallback).

Measured on R9700 Flash-Next pp16384: +1.1% (4680 → 4734 tok/s, 3 fresh processes); KLD (paired, same binary) WT2 +0.0006, code24 −0.0025, inside the bar. The gemm and the A8 quantizer modules are registered for exact gfx1201 and added to the three walked Flash-Next route plans. gfx1151 keeps the F16 route (measured 0.79-0.95x of it on the GEMM; opt-in `HIPFIRE_MQ6_I8=1`).
