Each kind checks its exact operand widths and accepts only the modifiers `llvm-mc -mcpu=gfx1201` accepts (`index_key`, `neg_lo`/`neg_hi`, `clamp`). The text parser and printer use LLVM's `index_key:N` spelling. The emulator now runs the 16-bit-out and FP8/BF8 SWMMAC kinds, but only in an exact domain: finite normal inputs where `|C|+Σ|a·b| ≤ 2^P·q`. Everything outside it is still a hard error. Cookbook recipe `10-swmmac` (a 2:4-sparse f16 tile and an FP8 tile) passes `hw_diff` on gfx1201 card B: emulator, hardware and CPU reference agree on all 256 words. No existing kernel's bytes change.
- **`mq6_i8_gemm` has a tile axis: `Spec.tile` = `T128x128` (shipped) | `T256x128` | `T128x256` (weight rows x tokens per workgroup).** The wide tiles run 16 waves (512 threads, 55296 B of LDS) of the shipped 32-row x 64-token per-wave tile, so the register map, the K-loop bundles and the fold are the shipped ones and the kernel stays at the 192-VGPR ceiling; occupancy per WGP is 2 workgroups (32 waves) against the shipped tile's 3 by LDS (24 waves). Staging rounds, the LDS layout (`Tile::layout`, the DS / SZ planes chunked per 128 so the fold's `ds_load_2addr_b32` offsets stay in 8 bits), the raster shifts, the wave split, the metadata lanes, the epilogue coordinates and the launch geometry all follow the tile. `T128x128` is byte-identical (the pinned digests and the module text are unchanged), keeps its variant name and symbol; the new tiles are `256x128x16-...` / `128x256x16-...` and `..._t256x128` / `..._t128x256`. Each wide tile is bit-equal to the exact CPU reference and to the shipped tile on the interpreter over ragged edge shapes (`peacemaker-isa/tests/mq6_i8_gemm.rs`); `peacemaker-isa emit --kernel mq6_i8_gemm --tile`, `Mq6Spec.tile` / `Mq6Tile` in `.rip`, the twin (twelve variants, byte-identical to `emit`) and `pm_loop --kernel mq6_i8_gemm --tile 128x128|256x128|128x256` (baseline stays the shipped object) cover every tile.
- **`.rip` scripts can compose the production `mq6_i8_gemm` generator at wait / barrier granularity.** `mq6_i8_gemm::blocks` (new, public) exposes an opaque `Gen` and instruction builders at the granularity of the generator's own functions: fetches, weight decode, WMMA step, the VOPD fold in four stages, seed fill, the prologue's set-up and the epilogue emit straight into the builder, and everything that touches LDS (`store_w_insns`, `store_a_insns`, `meta_store_insns`, `step_load_insns`, the fold loads) *returns* `Instruction`s. A `.rip` script issues them through the checked driver on rings it made itself (`wg.lds`, `Ring::new`, `begin_write`, `ds_store`, `ds_load_cur`, `wait_all`, `signal` / `wait_arrived`, `loop_carried`), so a wait, a split-barrier signal, the decode's place among the WMMAs and the fold order are script statements and the typed core stays sealed (no `Lend`, no `Auth`). `Mq6Gemm::emit` / `emit_module`, `Mq6Gen::new`, `Mq6Spec { epi, raster, arch }`, `Mq6Epi`, `Raster` and the `mq6::*` natives are bound; the committed twin `kernels/mq6_i8_gemm.rip` re-emits `emit`'s `s_text` and proof for every valid spec (`tests/mq6_i8_gemm_twin.rs`), the rust `emit` / `prologue` / `kloop` are rewritten over the same builders with `peacemaker-isa/tests/mq6_i8_gemm_digests.rs` pinning every emitted symbol and the module text to the pre-refactor bytes, and `pm_loop --kernel mq6_i8_gemm --rip FILE` times a variation. The `.rip` definedness check (R0604) no longer demands a write of the high half of a wave32 lane-mask source (`v_cndmask_*` select, `v_*_co_ci_*` carry-in), which the table models as a 64-bit pair. Docs: reference §14, cookbook 12.
- **`.rip` scripts can compose the production `iu4_gemm` generator.** `Driver::typed` (new, `peacemaker-author`) runs a typed-core body on a runtime driver's own backend and session: it refuses under wave-uniform control and after a wave exit, builds the `Workgroup` through a crate-private constructor (no new seal, no `Auth` leaves the crate), and lends LDS rings across with `Lend::{give, take, give_back, consumed}` (phase, drained token, tag, owner and live checks; every taken ring must come back) plus `Lend::end` (the exit's branch flag is shared) and `Lend::wg_cond`. `iu4_gemm::blocks` exposes the generator's phase blocks (`declare_lds`, `prologue`, `kloop`, `block`, `block_stepping`, `step_descriptor`, `trip_end`, `trips_cmp`, `epilogue`, `gdn_epilogue`) over an opaque `Gen`, and `iu4_gemm::emit` and its K-loop are now written over them: every valid `Spec` emits the same bytes (digests pinned by `iu4_gemm_emit_digests_pinned`). `.rip` gains `Iu4Gemm::emit` / `emit_module`, `MoeSym::emit` / `emit_module`, the `Iu4Spec` / `MoeSymSpec` literals and spec enums, and the `iu4::*` block natives; the committed twin `iu4_gemm.rip` re-expresses `emit` and the K-loop in script and is byte-identical (`s_text` and proof) to the Rust kernel for every valid spec. See `peacemaker-rip/docs/cookbook/11-production-blocks.md`.
- **`pm_loop`: one command closes the iteration loop for PM production generators.** `cargo build --release -p rdna-compute --features lab --example pm_loop`, then (through `fabric-run.sh --class timing` on an idle gfx1201 card) `pm_loop --kernel iu4_gemm --tile 256x128x16 --epi set --shape M=17408,N=512,K=5120` or `--kernel qwen4_moe_sym --epi gate_up_nt8` emits the variant with the native writer, runs M7 on every export through the cert cache, checks it on the card against the CPU reference and against the shipped production object (the embedded `.hxaco` and its selecting source line, or a second emitted variant via `--base-<knob>`), ABBA-times it exactly like `pm_decode_twins time` (shared `examples/support/abba.rs`) and prints one JSON record (schema 1: resources per export, cert-cache hit/miss, `max_abs_err`/`tolerance`, `identical_to_baseline`, medians, ratio, `separable`); a correctness failure exits non-zero with the record. Supporting API: `iu4_gemm::Spec::from_knobs`, `qwen4_moe_sym::Spec::from_epi` (the CLI now calls them; emitted bytes unchanged), `Fold` also parses `k256shared`/`k256pow2` (still closed by `Spec::validate`), and `pm_check::m7_status` reports whether a certification came from the cache. `--kernel iu4_gemm --rip FILE.rip [knobs]` runs the same loop on a `.rip` composition instead of the Rust generator (the knobs still give the launch geometry): the file is compiled for the knobs' variant, refused (exit 3, stage `rip`) unless its symbol, kernarg layout, workgroup size and LDS match `iu4_gemm::emit`, and the record carries `candidate.rip = {path, sha256, variant, identical_to_generator}`, so a `.rip` logic edit is emitted, certified, checked and ABBA-timed with no Rust rebuild. `--kernel mq6_i8_gemm --epi set|set_bf16 [--raster banded|linear] --shape M=..,N=..,K=..|fn:<name>` adds the MQ6G256V2 x A8 INT8 prefill GEMM: the twelve Fn gfx1201 shapes are presets (`fn:m12288k2560-n16384`, ...), the baseline is the shipped `gemm_mq6g256v2_mmq_i8_pm_gfx1201.hxaco` entry the runtime selects (file:line + sha256 recorded), the launch is `mq6_i8_launch`'s, and correctness requires the candidate to be bitwise equal to the shipped baseline and to an exact CPU reference (all pairs while M*N*K <= 2e9, else a sampled grid; the record names the coverage); `--emu --raster linear` runs the candidate on the emulator. `--rip` accepts this kernel too, ABI-checked against `mq6_i8_gemm::emit`. `--kernel qwen4_moe_sym` adds `--epi down_gp_nt4|down_gp_nt8` (the grouped-position down twin, baseline = the shipped `qwen4_moe_down_gp_pm_gfx1201.hxaco` NT4 entry, file:line and sha256 recorded, the plane built host-side from the same records) and the Flash-Next prefill presets `fn:gate_up_nt4-t4096|t16384` and `fn:down_gp_nt4-t4096|t16384`; correctness for this kernel requires bitwise equality with the shipped baseline AND the exact reference. `--rip FILE.rip` now accepts the qwen4_moe_sym down entries: `crates/peacemaker-isa/src/kernels/qwen4_moe_down_gp.rip` composes the K-loop from the `qdown::*` natives of `qwen4_moe_sym::down_blocks` (`QDownGen`), byte-identical (`s_text` and proof) to `emit`/`emit_down_gp` for `down_nt4|nt8` and `down_gp_nt4|nt8`; the prologue, a fold, the tail and the stores stay Rust blocks. `--rip` also takes the PM producers: `--kernel iu4_c8_producer_pm --export rotate|norm|sigmoid_rotate|norm_out`, `--kernel moe_rotate_i4_pm [--variant gp]` and `--kernel gdn_chunk_prep_pm` compile `iu4_c8_producer.rip` / `moe_rotate_i4_pm.rip` / `gdn_chunk_prep.rip` (untyped-`Builder` twins over the new `blocks` modules and the `c8::*` / `rot::*` / `gdn::*` natives, byte-identical `s_text` and proof to the Rust emit of every export; the norm's LDS exchange, the order of its phases and `gdn_chunk_prep`'s loops are script statements), ABI-check the result against the Rust emit and time it; the Rust producers are pinned to their pre-refactor digests (`peacemaker-isa/tests/producers_pinned.rs`).
- **`pm_loop` covers the PM producer generators of the gfx1201 A3B prefill, and says when a difference is immaterial.** `--kernel iu4_c8_producer_pm --export rotate|norm|sigmoid_rotate|norm_out` (`--shape a3b:chunk|a3b:tail|a3b:chunk4k`, rows/K/awq overrides), `--kernel moe_rotate_i4_pm [--variant rows|gp] --shape a3b:t4096|fn:t4096|...` and `--kernel gdn_chunk_prep_pm --shape a3b:t4096|t8192|...` emit the module with the native writer, M7 every export, launch exactly as the production launchers do, and compare the candidate to the shipped `.hxaco` object (bitwise identity is the pass criterion) and to an exact CPU reference where the repo has one (the four C8 exports and both MoE rotate twins: FWHT, signs, C2/C8 quantizer, all output bytes; the GDN chunk-prep has none, so identity alone decides and the record says why); `--emu` runs the candidate on the emulator at a small shape or reports its refusal. The producers share one generic `Workload` (`examples/pm_loop/prod.rs`) and the input, shape-preset and emulator builders in `examples/pm_loop/common.rs`, which the GEMM workloads now use too. New `--min-effect` (default 0.005): `material` = `separable` AND `|block_ratio - 1| >= min-effect`, because the paired sign test also resolves real but immaterial placement and order effects (two byte-identical objects came out "separable" at 0.2-0.3%); the verdict reads `faster/slower (material)` or `separable but below min-effect`. On gfx1201 every producer is bit-identical to the shipped object at its main A3B/FN shape and none is material (candidate = shipped code: block ratios 0.9997-1.002).
- **Kernel-level PM-vs-hipcc timing for the gfx1201 decode projections, plus a first measured answer.** `pm_decode_twins time [--synthetic] --time N --rounds R` adds HIP-event ABBA sampling to the existing byte-identity oracle: warm both arms, require both to match the captured pre/post bytes, then time N calls per arm per block over R rounds on one stream, reporting median/min/p90/mean/spread per arm, the PM/incumbent ratio, and a conservative `separable` flag that refuses to claim a delta smaller than the observed spread; device clock/power/cap state is recorded before and after, and the JSON carries both arms' identities, the capture hash and the launch geometry. `--synthetic` builds every buffer from the capture manifest's declared sizes with deterministic non-zero weight data and zeroed outputs when the large `.bin` payloads are absent (the shipped decode captures list but do not store the 27.8 MB weight buffer), and still requires both arms to produce identical bytes before any sampling. Measured on one gfx1201 card at the captured occupancy-0 geometry, 600 calls per arm: PM/hipcc median ratios were `fused_gate_up 0.998`, `fused_qkv 0.999`, `fused_qkvza 1.001`, `gemv_multirow_default 1.000`, `gemv_residual 1.003` — geomean **1.0003**, none separable at this call count. Read that as kernel-body parity, not an end-to-end decode claim: inputs are synthetic (identical for both arms), one capture per module, and launch overhead is excluded. The PM twins exist to remove hipcc/JIT dependence at equal speed, not to be faster; `.rip` versus its PM twin is 1.00× by construction (the assembly is byte-identical).
- **The `.rip` CPU emulator is now checked against silicon.** New example `peacemaker-rip/examples/hw_diff` takes a `.rip` source and a `run` case, executes the case on the emulator first (it must already pass), then loads the *same* assembled code object on a real GPU (`module_load_data` / `module_get_function`), uploads every buffer's `initial_bytes`, patches the pointer kernarg fields and launches once with `launch_kernel_blob` at the case's grid/block/dynamic LDS. It reports three verdicts — emulator vs case, hardware vs case, emulator vs hardware — with per-buffer `first_mismatch`, `max_abs_diff`, `guard_ok` and input `changed`; device arch, grid, block and LDS go into the receipt. It refuses an arch that does not match `hip.get_arch(device)`, refuses block > 1024 threads, grid dimensions > 65536 and total threads > 10^7, and documents that the caller must hold `scripts/gpu-lock.sh`. First run: all nine cookbook recipes (ten case executions) agree **exactly** on gfx1201 — integer buffers bitwise, floats within the case tolerance, guards intact and inputs unchanged on both sides — covering integer ALU, IEEE divide, multi-workgroup LDS handoff, loop/device-loop shapes, the BF16 WMMA tile and kernarg loads/waits. Not covered by this result: gfx1151 (this host enumerates four gfx1201 and no gfx1151 GPU) and instruction mixes outside the cookbook corpus. The `run` case API (`Case::parse`, `initial_bytes`, `kernarg_with_addresses`, `emulate`, `compare`, `agrees`) is public so oracles reuse one schema instead of forking it. No kernel bytes changed.
- **Kernel packs declare the complete fn-lanes source exports.** The gfx1151 `gdn_lanes` index now includes the tensor-ops kernels its shared translation unit compiles, and gfx1201's Q8 wide index includes the staged BF16 scaled-add export. Kernel implementations and dispatch selection are unchanged.
- **A3B prefill: the four byte-identical late-H PeaceMaker/epilogue routes are on by default on exact gfx1201.** `HIPFIRE_MOE_ROTATE_I4_PM`, `HIPFIRE_PREFILL_IU4_C8_PM`, `HIPFIRE_GDN_CHUNK_PREP_PM` and `HIPFIRE_MOE_SHARED_DOWN_SIGMOID_EPI` now have exact-gfx1201 `QUALIFIED` rows, so stock `hipfire bench --matrix` gets the speed that previously needed four explicit opt-ins; explicit `0` restores each incumbent and other architectures are unchanged. Evidence on beta `272e16c5b4`: all four existing byte oracles `all_byte_identical`; the A3B kldseq rule (Qwen wt2/agentic × prefill-prompt/per-token, FP8 KV) byte-equal between stock and the four routes (paired KLD delta 0); qwen3.6-35b-a3b-d53.mq4rs pp16000 stock 16625.7 → 17035.8 tok/s (3 fresh processes per arm, card A). `iu4_c8_pm_oracle` now requires the explicit kill `HIPFIRE_PREFILL_IU4_C8_PM=0`, because an unset flag would route its HIP incumbent arm to the PM twin.
- **A3B prefill: the MoE down GEMM reads a grouped-position activation plane (byte-identical, exact gfx1201).** Under the existing `HIPFIRE_MOE_ROTATE_I4_PM` route the down A4 producer writes each record at its grouped position (`g * P + row`) and the down NT4/NT8 entries read a tile's 16 records contiguously, instead of gathering 16 scattered flat-slot records through `sorted[]`. New twins in a separate bundle `qwen4_moe_down_gp_pm_gfx1201.hxaco` (SHA-256 `e136e40e…`): `moe_rotate_i4_gp_pm_gfx1201` and `qwen4_moe_down_iu4_sym_gp_pm_gfx1201_nt{4,8}`; the qualified `qwen4_moe_iu4_sym_pm_gfx1201` (`0eea1673…`) and `moe_rotate_i4_pm_gfx1201` bundles are untouched and remain the oracle anchors. Record bytes, every fold and rounding and every store are the incumbent's; padding rows still write no record and read as +0. No knob: `Gpu::qwen4_moe_rotate128_i4_gp` is used by the two Mq4Sym down callers and is exactly `qwen4_moe_rotate128_i4` wherever the PM producer, the PM NT4/NT8 descriptor or the shape does not apply (slab/E8P/W3 consumers keep the flat sidecar). The down scratch is pre-sized for the padded grouped rows (+`min(L, E) * 15 * 4 * 72` bytes, 1.1 MB at A3B 8192 rows) so the producer never grows it mid-prefill. Evidence: `qwen4_moe_sym --geometry a3b` check at 8192/7808/128 tokens x one/all/skew (and host-mapped NT8, graph, stress) all `pm_nt1/nt4/nt8` anchors 0 byte mismatches over both whole output buffers; `moe_rotate_i4_pm_oracle` all 12 cases byte-identical through the position mapping with every pad record still poison. rocprof pp16000 (four late-H flags, one process): down 88.21 → 79.38 ms/pass, producer 24.98 → 24.12 ms/pass.

- **First-request JIT carry preserves current beta's registry and walked-plan behavior.** Pack declarations include the later HC-write widening and the native A3B module's shared-source exports; historical walk digests remain provenance while HIP entries bind the current registry recipe. Three later beta descriptor-forwarding sites have explicit cited dynamic exceptions (86 dynamic rows total), not a claim of proved runtime coverage.
  - The dispatch completeness test follows beta's shared `residual_kernel` table and pins both residual wrappers' forwarding edges, retaining the MQ3 fix without restoring the obsolete duplicated SwiGLU match.
- **A3B MoE prefill routing glue: wave-per-row fused router and multi-workgroup stable scatter (byte-identical).** `HIPFIRE_MOE_ROUTER_TOPK_MULTIROW` (on at exact gfx1201 by qualification) now runs `moe_router_softmax_topk_k8_wave`: one wave32 per row, eight rows per 256-thread block, any row count, reproducing the one-row fused router's softmax trees, bit-reversed tie order, renorm and clamp operation for operation (ids and weights byte-identical on the oracle's random, tie, non-finite and flat-tail rows, 8..8192 rows). `moe_scatter_fused_k8` on exact gfx1201 runs the new three-launch `moe_scatter_stable_k8` twin (per-chunk histogram, offsets + placement, inverse permutation) once the batch has four 1024-slot chunks: counts, offsets, tile ids, padding and `inverse_perm` are identical to the single-workgroup kernel and slots sit in ascending flat-slot order inside each expert instead of LDS-atomic arrival order (the grouped GEMMs compute each row independently and the combine reads `inverse_perm`). Oracles: `moe_router_topk_multirow_oracle`, `test_moe_scatter_permute_k8`.
- **gfx1201 A3B shared-expert down: the `HIPFIRE_MOE_SHARED_DOWN_SIGMOID_EPI` fold runs a builder `_b1` entry (bit-exact).** The certified `gemm_mq4g256v2_residual_mmq_iu4_gfx12_b1.hxaco` (SHA-256 `49cc18ee…`, was `5cf347e7…`) gains `gemm_mq4g256v2_residual_mmq_iu4_full_add_sigmoid_b1`, appended after `qkvzagdn` (every earlier symbol's code is unchanged; `peacemaker-isa emit --kernel iu4_gemm --epi addsigmoid`, certified with `iu4_gemm.k128-128x128x8-cacc1.addsigmoid.contract.json`). It is `full_add_b1` with the hipcc V3 `add == 2` store `Y = fma(sigmoid(gate[token]), 0.0f + acc, Y)`: the sigmoid is hipcc's own `1.0f / (1.0f + __expf(-s))` lowering imported as `iu4_gemm.sigmoid.region.s`, and the `b128` stores keep V3's kernarg layout (`shared_gate` at offset 40). `Gpu::try_gemm_mq4g256v2_shared_down_sigmoid_epi` selects it whenever the `_b1` ADD is eligible (`HIPFIRE_G12_IU4_ISA`, `m % 4 == 0`, 16-byte-aligned output; not the `_b1_control` bundle) and otherwise keeps the V3 entry. `shared_down_sigmoid_epi_oracle` now carries the A3B chunk rows 7808 and 8192 and a V3 anchor arm: all 16 cases are byte-identical between the incumbent unfused sequence, the `_b1` entry and V3. rocprofv3 kernel time at M=2048, K=512, rows 7808/8192: V3 247 µs, `_b1` sigmoid 214 µs per call; the call is Y read+write bound (a 64 MB device copy of the same traffic takes 227 µs).
- **A3B MoE prefill: the standalone `rmsnorm_f32` (MoE normalize) and `sigmoid_mul_f32` (FA output gate) folded into the exact C8 IU4 PM producers they feed (`HIPFIRE_PREFILL_IU4_C8_PM`, byte-identical).** Two new exports in the `iu4_c8_producer_pm_gfx1201` module (80-byte kernarg block = the frozen 72 bytes + one pointer @72; the two original exports' code is unchanged): `iu4_c8_sigmoid_rotate_pm_gfx1201` forms `attn * sigmoid(gate)` per element in registers (hipcc's range-reduced `expf` and IEEE division op for op) in front of the rotate, and `iu4_c8_rmsnorm_out_rotate_pm_gfx1201` runs the RMSNorm in the reduction order of the standalone `rmsnorm_f32` (cross-wave levels of its `sdata` tree first, then the wave; the fused RMSNorm export's order differs, so it cannot stand in) and also stores the normalized F32 row that the router, shared selector and routed-expert producers read. `Gpu::mq_sigmoid_rotate_x_i4_c8_pm` / `Gpu::fused_rmsnorm_out_mq_rotate_i4_c8_pm` launch them; the MoE FA finish (`batch_chunk_full_attn_moe_finish`) and the grouped-prefill normalize stage (`fold_prefill_norm_into_input_basis`, skipping the input-basis stage it replaces) take them only where the PM rotate is admitted today (eager, supported shape, F32 operands, disjoint outputs, the F3 producer-fused arm) and otherwise run the unchanged standalone-pass chains. The FA fold leaves the attention buffer ungated (nothing reads it after the finish: the residual GEMM consumes the sidecar, and the rotated F32 side output and its activation tap are still written). Byte oracle `iu4_c8_pm_oracle` now covers both folds against the unfused chains (`rmsnorm_batched` / `sigmoid_mul_f32` then the HIP exact rotate; sidecar, rotated F32, normalized F32 row, attention input untouched) at rows 512, 4096, 7808, 8192, K 2048/4096, zero/random/large data, with and without AWQ: all 72 fold cases and the 18 plain-export cases at rows 7808 are byte-identical. Isolated launch-pair time at the A3B chunk shapes against the HIP chains: sigmoid + rotate 1473 -> 882 us (8192 x 4096), RMSNorm + rotate 700 -> 425 us (8192 x 2048).
- **Internal test fix: `qsa_bf16_scores` poisoned outputs use the existing pool allocator.** The fixture's `poisoned` helper now takes `&mut Gpu` and allocates through the existing `alloc_tensor(&[len], DType::Raw)` plus the existing `poison` helper, matching `free_tensor` pool ownership so the guarded outputs the preceding case releases are reusable; the previous `upload_raw` malloc-fresh path could not reclaim those slots. The three affected `poisoned` call sites propagate the mutable borrow. Assertions, rows, data, skip behavior and test count are unchanged; no production code changes.

- **Flash-Next fn-lanes: an AR singleton now promotes into a lane when a batched peer queues (Strix Halo 8-request AR wave 53.7 -> 75 tok/s aggregate).** Only the speculative route promoted before; on the AR route (`--spec off`, `serve.vmm_batch`) the first request ran its whole generation alone while the other seven waited. `generate_ar_with_forward` now promotes a Qwen4 request at its first committed boundary with a peer queued (greedy, no device penalty prepass, no forced think close), handing the picked but not yet fed or streamed seed to the lane, which feeds and streams it. Greedy text is unchanged (the promoted request's text equals its singleton text).
- **Flash-Next fn-lanes on gfx1151: the GDN decode Core of up to 8 AR lanes runs as two launches instead of two per lane** (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_GDN_LANES`, `0` kills it). Bytewise the per-lane launches. Admission (`gated_delta_core_lanes`) is separate from the launch (`GdnCoreLanesPlan::launch`), so the interpreter announces each grouped step to `MoeStepHooks::before_step` exactly once, after every refusal check and before the grouped launch; a refused group falls back to the plain path, which announces each step once.
- **Flash-Next routed MoE down on gfx1151: four weight rows per wave** (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_MOE_DOWN_R4`, `0` kills it): the K = 640 MQ4G128V2 down loads each pick's activation slice once for four rows instead of once per row. Byte-identical; MTP verify window ~-0.9 ms, 8-lane step ~-0.6 ms on Strix Halo.
- **Flash-Next single-token shared-expert down and its BF16 residual fold run as one launch on gfx1151** (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SHARED_DOWN_FUSE`, `0` kills it). Byte-identical. With the routed-down change: greedy decode geomean of the AR/MTP/8-lane arms 46.8 -> 48.2 tok/s on Strix Halo.
- **Flash-Next MTP verify on gfx1151 takes the lane-rows PM kernels for its MQ6 and Q8 row projections** (column-identical to the one-row GEMVs, already used by the lane step; `HIPFIRE_FN_LANE_PM_ROWS=0` kills both). Greedy MTP text unchanged; Strix Halo greedy MTP code decode 68.8 -> 75.7 tok/s.
- **GDN Q8 decode step: the second and third passes load the next state word while working on the current one** (it waited on each 16-byte word in turn). Bytewise unchanged; fn-lanes 8-lane step 87.3 -> 82.9 ms on Strix Halo.
- **Automatic gfx1201 BF16 HC-write eight-column path.** On exact `gfx1201` with `branches == 4`, `hidden == 2560`, 16-byte aligned stream/mixed/output bases, and `rows >= 16` (the measured crossover), [`hyper_write`] takes the `hyper_write_bf16x8_gfx1201` widening (grid `[5, rows, 1]`, block `[256, 1, 1]`, LDS 0); below the gate or on ineligible shapes it keeps the `hyper_write_bf16x2` path. Per-column arithmetic, gate computation, seven-argument ABI, validation and the F32 path are unchanged. No model or performance claim.
- **`peacemaker-rip features`: the offline fact sheet an agent needs before spending GPU time.** New verb `features FILE [--arch LIST|all] [--variant LIST] [--routes FILE] [--json]` reports, per arch×variant and with no GPU, the emitted instruction count, VGPR/SGPR/LDS and wave size (read from the emitted `.amdhsa_wavefront_size32` descriptor, never inferred from the arch), source and assembly SHA-256, the static schedule features from `cost_lint` (route-free `wmma_per_trip`, `valu_per_wmma`, `independent_chains`, `wait_depth_before_wmma`, VMEM packets and operand bytes; `padding_fraction`, `k128_epochs` and `prefetch_distance_epochs` only with `--routes`; `drain_pressure` stays null because it is a paired-object comparison), and emulator executability — the modeled instruction count plus every mnemonic the `peacemaker-ir` semantics table refuses, with occurrence counts. A target that cannot be assembled, lifted, modelled or costed reports a structured `{stage, message}` rather than partial data. Findings on the committed QSA kernels: both score variants, both BF16 score variants and all four gather targets are fully modelled; `qsa_topk`'s select is not — 414 occurrences across `ds_load_b64` (52), `s_cmp_lg_u64` (1), `s_sub_u32` (23), `v_bfi_b32` (120), `v_cmp_gt_i64_e64` (214) and `v_subrev_nc_u32_e32` (4). `check` output is unchanged.
- **`peacemaker-rip run`: a kernel executes on the CPU before it touches a GPU.** New verb `run FILE [--case FILE.json] [--arch LIST|all] [--variant LIST] [--json] [--dump OUT]` compiles the script, assembles the native code object (`native::assemble`, no ROCm tools), lifts it and runs the declared grid on `peacemaker-ir`'s in-order wave32 emulator, then compares typed buffers. A case declares block/grid/dynamic LDS, buffers with a dtype (`u8`..`u64`, `i8`..`i64`, `f32`, `f64`, `f16`, `bf16`, plus a hex `bytes` escape) and kernarg fields (pointer binding, integer/float scalar, or raw bytes at an offset). Output buffers are `0xAA`-initialised with a 256-byte guard region so overruns are detected, inputs must be unchanged after the run, and float outputs compare within a declared tolerance. The report carries per-buffer `first_mismatch`, `max_abs_diff`, `guard_ok` and an input `changed` offset; an emulator refusal names the mnemonic; exit 0 iff every buffer passes. `--dump` writes a behavior-capture case (pre-run `values`, observed `expect`, `source: "dump"`) so a golden can be pinned after eyeballing and re-run exactly — it records behavior, not correctness. Validation fails closed on an unknown dtype, a missing kernarg size, overlapping fields, an unknown pointer target, duplicate buffer names and length mismatches. Corpus: all nine cookbook recipes, 22 case/variant/arch executions, including the two-workgroup LDS reversal, the BF16 WMMA tile (exact on both arches) and kernarg loads/waits with a prefilled output preserved. No committed kernel bytes changed.
- **Fixed: the emulator's semantics table no longer refuses instructions it can execute.** `peacemaker-ir/isa/semantics.tbl` is the emulator's admission gate — `Emulator::new` hard-errors with `no semantics for {name}` — and it had drifted behind the handler code, so `qsa_topk`'s select could not run on CPU for six names even though one of them (`s_sub_u32`, handler at `emu/alu.rs`) was already implemented. Added rows for `ds_load_b64`, `s_cmp_lg_u64`, `s_sub_u32`/`s_sub_co_u32`/`s_subb_u32`/`s_sub_co_ci_u32`, `v_bfi_b32`, `v_cmp_gt_i64_e32`/`_e64`, `v_subrev_nc_u32_e32`, and 16 further unclassed existing handlers the new ratchet found (`s_cmp_eq_u64`, `s_bitcmp0_b32`, `v_fmaak_f32`, `v_mul_hi_i32`, `v_min3_num_f32`, `v_fma_mixhi_f16`, `v_max_f32_e64`, `v_mul_f32_e64`, `v_subrev_f32_e32` and the `v_dual_*` family). Two handlers were new: `s_cmp_lg_u64` (full scalar-pair compare, SCC = unequal) and `v_bfi_b32` (`(S0 & S1) | (~S0 & S2)` with S0 as the mask, per the RDNA ISA, matching the builder's own documented rule). `peacemaker-rip features` now reports `qsa_topk`'s select as 0 unmodeled of 4,951 instructions, so every committed `.rip` kernel is CPU-executable. The drift ratchet `handler_literals_are_covered_by_semantics_tbl` filters emulator string literals through the ISA name universe and requires a table row per instruction name, so a handler added without its row fails the suite; a row without a handler stays unaudited by design, because family/prefix dispatch cannot be inverted. Committed assemblies are unchanged.
- **`peacemaker-rip features`: the offline fact sheet an agent needs before spending GPU time.** New verb `features FILE [--arch LIST|all] [--variant LIST] [--routes FILE] [--json]` reports, per arch×variant and with no GPU, the emitted instruction count, VGPR/SGPR/LDS and wave size (read from the emitted `.amdhsa_wavefront_size32` descriptor, never inferred from the arch), source and assembly SHA-256, the static schedule features from `cost_lint` (route-free `wmma_per_trip`, `valu_per_wmma`, `independent_chains`, `wait_depth_before_wmma`, VMEM packets and operand bytes; `padding_fraction`, `k128_epochs` and `prefetch_distance_epochs` only with `--routes`; `drain_pressure` stays null because it is a paired-object comparison), and emulator executability — the modeled instruction count plus every mnemonic the `peacemaker-ir` semantics table refuses, with occurrence counts. A target that cannot be assembled, lifted, modelled or costed reports a structured `{stage, message}` rather than partial data. Findings on the committed QSA kernels at introduction: both score variants, both BF16 score variants and all four gather targets were fully modelled; `qsa_topk`'s select was not — 414 occurrences across `ds_load_b64` (52), `s_cmp_lg_u64` (1), `s_sub_u32` (23), `v_bfi_b32` (120), `v_cmp_gt_i64_e64` (214) and `v_subrev_nc_u32_e32` (4). The semantics-table reconciliation above reduces that to zero. `check` output is unchanged.
- **M7 certification is cached by content, so re-checking unchanged bytes is free.** `pm_check::m7` memoizes its receipt under a key of the exact ELF bytes, arch, symbol and schema plus the SHA-256 of the running executable image, which conservatively covers the checker, lift/IR tables, analyses, compiler version and feature flags; the input audit found no other external checker input. Hashing the whole image in every CLI process would cost more than the 174 ms it saves, so a `binid.json` record binds the executable's `{dev, ino, size, mtime, ctime}` to its digest and a fresh process pays one `stat`. Entries are self-checksummed and strictly parsed — truncated, edited, oversize, wrong-schema or key-mismatched entries are deleted and recomputed — published atomically, capped at 512 with eviction that never removes the entry just used, and `HIPFIRE_CERT_CACHE` selects the directory (`0` disables it, an unwritable root warns once and continues uncached). Measured on `build --certify qsa_topk.rip gfx1151 select`: 296.9 ms cold to 124.0 ms warm (median of 3, load average 2.4–3.2); the seven committed assemblies are unchanged.
- **`.rip` variant and arch discovery is declared, not guessed: `check` now reads `const VARIANTS` and `const ARCHES`.** `peacemaker-rip check FILE` exited 2 on three of the four committed kernels because discovery could only read `enum Kind`, while `qsa_score`, `qsa_score_bf16` and `qsa_topk` take `fn emit(arch, variant)`. A script may now declare `const VARIANTS: &[&str]` and `const ARCHES: &[&str]`; precedence is an explicit `--variant`/`--arch`, then the consts, then `enum Kind` and the default arch list, and `--arch all` resolves to the declared set. Empty or malformed declarations keep the usage error, and an explicit `--arch` still surfaces the script's own refusal as an error instead of silencing it. The committed kernels carry their declared sets; `qsa_topk`'s histogram table is renamed `HIST_VARIANTS` on both the `.rip` and its Rust twin because `VARIANTS` is now reserved. All seven committed assemblies stay byte-identical.
- **`.rip` reaches the checked builder's runtime and untyped surface without a Rust twin.** Each binding is 1:1 onto the API the typed core calls, and the front-end `validate::instruction` operand/effect layer is kept on every instruction-taking path: `KernargLayout::pointer_access` (`read_only`/`write_only`/`read_write`), `RegPlan::add_range`, `Builder::{release_store_sources, ds_crosslane, push, control, lds_slot, lds_relayout, ds_store, ds_load, loop_, barrier_signal, barrier_wait, barrier_with_scope}`, runtime `VopdOp` construction for `Builder::vopd`, and the runtime `Wmma::iu4`/`Wmma::fp8` constructors. `control` keeps the core path alone, because symbolic branch labels do not round-trip through text, and its branch/`s_endpgm` restrictions still fire. Still refused, each with its reason recorded in `crates/peacemaker-rip/tests/vocabulary.rs`: borrowed program/ledger inspection, untyped `label`, ledger-wide `wait_all`, the `barrier` shorthand, const-generic `vopd_ff`/`vopd_ff_shared_src1` (parity and bank witnesses have no runtime form), `RegPlan::temp_v`, `verify_access`/`verify_lifetimes` (emission and `finish` already run them), and integer `rotate`/`prime`/`retire_cur` (the driver's slot mapping is private; use `Workgroup::barrier`). `Wmma::swmmac` stays unbound: its constructor omits the implicit destination accumulator read from `uses`, so the IR validator rejects its own output — a core defect in `crates/peacemaker-isa/src/insn.rs`, not a front-end limitation.
- **Fixed: gfx1100/gfx1151's missing `v_cvt_u32_u16_e32` encoding.** The existing typed 32-bit destination/16-bit source form preserves low/high-half source selection and rejects undefined opcodes. Historical C1 code remains historical-source coverage, not current gfx1151 qualification; GPU arithmetic and serving defaults are unchanged.
- **Fixed: PeaceMaker emulation implements native-C1 scalar, true16, carry and execution-mask operations.** Scalar-64 shifts and overlapping moves, signed immediate overflow and high multiplication, EXEC save/intersection, true16 half writes and explicit vector carry use the instruction's real flag and aliasing rules. Existing exact branch, comparison, d16-load and dual-integer handlers are registered; inactive lanes and unrelated flags remain intact. GPU arithmetic and serving defaults are unchanged.
- **Fixed: Qwen3.5 MoE (A3B, Ornith) DFlash and native MTP produced corrupted greedy output.** The batched MoE DeltaNet layer body had stopped writing the GDN tape (a regression since 420065b05), so the rollback after a partially accepted draft replayed the previous window's q/k/v/α/β into every MoE DeltaNet layer and corrupted the recurrent state. On Strix Halo, A3B DFlash τ fell from 7.47 to 2.5 with the reply cut off after 15 tokens. The tape copy is restored, and A3B DFlash and MTP greedy output is byte-identical to 9077c8b06 again. Dense models were not affected.
- **Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 dense tensor parallelism on the generic mesh executor now splits attention and DeltaNet heads like the hand dense-TP route, and is byte-identical to it under emulation (#927 item 4, step 3, HIPF-142).** New `SplitRule::HeadMixer` for head-parallel mixers: whole input, head-split input projections (`HeadSharded`, `FusedQkv`, `ColumnShard { axis: 0 }`) and state, `RowShard { axis: 1 }` output projection, Partial output reduced by its consumer (a fused `AllReduceAdd` for an `Accumulate`); admission refuses, allocation-free, a mixed policy and head or KV-head counts that do not split evenly. `DeltaNetMixerOp` and `GatedAttentionOp` take `output: MixerOutput`: `Residual` is the fused single-device body, `Write(out)` the former hand `dense_tp_{deltanet,attention}_partial` body moved verbatim (compacted KV and a prerotated input refused), which the hand decode route now runs. `qwen35::mesh_tp` loads ranks with the hand route's layouts (`tp_rank_layouts`: `dense_tp_rank_layouts`, even splits only) and runs two `AllReduceAdd`s per layer. On gfx1151 with `HIPFIRE_EMULATE_GPUS=2` and `=4`, `qwen3.5-9b.mq4` and `qwen3.8-27b.mq4-xt` (16-token prefill epoch, then 16 decode epochs) produce logits byte-identical to `forward_prefill_dense_tp` + `forward_scratch_dense_tp` over the same shards and the plain card's greedy tokens 17/17; the hand route's dumps and launch traces are unchanged by the move. Product dense TP (serve, bench, MTP and DFlash dense TP) stays on the hand route until the executor has decode graph capture, uneven TP3/TP5 layouts, the peer-rooted reduction and verify captures.
- **Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 dense models run tensor-parallel prefill and decode on the generic mesh executor, under emulation (#927 item 4, step 2, HIPF-142).** `qwen35::mesh_tp` declares one step program for both routes: replicated embedding, mixers and head; per layer `GatedMlp` (`SplitRule::GatedMlp`, `Product` ladder) writing the rank's FFN partial, and a residual `Accumulate` that the splitter turns into one rank-ordered `AllReduceAdd` into `x`. A decode epoch runs it over one token on the decode scratch, a prefill epoch over up to the batch scratch's rows (batched mixers as in the hand dense-TP prefill, the `Product` rows' TP `Partial` epilogue; the logits are the last row's). Each rank holds every attention and DeltaNet head and its even block of the FFN intermediate in whole G256 groups; ranks are built only by `Qwen35TpRank::load`, which derives the layout (`ffn_rank_layout`) and loads the weight slice with it, so `Qwen35TpBindings` checks the slice each rank holds, not a label. The bindings check the ranks against the plan of exactly those shards and refuse, before any launch, a prefill past the batch scratch, tokens that disagree with the epoch rows, a KV end past `physical_cap`, sessions and checkpoints. Prefix repair is refused through a new host-only `MeshStepBindings::admits_prefix_repair` capability that `Gpus::repair_mesh_prefix` checks before the first callback, so the refusal leaves the mesh healthy (Qwen4 TP bindings declare it too); before, the binding's error poisoned and quarantined the mesh. 1-row Prefill epochs (a `rows % cap == 1` prompt tail, or one token after a prefill or a decode) write their KV row at its own position through the shared attention fix of #937. On gfx1151 with `HIPFIRE_EMULATE_GPUS=2` and `=4`, `qwen3.5-9b.mq4` and `qwen3.8-27b.mq4-xt` (16-token prefill epoch, then 16 forced-token epochs, two of them 1-row Prefill epochs) are byte-identical to a single-device run of the same shards that adds the partials in rank order, and match the plain single card's greedy tokens 17/17 (max logit difference 0.055–0.067). Attention and DeltaNet head splits and a loader route follow; the hand dense-TP route is unchanged.
- **Dense FFN tensor parallelism: a real `GatedMlp` split rule and the first emulated TP forward through the generic mesh executor (#927 item 3).** `SplitRule::GatedMlp` splits gate/up by rows (`ColumnShard { axis: 0 }`) and down by columns (`RowShard { axis: 1 }`) along the intermediate, with the input whole; the output is a partial sum that its consumer reduces (a fused `AllReduceAdd` for an `Accumulate`, else an `AllReduce`), and all-`Replicate` weights or a single TP part keep it whole, so Qwen4 PP plans are unchanged. Admission refuses, allocation-free, a mixed policy, a down weight that does not share the gate/up intermediate, `intermediate % (parts * group) != 0` and the `SandwichWide` ladder (`MlpLadder::tp_shardable`; its post-norm epilogue cannot take a partial sum). The Qwen4 step graph now declares each dense layer's FFN weights. On the Qwen4 dense developer profile, `Qwen4Weights::shard_dense_ffn` (which records its `(rank, parts)`), `qwen4_tp_plan` (BF16 dense FFN only; a packed FFN or a MoE profile is refused before anything is allocated) and `Qwen4TpBindings` (checked against the plan of exactly these shards: rank `i` holds slice `i`, every gate/up/down shape, one `AllReduce` per dense layer) run each rank's program in one segment per collective (`forward_mesh_chunk` takes the op segment and refuses an out-of-order or repeated one) with every non-FFN op replicated. A TP rank's FFN writes its F32 partial (`MlpStorage::Bf16SourcePartial`, set only on sharded weights), so the sum is rounded once by the HC write, as on one card, instead of once per rank before the sum. Emulated TP2 and TP4 on gfx1151 are byte-identical to a single-device run of the same shards that sums the FFN partials in rank order. Against the plain single card over 481 teacher-forced positions, the 2-layer developer fixtures are bitwise identical, and the deeper ones agree on argmax at 481/481 positions (4 layers) and 474/481 (TP2) to 479/481 (TP4) (8 layers); what remains is the f32 order of the rank sum (per-rank partials added in rank order instead of one GEMV), which occasionally flips a BF16 rounding at the HC write. With each rank's partial rounded to BF16 the 8-layer agreement was 434-436/481. The loader has no Qwen4 TP route yet, and sessions, checkpoints and prefix repair are refused on TP.
- **Internal: the Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 dense FFN runs as the shared `GatedMlp` op on a new `Product` ladder, decode and batched rows; `SwigluFfnOp`, `Step::SwigluFfn` and the public batched FFN entry are gone (#927 item 4, step 1, HIPF-142).** The `Product` ladder admits a pre-norm, SiLU and F32 storage with two outputs: `Residual` and `Write` (the dense-TP partial). Decode (one row, `Step::GatedMlp`) runs the former `SwigluFfn` body moved verbatim (fused SiLU·rotate + SwiGLU-residual GEMV for MQ, residual GEMV for HFQ, GEMV + add for the rotated formats, CPU-offload split); the hand dense-TP FFN partial now runs through its `Write` arm. Rows (prefill, DFlash verify, dense-TP prefill) run through `gated_mlp::execute_product_rows`, which checks the op against its batch scratch and drives slice 2's batched ladder (`Residual` / TP `Partial` epilogue); HIP error codes are kept. `MlpLadder::Product` is TP-shardable. No launch or numeric change on gfx1151: oracle dumps (prefill + decode logits, GDN/conv state) and the per-launch kernel/grid trace are byte-identical to the base for 9B mq4 (37 and 2100 rows, DFlash hidden capture), 27B mq4-xt (2100 rows at 512-row chunks), 13 4B formats covering every down-projection arm, and the hand dense-TP route (TP2/TP4) under emulation; greedy serve transcripts (27B mq4-xt DFlash battery, 9B 2k prompt) are identical.
- **Fixed: Qwen3.5 dense TP writes a 1-row prefill chunk's K/V at its own position.** A prompt with `len % prefill_max_batch_tp == 1`, an MTP non-tape replay of one accepted row, or a DFlash non-tape replay with no accepted drafts ran a 1-row batched attend. The attention family then took the decode writer and attend, which read the decode scratch `pos_buf` that a prefill never uploads: the row landed in a stale slot (or faulted) and its own slot stayed empty. `AttnParams` now takes a one-row call's position from its `positions` tensor; decode (no `positions`) and multi-row calls are byte-identical. (HIPF-151)
- **Fixed: share verified-artifact cache identity with developer quality tools.** CLI and runtime use one schema-compatible cache; read-only digest lookups refuse missing, stale or malformed records without rereading model payloads.
- **Developer tooling: make the existing Flash-Next quality campaign target explicit.** Device, kernel-pack, placement and cached artifact identity are bound to the selected target; original teachers and quality bounds are unchanged.
- **Fixed: recording inventory includes the existing native-FP8 Q-preparation admission helper.** Predicate classification, capture behavior and serving defaults are unchanged.
- **Generic mesh executor: pure tensor-parallel meshes and their `AllReduceAdd`/`AllReduce` collectives (#927 item 2).** `Gpus::provision_mesh_edges` now admits a pure TP mesh (PP = EP = 1) beside pure PP; TP×PP and any EP axis are refused before any mesh state is written. A TP collective runs once every rank reaches it, over the group of every rank in rank order, with the hand dense-TP contract `x + (p0 + p1 + …)` on every rank. The transport is fixed at provisioning, one route each: when every rank pair passes `qualify_peer` (or is one device under `HIPFIRE_EMULATE_GPUS`), each rank pulls every partial with the same kernel copy `qualify_peer` checks (never `hipMemcpyPeer`, which writes nothing into allocations made after peer enable) and folds the sum locally; otherwise the hand route's host-staged rank-order reduction. RCCL is not used. Scratch, events, host staging and kernels are prepared at provisioning; the whole epoch is validated before the first enqueue and a failed drain quarantines as for PP edges. `BoundaryIo` gains `into` (the `AllReduceAdd` target) and `Gpus::mesh_tp_epoch()` names the group's descriptor epoch; the Qwen4 PP adapter sets `into: None` and is otherwise unchanged. Under `HIPFIRE_EMULATE_GPUS=2` and `=4` on gfx1151 both transports are byte-identical to the single-device rank-order sum over three epochs with distinct partials.
- **Fixed: Qwen3.5 dense TP writes a 1-row prefill chunk's K/V at its own position.** A prompt with `len % prefill_max_batch_tp == 1`, an MTP non-tape replay of one accepted row, or a DFlash non-tape replay with no accepted drafts ran a 1-row batched attend. The attention family then took the decode writer and attend, which read the decode scratch `pos_buf` that a prefill never uploads: the row landed in a stale slot (or faulted) and its own slot stayed empty. `AttnParams` now takes a one-row call's position from its `positions` tensor; decode (no `positions`) and multi-row calls are byte-identical. (HIPF-151)
- **A3B native FP8 FA2 Q-resident specialization for H16/KV2/D256.** Ports the dense qresident-v2 FP8-Q/KT48 FA2 body to the A3B geometry with its own Direct (`attention_fp8_e4m3_fa2_gqa_qresident_v2_q8_a3b_gfx1201`) and Range (`attention_fp8_e4m3_fa2_gqa_qresident_v2_q8_range_a3b_gfx1201`) symbols in one module; Q arrives from the upstream F32 fused-Q prep as E4M3 codes plus F32 per-head scales (not the older F16-first packet path), consumed from one Raw `fa_q_batch` allocation as a code plane plus scale plane with checked total-row offsets and live-prefix views. General true-prefill tails (2..=32768 rows, tiny tails included) take the whole-batch native Direct before the F32 fallback; the legacy `fa_ragged_packet_split` tail-64..=511 admission is unchanged, and the explicit Range path supports 1+ rows but GEN Range is unobserved, so no claim that tiny callers use Range. Persistent KV stays native FP8 E4M3; KV selection, FA2 eligibility and resident IU4 stay independent and stackable, and AR/verify plus legacy H24/F16/Q8 routes are unchanged. `FP8_KV_QUALIFIED` F16-Q rows are unchanged and are not FP8-Q qualification; no new knob or default is added. PP16000 scope only: four original opt-ins (`HIPFIRE_MOE_ROTATE_I4_PM=1`, `HIPFIRE_PREFILL_IU4_C8_PM=1`, `HIPFIRE_GDN_CHUNK_PREP_PM=1`, `HIPFIRE_MOE_SHARED_DOWN_SIGMOID_EPI=1`), not the stock default; qwen3.6-35b-a3b-d53.mq4rs median 17478.9 and ornith-1.5-35b-a3b-d53.mq4rs median 17383.8 strict medians, 6 fresh processes total, 18 measured samples (9 per model; 3 per process after 2 warmups), source dc307/tree fb056, CLI efa37fc4 / daemon 8a43d456, immutable kit 860802; joined-primitive plus same-codec eager/graph full-state comparison passed on both models over raw state scope. The actual 522/128 GEN smoke was a coherent bounded prefix with mid-Python/length-runaway true, not a complete answer. Quality plus all three final CPU gates are REQUIRED (throughput/state alone are not qualification); not a stock gain, default, release, tag, or SITE claim.
- **A3B native FP8 FA2 Q-resident prefill is ~13% faster per layer on gfx1201, byte-identical.** The Direct/Range bodies fill the V tile with one 4-aligned `u32` load per key and transpose the 8-key x 4-dim byte block with `v_perm_b32` (instead of 32 byte-gather loads per thread), load K as one 16-byte chunk per thread across all 24 waves, raise wave priority around the WMMA bursts (`s_setprio`) and skip compute in waves whose 16 rows all lie past the run's last query. Per query row the KV tiles, the online-softmax arithmetic and every operand byte are unchanged: the A3B native oracle gained the pp16000 chunk geometry (8192 rows from 0, 7808 rows from 8192; candidate digests recorded) and matches the independent reference and the previous kernel on all 32 cells; the dense H24 entries compile to identical code. Kernel microbench (R9700, one layer): 8192 rows/ctx 8192 3.82 -> 3.29 ms, 7808 rows/ctx 16000 10.97 -> 9.50 ms.

- **Strix Halo (gfx1151): Flash-Next speculative verify takes the PeaceMaker multi-column row kernels; native MTP decode +6 % (HIPF-135).** A Qwen4 verify forward (2..=8 rows, native MTP and DFlash2) and the DFlash2 draft head ran the incumbent HIP rows kernels, which re-read the activations once per weight row and fall off a cliff at 7-8 rows (`gemv_q8_0_k8_rows_r7/r8` compile rolled: 120 µs vs 24 µs at 4 rows). They now take the lane step's `qwen4_lane_rows_pm` kernels (`HIPFIRE_FN_LANE_PM_ROWS`, kill switch `0`), each column byte-identical to the 1-row incumbent, so tokens do not change (greedy MTP and DFlash2 B=4/B=8 equal AR on 10 prompts × 512 tokens). `qwen3.8-flash-next-gptq3.mq4`, daemon, greedy, 20 tau prompts × ≤1024 tokens, A/B/A against the previous head: MTP default 52.3 / 52.2 → 55.6 tok/s; DFlash2 (mq4v2 draft) block 4 43.8 / 43.7 → 46.3, block 8 33.4 / 33.5 → 42.5 (both with the selector re-grid below). Kernel trace per DFlash2 window: block 4 66.4 → 61.3 ms, block 8 111.2 → 86.5 ms.
- **Strix Halo (gfx1151): the DFlash2 selector top-K and the batched argmax take the re-gridded row selectors.** `select_regrid_enabled` now admits exact gfx1151 next to gfx1201 (`HIPFIRE_SELECT_REGRID_OFF=1` opts out); `examples/test_select_regrid` is byte-identical to the shipping kernels on gfx1151 (210 launches, ties and NaNs included) and times 15 × 248,320 K=16 top-K 1,356 → 62 µs and 16 × 248,320 argmax 181 → 24 µs. `topk_values_batched_f32_verified_regrid` is gone: the online draft tuner calls `topk_values_batched_f32`, which now takes the same arch gate.
- **Flash-Next DFlash2 verifies only the draft's confident prefix: block 8 42.5 → 52.0 tok/s greedy on Strix Halo (HIPF-135).** Every DFlash2 window verified its whole block, and each extra verify row costs Flash-Next about 6 ms on gfx1151. A window now verifies the longest draft prefix whose running product of selector confidences (softmax at temperature 1 of the selected candidate over the row's top-16 scores, `DflashCandidateProposal::confidence`) stays at or above 0.5, at least one draft; the draft forward still proposes the whole block. The cut is draft-side only, so greedy output stays AR's (10 prompts × 512 tokens, blocks 4 and 8) and sampled acceptance keeps AR's law. Same 20 prompts: block 8 acceptance length 3.56 → 2.95 and 42.5 → 52.0 tok/s greedy (sampled 50.7), block 4 46.3 → 48.2; native MTP default stays faster (55.8). Qwen4 `speculation.dflash_block = auto` therefore resolves to 8 (was 4).
- **Flash-Next can decode with the incoai DFlash2 draft: `--spec dflash --model-draft qwen38-flash-next-dflash2.<f16|mq4v2>.hfq` (HIPF-132).** Native MTP stays the default; DFlash2 runs only when requested with its draft (an arch-20 `dflash_convert` artifact with the candidate selector), on a single card with GPU-resident experts (EP, PP and CPU-hosted routed experts refuse it). The drafter is the new target-generic `hipfire_runtime::dflash2_spec::Dflash2Speculator` (name `dflash2`): one non-causal sliding-window draft forward over `[seed, MASK×(B-1)]`, the target's head over the draft rows, and the selector's walk through each row's top-16. Greedy accepts the target-argmax prefix, so the output is the AR stream; sampled draws from the selector's softmax and accepts with sparse-q rejection sampling against the AR sampler's own law (temperature, top_k, top_p, min_p); penalized requests stay AR (the route takes only a `dflash2` speculator, `GenerationRouteInputs::speculator_is_dflash2`). The Qwen4 target captures the draft's `target_layer_ids` (5, 15, 25, 35, 45) as each layer's completed output averaged over the four hyper-connection streams (new `hc_mean_capture_f32` kernel), launched between the interpreter's steps through the new `MoeStepHooks::before_step`, so the verify program and its fusions are the ones it runs without capture. A capturing prefill is planned GPU-only: the NPU trunk pair executor and the S1 layer-major prefill lower their own steps, so a DFlash2 request bypasses both (on Strix Halo, prompts above one 8192-row chunk used to fail on the default NPU route). A partial accept keeps its rows with the GDN row-capture rollback instead of a replay; a window that fails after its verify rolls the target back (`SpecTarget::abandon_verify`), and a reset drops a stale verify ticket, so one failed window no longer wedges the load. The host keeps only the draft's 2048-row feature window (at most 2 × 2048 rows × 51,200 B), not one row per context token. Width: `speculation.dflash_block`; Qwen4 `auto` is 8 (the fastest on gfx1151 with the confidence cut below), an explicit width is clamped to the GPU's row-exact verify rows (8 on gfx1151). Known gap: the DFlash2 route never reuses the Qwen4 session/prefix cache, so every request prefills cold (HIPF-143). Measured on Strix Halo (gfx1151, gptq3 target): token ids equal AR on 10 prompts × 512 tokens at B=4 and B=8, and decoded text equal AR on 40 thinking chats × ≤1024 tokens; acceptance length (completion tokens / verify steps) on the card's 5 tasks (8 prompts each, xhigh thinking) is 2.93 greedy / 2.90 sampled at B=4 against the card's 2.83–3.26, and native MTP at K=3 reaches 2.91 / 2.80 here. Decode on a 10-prompt subset: AR 32.5 tok/s, DFlash2 B=4 43.1 / 44.4 (mq4v2 draft; f16 draft 40.9 / 40.7), native MTP (default) 52.4 / 49.9, so DFlash2 is not yet faster than native MTP on this box.
- **Native FP8 FA2 preserves F16 Q while reducing its direct kernel to one 32-KiB K-then-V stage and 224 VGPRs.** All five waves rendezvous at four ordered barrier pairs; the 60-byte ABI, F16-Q arithmetic and independent FP8-KV selection are preserved. Q8 retains its original image and 64-KiB launch contract. The regressing streamed down-NT8 experiment is excluded and resident IU4 down stays NT4. The matched native-Auto PP16000 diagnostic measured 13,100.7 tok/s with resident NT4; the strict 16,000–20,000 tok/s target remains unmet, and host-mapped NT8 performance is not established.
- **Walked HIP plans now bind live current registry recipes rather than historical whole-source text.** Historical captures and pins are retained; existing kind, compiler flags, profile, symbol, shape, admission and pack contracts, plus strict embedded-image SHA checks, remain enforced. No kernel arithmetic, public API or feature-default changes.
- **A3B resident-IU4 prefill admits the guarded 8192-row rung with full-width loader/PBS/Q16 reservation and unchanged fail-closed memory checks.** Native Auto FP8 KV and FA2 remain independent, stackable optimizations. Core Q8/FP8 eager-versus-graph full-state parity and eligible native generation checks passed. The PP16000 diagnostic measured 12,527.9 tok/s, below the strict 16,000–20,000 target; it is not the historical single PP4096 sample of 16,006.0 tok/s. Runtime binaries retain their actual 5c1c/529798 identities; later formatting/map corrections do not relabel them.
- **Fixed: S1 quality campaign binds the sealed kernel pack through the actual cold lookup and fails closed on runtime JIT/fallback evidence.** Each `run-phase` installs the sealed pack at the resolver's private `HOME/.hipfire/bin/kernels` lookup (the existing gap-cell pattern; no global compiler change), and `run-phase` plus `report` now require every actually-resolved kernel object to be an `indexed package verified` hit under the sealed pack dir, with an empty phase-private kernel cache and no compiler-fallback markers in stderr; any runtime JIT, fallback or unbound used-code identity fails the phase and the report's `mechanical_pass`. The bare `moe_scatter_stable_top10` caller now resolves the already-registered canonical gfx1100 twin module, so all 41 same-name runtime sources match their pack index with no duplicate pack entry. Math, precision and defaults are unchanged.
  - S1 `--execution-recipe` makes the target, tool/source ELF, source-bound pack, reference origin and expected placement/resource contract explicit. Genuine prior-SHA `VerifiedCache` provenance stays in `HIPFIRE_HOME` while kernel lookup uses a cold private `HOME`; missing/stale/wrong-digest provenance refuses without a fresh payload hash or manufactured cache hit. The original gfx1100 teacher, seven primitive cases and KL bounds (16K ≤ 0.03948458079446915; 4K ≤ 0.027284316982763658) are unchanged: a gfx1201 target is not a new teacher or cross-architecture greedy proof. Hardware placement, quality and qualification remain pending.

- **Flash-Next on gfx1100: aggregate NT1 symmetric-IU4 MoE prefill route, a default-OFF candidate (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_MOE_SYM_IU4=1`; `=0`/unset is the incumbent F16 WMMA route, byte for byte).** The route runs prefill chunks of 512+ rows, and the S1 slow-link layer-major host-layer windows (`AggregateSymIu4`, receipt window route `aggregate-sym-iu4`), on the grouped IU4 gate/up and down GEMMs (the shipped gfx1100 NT1 module and K3 down producer) for symmetric MQ4 artifacts; an unsupported forced request prints one diagnostic and keeps the incumbent. The S1 admission resolves the route before the census from the artifact source headers, charges both A4 sidecars with no window F16 input, and refuses a final-header shortfall before serving; the receipt's `moe_iu4` names the route, descriptor, tile counts and header verdicts. The numerics intentionally differ from the F16 route, and no 16K/32K or product performance is claimed.

Actual eligible headers, descriptor, rows and resource admission determine whether the feature is active. FP8 KV and FA2 remain independent, stackable choices; the A3B H16/KV2/D256 FA2 specialization is not an applied Flash-Next H24/KV2/D256 QSA FA2 port or evidence of a Flash-Next gain.
- **S1 slow-link prefill: developer switch for WHICH layers stay resident (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SLOWLINK_RESIDENT_LAYERS`, default `front`).** The admitted resident COUNT `N` is unchanged; the switch picks the set: unset or `front` is the incumbent leading layers `0..N`, `spread` is `floor(k*T/N) + floor(T/(2N)) + 1` clamped to `T-1` (48 layers, 9 resident: 3, 8, 13, 19, 24, 29, 35, 40, 45), or a comma list of exactly `N` distinct layer indices. Any other value, an empty one included, fails the S1 load naming the variable. New `expert_residency::place_routed_experts_set` host-maps every routed expert outside the set (MTP always host); `place_routed_experts` and the unset/`front` placement and stderr are unchanged.

- **Fixed: the serve harness stamps `kv_mode_effective` from the loader's actual split `effective K=… V=…` line when no loaded ACK is present.** The consumer fallback only matched the singular `effective KV=…` grammar, so the real `effective K=q8, effective V=q8` (and `effective K=q8 V=q8`) lines left `kv_mode_resolved=UNOBSERVED`; it now stamps the canonical mode when K and V agree, and stays UNOBSERVED on mismatch, partial, or requested-only lines. ACK-first precedence and the singular fallback are unchanged.

It does not change production routing, row admission, or defaults.
- **Fixed: PeaceMaker emulation recognizes the existing unsigned-compare and VCC-branch handlers.** Registers `v_cmp_le_u32_e32` and `s_cbranch_vccnz` so those instructions are dispatched instead of rejected as unsupported; handler math and kernel defaults are unchanged.
- **Fixed: PeaceMaker emulation dispatches the existing signed `s_cmp_le_i32`, explicit-encoding unsigned comparisons, shift and byte conversion, and mixed FMA handlers.** Native row-tile CPU oracles no longer refuse those implemented instructions as unsupported; handler arithmetic, qualification refusals and serving defaults are unchanged.
- **Fixed: PeaceMaker definedness checks cover every execution-mask group and solve loop flow in reverse postorder.** ROBDD predicates preserve group-wise lane coverage, and reverse-postorder iteration handles backedges without changing kernel or serving defaults.
- **Internal: CPU-split trace brackets share the caller's join-entry clock.** The existing `HIPFIRE_CPU_SPLIT_TRACE=1` diagnostic reports optional middle, scatter, retirement and release boundaries in nanoseconds from one host `Instant`, and the actual device join-word address. Empty CPU phases remain absent, and the JSON record is emitted only after the successful CP-wait release. These are host clock observations, not GPU timestamps or proof of exposed CPU work; split math, ownership, defaults and the disabled trace path are unchanged.
- **`eval_hipfire --scoring-mode prefill-prompt` (qwen35, opt-in): whole-window KLD through the plain prompt-prefill route.** `prefill-whole` captures its hidden rows through `forward_prefill_batch`'s verify capture, which selects the speculative-verify kernels (`DispatchWorkload::SpeculativeVerify`; the GDN chunk scan is never admitted), and the split default `prefill` mode does the same for its scored-region call (its prefix call captures nothing and has plain prompt-prefill admission). `prefill-prompt` runs the same one-call whole-window plan through `forward_prefill_batch_capture_hidden`, whose chunk planning, admission (GDN chunk scan included where a plain prefill admits it: the chunk scan's row admission requires rows >= 64 and either rows <= 512 or commit stride 512) and `DispatchWorkload::Standard` are exactly a production prompt prefill's, so it measures the route a served prompt takes. The existing `prefill`, `prefill-whole` and `per-token` modes are unchanged (forward calls source-pinned by `eval_common`'s tests), and kldseqs from `prefill-prompt` are not comparable with `prefill-whole` kldseqs where a route is capture-gated. `--help` and the `--scoring-mode` error now state every mode's admission. No new environment variable.
- **A3B native FP8 KV `auto` default on the qualified route only.** Carry the codec-aware PeaceMaker prefill/F5 writer integration and corrected FA leaf, with independent native IEEE/NaN/scale and long-context writer oracles plus a same-codec eager/native-graph state oracle. - **Flash-Next native MTP: causal per-row margin evidence for the derived depth chooser (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_MTP_DERIVED_K=1`, developer-only, default OFF).** After each drafted row the single re-solve re-keys every measured legal depth `1..=hi` to the `NativeMargin { observed_depth, bin }` cell (`bins [0,0.25) LtQuarter`, `[0.25,1.5) LtOnePointFive`, `[1.5,3) LtThree`, `[3,6) LtSix`, `[6,+inf) GeSix`; negative/non-finite margins carry no evidence and fall back to the unconditional depth with an explicit `derived_k_margin_dropped` trace). Only the legal hi governs the domain; unsupported margin cells keep the pre-decision evidence; the commit ages residuals once through the runtime `observe_with_margins` path (reused scratch, no per-row allocation). Commit lines carry truthful `margin_evidence:"measured"` exactly when the re-solve used a measured cell, else `"unmeasured"`. The lab forced-window receipt adds `native_draft_margins` (native only: the actual captured head-row vector, `Some` finite/non-negative else `None`, never padded) plus `outcome_mismatch` (requested/actual mismatch returns the observed measurement as a raw incomplete receipt, never a priced window or an `Err`). The policy binds the loader's immutable measured-load descriptor once per request (`with_measured_load_identity: Option<Arc<Qwen4MeasuredLoadIdentity>>`, cached canonical JSON compared to the runtime admitted identity; missing/mismatch keeps the real incumbent) and invalidates on copy-lane mode flip or AR-reference fallback/record transition (`fn_measured_reference_supported` against the live retained fallback/record state). No measured book is populated today (bootstrap empty): nothing is width-64 shipping-qualified. `native_mtp_proposal_drafts(63)` sizes 63 drafts (64 rows, direct-capture reservation before placement) with derived off and the copy lane off; the incumbent execution tables and prunes are unchanged.

This change does not add Qwen3.x or DFlash trace behavior, kernels, or device-to-host transfers.
- **Flash-Next native MTP gains opt-in derived-rate depth/AR selection (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_MTP_DERIVED_K=1`, default OFF).** The shared controller chooses expected emitted tokens per total-window cost over feasible native and copy depths, preserving the AR floor, probe budget, shallow re-probes, retirement and copy contracts. Actual allocated storage and qualified per-call rows, explicit user overrides, codec/reference-mode support, context and remaining budget bound the domain; neither the incumbent depth nor an old 8/10-element statistics buffer is an economic ceiling. Historical phase/width price data remain unchanged, and missing same-mode measured prices retain the incumbent with an unsupported reason rather than invented costs. Default qualification remains eight GPU rows and four CPU-owned rows; the 64-row executor extent permits at most 63 drafts plus the seed, not a forced K63 policy. Reference-parity hooks execute real proposal, lookup, confirmation, verify, rollback and commit work; receipts distinguish timing-only experiments from numerical and shipping qualification. Sampled requests and unsupported state/route modes retain their existing admission boundaries. No widened performance or default capability is claimed.
  - **Frozen measured-price contract:** active generic `fn_measured_*` consumers use measured records first, with the legacy OffPool profile only as an explicit data-only fallback in `fn_width_cost_v1.rs`. OnCopy n-gram total prices are separately keyed by the pre-window confirmation-needed state: `true` includes one head confirmation step, established-source `false` includes zero; totals are neither mixed nor charged for confirmation twice. Mode-aware conditional depth counts use real OnCopy accepted-prefix outcomes with EOS/terminal censorship; missing same-mode counts are unsupported, never the old 0.8 prior or OffPool counts. Post-profile refreshes change measured payload data only. The reference-parity `oracle::dev_run_forced_window` receipt records requested/actual drafts, offer and accepted prefix, source/cost mode, executor-latched route, requested/actual confirmation, terminal status and synchronized total time; requested width alone is not execution proof.

A present generic slot never fills missing prices or counts from historical same-card data; native parents must match the admitted identity. The shipping bootstrap book remains empty and unadmitted, with no default or width promotion.
