It applies only to exact gfx1100 on a measured narrow discrete link with the qualified MQ4 packed recipe, a long enough context and a request of at least 1,537 rows; a short context, a fast link, unified memory or an unmeasured link never selects it under either selector, and expert/tensor/pipeline parallelism, the CPU expert splice, a selected NPU trunk and the other unsupported modes stay on the incumbent before any reserve or mutation. **Measured base on the XTX at pp16384 is 1,738.9-1,750.2 tok/s (accepted release, ~1.87x beta); 2,000 tok/s is not a release block.** Route-relative quality caps are same-route decode caps, never teacher-paired: mean KL(beta4096||candidate) 16K 0.03206548313867323 against the benign-beta upper 0.03948458079446915, and 4K 0.024549946338726408 against 0.027284316982763658, with 7/7 same-route determinism and coherent decoded text. The required followup stack (ordered placement + IU4 + QSA, thin 2054) is not promotion and not a base gate: QSA currently fails 4K (0.029107700567698017, excess +0.001823383584934359) and no waiver exists. No f32 GDN carry ships in base and none is planned: the f32 carry is DROPPED entirely and is never resurrected; the inert q8wmma trunk lever is removed. D2 keeps its truth: decode and <=4-row verify only, armed by the per-load measured default or an explicit `memory.offload_exec`, unchanged by S1. Serve-kit note: thinking-off battery requests derive the off sentinel cap 1 (None), never an explicit 0 that the daemon reads as uncapped on effort-carrying requests. The accepted base is an observed historical exception only (two fresh processes, six samples per arm) and claims no final base CI/serve PASS; a qualified new-stack claim needs ABBAAB with 3 fresh processes per arm after quality passes, flat all-nine candidate medians >= 2000 tok/s. The 1,400 tok/s pp16384 figure was the original historical S1 gate floor and is kept only as history below. H0's one-layer synthetic transfer experiment (~190 ms per host layer at 8,192 rows, copy-bound at 99.9% of 7.09 GB/s) bounds the possible gain but its 1,407 tok/s projection is inferred, not a measured full-path result. The route is not bit-identical to the incumbent's 8,192-row manifest; promotion requires, on the XTX, same-route determinism, exact greedy ids against the beta autoregressive route, state/session/abort oracles, the paired 24-sequence code24 decode KLD verdict and a matched fresh-process A/B. Status: the last correctness hold (j1759) is **incomplete**: its primitive 80 s cap expired during the 82 s model load, only `identity.manifest` passed and every other check was skipped, so there is no correctness or memory pass; the replacement correctness hold (j1761) then **failed** at its first payload primitive with a real `hipMalloc` out-of-memory after ~110 s (identity and load passed; all seven primitive cases share that one initialization error and no product state cell ran, so product headroom was not exercised), which the loader now answers with an explicit primitive-self-test versus product admission purpose; a further hold is approved only after the CPU admission proof, the route stays default OFF. Its memory criterion is the minimum observed free VRAM in the product state cells, at least 512 MiB (536,870,912 B) over the whole run, from an independent 20 ms sysfs used/total sampler plus the in-process `hipMemGetInfo` pre-load/post-load/end points; primitive peak, owned bytes and the residual are informational only (not driver attribution). Validation harness: `qwen4_slowlink_gate` (`--mode primitives|state|product|perf`), `qwen4_greedy_ids --receipt`, `qwen4_kld pair`, `qwen4_parity --mode slowlink-state`; see `docs/VALIDATION.md`.
  - [Historical development receipts below: NOT current acceptance; no final base CI/serve PASS is claimed.] Adaptive admission: Hold 1 `j1811` failed at admission with no primitive, state, headroom or seal result; the fresh free device memory after the host link and runtime initialization was 25,560,088,576 B against 25,713,180,672 B before it (a measured 153,092,096 B interval, never an assumed constant), which put the same-purpose primitive projection 39,483,884 B short of a fixed ten-layer floor. That floor is removed. The loader keeps the largest resident layer count that fits (ten preferred) and `qwen4_slowlink_gate`'s `load.placement` check carries a scalar admission witness read from the same shared quote (free before initialization, free at admission, measured initialization interval, non-expert, backed layer and joint reserve bytes, needed and slack bytes, the ten-layer preferred deficit as information) and refuses a missing, tampered, oversubscribed or non-maximal one: the selected count must fit, one more must not, and a host layer must remain. The sealed manifest's resident count and census are labelled reference data, never an acceptance target; the receipt reports the actual accounting beside them. Route receipts close resident plus host layers on the 48-layer trunk with a per-host-layer byte bound instead of a fixed 38-host-layer cap. The 512 MiB safety margin, 1 GiB runtime budget, 768/512 tiles, all seven primitives, state, headroom and greedy/KLD thresholds are unchanged and S1 stays default OFF; this records no hardware result.
  - Hold procedure: every S1 hold cell on a branch that carries the D2 default switch must set `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_D2_DEFAULT=0` and record itself as the non-default arm, alongside the H1 pin `HIPFIRE_OFFLOAD_EXEC=pcie`; this branch has no such switch and reads no such variable, and a hold on it is not a shipped-default result.
  - Primitive diagnostics initialize and report each requested case independently. A setup error belongs to that case, with an unknown mismatch count, and no longer discards earlier results or appears as seven arithmetic failures; a global refusal is reported once, leaving the required cases unproved.
  - Hold 1 `j1766` reached ten resident layers and a 1,536-row tile without an observed OOM, then failed the slab-only prepared-call guard on the real aggregate qt44/qt53 artifact. This is a product route gap, not an arithmetic mismatch: state, product headroom and decode/greedy cells did not run. Aggregate/slab capability coverage and independent primitive reports must be proved on CPU before the next correctness attempt; S1 remains default OFF.
  - Partial-window route views use the window's actual decode, F32-tail and slab few-row cohorts, bounded by the admitted full-window reserve without changing tile exits. A three-row aggregate remainder after 16K is an F32-only window, not a 48-row cohort or a forced WMMA tile.
  - Aggregate and slab are distinct capability-selected routes. Aggregate windows retain the incumbent's WMMA arithmetic at 512 or more routing rows, F32 grouped/indexed arithmetic at 2–511 and one-row decode, all on the same leased payload sweep. A separate count array covers the full 3,066-row F32-tail bound without packed-count truncation or an extra count barrier.
  - S1 count readbacks retain their host targets until the compute stream is confirmed joined, including a failed second enqueue. An unconfirmed join quarantines the targets instead of freeing memory still writable by the device; the original error is preserved.
  - Hold 1 `j1778` failed S1 initialization on the route-region allocation and the state cell then ran the incumbent until its cap expired, losing its timings; this is a proof and ownership correction, not a promotion, and S1 stays default OFF. The placement census and the runtime now share one F16-shadow capability predicate (the census had charged the real artifact's 1,298,923,520 B of model-lifetime BF16-to-F16 shadows only on exact gfx1201, so gfx1100 charged none; the 512-row threshold and cold-owner bound are unchanged), and admission evaluates tile and resident layers jointly without lowering the >=10 resident floor, the 16,384-row window or the lookahead charge (the tile is now the admitted purpose profile, below). Every admitted S1 owner is bound once at the selected load and requests only consume it; an allocation failure is a named load failure reporting whether cleanup parked or quarantined the owners. The packaged `tensor_ops` index now lists the supported Q8 exports and each indexed symbol is checked against the compiled object. No new env or config knob, cache reservation or eviction path.
  - `qwen4_slowlink_gate` persists its progress: bounded JSONL records in `<output>.progress.jsonl` (no new flag), each flushed as observed, carry every case/stage/phase and repeat start and end, each completed repeat's raw receipts, compact window list, wall time, digests and cache occupancy/evictions, the primitive cases one at a time, every check row, the error text and the existing `pre_load`/`post_load`/`end` point samples (plus a `load_failed`/`run_failed` point when the GPU is still owned; not the HIP free at the failing allocation), with UTC and monotonic times that the stderr echo repeats. The report is written once, atomically, and only a complete run can be `pass`; an aborted run writes `incomplete` with a sidecar summary that names the last completed repeat and every unexecuted required check without filling any in, and a sidecar write error fails the new required check `progress.durability`. The legacy `perf` cell is unchanged.
  - The admitted S1 tile is per purpose: a 768-row `product` profile (every state, headroom, greedy and perf cell) and a 512-row `primitive_selftest` profile (`--mode primitives`, kernel correctness only, not a product-shape qualification); the earlier 1,536-row tile description above is superseded, and 1,536 remains only the generic validator bound and the bound of the approved named incumbent bypass for requests of at most 1,536 rows. One H1 manifest seals both as full ledgers (`memory_ledger.profiles.product` and `.primitive_selftest`, no flat fallback; the root `device_owned_bytes` is the MAX of the two, since they load sequentially). `identity.manifest` fails if a profile is incomplete or its arithmetic does not close or either tile differs from the tile the loader admits for that purpose; every layer-major receipt must name exactly its cell's profile tile, and `load.placement` fails unless the bundle's admitted purpose, tile, window rows and resident layers equal the selected sealed profile. A product receipt at 1,536, 1,024 or 512 rows is a failure although under the old bound. No cut, repeat or case was removed.
  - The sealed profile ledgers carry their census terms as `{name, bytes}` arrays whose checked sums must equal the profile's tile census and extras bytes, with the cold F16 weight-shadow bound present exactly once (in the tile census, never the extras); the hardware tests judge product receipts at the bundle's admitted product tile, not the generic bound.
  - Hold 1a R3 showed the session cache skipping large snapshots under the device memory guard (17 skips; the 16K case published 0 pooled bytes and its 8192/16384 restores planned 0 rows), so multi-turn prefix reuse recomputed instead of restoring: a failure the gate keeps as FAILED. S1 now opts the session cache into a generic, bounded **pressure-selected pinned-host snapshot tier** (no new flag, no architecture, card or format gate): a capture the device guard refuses is copied directly into its final pinned host allocation, bounded by the cache's existing host budget (the gate fixture's 2 GiB) with normal eviction, and restored straight back into the live context; the device budget is the admitted profile's new `device_snapshot_budget_bytes` (discretionary capacity above the full S1 peak and safety, not extra reserve or safety credit) and the 512 MiB floor still applies to device-policy allocations. Without an S1 profile the non-S1 cache and admission are byte-for-byte unchanged and allocate nothing extra. `SessionCacheUsage` gains additive host ownership fields and counters (`host_budget_bytes`, `host_pool_bytes`, `host_pending_bytes`, `host_resident_bytes`, `host_deferred_release_bytes`, `host_parked_bytes`, `host_captures_total`, `host_restores_total`, `host_evictions_total`, `host_skips_total`, `host_total_bytes()`); the device fields and `device_total_bytes` stay device-only.
  - `qwen4_slowlink_gate` accepts actual host pool captures and restores as successful storage (no positive device pool bytes required) while still requiring every requested cut to be captured and planned at exactly its reused rows with no recomputation, and fails an empty or missing snapshot. It emits the pressure host policy, device and host pool occupancy, and the per-case host capture/restore/eviction/skip deltas alongside the device-only fields (no new logs by default); the seven primitives, cuts, routing, teardown and identity checks and the 512 MiB whole-product gate are unchanged.
  - Status: not a promotion and not a GPU pass. The host envelope (S1 host census 52,930,156,544 B + 2 GiB host pool + 620,021,760 B pending ceiling + 2 GiB driver allowance = 57,845,145,600 B, within the 54 GiB declaration with 136,912,896 B to spare) is a source-derived estimate, not a measurement, and the tier does not by itself recover the active-compute headroom the hold missed. S1 stays default OFF and unqualified.
  - The gate's `load.placement` detail additively reports the admitted profile's allocation-granule census (`granule_census`): the allocation granule, the LOGICAL payload (the seven owned and two budget census terms, unchanged and still logical), the per-owner backing padding (base-reserve owners, S1 owners listed by name, and the per-resident-layer slack) and the PHYSICAL figures (`owned_s1_bytes` and `reserved_s1_bytes` = logical + padding, each counted once, with `reserved_s1_bytes` checked against the profile's own `reserve_bytes()`), plus the device snapshot budget. The physical figures are the **S1 increment** charged beside the incumbent base reserve (the base reserve's payload is not in the profile), not the total model-owned bytes. The session-cache usage fields stay payload bytes and are labelled so (`byte_units`). Diagnostic only: the non-gating residual diagnostic, every gate and the 512 MiB sampler threshold are unchanged, and no arena claim is made.
  - S1 loads (only) now plan the resident non-expert weights and their F16 shadows into bounded, exact-size device roots: one plan per load (bytewise name order, 256 B member alignment, deterministic next-fit, each root capped by the largest eligible allocation the load would already have made), shared by admission, fulfilment and the shadow cache, with weight roots allocated at load and shadow roots allocated lazily at exactly the planned size. Allocation-granule padding is charged per root instead of per weight. No new knob, no architecture/card/format gate, and no change to the 768/512 tile, the adaptive resident count (ten preferred), the 1 GiB runtime reserve, the 512 MiB safety margin or the whole-product 512 MiB external + HIP minimum-free gate; non-S1 loads build no plan and are unchanged, and host session semantics are unchanged. The gate's `load.placement` detail additively reports `arena_census` (and the run `arena_census_end`): planned payload, root requests and granule backing beside the ACTUAL live roots and capacities; a lazy root that is not allocated is never reported as actual, and a root whose capacity is not its request, a census of the wrong length or an S1 profile without a plan fails the receipt. The residual stays non-gating and the seven primitive checks are unchanged. The real-model projection (1,096 core weights, 291 shadow owners, 9 + 2 canonical roots, 1,010,670,848 B projected recovery, 48,509,588 B slack at N = 10 / tile 768, 113,608,212 B at the primitive 512 profile) is a source projection only; no GPU recovery has been measured or is claimed, and S1 stays default OFF.
- **Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 single-GPU decode layers run as typed hybrid `Step`s (`DeltaNetMixer`, `GatedAttention`, `SwigluFfn`) from `hipfire_dispatch::pipeline::hybrid` (#666 G8 slice 1, HIPF-117; recut of #795 from current beta).** The executor bodies and every Qwen3.5 decode fusion gate (compact GDN QK, gated-norm MQ rotate, FA prep, Q8 KV-write fold, FA gate epilogue, QKVZA/conv scalar prep, conv QK norm) now exist once, in dispatch; the qwen35 copies are gone and the hand arms, dense TP, the batched-prefill FA fallback and the exact VMM slot route call the dispatch copies. No launch or numeric change: oracle dumps and greedy serve transcripts are byte-identical to beta, and calibration taps per decode token are unchanged. A failing decode launch now reports its HIP error wrapped once instead of twice. Design record: `docs/design/qwen35-declarative-program.md`.
- **Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 batched prefill and speculative-verify layer bodies (dense SwiGLU FFN, gated full attention, gated DeltaNet) run from `hipfire_dispatch::pipeline::{batched, batched_attention, batched_deltanet}` as the rows > 1 executors of the slice-1 ops (#666 G8 slice 2, HIPF-118).** The bodies moved verbatim from current beta (PM FP8 verify math, `ChainVerifySplit` and gfx1100 split verify, tile attend, IU4 verify, FP8-stream opt-outs, gfx1201 lane-batched verify, the A3B PM whole-chunk attend and F5 Q-prep route, the A3B native FP8 resident FA2 prefill admission `gfx12_fa_prep_fp8q_admitted`, the GDN chunk-scan views and layer); the two copies of the dense FFN body are one executor, the GDN chunk-scan, FA PM and FP8-Q prep helpers shared with the arch-side MoE bodies exist once in dispatch, and the verify context reaches dispatch as the `DflashFusionCtx` enum. The arch crate binds views in `qwen35/program.rs` and keeps the chunk loop and multi-request lifecycle; the per-token FA fallback, dense TP attention and the F2 chunk pair remain arch-side (listed in the design record). No launch or numeric change measured on gfx1151: oracle dumps, ragged-prefill hashes and greedy serve transcripts are byte-identical to beta. The gfx1100/gfx1201-only routes (gfx1100 `ChainVerifySplit`, gfx1201 lane-batched CB verify, PM FP8 verify scope, IU4 verify, FP8-stream producers, gfx12 FA prep, A3B PM/F5, A3B native FP8 FA2 prefill) are token-identical moves without a hardware receipt yet.
- **Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 MoE-layer batched prefill and verify mixers (DeltaNet-MoE linear attention, FA-MoE prep, attend and output projection, PARO arms included) run from `hipfire_dispatch::pipeline::batched_moe` (#666 G8 slice 3, HIPF-119).** `execute_deltanet_moe_layer_batched` and `attention_moe_{prep,finish}_batched` / `execute_attention_moe_layer_batched` are current beta's bodies (MoE GDN chunk scan, fused GDN preamble, indexed Q/K, exact gfx1201 IU4 producers, A3B F5 PM Q-prep, A3B native FP8 FA2 Q prep), and their MoE-only route gates moved with them. They stay separate from the dense executors (always-residual output projection, PARO Givens arms, the MoE conv/QK-norm sequence) so the numerics do not move; MQ3G256/MQ3-Lloyd projections are now also refused inside the executors. The arch binds the layer's sealed MoE FFN, CPU expert splice included, as a callback. Oracle dumps, the sealed MoE oracle, emulated EP route oracles and greedy A3B/Ornith transcripts are byte-identical to beta. PARO byte identity shows a faithful move, not correctness: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-PARO never reaches these bodies (F32 shared expert, so prefill stays per-token), and shisa-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-PARO, which does with `HIPFIRE_PARO_BATCHED=1`, decodes degenerate text on beta and here alike (HIPF-137). Design record: `docs/design/qwen35-declarative-program.md`.
- **Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 decode has one layer loop, and the native MTP head runs its layer as the trunk's typed steps (#666 G8 slice 4, HIPF-120).** DFlash hidden-state capture, VL (t, h, w) mrope and `memory.offload_exec=cpu` models now run the `hipfire_dispatch::pipeline::hybrid` step program instead of hand-written decode arms (`GatedAttentionOp` gained an `mrope` operand); the hand arms are deleted and `HIPFIRE_FORWARD_LOWERED` no longer affects Qwen3.5 (the exact VMM slot route drops its refusal for it; llama, qwen2 and deepseek4 still read the variable). The MTP head runs `[GatedAttention, SwigluFfn | Moe]`, and MoE heads load their experts through the trunk MoE loader as a sealed `MoeFfnWeights`; the hand MTP attention, FFN and MoE bodies are gone, and the qt53 routed-down admission checks stay on the MTP head. One numeric route change: on a CPU-spilled model whose shape admits the fused gated-norm MQ rotation (A3B), the DeltaNet output projection's CPU step now reads the GPU-rotated activation where the hand arm rotated on the CPU, so `offload_exec=cpu` output can move in its last bits (greedy text was identical on gfx1151). Everything else is byte-identical to beta on gfx1151: every layer's captured hidden row through `forward_scratch_with_hidden` (9B, 27B-xt, A3B, 16 4B formats), the prefill/decode oracle dumps, MTP transcripts and tau (dense 27B-xt, A3B, Ornith), DFlash 9B and 27B-xt battery and chain, 27B VL image answers and CPU-spilled 9B/A3B/27B-xt; Redline decode tapes are unchanged. Design record: `docs/design/qwen35-declarative-program.md`.
- **ParoQuant `group_size=64` checkpoints load and generate (#651); SmolLM2-360M PARO now runs on gfx1151.** SmolLM2's hidden size 960 is 15 groups of 64 and no whole number of 128s, so it needs group size 64; until now every Paro tensor was tagged `ParoQ4G128` and decoded with 72-byte groups and a 128-channel Givens rotation. The shared Paro loader now picks the dtype from `quantization_config.group_size`: `ParoQ4G64` is the HFQ4-G64 layout (40-byte groups: f32 scale, f32 zero, 32 B nibbles) with a 64-channel Givens rotation (`DType::paro_group_size`), served by new portable `gemv_hfq4g64` / `gemm_hfq4g64` kernels and a G64 twin of `givens_rotate_to`; the LLaMA batched prefill (`forward_prefill_batch`) admits it, but serve still prefills LLaMA-arch models such as SmolLM2 one token at a time, because its batched-prefill gate admits Qwen3 only. G64 and G128 never share a GEMV, GEMM or rotation kernel. Group sizes other than 64/128, and AWQ tensors whose sizes do not match the declared group, are refused at load; qwen3.5 Paro checkpoints (dense and MoE), whose routes bind only the G128 kernels, refuse G64 when the source is opened. On gfx1151 SmolLM2-360M PARO greedy output matches a CPU torch emulation of the checkpoint token for token. G128 artifacts keep their kernels: Qwen3-0.6B-PARO hand-path decode logits are bit-identical to beta.
- **Fixed: LLaMA/Qwen3 ParoQuant safetensors models decoded garbage on the default decode path.** The shared dense forward (`arch_spec::dense_forward`, on unless `HIPFIRE_FORWARD_LOWERED=0`) normalized Q/K/V and gate/up inputs with the FWHT rotation and fed that one activation to every projection, but a Paro weight carries its own Givens rotation per projection. Givens weights now get a plain RMSNorm and each GEMV rotates its raw input, so Qwen3-0.6B-PARO greedy tokens match `HIPFIRE_FORWARD_LOWERED=0`. The native PARO4-G128 fused gate/up kernel, whose rotation is embedded in the weight bytes, is no longer admitted for safetensors weights carrying a sidecar rotation.
- **Fixed: Q8 KV decode attention for 64-wide heads (SmolLM2) on the flash path.** The Q8 flash decode tile walks `head_dim` in 128-wide halves, so with `head_dim` 64 it read the next head's Q/K and wrote past its partials row (incoherent output on gfx11/gfx12, where the flash path is the default). A head that is not a multiple of 128 now uses `attention_q8_0_kv`, which reads the position from `pos_buf` on a fixed grid and is graph-replay safe. That kernel walks the context serially, one block per head, so 64-wide-head Q8 decode slows with context: SmolLM2 on gfx1151 decodes 72.1 tok/s at 712 tokens and 24.7 tok/s at 3,445.
- **Tokenizer: an HF byte-level BPE vocabulary without a symbol for every byte now loads, as in HF.** SmolLM2's trained vocab has no symbol for bytes such as 0x04 or 0xff, and hipfire refused it as damaged. With no `unk_token` and no `byte_fallback`, HF drops such a byte; hipfire's `tokenizer.json` path now does the same. GGUF and HFQ-metadata vocabularies still require all 256 byte symbols.
- **Fixed: Redline no longer replays a tape that is missing kernels (HIPF-121).** A launcher that called `hip.launch_kernel` directly instead of the `launch_maybe_blob` funnel ran during the capture window but was never recorded, so every replay skipped it. Legacy Qwen3.5-4B `mq5` under `replay.backend=redline` decoded garbage from the second token ("The sky sky sky5 prospect…"); on Strix Halo the tapes of the Qwen3.5 `mq5`, `q8-mixed`/`q4k-q8embed` (Q4_K), `q8hfq`, `hfq2g256`/`hfq2g128` and `bf16` formats lacked 1–248 launches per token. Prepare now compares the kernel launches the window issued on the capturing thread with the tape and refuses an `unrecorded launch` (sticky HIP fallback) for every automatic Redline route; Qwen4's own census is folded into that shared check. All remaining raw launchers in `gemv.rs` plus the fused Q4_K QKV/gate-up GEMVs go through the funnel (blob ABI bitwise equal to the kernelParams launch for every launcher runnable on gfx1151), and the Qwen3.5 window opens after the embedding, which is a per-token input outside the tape. Three Q4 GEMVs, both Q8HFQ GEMVs and the fused Q4_K launchers used the null stream, so the AR hipGraph never captured them either: Q4_K and Q8HFQ decode under the AR graph was garbage too and now matches eager. Strix Halo, greedy 64 tokens, eager vs redline: 20 Qwen3.5-4B weight formats plus 9B KV/state variants, 27B, 35B-A3B (AQL and default PM4), LFM2.5 and DeepSeek-V4 are token-identical with the route retained (63 replays). `scripts/redline-greedy-parity.py` gains `--backend redline`, `--transport` and `--require-retained`.
- **Fixed: Flash-Next load no longer scans every routed expert header before choosing the scratch mode; the scan ran even when compact mode could not be selected (regression from b9ab7f229).**
- **Flash-Next on gfx1100 now defaults to an 8192-row prefill chunk on measured narrow discrete links (<16 GB/s), using the same narrow-link predicate as G2 DMA staging.** Only that automatic narrow-link policy may trade resident expert layers for activation scratch; fast links, UMA and gfx1201 keep their previous placement policy. On XTX (7.1 GB/s H2D), MQ4 split + q4 PLE, one P1 hold against exact beta `d8865a16b`: pp8192 **265.1 → 931.9 tok/s (3.52×)**, at the cost of pp512 **72.3 → 61.9 (−14.38%)** and tg64 **5.699 → 5.089 (−10.71%)**. The chunk grows **2048 → 8192**, resident expert layers fall **10 → 5**, and pinned host experts grow **48.6 → 54.9 GiB**, plus the unchanged **2550 MiB** borrowed-stage restore mirrors. All **8 × 128 greedy AR token IDs match**. Single measured sample per bench row, one warmup; not a timing measurement of the later PLE-prewarm-budget change. Opt out with **`HIPFIRE_PREFILL_CHUNK_ROWS=1536`** to retain the smaller placement reserve and resident layers. Explicit chunk settings remain authoritative on every link.
- **Flash-Next mq2 host-expert prefill now DMA-stages through borrowed resident slab VRAM on measured narrow discrete links (<16 GB/s).** Mixed-codec layers that exceed their donor stage a whole-expert prefix; the remaining pointer-table entries keep their host addresses. At most 33.6 MiB (4% of one cold layer) remains host-read on the XTX mq2 split. Donor restoration uses 1621 MiB of pinned host copies; no dedicated VRAM or resident layer is taken. Explicit staging overrides, gfx1201 and tier layouts retain their existing behavior. CPU tests cover the real artifact's 48-layer layout, unchanged placement, full-fit and host-tail pointers, expert-boundary cuts, and donor restoration. Each host layer logs staged and host-tail bytes once at load.
  - **XTX mq2 split + q4 PLE, shipped 8192-row default (j1758, fixed ABBA against exact beta `ff799626e`):** pp8192 **63.5 → 1,422 tok/s (22.4×)**; pp512 retains **98.1%** and tg64 **99.86%** of baseline. Placement stays **7 resident layers / 33.4 GiB pinned host experts**. All **8 × 64 greedy token IDs** match beta exactly, and two candidate processes are deterministic.
- **Fixed: the Nix flake builds and runs again (#645, #162).** The kernel package failed with `Could not resolve the HSA runtime (libhsa-runtime64.so)`, because `HIPFIRE_ROCM_PATH` pointed at nixpkgs `clr`, which lacks `libhsa-runtime64` (v0.4.2.1 is affected too). New `nix/rocm-root.nix` joins `clr`, `rocm-runtime` and `rocm-device-libs` into one root; the kernel build, the dev shell and the `hipfire`/`hipfire-daemon` wrappers use it, the wrappers as a default so a user's `HIPFIRE_ROCM_PATH` still wins (the "Bring your own ROCm" docs now set it). The device bitcode now comes from that root, so `HIPFIRE_HIPCC_EXTRA_FLAGS` is no longer set: a daemon launched by `hipfire run` takes its `HIPFIRE_*` settings from the CLI's resolved config, not its own environment, so the wrapper's flag reached only the kernel build, packaged kernels failed their identity check and the runtime JIT fallback could not find the device library. `gpuTargets` outside the kernel registry (such as `gfx1200`) no longer fail the build; they package no kernels, JIT at runtime and print an evaluation warning naming them. The overlay no longer reads the deprecated `system` alias, and `docs/NIXOS.md` maps `gfx1200` to the RX 9060 class and the R9700 to `gfx1201`.
- **Gemma 4 EAGLE serves sampled, penalized and `logprobs` requests instead of silently running them on AR (#837, HIPF-104, @fivetide).** With `HIPFIRE_GEMMA4_EAGLE=1` and a drafter loaded, only greedy, penalty-free requests without `logprobs` took the EAGLE route. Now every tool-free request that fits does. Greedy requests verify by argmax as before (token-identical to the previous route). Sampled and penalized requests verify by naive sampling: drafts stay the draft head's argmax, each verify row draws one token with the AR sampler (temperature, top-p/top-k/min-p, request seed) against the prompt + emitted + earlier-draft penalty history, and a draft is accepted if it equals its row's draw, so the output follows the AR distribution up to batched-verify rounding (the same caveat as greedy). `logprobs` come from the verify rows that produced each token. On gfx1151 (`gemma4-12b.mq4` + `gemma4-12b-assistant.q8f16.hfq`, six chat prompts × 256 tokens) EAGLE runs at 16.4–17.5 tok/s against 21.3–21.5 for AR (τ 2.83 greedy, 2.80 at temperature 1). The 26B-A4B drafter (`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant`, quantized with `--arch-id 22`) runs at about half its AR speed, so EAGLE stays opt-in.
- **Strix Halo (gfx1151) 27B DFlash with a Q8_0 lm_head (`qwen3.8-27b.mq4`): the 16-row draft and verify lm_head is 6x faster, DFlash decode 1.8x (#754, HIPF-100).** `gemm_q8_0_wmma` ran one wave per 16 rows and loaded each 2 B aligned 34 B Q8 block byte by byte: 40-47 ms (29-35 GB/s) for the 248320 x 5120 head at 15-16 rows, twice per cycle, so DFlash on chat prompts (τ 1.6-1.8) ran at AR speed (13-14 vs 14.4 tok/s). Exact gfx1151 at 1..=16 rows now launches `gemm_q8_0_wmma_gfx1151_xlds` (4 waves x 16 rows per block, X slab in LDS, 17 b128 loads per row group): 6.2-7.4 ms (183-219 GB/s), outputs byte-identical. Under the existing `HIPFIRE_GFX1151_XLDS` switch (`0` restores the base kernel); other arches and MQ4V2-head models (`.mq4-xt`/`.mq4-xts`) are unchanged.
  - Measured (Strix Halo, `qwen3.8-27b.mq4` + `qwen38-27b-dflash-mq4.hfq`, daemon protocol, 384 tokens, thinking off, interleaved AR / beta / this x2): AR 14.4 tok/s; DFlash chat (44-token prompt, τ 1.80) 14.1 → 26.0, code (262 tokens, τ 12.2) 66 → 119, 2K-token code (τ 2.91) 19.6 → 34.6; thinking on: chat 14.2 → 25.7, code 35.8 → 64.3. Cycle 207.6 → 107.7 ms (draft 68.4 → 16.2, verify 133.6 → 85.8), so DFlash now beats AR above τ ≈ 0.55 instead of τ ≈ 2. Every output hash equals beta's; greedy DFlash text equals AR's.
- **Fixed: legacy 3-bit dense Qwen3.5-family models (`MQ3G256`, e.g. the registry `qwen3.6:27b-mq3`) decode again (#789, HIPF-105, @fivetide).** The FFN down-projection pre-rotates its input for `MQ3G256` and takes the fused SwiGLU-residual route, but `dispatch_swiglu_residual` had no `MQ3G256` arm, so every decode failed with `unsupported gemv.swiglu_residual` before the first token (the #810 `MQ6G256` bug, one width down). The residual and SwiGLU-residual dispatchers now share one dtype → kernel table (`MQ3G256` launches `gemv_hfq3g256_residual`, as `dispatch_residual` already did), and a unit test fails when a dtype planned for either route has no arm. `gemv_hfq5g256_residual` (legacy `MQ5G256` `wo`/`w_down`) now launches through the recorder-aware `launch_maybe_blob`, so retained tapes replay it. On gfx1151 `qwen3.6:27b-mq3` decodes coherently with identical text eager, under the hipGraph and under Redline retained replay; `qwen3.5:9b-mq4` output is unchanged.
- **Fixed: experimental multislot no longer drops Qwen3.8's supported reasoning effort.** Its load acknowledgement hardcoded `reasoning_effort_native: false` and `reasoning_efforts: []`, so HTTP/config resolution discarded valid `low`, `medium`, and `xhigh` values. It now probes the actual slot template, as the ordinary loader does. The bug was present in v0.4.2.
- **Reasoning-effort warnings describe the loaded template, not a guessed Qwen version.** A template without semantic effort support no longer gets mislabeled Qwen3.6; HTTP and config warnings explain that native effort is unavailable and recommend `thinking_budget` or `max_think_tokens` for a cap. `native` is not an effort value; the Qwen diagnostic names `low|medium|xhigh` and its existing fallback. Config documentation explains template capability reporting and supported families.
  - A failed effort-capability probe now logs its render/missing-template reason and effective template source. `/health.reasoning_effort_probe_error` carries the reason (`null` after a successful probe), distinguishing a failed probe from a template that simply ignores effort. A CPU regression probes the exact registry Qwen3.8-27B MQ6 template, which supports `low`, `medium`, and `xhigh`.
- **Fixed (source): `tape_copy_batched`, `conv1d_silu_split_f32_lanes` and `bf16_round_trip` are now in the kernel registry, so rebuilt packs carry them.** `bf16_round_trip` (`Gpu::bf16_round_trip_f32`, the Qwen4 MoE/dense-FFN/QSA BF16 storage boundary, observed compiled after `ready` on the R9700 Flash-Next MQ2 pilot) is registered for every supported arch (module `bf16_round_trip`, symbol `bf16_round_trip_f32`, source `BF16_ROUND_TRIP_SRC`; no arch guard) with CPU test `bf16_round_trip_matches_launcher_and_compiler`. The DFlash verify tape-capture copy (`Gpu::tape_copy_batched`, default singleton and continuous-batching verify) and the lane-batched continuous-batching verify conv (`Gpu::conv1d_silu_split_f32_lanes`) are static HIP modules whose launchers pass a fixed module key, symbol and source to `ensure_kernel` (only kernarg values and grid vary), but had no registry entry, so a compiler-free pack had no object for them and the first request needed hipcc (the historical slim-image failure noted under the container entry below). `tape_copy_batched` has no arch guard and is registered in every supported inventory; the lane conv is registered for exact gfx1201, the only arch `lane_gdn_batch_admitted` admits. CPU test `dflash_tape_copy_and_lane_conv_match_launchers_and_compiler` compares each entry's module, symbol, source and compile recipe with the launcher constants and `KernelCompiler::recipe_for_source`; the gfx1201 inventory-size assertion becomes 92 + 161 (the pack counts in the draft-twin entry below predate these modules). Packs must be rebuilt to carry the objects; the slim `runtime` image has not been re-exercised with this change, and the compose default stays `full`.
- **Fixed: the gfx1201 kernel pack now carries the DFlash draft overwrite GEMM twins, so a compiler-free (slim container) install can serve the default `qwen3.8:27b-mq4-xts` with its draft.** `gemm_mq4g256v2_overwrite_wmma_gfx12` (one-tile) and `gemm_mq4g256v2_overwrite_wmma_gfx12_vt` (the ten `_vt{2,3,4}w{4,8}` / `_vt{4,8}w{4,8}_k32` verify-tile symbols, the residual twin's set) were launched by the gfx1201 draft route (`gemm_mq4g256v2_overwrite_gfx12_dflash`) but missing from `kernel_registry`, so the pack built from it had no object for them. With hipcc present they were JIT-compiled on first use; without it the first draft request failed with `gemm_mq4g256v2_overwrite_wmma_gfx12_vt: no usable cached kernel image exists, but hipcc is unavailable` (slim `hipfire` runtime image on R9700, chat 400). Both modules are now registry entries with the launchers' own source expressions and module keys; the exact-gfx1201 inventory grows 248 → 250 modules, gfx1100 (237) and gfx1151 (231) are unchanged. A CPU audit of the default `qwen3.8:27b-mq4-xts` dispatch on exact gfx1100 and gfx1151 found no further missing default kernel: the gfx1100 S7 draft collapse GEMMs (`gemm_mq4g256v2_overwrite_ksplit_lds_dflash_gfx1100_ks*`, `mq_rotate_x_f16_dflash_gfx1100`) are vetoed by the default-on `HIPFIRE_RESIDUAL_LDSSTAGE` and the gfx1151 draft has no collapse route. CPU test `gfx1201_draft_overwrite_twins_are_packaged` pins the module keys, symbols, sources and that no other arch carries them; the gfx1201 inventory-size assertion is 92 + 158.
- **An interrupted `hipfire bench` kills and reaps its daemon, so the GPU reservation is free when the bench has exited.** The bench spawns the daemon and holds its machine-wide per-GPU `flock`; `Drop` already killed it on a normal return or error, but SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP stopped the CLI without running `Drop`, leaving the daemon (still loading or compiling kernels) alive and holding the lock. A timeout harness that SIGTERMed the bench therefore saw the next arm on the same cards fail with `hardware.devices … already reserved by holder PID …` (the corrective flash-pp3 hold: bench killed at 269.7 s, decode 0.0 s later failed on the old daemon's lock). The CLI now installs a handler that SIGKILLs and `wait`s every daemon *this process* spawned (via the new `Engine::terminate_spawned`; a daemon another process owns is never touched) and exits 130. `wait` returns only after the daemon's teardown, which releases the lock, so a pinned-memory-heavy daemon that takes seconds to die can no longer outlive its bench. A `kill -9` of the CLI itself cannot be handled; the daemon then exits at the next stdin read (EOF). The timeout in that hold was the harness's own (0.62 × a 435 s arm budget): neither the CLI, the client nor the daemon bounds a load, so no product timeout was raised. CPU tests: `crates/hipfire-cli/tests/bench_daemon_lifetime.rs` (SIGTERM during a never-answering load, a failed load, an unrelated daemon left alone) and the `hipfire-client` `terminate` test.
- **`hipfire bench --matrix` runs on every topology `serve` admits — single card, pipeline-parallel, dense tensor-parallel and expert-parallel — and reports which one it measured.** The daemon's synthetic `bench_prefill` / `bench_decode` probes used to refuse any load with `pp>1` or EP (`bench_prefill requires a single-GPU model (pp=1, non-EP)`); they now run through the same forward entrypoints `serve` uses on the loaded topology. The `--matrix` JSON gains `topology: {pp, tp, ep, cards}` read from the daemon's probe answers (TP and EP kept distinct, `cards` = identifiers of the cards actually holding the model, a non-empty string array; `null` when a daemon reports none, never a guessed single card). The run fails if its rows disagree or contradict the load's `pp`. Rows stay synthetic (fixed token ids, primed decode context; no prompt, speculation or HTTP path) and single-card output is otherwise unchanged. CPU test pins the report shape for single, PP, TP and EP. See [CLI.md](docs/CLI.md#bench-matrix-topology).
- **Flash-Next prefill on gfx1201: the MQ6 trunk GEMM stages its output tile through LDS and picks a 256-row entry when its workgroup count fills whole rounds (`qwen4_mq6_x4_pm_gfx1201`; byte-identical outputs).** The 128-row `_w8` and the new 256-row, 512-thread `_w16` entries store the result through a coalesced LDS-staged epilogue. For M > 64, `_w16` is chosen iff `ceil(M/256) * ceil(tokens/256)` is a multiple of 32, so the launch is whole rounds of one 16-wave workgroup per WGP over the R9700's 32 WGPs; every other launch keeps `_w8`, and M <= 64 keeps `_w4`. Output bytes equal the hipcc `gemm_mq6g256v2_wmma_gfx12_bt8_x4` (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_MQ6_X4_PM=0` keeps it).
- **Fixed: standard `hipfire bench` now honors `--warmups N`.** The standard path ignored the flag and always sent one short warmup request, whatever `--warmups` said. So earlier standard-mode `hipfire bench` numbers (prefill/decode tok/s, `--json` runs) were measured after one short warmup, not after the default 10 or the count requested. Standard now sends exactly `N` discarded warmup requests with the same prompt and `--max-tokens` as the measured runs, `--warmups 0` skips them, and `--json` reports the count actually run as `warmups_run`; existing JSON fields are unchanged. Time-to-first-token (`--ttft`) and `--matrix` warmups are unchanged.
- **First-class container path.** `compose.yml` runs the engine with an init model pull, a healthcheck, and opt-in `monitoring` and `halo-tune` profiles (docker compose and podman compose); the ROCm 10.1 `full` (default, carries hipcc so a route outside the baked packs compiles once) and slim `runtime` (no compiler) images bake gfx1100/gfx1151/gfx1201 kernels and start through a non-root entrypoint. Measured on Strix Halo (gfx1151): the slim `runtime` image failed the first chat request because `tape_copy_batched` is not in the baked packs (`no usable cached kernel image exists, but hipcc is unavailable`), so the compose default is `full`. `docs/CONTAINER.md` is rewritten as a quickstart.
- **Fixed: the container entrypoint no longer fails to write a bind-mounted host model directory under rootless podman.** Rootless maps container root to the invoking user and the dropped-to uid 1000 to a subordinate id, so `HIPFIRE_MODELS_PATH=/host/dir` (owned by the user) was read-only to `hipfire` and the init pull's missing-sidecar download failed with `Permission denied`. When a rootless user namespace is detected and the models directory is not writable by `hipfire`, the entrypoint keeps the namespace root (the host user) instead of dropping; rootful runtimes still drop. Documented in `docs/CONTAINER.md`.
- **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on Strix Halo (exact gfx1151) now keeps the GatedDeltaNet recurrent state in F32 by default; `memory.state_quant` is the new setting and `state_quant = "q8"` restores the previous Q8 state.** The F32 state has no per-token requantization, so the gfx1151 default is not bit-identical to the old Q8 default. The state is larger: each live recurrent set, the transaction mirror, the native-MTP capture ring and every session-cache or prefix entry store the F32 bytes, and admission and the placement reserve charge them; hipfire never lowers the context, cache budget or lane count, and never falls back from F32 to Q8 on its own. gfx1100, gfx1201 and every other arch keep their previous `auto` (Q8 where the head geometry allows it), the stock-FP8 profile stays F32-only, and Qwen3.5 is unchanged. `memory.state_quant` (legacy key `state_quant`, env `HIPFIRE_STATE_QUANT`) accepts `auto`, `q8`, `fp32` and, for Qwen3.5 only, `q4`; an explicit value is honored or refused, never rewritten. The session-cache scope separates the two formats, so snapshots are never restored across them. Kill switch: `hipfire config set state_quant q8` or `HIPFIRE_STATE_QUANT=q8`.
  - **Quality** (Strix Halo, Flash-Next GPTQ3; gate binaries `A-de86803d7`, built from beta `c80b9e3e7`, so they predate the K1-C1/Cn gfx1151 decode GEMV changes and the WY GDN kernel fix `0d06c380b`): decode KLD against the BF16 reference, paired per chunk, F32 − Q8 is −0.006848 (95% CI −0.009145 to −0.004703) on code24 (24 chunks; mean KLD 0.078394 → 0.071546) and −0.011792 (95% CI −0.014177 to −0.009682) on a WikiText-2 10-chunk subset (the first 10 of 24 chunks × 2048 tokens, not comparable with 24-chunk figures; 0.086869 → 0.075077).
  - **Speed, same gate binaries** (one process per arm, Q8 then F32, one run each): without speculation decode 34.3 → 33.8 tok/s (−1.46%) and short-prompt prefill 178.8 → 175.7 tok/s (−1.73%); with native MTP decode 54.4 → 55.3 tok/s (+1.65%) and prefill 194.3 → 191.8 tok/s (−1.29%); 8K-prompt TTFT 4,020.8 → 4,016.3 ms.
  - **Release 16K prefill lane** (the release driver and prompts, NPU auto, fresh processes) on the land build, i.e. beta `0d06c380b` plus this change (the build predates three later beta commits: the opt-in D2 hot-set split, the scratch-scan guard and the native-MTP re-arm after thinking; none is on the cold 16K prefill path): one hold of 6 processes × 3 requests interleaved by process Q8, F32, F32, Q8, Q8, F32 (Q8 through `HIPFIRE_STATE_QUANT=q8`) measures F32 2,389.98 tok/s (median TTFT 6,843.2 ms) and Q8 2,394.77 tok/s (6,829.5 ms), against the 2,386 tok/s release threshold. Paired Q8 − F32 by process block: +5.4, +6.6 and −4.5 tok/s (mean +2.5 tok/s, +0.10%). An earlier F32-only hold (3 processes × 3, run right after a 23-minute correctness hold) measured 2,370.62 tok/s, below the threshold, against 2,395.52 tok/s for beta Q8 in a separate hold.
  - **Memory and identity:** both formats admit the 262,144-token maximum context with and without native MTP; the MTP context commit grows from 6,956 to 8,238 MiB. With F32, native MTP output equals AR on the seasons prompt (256 ids; batched, incremental, adaptive and full-head routes give identical ids and text) and on a 64-token greedy prompt, and all 7 session-cache hardware tests pass (restore equals cold for chunk-chain, resident, tail, disk-after-restart and message-end snapshots, plus the retired-turn and terminal-stop live commits).
- **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: new explicit opt-in GDN recurrent-state format `q8_ef` (`memory.state_quant = "q8_ef"`, `hipfire config set state_quant q8_ef` or `HIPFIRE_STATE_QUANT=q8_ef`). It is not the default on any arch, and `auto` never selects it.** `q8_ef` is plain Q8 state plus one live f16 error-feedback residual per GDN layer per live owner (+54 MiB on Flash-Next, independent of the native-MTP capture-ring rows); the ring, the transaction mirror and every session-cache, prefix and disk snapshot stay plain Q8. The residual is zeroed on reset, rollback (keep-0 and partial) and every session/prefix/disk restore, so a restored or rolled-back continuation intentionally differs from the uninterrupted `q8_ef` continuation, and MTP output is not guaranteed to equal AR output. It has its own `q8_ef-reset` session-cache scope, never mixed with the `q8` or `fp32` scopes, and is refused on the stock-FP8 profile, on Qwen3.5 and without 128×128 heads.
  - **q8_ef: sampled requests use AR until the sampled-MTP law is verified.** Under `q8_ef`, temperature > 0 requests run AR instead of native MTP, and the load logs `qwen4 native MTP sampled: off for GDN q8_ef (…)`. Greedy native MTP is unchanged, and `q8`, `fp32` and the default keep `speculation.mtp_sampled`. The rejection-sampling law under the EF reset history has not been verified on a GPU yet.
  - **Refused with the inline WY developer route:** `q8_ef` together with `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_GDN_Q8_INLINE=1` fails the load on every arch ("unset one of them"). No GPU has run a `q8_ef` inline-WY chunk kernel, so none ships; a `q8_ef` chunked prefill always runs on its F32 reconstruction.
  - **Quality** (decode KLD against the BF16 reference on code24, 24 chunks × 512, paired per chunk, 95% bootstrap CI, graph off): on Strix Halo (gfx1151, default F32) `q8_ef` measures 0.071987 against F32 0.071546 and `q8` 0.078394. `q8_ef` − F32 is +0.000441 (−0.001301 to +0.002306), `q8_ef` − `q8` is −0.006406 (−0.008538 to −0.004098), and 93.6% of the `q8` → F32 gap is closed. On R9700 (gfx1201, default `q8`; `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_VRAM_LAYERS=14`, routed experts of layers 0–14 in VRAM and the rest host-mapped) `q8_ef` measures 0.073598 against `q8` 0.082302 and F32 0.074518. `q8_ef` − `q8` is −0.008704 (−0.011854 to −0.005680), and `q8_ef` − F32 is −0.000919 (−0.004398 to +0.002255).
  - **Correctness:** the GDN state oracle (`q8`, F32 and `q8_ef`; graph off and on; 1,680 cases per format each) has 0 hard mismatches on Strix Halo and on R9700. Native-MTP product routes under `q8_ef` (AR, batched, incremental, adaptive and full-head; two fresh processes each; two prompts) give identical token IDs and final live state per route on R9700, and on Strix Halo for every fixed route (the adaptive route's wall-clock chooser decided differently between its two Halo runs on one prompt, which is not required to repeat). Every rejected batched window resets the residual to exactly zero, and full-commit windows keep it. A session or transaction restore zeroes the residual, and a restored continuation's first 16 greedy IDs equal the cold run's (Strix Halo). Greedy text is coherent on both cards. On Strix Halo the `q8` and F32 decode logits are byte-identical to the F32-default gate run, and every pre-existing kernel's code object is byte-identical to beta's (gfx1201, gfx1151 and gfx1100).
  - **R9700 loads:** both walked gfx1201 route plans (monolithic and split MQ4 XTS) were re-walked for this change's `tensor_ops` and `fn_gdn_dense` sources; their route and symbol sets are unchanged. They cover the default `q8` state only, so a `q8_ef` load has no closed route plan (`gdn = q8_ef is outside the walked ["q8"]`) and compiles its kernels on first use. Default loads of both artifacts stay planned (route preloaded, 0 kernel compiles), and sealed AR walks of both plans pass (637 requests, 0 errors, 0 off-plan kernels).
  - Timing for `q8_ef` has not been measured.
- **Fixed: a repetitive prompt no longer turns the Qwen/Flash-Next GDN prefill NaN on gfx1151 and gfx1100.** The chunked (WY) GDN prefill kernel (`gated_delta_chunk_gate_wmma` and its Q8-state and NPU-arena twins) inverted the 16×16 WY matrix `T = (I − L)⁻¹` as `(I+P)(I+P²)(I+P⁴)(I+P⁸)` with F16 WMMA operands. With repeated tokens `k_i·k_j ≈ 1` inside a chunk, the partial products reach ~10³ while the exact `|T| ≤ 1`, so F16 rounding left an O(0.5–0.9) error in `T`; the state update then stopped contracting, `|S|` grew ~2×10⁴×, `Vn`/`Dm` overflowed F16, and a value head was NaN for the rest of the prefill (the MoE non-finite guard then failed the request closed). `T` is now computed in F32 by forward substitution of the F32 `L` (`T_i = e_i + Σ_{m<i} L_im T_m`, `fmaf`, fixed ascending order, one lane per column, 120 `fmaf` per lane, 1 KiB of LDS) and rounded to F16 only for the WMMA operand; every other operand and the epilogue are unchanged. A CPU emulation of the new arithmetic (`scripts/lab/qwen4_gdn_replay.py --variant fs32`) has 0/24 blow-ups at 2048 and 4096 rows over beta 0.5–0.999 and g 0…−0.1, and its random-key output error equals the old kernel's (BF16 output rounding). `gdn_wy_repeat_check` is a synthetic GPU oracle (repeated-key and random-key cases against an f64 reference). Measured on Flash-Next (the numerics are not exact, so natural greedy output is **not** byte-identical to before: on XTX, base vs fix native greedy agrees at 56/197 aligned positions = 28.4%, 0 of 4 natural sequences byte-identical, and all fixed natural outputs were read and are coherent): **Halo (gfx1151)** prefill KLD against the BF16 reference improves, code24 0.098913 → 0.098123 (Δ −0.000790) and WikiText-2 0.091989 → 0.087895 (Δ −0.004094); prefill throughput costs −1.7% at 512 rows (1465 → 1440 tok/s) and −2.3% at 8192 rows (2119 → 2069 tok/s). **XTX (gfx1100)** KLD: code24 0.073201 → 0.072364 (Δ −0.000837) and WikiText-2 0.063780 → 0.060450 (Δ −0.003330). Fault rate on repetitive prompts, faulted/runs: Halo amber 0/10 and cedar 0/10 with the fix versus 12/12 and 6/12 before; XTX amber 0/10 and cedar 0/10 versus 4/4 and 1/4 before; natural prompts 0/4 on XTX, unchanged. XTX GPU-kernel trace (rocprofv3, base/fix/fix/base, one cold 8294-token request per arm, 216 `gated_delta_chunk_gate_wmma` calls per request = 6 chunks × 36 GDN layers): pooled per-call median 511.7 µs → 542.9 µs, i.e. +6.8 ms (+6.6%) of kernel time per request, under 1% of the offload-bound time to first token. MTP matches AR token-for-token: 4 of 4 natural XTX pairs (46, 49, 43 and 42 committed tokens, IDs, text and finish identical) and the 256-token Halo pairs. The changed kernel is reached only by prefill of ≥512 rows, so decode and MTP verify cannot run it.
- **Strix Halo prefill no longer pays for the GDN WY F32 `T` fix. At 16K the GDN chunk kernel is 364.6 ms, down from 610.8 ms (v0.4.2: 372.2 ms).** The F32 forward substitution raised `gated_delta_chunk_gate_wmma` and its Q8-state and NPU-arena twins to 246–251 VGPRs. That is five waves per SIMD on the 1536-VGPR gfx11 register file, so two 8-wave blocks fit per WGP; gfx1151's 20 WGPs then held only 40 of the 48 value-head blocks, and the other 8 ran as a second serial pass over every chunk (kernel time +64%, +238.6 ms per 16K prefill). `L` now stays in registers and each `L_im` is read as a scalar operand (`v_readlane`) instead of through a per-row LDS round trip, the 16 substitution rows overlap in one basic block, and gfx1151 is pinned to six waves per SIMD (`amdgpu_waves_per_eu(6)`). That restores the pre-fix footprint: 237 (F32) or 239 (Q8) VGPRs and 31,168 B of LDS. The arithmetic is unchanged, and on Strix Halo the result is byte-identical to the F32 fix: the `gdn_wy_repeat_check` raw output and state bytes match (the oracle gains `--dump-dir` to write them), Flash-Next prefill `.kldseq` and logits SHA-256 match current beta exactly on code24 (KLD 0.100487) and WikiText-2 (KLD 0.092276), and the amber/cedar repetitive prompts still fault 0/4 and 0/4. In one Halo hold, against beta in the same hold on the release 16K lane (three fresh processes per arm, interleaved, NPU auto), median TTFT goes from 7,046.9 to 6,818.9 ms, i.e. 2,320.9 → 2,398.5 tok/s (+3.3%); the slowest of the six samples is a candidate that includes the one-time JIT compile of the new arena kernel. pp8192 synthetic goes from 2,071.5 to 2,128.8 tok/s (+2.8%, one sample each). gfx1100 is not pinned, because its 24 WGPs hold all 48 blocks at two per WGP; its F32 build lands at 239 VGPRs and six waves and is arithmetic-identical, but it was not timed.
- **R9700 Flash-Next mq4 hot-set trade-off:** versus hot set off, prefill is +18–19% at 8K/16K, but short-context decode is −9.5% and pp512 is −6% (j1333, beta `18b216848`). Versus v0.4.2.1, long prefill is +15–23% and decode is −3 to −11% (`fp8-prefill-matrix/RESULT.md`). The kill switch is `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_HOTSET=0`.

- **MQ4 routed-expert down GEMV no longer drops input groups when `moe_intermediate_size` is not 512.** The atomic-free expanded down kernel (`gemv_hfq4g256_moe_down_k8_indexed_batched_expanded`, all RDNA targets) had been specialized to two 256-wide groups since July, so any other K read only the first 512 inputs. LFM2.5-8B-A1B (K=1792) decoded whitespace and terminator loops; MiniMax M2 (K=1536) MQ4 experts used the same kernel. Other K now take a per-group loop. K=512 output is bitwise unchanged (Qwen3.5/3.6 A3B). The opt-in gfx1100 `HIPFIRE_MOE_DOWN_LAST_COMBINE` down+combine kernel is also a K=512 body, so it is now admitted only when the expert-down K (`mi`) is 512; any other K falls back to the expanded down (the per-group loop kernel) plus the separate combine, even with the variable set.
- **Windows: HFQ tensors still load after a unified-memory (UMA) load drops the mmap, so DeepSeek-V4 on a Strix Halo no longer fails with `deepseek4: tensor 'embed.weight' missing in HFQ` (#869).** UMA loads call `HfqFile::drop_mmap()` and then read every tensor through `tensor_data_pread`/`tensor_data_vec`. On non-unix targets those delegated to the mmap accessor, which returns nothing once the mapping is gone, so each tensor reported missing. Windows now reads through positioned reads (`FileExt::seek_read`) with the same exact-read loop as unix: short reads continue at the advancing offset, `Interrupted` retries, EOF before the indexed length refuses the tensor instead of serving a zero-filled tail. Unix reads now use the same shared loop (`File::read_at`, i.e. `pread`, unchanged semantics); page-cache eviction stays unix-only. Targets with neither call keep the mmap delegation. CPU tests drop a real mmap and read two tensors back by offset, and the loop's offset/short-read/EOF/interrupt/overflow logic is tested platform-neutrally with a fake reader.
- **Windows gfx1100: `experimental.graph.ar` (AR-forward hipGraph capture) now defaults to off — workaround for silent wrong output (#655, item 1).** On Windows with an RX 7900 XTX (exact `gfx1100`) the default-on AR graph replay produced token soup (garbage tokens, no error). Until that replay is fixed, an unset `experimental.graph.ar` resolves to `false` on Windows exact `gfx1100` only, so decode runs the direct (eager) path; AR graph capture there is opt-in with `hipfire config set experimental.graph.ar true` or `HIPFIRE_AR_GRAPH=1`, and an explicit `true` or `false` always wins. Linux gfx1100, every other architecture on Windows (including gfx1101/gfx1151/gfx1201) and every non-Windows host keep the previous default (on). The default is resolved in `rdna-compute` `FeatureFlags` (built-in defaults are carried as absence in the process config, so no config schema value changes); `bench --redline` still forces it on. This is a workaround, not the replay fix, and addresses only the token-soup item of #655; its other items are separate. CPU tests (`crates/rdna-compute/src/feature_flags.rs`, `graph_ar_*`) simulate Windows on any host and cover the platform x architecture matrix, explicit overrides and the process-config round trip.
- **Fix: the Qwen3.5 batched Q8 lm_head, the DFlash Q8 lm_head dispatch key and the Gemma4 spec-verify Q8 lm_head no longer abort on more than 64 rows (#732); `gemm_q8_0_batched` now takes any row count.** The scalar Q8_0 batched kernel holds at most 64 rows per launch, and `gemm_q8_0_batched` asserted above that (`gemm_q8_0_batched: batch_size N exceeds kernel MAX_BATCH=64`). #767 chunked the MTP call sites but left three unbounded ones: `lm_head_batched` in the Qwen3.5 batch forward (Q8_0 output weights, e.g. native MTP verify of a long block), the `GemmQ8_0Batched` dispatcher key (which relied on its one caller to pre-chunk), and the Gemma4 `forward_batch_spec` lm_head. All three now call `gemm_q8_0_batched_f32_chunked`; the Gemma4 site stays on the scalar kernel rather than the WMMA variant, and the MTP probe's Q8 lm_head (at most 3 rows) uses the wrapper too. The 64-row split itself now lives in `gemm_q8_0_batched`, so no caller can trip the cap: it launches once per `rdna_compute::gemm::q8_0_batched_chunks` chunk through bounds-checked sub-views (nothing at 0 rows), and a private single-launch function keeps the 64-row assert. A row's reduction does not depend on the batch size, so output bytes are unchanged and calls of 64 rows or fewer are the same single launch as before. CPU tests pin the split at 63, 64, 65, 70 and 129 rows (offsets, coverage, 64-row cap); a GPU test (`rdna-compute/tests/gemm_q8_0_batched_rows.rs`, ignored without a GPU) checks every row of a 1/63/64/65/70/128/129/256-row call bitwise against a one-row call and that nothing is written past the last row.
- **gfx1030 (RDNA2) + MQ4G256V2 + DFlash is refused at load with an actionable message instead of failing in the first `spec_step` (#771).** DFlash's verify runs `gemm_mq4g256v2_batched_lmhead` over the target's output layer. The reported `no v2 source` error is from 0.3.1; the generic non-WMMA x-batch scalar fallback now exists in `rdna-compute`, but DFlash's batched lm_head admission for MQ V2 / MQ3 formats is validated only on the gfx11/gfx12 WMMA set, and nothing validates it on gfx1030. The admission gate (`dflash_lm_head_quant_supported`, read-only, before any teardown) therefore stays and now names the GPU, the weight format (`quant_type=44, MQ4G256V2`), that batched lm_head admission is unsupported there, and the way out: `speculation.dflash = off` / `--spec off` for autoregressive decoding, or a Q8/HFQ4/MQ4G256 output layer. AR on gfx1030, any non-DFlash load, WMMA arches (gfx1100–gfx1201) and the Q8/HFQ4/MQ4G256 output layers are unchanged. CPU tests (`dflash_lm_head_refusal_771`) pin the message (including that it does not claim a missing kernel), the gfx1030/gfx1010/gfx942/gfx906 refusals for qt 17/44/47/48/49/50, the WMMA-arch admission and the supported-quant alternatives on gfx1030. Docs: `docs/load-refusal-wording.md` row 29, `docs/CONFIG.md` `dflash_mode`.
- **`hipfire config list` groups settings by intent and shows what each one will do now, who set it and when a change applies; new `config overrides`.** Rows sit under Quality, Speed, Memory & context, Speculation, Hardware & devices and Advanced, each with a *using now* value predicted for the GPU in `install.json` (an `auto` or arch-gated default such as `fp8` KV on gfx1201 resolves to the concrete value and reads `fp8 (auto)`), a *from* label (`default`, `default · gfx1201`, `registry`, `profile dev`, `you`, `this model`, `env HIPFIRE_…`) and an *applies* label (`next message`, `new chat`, `next model load`, `serve restart`); rows the model or GPU does not use say so. New flags `--group G`, `--changed`, `--search TEXT` and `--model M` (same as `hipfire config M list`) work on both forms and on `--json`, which keeps every earlier field and adds `group`, `effective`, `origin`, `from`, `applies` and a top-level `gpu_arch`. `config explain KEY [--model M]` gains `effective:`, `from:`, `group:` and `applies:` lines (and the same JSON fields). `hipfire config overrides [--json]` lists every per-model value in `models.toml` next to the all-models value. The per-model `list` output format changed accordingly; `config profile set` help now says profiles are merged, not replaced. See `docs/CONFIG.md` "Reading settings".
- **hipfire-tui Settings: every non-deprecated config key is editable inline, and the KV cache row offers `fp8`, `bf16`, `f16` and `f32`.** The Advanced view could only edit a hand-picked subset of keys; the rest answered "not editable inline", so `kernel.iu4_prefill` and `memory.kv_cache = "bf16"` could only be set with `hipfire config set`. Each key's editor (cycle an enum, toggle a boolean, type a number or text) now comes from its `ValueRule` in the shared schema, with the curated option order kept only where it reads better (`hipfire-config` remains the sole validator). The KV list is the schema's mode list minus the deprecated `asymN`/`turboN` aliases and the `legacy-*` Givens opt-outs. `developer.qwen4_moe_sym_iu4` is editable and written as a TOML boolean (`= false`), never a string. Underneath, the Settings tab gets its new row model (`SettingsModel`): intent groups (Quality, Speed, Memory & context, Speculation, Hardware & devices, Advanced), a predicted "Using now" value per row from the active model's registry card and the GPU, the layer each value came from (`default`, `registry`, `you`, `this model`, `env HIPFIRE_KV_MODE`), a lock for values an environment variable owns, a virtual Prompt processing row that maps Fast/Accurate to the per-GPU prefill key, plain-language explainers whose trade-off numbers are read from the measured-evidence table, and one shared search rule with `hipfire config` and the profile wizard.
- **hipfire-tui Settings: one list grouped by intent replaces the easy/advanced views.** Quality, Speed, Memory & context, Speculation, Hardware & devices and Advanced each show a *using now* value and who set it (`●` marks anything set by you, a profile or the environment); at 160 columns they also show when a change applies and a "why this value" pane (options on this GPU, the resolution chain, measured KLD and tok/s, the keys written). `/` searches by name, key, env var or description (every printable key goes into the box, `Esc` restores the group), `c` shows changed rows only, `h` hides rows the model does not use. Rows an environment variable owns are locked with the variable named; `Del` on a model-card value says so. The KV cache, KV layout and context rows show serve's live values when its resident model is the active one, and process-scoped rows say `↻ restart to apply` when `config.toml` is newer than serve. `e` and `a` are removed.
- **hipfire-tui Settings: `p` opens the Tuning presets (chooser, preview with measured trade-offs, save), `u` undoes the last tuning, and the header names the preset in effect.** `hipfire config tuning` with no subcommand now opens this screen (`hipfire-tui --tuning`) instead of printing status; `config tuning status` still does. The preview lists every line with a `[x]`/`[ ]` tick, its `from → to` change and the measured quality/speed numbers (or "not measured on this GPU"), says why an unmet line (for example a missing `.ple-q8`) cannot be ticked, and checks for an environment override, a per-model value and a running serve before anything is written. `y` saves exactly the ticked net diff, `Y` saves and restarts serve, `config.toml` stays byte-identical until then. Keys a preset owns read `●` / From `preset`, and a hand edit turns the header into "Quality-first (edited)". At 160×48 the three presets show as cards over a full-width preview table. The plan's local-file facts moved into `hipfire_registry::tuning_plan_env` / `split_model_files`.
- **hipfire-tui Settings: per-model scope, an overrides list and an own-values count on the Models tab.** The header reads `Editing: all models  m`; `m` opens a picker (All models, the active model, other installed models, each with its own-value count) and in a model's scope the group box reads `Quality · values for qwen3.8:27b only`, rows resolve for that model and every change is written to `models.toml` through the same `set_model_override` / `remove_model_override` as `hipfire config <model> set` / `reset` (the file is byte-identical either way). `Del` removes that model's value so it follows "all models" again, `R` removes all of its values after a y/n. Process- and Diagnostic-scoped keys, `developer.*` keys and the Prompt processing row read `all models only (locked)`, and `←/→/Del/Enter` on them explain instead of failing on save. In the all-models scope a row the active model has its own value for reads `this model` and the explainer warns that the change won't affect it. `o` (Settings, or the Models tab on a model) opens Per-model overrides: model, setting, value and the all-models value, with `Enter` to open that value in Settings and `Del` to remove it; at 160×48 it is a models list with loaded / on-disk state beside that model's own values. Restart-pending badges now also watch `models.toml`.
- **`/stats` reports the resident model's KV mode, KV backend and context.** A new `loaded_config` object (`model`, `kv_mode`, `kv_backend`, `max_seq`) carries what the daemon's load ack reported, so a client can show the values in use rather than predict them. It is `null` while no model is resident. `/health` is unchanged, and the TUI's serve stats parse the field tolerantly (an older serve without it still works).
  - The TUI Dashboard's serve uptime now reads serve's `uptime_sec` field; it read `uptime_s`, which serve never sends, so it always showed 0.
- **`hipfire config list` groups settings by intent and shows what each one will do now, who set it and when a change applies; new `config overrides`.** Rows sit under Quality, Speed, Memory & context, Speculation, Hardware & devices and Advanced, each with a *using now* value predicted for the GPU in `install.json` (an `auto` or arch-gated default such as `fp8` KV on gfx1201 resolves to the concrete value and reads `fp8 (auto)`), a *from* label (`default`, `default · gfx1201`, `registry`, `profile dev`, `you`, `this model`, `env HIPFIRE_…`) and an *applies* label (`next message`, `new chat`, `next model load`, `serve restart`); rows the model or GPU does not use say so.
