Each key's editor (cycle an enum, toggle a boolean, type a number or text) now comes from its `ValueRule` in the shared schema, with the curated option order kept only where it reads better (`hipfire-config` remains the sole validator). The KV list is the schema's mode list minus the deprecated `asymN`/`turboN` aliases and the `legacy-*` Givens opt-outs. `developer.qwen4_moe_sym_iu4` is editable and written as a TOML boolean (`= false`), never a string. Underneath, the Settings tab gets its new row model (`SettingsModel`): intent groups (Quality, Speed, Memory & context, Speculation, Hardware & devices, Advanced), a predicted "Using now" value per row from the active model's registry card and the GPU, the layer each value came from (`default`, `registry`, `you`, `this model`, `env HIPFIRE_KV_MODE`), a lock for values an environment variable owns, a virtual Prompt processing row that maps Fast/Accurate to the per-GPU prefill key, plain-language explainers whose trade-off numbers are read from the measured-evidence table, and one shared search rule with `hipfire config` and the profile wizard. The screen itself switches over in a follow-up.
- **`hipfire config tuning` previews, applies and undoes speed-vs-quality presets per GPU.** `status`, `show <balanced|quality-first|low-power> [--arch gfxNNNN] [--json]`, `set <preset> [--skip <line>]... [--yes]` and `undo [--yes]` merge only the ticked lines of a preset into the global `config.toml` after printing the net change, the measured trade-off of each line (from the shared evidence table) and conflicts (an environment variable or a per-model value that overrides a key). Quality-first writes the accurate prompt-processing route (`kernel.iu4_prefill = false` on gfx1201 and gfx1100, and on gfx1151 until PR #902 lands), `developer.qwen4_moe_sym_iu4 = false` on gfx1151 and gfx1201, and `memory.ple_format = "q8"` on gfx1151 when every installed Flash-Next split base has its `.ple-q8`; Low-power writes `reasoning.effort = "low"`; Balanced gives back what the applied preset still owns. `~/.hipfire/tuning.toml` (`ConfigPaths::tuning_toml`, `hipfire_config::tuning`) records ownership and one undo level, so a key you edited since is kept and reported, and apply then undo restores `config.toml` byte for byte. Without a terminal, `set` and `undo` refuse (exit 2, nothing written) unless `--yes` is given.
- **The serve bearer key (`serve.api_key_file` / `--api-key-file` / `HIPFIRE_SERVE_API_KEY_FILE`) must be printable ASCII; a non-ASCII character is now refused, naming the file (#655).** The key is sent as an `Authorization` HTTP header value. The key file already refused whitespace and control characters, but still accepted non-ASCII characters (a 16-character `é` key passed the 32-byte minimum), which are not reliable header content. The same rule now applies to every `BearerToken` (key file and in-memory values): a space, tab, line break, control character or non-ASCII character is rejected before serve starts or a client connects, with an error such as `invalid value for serve.api_key_file: /path/key holds a token that contains a non-ASCII character (U+00E9) at character 5; it must be a single line of printable ASCII characters because it is sent as an HTTP header value`. The message names the character by kind and position and never prints the key; the character rules are checked before the length minimum. Trailing whitespace in a key file is still trimmed (the usual final newline) and printable ASCII punctuation is still accepted. An existing key file containing non-ASCII characters must be regenerated (for example `openssl rand -hex 32`). Together with the `HF_TOKEN` check in the next entry, this covers every user-supplied HTTP header value in hipfire.
- **Speculative decode retires a request to plain AR once its drafter cannot pay for the cycle (#693).** Qwen3.5-family DFlash and generic (llama-family) DFlash requests at temperature 0 now judge every 16 spec cycles: when two windows in a row commit fewer tokens per cycle than the break-even line `HIPFIRE_SPEC_RETIRE=<base>[,<per_1k_ctx>]` (default `1.5`, flat), the rest of the request decodes one target token per step on AR's single-token forward, with the draft context kept whole so a follow-up turn on the prompt cache still drafts (measured τ 12.66 on a turn after 910 retired tokens vs 12.29 without). The decision reads token counts and position only, so a greedy request retires at the same cycle and returns the same bytes on every run; `done` reports `spec_retired`, `spec_retired_at` and `ar_tokens`, HTTP `timings` passes them through, and `/metrics` counts `hipfire_spec_retired_total`. Default `1.5` sits under the smallest measured cycle/AR cost ratio (Strix Halo Qwen3.8-27B MQ4 + MQ4 DFlash: 1.6 at 2K, 1.73 at 32K), so it only retires drafters that already lose to AR; a box whose verify cost grows with context sets its measured line (`off` disables). On Strix Halo at beta `c1a6be48e` DFlash beats AR at every context up to 32K on the #693 prompt (26.4 vs 13.7 tok/s at 32K), and the default leaves those requests byte-identical; a forced retirement at 32K decodes its AR phase at 13.1 tok/s against AR's 13.7.
- **`hipfire pull` and `hipfire quantize` check `HF_TOKEN` (and `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN`) before they download, and say which variable is wrong (#655).** A token with a trailing newline or space, wrapped in quotes (Windows `set HF_TOKEN="hf_..."` keeps them), or holding a non-ASCII character is not a legal HTTP header value, and the download failed with the unrelated `download request failed: http: failed to parse header value`. The token is now checked up front, before the registry is read or any request is sent, and rejected with a message such as `invalid value for environment variable HF_TOKEN: the token contains a newline at character 7; remove stray spaces and line breaks, such as one copied along with the token. Fix or unset HF_TOKEN to pull`. Only letters, digits and `- . _ ~ + /` (with `=` as trailing padding) are accepted; the message names the first bad character by kind and position and never prints the token. A bad value is rejected, not trimmed. An empty `HF_TOKEN` now counts as unset in `hipfire pull` as it already did in `hipfire quantize` (it previously sent an empty `Bearer` header and hid `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN`), and a non-UTF-8 value is refused instead of being sent with replacement characters. `hipfire quantize --qwen4-flash-next` reading an `hf://` source applies the same check. The `serve.api_key_file` token was already validated and names its file.
- **`developer.qwen4_moe_sym_iu4` is a typed boolean, so `config set … false` now disables the symmetric IU4 MoE route.** The Flash-Next (Qwen4) grouped symmetric IU4 MoE prefill route read `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_MOE_SYM_IU4` as the strings `1`/`0` only, so `hipfire config set developer.qwen4_moe_sym_iu4 false` (stored as the string `false`) and `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_MOE_SYM_IU4=false` were silently ignored and the route stayed requested. The key now accepts `true`, `false`, `1` and `0` (`true`/`false` case-insensitive) from `config set`, TOML (a boolean, a string spelling or the integers 0/1) and the `HIPFIRE_*` environment variable, normalized to a boolean; any other value (`on`, `yes`, `2`, an empty value) is rejected when the configuration is built with `invalid value for developer.qwen4_moe_sym_iu4: expected a boolean: true, false, 1 or 0`, instead of being read as unset. Unset still requests the route on gfx1151/gfx1201, and `1`/`0` behave as before. A previously stored invalid string now fails the config load until it is corrected. Changelog correction: the v0.4.0 entry for `kernel.iu4_prefill` said the key also supports per-model opt-out; it is process-wide and `models.toml` rejects it, so it can only be disabled globally.
- **`hipfire doctor --npu` warns when a Strix Halo is running below full power.** hipfire's published speeds are measured on the performance power mode at the GPU's default power limit, and a laptop or mini PC left on a low-power or balanced mode, a GPU power-saving profile, a lowered power limit or a lowered GPU clock ceiling is slower with no error to show for it. A new `power` check reads the system power mode, the GPU power profile, the power limit against its default, the GPU performance level and the GPU clock ceiling against the hardware maximum, and prints a plain `WARN` that names each cause, says the published speeds assume full power, and gives the fix (for example `powerprofilesctl set performance`, or raising the power limit in the BIOS or your vendor's tool). It never blocks, never changes the tier and never stops the calibration. An idle GPU clocking down is not a warning. The report gains a `warn` check status; the check reads sysfs only.
- **Flash-Next D2 lab gates pin the hot/cold partition and retain truthful Timing repeat receipts.** Lab-only `qwen4_kld --hotset /abs/SIDECAR --hot-budget-mib N` admission holds the CPU/PCIe plan fixed for the unchanged WT2/code24 S11 `s11ref --decode` quality fixtures; `qwen4_cpu_split_parity` records per-run hashes for same-route Timing repeats. Earlier missing Timing hashes do not establish determinism. These are lab-tool changes only; the whole-layer D2 measured default's XTX identity, determinism and paired-KLD receipts are in the measured-default entry below.
  - Reference-only repair: Full's unmasked routed replay must skip the shared prelude so it does not sigmoid the live BF16 shared scalar twice before `SharedDown`. Original routed ids/math and production Timing are unchanged; this is not a corrected GPU pass or evidence of same-route determinism.
  - Matched baseline/D2 loads explicitly pin R9700 KV FP8/GDN Q8 and XTX KV Q8/GDN Q8: manual lab tools use `HIPFIRE_KV_MODE`/`HIPFIRE_STATE_QUANT`, while daemon JSON `load_params` uses `kv_mode`/`state_quant` (not `kv_cache`; the daemon does not read the GDN environment pin). Retain actual resolved `kv_mode`, `qsa_state` and `gdn_state` proof per load, not requested pins alone. Old source-derived `auto` formats are not runtime observations or retroactive pins; old `4363` XTX F32 binaries cannot certify new beta Q8, and forcing old `bf16` is not the default-format gate. R9700 FP8 math is unchanged, with the admission-census delta recorded separately. No GPU quality pass is claimed.
- **The CPU routed-expert splice runs on a pinned physical-core pool.** With `memory.offload_exec=cpu|passback`, the splice's CPU work (gate_up, SwiGLU + rotate, down, combine) now runs on its own lazily built rayon pool with one worker per physical core of the process's allowed CPU set, each pinned to a distinct core, instead of the global pool's 32 logical CPUs (SMT siblings cost 10 experts x 1 row 438 us vs 365 us at 16 threads on Strix Halo). Knobs: `HIPFIRE_CPU_EXPERT_THREADS` (`0`/unset = physical cores) and `HIPFIRE_CPU_EXPERT_PIN` (`0` = unpinned; default on); unreadable topology or a pinning failure falls back to an unpinned `available_parallelism()/2` pool. Output bytes are unchanged and independent of the worker count (CPU test across 1/3/16-worker pools).
- **Qwen MoE sizes its own context on unified-memory GPUs (#823).** With `max_seq` omitted, Qwen3.5/3.6 MoE (`qwen3.6-35b-a3b`, `ornith-1.5-35b-a3b`) on gfx1151 now gets the same automatic context as dense Qwen VMM: min(trained window, post-weight card capacity), with the MoE minimum prefill scratch charged through `PrefillBatchScratch::projected_allocation_bytes`. It previously stayed at 32768, so a coding-agent first turn (26K-token system prompt plus `max_tokens` 8192) was refused with `request exceeds loaded KV budget`. On Strix Halo both models now load at 262144 tokens (`bound=model`); a 260,615-token prompt prefilled without OOM, with GPU memory (GTT + VRAM) at 18.9 GiB after load and 25.2 GiB at that context. A 34,677-token request with `max_tokens` 8192 completes through `hipfire serve` on an empty config. Discrete GPUs keep 32768. A legacy `config.json` carrying `max_seq: 32768` (the old TypeScript CLI's built-in default) now loads and migrates without it, with a warning; a `config.toml` from an earlier migration keeps the value (`hipfire config reset memory.max_seq` removes it).
- **Halo NPU trunk calibration binds on a normalized trunk index digest, so one built-in record serves the monolithic MQ4 and its split MQ4 XTS base.** The calibration key field `model_index_sha256` (SHA256 of the raw HFQ header bytes, which change when the 128 PLE shard tensors move to a sidecar) is replaced by `model_trunk_index_sha256`: an index-only SHA256 of the arch id, canonical sorted-key metadata without `hipfire_ple_rows`, and the name/quant-type/shape/data-size of every tensor except the PLE shard tensors. The two built-in records (`halo-xdna2-stock-v2`, `halo-xdna2-overlay-v4`) change only that key field; measured data is untouched. `doctor` matches models on the same digest; trunk-overlay and expert-hot-set bindings keep the raw index hash. A user calibration file with the former field is refused and must be re-collected.
- **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4): the G2 long-prefill expert stage now engages on gfx1100 (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_STAGE=1`) without also setting `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_STAGE_MIN_ROWS`.** The default threshold was a fixed 2048 rows, above gfx1100's 1536-row prefill chunk, so the opt-in stage could never run there. It is now `min(2048, prefill chunk rows)` (`HIPFIRE_PREFILL_CHUNK_ROWS` or the arch default, as admitted at load); an explicit `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_STAGE_MIN_ROWS` stays authoritative and gfx1201 keeps 2048 (the stage is still default-on there only). The load log line reports the effective `min_rows`, its source (`env`/`default`) and the prefill chunk. Staging is byte-identical transport; the gfx1100 default stays off.
- **K1 slab GEMV launches supply every declared kernel argument.** The normal HIP `kernelParams` path now passes the zero `reserved@92` argument after `n_experts`, matching the 17 explicit arguments in the narrow and wide gfx1151/gfx1201 PeaceMaker images and preventing a host-side out-of-bounds pointer read. A GPU-free regression test checks every selectable embedded entry's metadata. The companion launcher audit also restores the missing expert-count argument in the gfx1030 MQ2-Lloyd grouped MMQ probe's blob argument list (CPU-verified only). Kernel images and the existing K1 96-byte blob path are unchanged.
  - Fixed: native MTP crash (SIGSEGV after the first token) on R9700 slab artifacts, betas 38ce67a44..c1a6be48e.
- **A client abort during a native-MTP or DSpark prefill is a cancel, not a validation error (#822).** `MtpDrafter::mtp_prefill` returned `Result<u32, String>`, so the Qwen4 (Flash-Next), Qwen3.5 and DSpark drafters reported an abort as `Err("… aborted")`, and the spec route answered it with `error(class=validation, rolled_back=true)` (logged by serve as `prefill: Qwen4 native MTP prefill aborted`, on nearly every turn of an agent client that cancels speculative requests). `mtp_prefill` now returns `PrefillOutcome`; an abort is `Ok(PrefillOutcome::Aborted)`, which takes the existing rollback and `aborted` + `done(aborted)` arm. Real prefill failures stay `class=validation`. GPU test: `crates/hipfire-generate/tests/spec_prefill_abort_hw.rs` (ignored by default).
  - CPU tests pin the classification: a prefill `Aborted` becomes a cancel (`aborted` + `done`, no `validation` error), a real `Err` stays `class=validation`, and `PrefillOutcome::into_first_token` turns an abort into an error for the never-abort oracle callers. Fix and GPU evidence by fivetide (PR #906).
- **MoE launcher argument layouts have a GPU-free regression gate.** `all_launcher_abi` compares the changed HIP kernels' declarations and PeaceMaker image metadata with the actual `kernelParams` arrays and packed blob layouts in serving code and launch probes. Missing or misordered arguments, wrong widths or offsets, unclassified callers and unsupported source syntax fail the gate; deliberate historical OLD-kernel fixture calls are classified separately. The ignored owner-mask hardware oracle now writes its expert-count argument explicitly instead of leaving it zero in padding. No runtime path or kernel image changes.
- **hipfire-tui: Models-tab pulls, serve status, Chat scrolling and profile apply work as a new user expects.**
  - **Pull:** the Models tab runs `hipfire pull <tag> --yes` with stdin closed, so the CLI's line prompt no longer hangs the pull at 0 % and swallows keys. `c` cancels a pull (the child is killed and reaped), quitting while one runs asks y/n first, and no `hipfire pull` outlives the TUI. `p` on an entry with PLE rows or draft sidecars opens a chooser that passes `--ple q4|q8` / `--no-draft`.
  - **Serve status:** `/health` is polled every 2 s on every tab (450 ms timeout), so Chat and Logs no longer report `HTTP not ready` for a live serve. Chat Enter queues the prompt until the serve is online and sends it then (Esc cancels); it starts `hipfire serve -d` only once the first check says the serve is down and no serve process exists.
  - **Chat:** the transcript follows new output; Up/Down/PgUp/PgDn/Home/End scroll, typing works while a reply streams, the input shows a cursor and scrolls, `/help` writes a note into the transcript, an aborted reply is marked `[stopped]`, reasoning is styled apart, and the token count is the serve's `usage.completion_tokens` (the request sets `stream_options.include_usage`), else labelled as chunks.
  - **Guards:** Esc never quits; Dashboard `x` (stop) and `R` (restart, which force-reaps this install's serve daemons) ask y/n; footers fit 80 columns and advertise `? help`; Home lists Logs.
  - **Settings:** the deprecated PFlash row and CASK/prefill keys are read-only and marked "(deprecated, removal 0.5.0)"; "Spec decode" is replaced by "Speculation" (`speculation.mode`); `ple_format` is editable; rows without curated help show the schema help; the value editor has a cursor; `hipfire config` opens on Settings (`hipfire-tui --settings`).
  - **Models:** PLE rows, hot sets, trunk overlays, registry sidecars and non-trunk HFQ files are no longer listed as models. The filter is the CLI's, moved to `hipfire-registry` (`is_listable_model_file`, `is_standalone_model`, `probe_hfq_arch_id`) and shared by both. Enter on a model that isn't downloaded no longer saves it as `default_model`; Have stays local/remote with a separate active marker; the header says `registry: bundled (<date>)` instead of `missing`.
  - **GPU stats:** Dashboard/System/Home use `amd-smi` (else `rocm-smi`) found through the ROCm-root lookup, so a ROCm with only `amd-smi` shows VRAM, load and the GPU name instead of "rocm-smi not installed" / "No GPU detected".
- **Config profiles merge instead of replacing the global config.** `hipfire config profile set <name>` and the profile wizard now overwrite only the keys the profile sets and keep every other key (devices, port, default model, kernel flags, `max_seq`, ...). The built-in `default` profile no longer pins any registry-overridable key (`memory.kv_cache`, `memory.max_seq`, `speculation.*`, `reasoning.*`, `generation.max_tokens`, `attention.flash`, `prompt.*`), so per-arch and registry defaults such as fp8 KV on gfx1201 and a model's DFlash default stay in effect. The wizard lists what a profile adds and overwrites and applies only on `y`.

- **Flash-Next (qwen4) on gfx1201: `auto` expert placement charges the HIP runtime's own device memory and retires the historical floor there.** Every traced allocation of a load and a 32K-token request equals a census item, but the device-wide VRAM use sits above them on an R9700. With the pruned W3-slab pack fully resident (compact scratch, 1024-row chunk) the gap is 929 MiB after load and 1,330 MiB at the request's peak. With the shipped `mq3-xts` and 30 routed layers in pinned host RAM it is 974 and 1,373 MiB, and about 1,380 / 1,383 MiB at 4096 / 8192 rows (956 MiB at 256 rows). This is memory the HIP runtime holds for code objects, HSA queues and their context-save areas, kernel scratch and the ROCr pools. The historical 6.5 GiB floor's stale F32 context used to cover it. On exact gfx1201, discrete, single-device loads the census now carries it as a measured `HIP runtime` term (1,408 MiB) and is the whole reserve (the placement log reads `census (historical floor retired)`); every other arch, unified memory and expert-parallel loads keep the larger of floor and census as before. The census also charges the lazy F16 weight shadows only at prefill chunks of at least 512 rows, the only rows the F16 WMMA arms run at. With the compact scratch, the shipped `mq3-xts` on a 32 GB R9700 at a 4096-row chunk keeps 18 routed layers at `max_seq` 8192 and 17 at 32768 (15 and 15 before). Placement only: no buffer, kernel or arithmetic change. Receipts: `rocprofv3 --memory-allocation-trace` against sysfs `mem_info_vram_used`, R9700, session cache off (slab-scratch-notes `rcpt/h1-proof-run1/p1024`, `rcpt/h2a-run2`, `rcpt/h2b-c8192-run3`).
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) on gfx1201: W3/MQ4 expert-slab artifacts take the compact forward scratch by default (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_COMPACT_SCRATCH=0` keeps the full plan; storage only).** The compact plan (`FnSymGfx1201`, a 512-row F32 fallback plus BF16 grouped-row MoE buffers and phase-aliased PLE/HC/GDN temporaries) used to need `=1` and symmetric IU4 headers, and refused every slab load. A slab layer runs two routes (`slab_route.rs`, `qt44_qt53_prefill.rs` `slab_k2`): rows within the few-row limit (decode, verify, at most 32 rows) take the K1 lane-union GEMVs, whose F32 gate/up `[lanes*10, 640]` and down `[lanes*10, 2560]` rows fit the 512-row fallback; longer rows take the K2 `gemm_qwen4_moe_w3_*_iu4_sym` grouped GEMMs, which write the same BF16 `[grouped_rows, moe]` / `[grouped_rows, hidden]` rows as the symmetric IU4 route the plan was sized for (the launchers check buffer spans). Taken for a `FlashNextSlab` manifest on exact gfx1201 single-device loads with the grouped MoE GEMM and BF16 PLE key/value weights; a symmetric-IU4 artifact still needs `=1`, and an expert-parallel load keeps the full plan. Forward scratch at the 4096-row default chunk is 4,388 -> 2,267 MiB (2,121 MiB saved), at 8192 rows 8,603 -> 4,363 MiB (4,240 MiB saved), which `auto` expert placement turns into more resident routed layers on an R9700. Placement/storage only: kernels, routes and arithmetic are unchanged. GPU receipts (gfx1201 R9700, `slab-scratch-notes/rcpt`): H2 `rcpt/h2a-run2` (chunk 4096/1024/256) and `rcpt/h2b-c8192-run3` (chunk 8192) all PASS, with the HIP runtime reserve raised to 1,408 MiB. H3 exact KLD `rcpt/h3-exact-run3`: all 8 KLD arms (31k-token and short prompts; the pre-change build at 15 resident expert layers, the new build at 15 layers by default, at 15 with `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_COMPACT_SCRATCH=0`, and at 17) match the pre-change 15-layer logits SHA and generated IDs exactly. Greedy decode: for four requests per arm (the 31k prompt and three short ones) the compact-default build equals the pre-change build in token IDs and finish_reason, and native MTP equals same-binary AR in IDs and finish_reason with MTP confirmed active (focused rerun `rcpt/h3-mtp-run4`, `closure.json` OVERALL PASS, which replaces the failed run3 MTP arms). Logprob streams are UNAVAILABLE: both builds returned zero logprob events, accepted only under the explicit empty-logprobs comparator flag, so there is no exact-logprob evidence; this is not a bitwise claim across every output channel.
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) host-placed routed experts can run on the CPU: `memory.offload_exec=cpu` (env `HIPFIRE_OFFLOAD_EXEC`; `HIPFIRE_MOE_CPU_EXPERTS=0` disables).** Opt-in; the D1 splice is never selected by default (an unset setting is `pcie`, except the Flash-Next D2 measured default below). AR single-token decode and `<=4`-row verify recompute each selected host-placed routed expert's FFN on the CPU; wide prefill and wider verify keep the GPU path over PCIe. Arming is fixed for the loaded model, so session snapshots never mix PCIe and CPU execution modes within that load. An armed load runs eager HIP only (`auto` retained replay disabled; `replay.backend=shadow`, active stream capture, the graph flag and replay recording refused at attachment). Speculation is width-capped to the 4-row splice: native MTP proposal capacity and `k` and the n-gram/copy lane cap at 3 drafts, MTP lanes refuse draft `k>3` at admission, any direct non-prefill verify or replay above 4 rows is refused before state mutation, and a terminal repair wider than 4 rows declines repair and falls back to reset. The splice emulates the GPU path's BF16 storage boundaries but keeps its own dot accumulation order, so output is not bit-identical to resident or PCIe execution. EP, the expert slab, the expert tier/hotset, AWQ experts and unsupported host dtypes are excluded and stay on PCIe. A load that arms the splice logs `qwen4 routed experts: CPU splice armed (offload_exec=cpu)`; existing native-MTP admission over host-mapped experts is unchanged.
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) hotset + `memory.offload_exec=cpu` split (D2, hotset-tier form; explicit opt-in via `memory.offload_exec=cpu`, no new variable, architecture-generic; the measured default of an unset setting is the next entry).** With the expert hotset applied and `memory.offload_exec=cpu`, hotset-hot routed experts stay on the GPU route while hotset-cold experts run on the CPU for AR decode and `<=4`-row verify (same cap and 3-draft speculation limit as D1). The CPU side has no arch gate: it arms on every layer of any tier plan the loader admitted. The loader's hotset defaults are unchanged: the default sibling `<model>.expert-hotset` applies on exact gfx1201 only (so gfx1201 arms by default under `cpu`), and an explicit absolute `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_HOTSET` sidecar path applies on any architecture (gfx1100 stays an explicit-path opt-in and never applies the sibling sidecar), subject to the existing hotset skips and the tier plan's per-arch format check. An explicit `memory.offload_exec=pcie` and the whole-layer D1 splice (architecture-generic, hotset-free loads only) are unchanged. The partition is deterministic and the router's ids/weights are untouched: per layer the rotated F32 activation, original I32 ids and F32 weights go down (10,320 B/row, no residual), masked ids (40 B/row) and each cold slot's raw F32 output (10,240 B) go up after the GPU down on the same stream, so decode costs `10,360 + 10,240 × cold_slots` B/layer (10,360–112,760), and the original canonical BF16 combine runs once for both arms. The CPU arm is a synchronous scoped pool (no job outlives the join). Eager only: graph and specialized capture, retained replay, shadow validation and AQL/PM4 are refused; EP, PP, the expert slab, AWQ, stock FP8 and non-uniform layouts are unsupported. A layer on a route with no masked ids or cold-slot installation (including a `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_STAGE_MIN_ROWS` forced to at most 4 rows, which would route a narrow window through a staged expert table) is not armed and the load logs one `[moe-cpu-split] qwen4: not armed on <arch>: <reason>` line per reason instead of failing calls later; the loader now reports one `CPU split (D2) armed on N layers (<count> <owner kind>, …; offload_exec=cpu|measured D2 default)` line (hot-set tier layers and whole-layer host aggregates are counted by kind, and the line names which trigger armed them), separately from the D1 splice line. The hotset digest and mode are part of the cache identity, and a load that arms nothing keeps the D1/`pcie` behavior and the empty identity unchanged. Hardware, quality and performance results for the tiered form are in `docs/CONFIG.md` ("D2 status and lab gate"); the whole-layer form's XTX receipts are in the next entry; the lab-only `qwen4_cpu_split_parity` example (`--features lab`, `HIPFIRE_OFFLOAD_EXEC=cpu`, `--hot-budget-mib N [--hotset /abs/P] [--layers ..] [--rows 1..4] [--steps ..] [--greedy] [--json OUT]`) is the same-input correctness/timing probe. Documented in `docs/CONFIG.md`, `docs/env-vars.md` and the `hipfire-dispatch` map.
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) with host-placed routed experts on a narrow host link: the D2 CPU split is now the measured per-load default when `memory.offload_exec` is unset.** Once per load, the engine measures the CPU GEMV on the splice's own pinned physical-core pool against the GPU reading the same host-mapped bytes over the link (zero-copy), on the host layers' real gate/up format, and arms D2 only when the CPU is strictly faster; a tie, a slower CPU, a failed measurement or a unified-memory device stays on PCIe. No host or link bandwidth is assumed anywhere: the comparison uses only what that load measured. It serves decode and `<=4`-row verify of the layers that place experts in host memory (hot-set tier layers and un-tiered QT44/QT53 aggregate layers); prefill and wider verify keep the GPU route over PCIe, placement and host allocations are unchanged, and the speculative width is not capped. **Opt-outs:** `memory.offload_exec=pcie` (an explicit value always wins, both ways) or `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_D2_DEFAULT=0` (`1` forces it on without the comparison); `HIPFIRE_MOE_CPU_EXPERTS=0` also turns it off. The CPU arm keeps its own accumulation order, so the output is not bit-identical to PCIe execution.
  - **Measured on the 7900 XTX (gfx1100) in a Strix Halo host** (hipx, 16 Zen5 cores; measured CPU read 113.55 GB/s: physical-core pool, 4 GiB, `bandwidth` rows at lines 31–51 of `offload-prefill-notes/cpugemm/runs/cpugemm-20261016T193002Z/accepted-summary.json`, under `/home/kaden/qcal/release-0.4.3`) with the card on PCIe 4.0 x4 (the selector measured 4.2 GB/s zero-copy over this link, 7.1 GB/s pinned H2D). Flash-Next mq4-xts split base, q4 PLE, KV Q8, GDN Q8, one card; candidate `7ce8af5bc` against its base beta `61788435d`, two interleaved ABBA pairs, one sample per cell, 8192-row prefill chunk. D2 armed 43 layers (44 under MTP; selector lines: CPU 107.5 / 109.7 / 113.5 GB/s against 4.2 GB/s). Receipts: `d2-default-gates/hold-results/d2-mq4-7ce8af5bc-h1` (j1769) and `d2-default-gates/hold-results/d2-kld-7ce8af5bc-h2` (j1770), under `/home/kaden/qcal/release-0.4.3`.

  - **Determinism:** the two candidate processes produce identical greedy token IDs on all 8 prompts × 64 tokens (exact). **Quality:** paired per-sequence decode KLD, D2 minus PCIe, code24 seq 0:10 (n = 10, the lab `qwen4_kld s11ref --decode --untiered d2|pcie` gate, both arms on the same placement): mean **+0.000554**, paired t 95% CI [−0.002191, +0.003299], bootstrap [−0.001667, +0.002874]. The rule passes (the CI lower bound is ≤ 0, so no significant regression); n = 10 is wide, and the interval admits a small positive delta.
  - **Accepted limits.** (1) A native-MTP verify of more than 4 rows (`k > 3`, a longer n-gram take) takes the unarmed PCIe route, so those rows carry the PCIe arithmetic, not the D2 decode's; the gfx1100 default `k = 3` verifies at most 4 rows. (2) D2 arithmetic depends on the placement: the native-MTP head's reserve shifts one resident layer (MTP cell 44 armed layers, 56.1 GiB pinned host; AR cells 43 layers, 54.9 GiB), which changes which experts run on the CPU. In the H1 hold, native MTP therefore differs from the D2 AR decode on 2 of 8 prompts (fiction_lighthouse at token 39, rust_csv at token 26; the other six identical), and the hold's MTP-equals-AR, equal-placement and equal-stage-state gates are reported FAIL for that reason; D2 AR also differs from the PCIe beta on 4 of 8 prompts (tokens 14, 39, 26 and 42), as the arithmetic differs by design. (3) The lab KLD loader sizes its own context and so places its own layers (37 host layers in H2, against 43 in the product serve load), identically on both arms; the KLD measures D2 against PCIe at that placement, not at the product serve placement.

- **Flash-Next D2 measured default: a fresh `hipfire calibrate` record now supplies the CPU-versus-link rates, so a calibrated load skips the engine-rate probe.** `hipfire calibrate` runs the selector's own `probe_rates` once per CPU-decodable `offload-bench` format at `k` = 5120 (a 192 MiB weight, 5 reps, the CPU arm on the splice pool) and stores each as an `[[calibration.devices.engine]]` entry with `pool = "splice"`; the `pool = "global"` entries are unchanged. At load, only after the explicit `memory.offload_exec`, the typed `developer.qwen4_d2_default`, `HIPFIRE_MOE_CPU_EXPERTS=0`, a load with no host split layers and a unified-memory GPU have decided (none of them reads the record), the selector looks up the tuple it would probe, (gate/up format, `k` = hidden size, `splice` pool, 192 MiB, 5 reps): (1) an exact entry of a fresh record wins; (2) a same-format `splice` entry at another `k` is used only when the margin `|cpu − link| / link` is more than 6%, the measured `k` sensitivity (7900 XTX `offload-bench` `mq4g256v2`, j1760: CPU 105.9 / GPU 4.25 GB/s at k = 5120, 111.8 / 4.19 GB/s at k = 2560); (3) otherwise the live probe runs exactly as before, so a stored figure never decides a close call. Flash-Next's `k` is 2560, so its load takes the 5120 entries through rule 2. The comparison itself is unchanged: D2 turns on only when the CPU rate is strictly higher. A stale record (a different GPU, PCIe link, RAM, CPU or probe version), no record, no entry for the device or format, an unusable rate, a record written before the `splice` entries existed (re-run `hipfire calibrate` to add them) or a margin inside 6% falls back to the live probe. The load logs the source on one line, `qwen4 D2 default rates (device N, <format> k=<k>): from stored calibration (k=<recorded>, wanted <k>) [calibrated <time>]` (an exact entry omits `, wanted <k>`) or `measured at load [<reason>]`. The D2 default resolves after the load's free-VRAM sizing reads and the stored path allocates nothing on the device, so unlike the host-link class it needs no 4 KiB copy and a calibrated and a probed load place the same experts. `hipfire calibrate --show` adds one `D2 default    Flash-Next mq4g256v2 k=2560: …` line per fresh device, the `d2_default::decide` verdict (`ON`, `off` or `not stored for this shape; the engine measures at model load (<reason>)`) on the same stored-rate lookup the load makes, assuming no explicit `memory.offload_exec` and host-placed experts; `--show --json` carries it per device as `d2_default` (`shape`, `status` = `on`/`off`/`probe`, `text`, `stored_k`, `cpu_gbps`, `link_gbps`). Docs: [CONFIG.md](docs/CONFIG.md#calibration-machine-written), [CLI.md](docs/CLI.md#hipfire-calibrate).
- **Fixed: the Flash-Next D2 measured default no longer enables D2 on a fast link (R9700 regression); it compares predicted decode costs of the model's real CPU arm against PCIe, pessimistically for D2.** This supersedes the previous entry's stored-calibration skip (`f4f4aae9f`): the record no longer supplies or replaces any figure. The first selector compared the dense, alone-and-best-of CPU and link bytes/s of a synthetic 192 MiB zero weight, so a CPU that streams dense data faster than a Gen5 link (an R9700: link 26–55 GB/s, CPU 34–154 GB/s) switched D2 on although a real decode step also pays the CPU-to-GPU handoff; a disturbed R9700 (j1406: healthy CPU 119.6 / link 54.8 GB/s against disturbed 47.7 / 55.4) flipped the raw selector and changed the output. It now predicts, per host layer and one full-cold decode row of `top_k` experts (`B` bytes): `PCIe = B / measured link rate + launch floor` against `D2 = the production CPU arm + CURRENT_COPY_TRANSPORT_HANDOFF_NS`, and arms D2 only when `D2 <= 85% of PCIe` (at least 15% faster). The decision costs are pessimistic for D2 and optimistic for PCIe: D2 is the **slowest** of 5 CPU arm samples plus the handoff, PCIe is the **fastest** of 5 live link samples plus the **minimum** launch-floor sample. D2 is chosen whenever that worst case still clears the margin, however wide the spread (an arm disturbed 3× on a 7900 XTX still wins: 0.39 ms × 3 + 0.806 ms against 26 MB at 7 GB/s); a worst case that does not clear, an inconclusive noisy run and any zero, non-positive or failed sample stay on PCIe. There is no spread threshold any more (the earlier `max/min > 1.2` reject is gone); medians and spreads are logged for information. The CPU arm is `moe_cpu_host_slot_outputs` itself (all three projections, the BF16 boundaries, the pinned splice pool) over the layers' actual resident expert spans, a non-zero activation, one untimed warm batch then 5 timed batches of `top_k` *different* cold experts (round-robin across the host layers, about 150 MB so the samples do not re-read one cached set; fewer cold experts than that fails closed). It takes each expert's real CPU codec and span lengths as input and every timed batch carries its own byte count, normalized to the median batch, so a codec or mix with different bytes per expert plugs into the same interface; an owner kind this base has no CPU span owner for (an expert-slab arena) is not D2 eligible and stays on PCIe. The link is 5 live zero-copy reads of 32 MiB plus 5 launch+synchronize floor samples. `CURRENT_COPY_TRANSPORT_HANDOFF_NS` = 806.1 µs is one named constant for today's copy transport (readiness wait 497.7 + post-CPU return 225.9 + result copy 18.2 + resume 56.9 + residual 7.4 µs, per layer, from the j1779 timeline in `xtx-decode50/PLAN.md` §0); it is deliberately conservative (its readiness term includes GPU prerequisites a PCIe route also waits for) and is the term a mapped-result or CPU-wait transport lowers once measured. The probe does not pause the PLE sidecar page-cache prewarm (no reusable pause guard exists on this base, and waiting for a full warm would add load latency): a contending prewarm only slows or scatters the samples, which the pessimistic rule turns into PCIe, never into D2. `hipfire calibrate` stops writing `pool = "splice"` engine entries (legacy entries stay readable and are ignored), and `hipfire calibrate --show` states that D2 is decided at model load (status `load`, or `off` on unified memory) instead of an on/off verdict it cannot make. The load log prints `qwen4 D2 default (N host split layers): ON|off (live samples (…): worst-case D2 … us vs best-case PCIe … us per full-cold decode layer (…x; D2 needs <= 85%) [medians: …]: CPU arm slowest … / median … [spread …] + … handoff; link fastest … / median … GB/s [spread …] + launch floor … ; real-arm probe … ms)`. The probe is about 6 short CPU batches plus 5 reads of 32 MiB over the link (tens of milliseconds on a 7 GB/s link, plus the one-time compile of the read kernel); a successful measurement is reused by a later load of the same shape in the process, a failed one is measured again.
  - **R9700 qualification (`j1417`):** one exclusive 419.9 s hold (600 s cap), three fresh default loads, all 48 host split layers on PCIe every time. The live probe added 88.3 / 92.2 / 85.4 ms wall per process, including setup and link measurements; calibration records do not skip it. Matched tg64 AR means were 48.98 / 48.92 / 48.96 tok/s versus D2-off 48.92 (+0.12% / 0% / +0.08%; pooled +0.07%), with about 0.20% within-process spread and identical 64-token IDs on all 28 requests. Receipt: `release-0.4.3/d2-selector-evidence/run-r9700-gate/GATE-RESULT.json`. This max-seq 8192 fixture is not comparable to the historical 32 tok/s fixture. No new XTX GPU check was performed; disturbed-arm XTX preservation is CPU-test evidence only.
- **Flash-Next native MTP: the draft head's context is now built with the pairing it drafts with, improving draft acceptance.** Head fills paired each token with its own target hidden, while draft steps pair it with the previous position's hidden; committed draft rows also kept the draft chain's guesses. Fills now use (token `p`, target hidden `p - 1`), with the prompt's first row keeping its own hidden, and accepted draft rows are rebuilt from the target's verified hiddens. Both fixes are unconditional, including AR catch-up and terminal repair.
  - R9700, mq4-xts, greedy, forced K=3: τ 1.519 → 1.655 over 15 prompts (1.5K–127K, natural text / Moby / code). Product route: 43.28 → 44.48 tok/s geomean on 9 prompts. Greedy token ids are identical in every prompt.

The base cell ran first after a host restart, so part of the product-route gain is cold start. Greedy token ids are identical in every prompt.
  - Exact: only drafts change; the target verifies every token, and sampled acceptance stays distribution-exact.
  - Session-cache snapshots of an MTP request now also carry the target hidden of their last row, so a prompt fill resumed from a cache hit pairs correctly. Older snapshots lack it: the session cache plans around a stored snapshot (or a parked conversation) the state refuses to restore, so the prefix is prefilled again from the deepest restorable boundary instead of failing the request.

(1) A pair group's interior snapshot row on the NPU-trunk prefill route (Halo, N=8192 on a 9417-token prompt) was published without saving the row. (2) A park of the committed live conversation for a bounded side request (N=17051 in an agent chain) is a capture at the live position, where no prefill boundary runs. Both now save the target hidden of row `N - 1` before the capture.
- **gfx1100/gfx1151: opt-in W4A8 MQ4V2 prefill, `kernel.gfx11_a8_prefill` (`HIPFIRE_GFX11_A8_PREFILL=1`, default off; IU4 W4A4 stays the default).** On symmetric MQ4V2, eager prefill with batch >= 64 and K % 256 == 0, the fused RMSNorm/FWHT, SwiGLU/FWHT (F1-lite h reader), sigmoid-gate and gated-norm producers emit the gfx1201 A8 sidecar (`block_i8_128`: int8 per 128, f32 scale, exact int sum) under `_i8_gfx11` symbols, and a new gfx11 iu8-WMMA GEMM (`gemm_mq4g256v2_residual_mmq_i8.gfx11.hip`: SET/ADD and fused gate/up SiLU, bit-identical to the gfx1201 A8 fold and to a CPU reference) consumes them; 256x256 CTA tiles (1024 threads) when the grid keeps every CU busy, 128x128 tiles otherwise. qwen3.8-27b.mq4-xts on gfx1151 (q8 KV, prefill-scored KLD vs BF16): WT2 0.039374 / code24 0.027297 against 0.040313 / 0.027348 with `kernel.iu4_prefill=false` and 0.069498 / 0.048487 for IU4; pp8192 604 tok/s and pp32000 521 tok/s against 347 / 320 (IU4 off) and 974 / 777 (IU4), i.e. 1.61x / 1.49x the IU4 prefill time (the socket sits at its 85 W limit on this route). The A8 producer launchers lose their `_gfx12` suffix (`fused_rmsnorm_rotate_mq_i8_batched` etc.; gfx1201 symbols unchanged), and the gfx11 IU4 GDN/sigmoid producers no longer run after an A8 producer already emitted the sidecar. Off by default on every architecture: the key trades prompt speed for roughly 43% lower KLD (prompts about 1.5-1.6x slower). Oracle: `crates/hipfire-runtime/examples/a8_gfx11_oracle.rs` (lab-only example, feature `lab`).
- **Flash-Next expert parallelism derives every rank's ownership and load identity from one sealed mesh plan (#861 slice 1; numerics unchanged).** Ownership (`e % N`), physical devices and load identity were re-derived at several sites, and each rank loaded against its own single-device mesh. A load now seals one `Qwen4EpSeal`: one EP mesh epoch, the admitted physical devices, the source generation and one sealed expert plan per routed-expert group (48 trunk layers plus the MTP head), planned by the shared `sealed_moe::plan_packed_expert_parallel` from the source's tensor index. Each rank's compact spans still follow the `e % N` stride the exchange kernels hard-wire; the seal checks that its plans give exactly that stride. Each rank fulfills its weights under the seal's identity for it (mesh epoch, logical rank, physical device): `fulfill_manifest_from_payloads` now accepts a pure EP mesh, and the public `fulfill_manifest_from_payloads_ep` is removed. The source generation covers the base file, the PLE rows sidecar and the trunk-overlay sidecar, which every rank resolves for itself; a rank whose files differ from the ones rank 0 sealed (a replaced base, or a `.ple-q4`/`.trunk-overlay` created or replaced while peers load) is refused before it allocates. The mesh also refuses a peer bound to another seal, rank or device. Logical emulation (`HIPFIRE_EMULATE_GPUS`) now also runs on gfx1151 unified memory (emulation only; physical EP admission is unchanged). Verified there, every rank aliased onto the one GPU: EP2, EP3 and EP4 AR greedy decode are byte-identical to one card (tokens, every logits record and peer mirror, every per-rank state digest) over 8-, 9-, 511-, 512-, 498- and 4,597-token prompts; EP2 native MTP (greedy and sampled) and EP3 native MTP (greedy) match one card in every window, token and semantic state digest (the rollback re-run's discarded `row_capture_output` scratch varies run to run on one card too and is excluded); one-card output is byte-identical to beta.
- **Qwen3.6-27B (gfx1201) loads without AWQ sidecars get a closed kernel route.** The 27B route plan carried only the AWQ producer modules, so a file with no `*.awq_scale.weight` tensors (whose rotate launches select the plain producers) had modules missing from its plan. The planner now reads the sidecar names in the header and, for each producer family whose projection weights lack one (RMSNorm: `in_proj_qkv`/`q_proj`/`gate_proj`; SwiGLU: `down_proj`; gated norm: `linear_attn.out_proj`; standalone rotate: `o_proj`), appends that family's plain decode and non-slab IU4 prefill producers plus the non-slab `_b1` GEMM symbols that read them. The AWQ closure is unchanged, so plans for AWQ files are identical to before; no kernel or numerics change. The VMM exact route's gated-norm rows twin stays AWQ-only: without a `wo` scale it takes the existing per-row path.
- **Flash-Next validation tools attach split-base PLE rows.** `fn_lane_oracle` and `qwen4_parity` now resolve existing sidecars before artifact admission and pass their row provider into bundle assembly, matching the replay gate. Missing q4 rows are refused rather than derived; validation criteria are unchanged.
- **E8P CPU reference fixtures use the developer configuration snapshot** for optional book and benchmark-fixture paths; both inputs are inventoried as developer-only settings.
- **FWHT-rotated 2/4-bit K cache at head_dim 256 (`fwht4`, `fwht2`) quantizes with matched thresholds.** The fwht4/fwht2 K writers unit-normalize the whole 256-dim head and rotate in two 128-wide FWHT blocks, so each coordinate has variance 1/256, but they applied the head_dim-128 Lloyd-Max thresholds (variance 1/128). They, the fwht4→fwht2 transcode, and the CASK asym4 fold on FWHT records now scale by √2 before quantizing; the per-head norm correction absorbs the scale, so the stored format and every reader are unchanged and head_dim 128 is byte-identical. The legacy Givens `legacy-asym4`/`legacy-asym2` writers are unchanged: Givens keeps per-channel outliers, and the same scale made them worse (27B KLD ×1.49 / ×1.15). Only Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 loads with an opt-in `--kv-k fwht4`/`fwht2` change; defaults (q8, fwht3) are untouched.
  - Kernel (gfx1151, synthetic hd 256): K reconstruction relMSE fwht4 0.0133 → 0.0093 (the 4-bit Lloyd-Max optimum), fwht2 0.153 → 0.120; hd 128 byte-identical; writer time unchanged.
  - Per-token KV-only KLD against same-weights F32-KV references (WT2, 2 × 8192): qwen3.8-27b mq4-xt fwht4/q8 0.00163 → 0.00125 (×0.76, paired 95 % CI 0.72–0.81), fwht4/lloyd4 0.00259 → 0.00218 (×0.84); qwen3.6-35b-a3b fwht4/q8 0.00982 → 0.00819 (×0.83), fwht4/lloyd4 0.01247 → 0.01151 (×0.92); qwen3.5-9b fwht4/q8 0.0466 → 0.0369 (×0.79, tail-dominated). Prefill-scored fwht2/q8: 27B ×0.82, A3B ×0.82.
  - Speed unchanged (fresh process per arm, A/B/A/B, 32K context): 27B fwht4/lloyd4 tg 11.74 → 11.74 tok/s, 9B fwht4/q8 tg 37.32 → 37.27 tok/s; serve battery 5/5 on both arms.
- **DeepSeek4: the batched SWA ring write is deterministic when a prefill chunk is longer than the window.** `swa_ring_write_batched_f32` (and its `_pos_f32` twin) launched one workgroup per chunk row, so with more rows than the 128-slot window several workgroups stored to the same slot with no ordering, and a slot could keep an earlier row's value. On Strix Halo (gfx1151, `deepseek-v4-flash-0731.mq2r`, one 1024-row chunk) beta left 123 stale slot columns in the V ring over 10 prefills (each stale element came from the row one window earlier; the K ring was never hit), so `swa_v` digests differed run to run. Only the last `window` rows now store; earlier rows return before writing. After the fix: 0 stale slots in 10 prefills, and repeated `ds4_rows_parity` chunked and launch runs have identical digests (4 of 4 each). Decode reads the V ring, so a stale V slot can change decode output. The DeepSeek4 parent probe uses the same kernel.
- **Pipeline-parallel (`pp>1`) Qwen3.5 decode now splits `<think>` reasoning from answer text, like single-card.** `generate_multi` wrote every released chunk as a `token` event with the think tags still in the text (and used the default EOS filter instead of the Qwen3.5 one), so a thinking model's reasoning arrived as `content` over a PP load while the same request on one card produced `reasoning` events. The decode, forced think-close and budget-alert paths now classify each committed token through `QwenArSemanticProducer`, and the end of the stream runs its shared finish, which releases held tail text (a partial `<think>` marker, an EOT-prefix) and resolves `finish_reason`. CPU tests drive the PP per-token seam and the single-card producer through the same scripted think-tag streams against an independent expected wire sequence, and pin `generate_multi` to that seam.
- **Registry: `decider:4b` (alias `decider`) — the Decider-4B judge for `POST /v1/systemone`.** A dense Qwen3.5-4B finetune (upstream Mapika/decider-4b, Apache-2.0) published as `hipfire-models/decider-4b`, file `decider-4b.mq4` (2,595,461,120 bytes, symmetric MQ4G256V2, uncalibrated). `scripts/registry_gen.py` maps the `decider` family to arch 5 explicitly (dense, like the Qwen3.5 base; an unmapped family aborts the whole daily run), and `scripts/test_registry_gen_decider.py` pins the mapping and the entry. No `[models."decider:4b".overrides.decide.calibration]` profile ships: the artifact is uncalibrated, and a calibration snippet is added only after one is measured.
- **Flash-Next keeps a long conversation across a short unrelated request.** In the measured 17-request Strix Halo chain (q8 state, 4 GiB pool), a 435-token side request displaced a 203K-token live conversation; the next main turn re-prefilled 174,164 rows from the prime's 40,960-row snapshot and took 96 s TTFT. Early-diverging requests with at most 8192 total prompt/output/write-lookahead rows can now park the main conversation's fixed state and overwritten rows under the existing memory guard and restore it byte-exactly for a live append. Tail/resident-restored turns also keep publishing session-exact pool snapshots instead of silently disabling capture.
- **Pruned Qwen4 slab CPU admission honors `qwen4.expert_keep`.** The fail-closed path now validates the original-id sparse table rather than requiring excluded experts, returning `ExpertSlabKernelsUnavailable` with kept-expert counts. Excluded experts still occupy zero payload bytes; supported GPU W3 admission is unchanged.
- **Qwen4 original-id expert pruning:** `qwen4.expert_keep` carries sorted per-layer keep lists and a verified SHA-256 of compact `{"layers":…,"mtp":…}` JSON. Router ids remain in the 512-way space; absent slab entries occupy zero payload bytes and publish null pointers. A separately registered masked top-10 kernel preserves the incumbent's wave-local selection, index-order float32 softmax, selected-probability renormalization and BF16 rounding, masking excluded logits before rounding; unmarked models retain their incumbent kernels and routing arithmetic. Pruned artifacts are single-device only: EP and expert-hotset/tier placement are refused, as is discrete host-streamed placement; resident discrete and UMA loads size the actual kept payload.
- **Qwen4 masked (`expert_keep`) router now fails closed like the dense router.** `moe_router_softmax_top10_masked_f32` takes the sealed call's `layer` and `row_base` and records into the same router fault word: a NaN or ±Inf logit of a kept expert, a failed softmax denominator (e.g. an empty keep row) or a failed selected-probability sum writes ids `-1` / weights `0` for the row and reports `layer, row` at the next readback check, exactly as the dense router does. Excluded experts' logits are never read, so NaN/Inf there cannot fault the row; finite kept rows keep the masked kernel's float32 arithmetic bitwise. The wrapper also rejects logits/top-k buffers too small for the fixed E512/top-10 geometry before launch. Dense-routed models do not take this kernel and are unchanged (their kernel sources are unmodified; the masked kernel's launch ABI gained `fault, layer, row_base`). The ignored gfx1201 test `expert_keep_route` now uses a finite-floor dense reference (the dense router rejects `-inf`), poisons absent logits with NaN/±Inf, and adds kept-NaN/±Inf and empty-mask fault cases.
- **Qwen4 pruned-expert handling is default-inert for dense artifacts.** Absent-expert (null pointer / empty-extent) acceptance in the resident, slab and slab-stage expert tables now applies only to experts outside the layer's `qwen4.expert_keep` row, so a dense null slab-stage entry or a dense tier/slab entry with an empty extent is rejected as before; the redundant empty-tier-entry skip is removed (tier placement of pruned artifacts is refused). `qwen4_i4_slabs` runs its per-record preflight only with `--expert-keep`, restoring the dense CLI's former error timing without a 24,576-file stat pass. Config admission requires `num_experts=512` and `num_experts_per_tok=10` whenever `qwen4.expert_keep` is present, matching the fixed masked-router kernel (synthetic configs with other geometry are refused instead of reading the mask out of bounds).
  - **Pruned CPU-expert placement stays unsupported.** The opt-in CPU routed-expert splice (`memory.offload_exec=cpu`) never arms on a layer that carries `qwen4.expert_keep`: its host owners index experts by original id, but pruned payloads are compact, so pruned artifacts remain single-device and fully resident. The loader still refuses host-mapped or streamed placement for them, and a direct bundle load with host-mapped pruned experts now simply does not arm the splice.
- **`hipfire bench --json` reports native MTP acceptance over the windows that drafted.** `spec_tau` is accepted drafts over every window, and the AR floor's tokens accept nothing: its timed AR tokens (the calibration token, plus the probes of a would-be retirement) and, once it retires a request whose windows cost more per token than AR, every later head-free AR token. A retired request therefore read as rejected drafts. One 7900 XTX running Flash-Next with host-offloaded experts (humaneval_0, 128 tokens) reported `tau 0.21`: its 16 native windows accepted 22 drafts (1.38 per window) at 840 ms each against a 175 ms AR token, and the request retired at window 23. Floor off, the XTX's drafts accept like the R9700's. The per-run `spec_mtp` now carries `windows_mtp`, `windows_floor_ar`, `windows_ar_retired`, `retired_at`, `accepted` and `tau_mtp` = `accepted / (windows_mtp - windows_floor_ar)`. The native MTP `done` event carries `accepted` (the exact numerator of `tau`) and `floor_ar_windows`. Reporting only; routing and generated tokens are unchanged.
- **Flash-Next pipeline parallelism (host-staged, opt-in, experimental): `topology.pp` 2..=8 runs Qwen3.8 Flash-Next as layer bands, one band per card, over cards that need no peer access.** The trunk is cut into contiguous bands over 2 to 8 cards of one exact arch (gfx1100 or gfx1201) with `tp = ep = 1`. It runs the packed `mq4` artifact and the expert-slab `mq3-xts`/`mq2-xts` builds (see the expert-slab bullet below). Every band keeps all of its routed experts resident (no host-mapped experts), and each band edge moves the hyper-connection streams through pinned host memory (`HIPFIRE_MESH_TRANSPORT=auto|host`; `peer` is refused because no byte-qualification evidence exists before side effects). The default `topology.pp = 1` is unchanged, and single-card, expert-parallel and dense tensor-parallel loads are untouched.
  - **Enable it.** `hipfire config set topology.pp N` (or `HIPFIRE_TOPOLOGY_PP=N`) applies to `hipfire run`, `serve` and `bench`, and the daemon load takes `params.pp` (an explicit value above 1 wins). There is no load-time `--pp` CLI flag: `hipfire bench --pp` stays the prompt-size list. The first listed card in `hardware.devices` is the output card and runs the **last** logical band (`output_norm`, `lm_head`, sampling and the MTP head); the other cards run the earlier bands in list order. `HIPFIRE_PP_LAYERS=a,b,…` gives the band counts in logical band order, the default is a uniform split, and the first band must hold at least 2 layers (the PLE layer).
  - **What runs.** AR decode, pipelined prefill (canonical chunks flow through the bands in order), per-band in-memory session caches (`memory.session_cache_bytes` is a per-band budget) and greedy native MTP on an explicit `--spec mtp`. The daemon's one speculative loop (`generate_spec`) drives the native drafter's mesh entries with the model's `Gpus`: prefill, window step, forced advance, terminal-prefix repair and reset. Sampled or penalized requests decode AR; MTP sessions are not distributed, so a native-MTP load attaches no session cache and a mesh MTP request reuses and publishes no snapshot. The router leaves single and EP calls unchanged and never promotes a mesh to lanes/VMM.
  - **Known limitation.** Only the all-band 4,096-token stride snapshots are reusable under PP; the single-card resident tail/lineage snapshot is not shared across bands, so prompts under 4,096 tokens are always prefilled cold.
  - **Memory.** Admission checks every band against its own card before any allocation (weights, F16 shadows, QSA context, state, forward scratch, native MTP terms and the reserve against free VRAM) and refuses naming `topology.pp`, each failing rank and its shortfall; rebalance `HIPFIRE_PP_LAYERS` or lower `memory.max_seq`.
  - **Faults.** After every mesh drain the bands' router-fault words and bounded-wait timeouts are read on every device: a non-finite router row or a wait timeout on any band fails the whole pipelined request (its logits are never read back) and quarantines the mesh, which then refuses further work until the model is reloaded. Fault words are cleared only when an idle request starts.
  - **What is refused.** Before any card is touched, with `qwen4: pipeline parallelism (topology.pp = N) does not support <subject>; drop the option or set topology.pp = 1`: DFlash, DSpark, n-gram drafting, DDTree, adaptive KV, an EAGLE drafter, CASK, PFlash, an experts-per-token override, a non-Single compute placement, the MTP n-gram modifier (`speculation.mtp_ngram = on`), host-mapped routed experts (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_VRAM_LAYERS`), the expert hotset, expert staging (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_STAGE=1`), session snapshots (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_TURN_SNAPSHOTS=1`), the session cache disk tier and the NPU trunk (`on`/`emulate`). Also refused: `HIPFIRE_EMULATE_GPUS` aliasing, too few visible devices, an unknown PCI identity, an arch other than gfx1100 or gfx1201, mixed arches, a malformed `HIPFIRE_PP_LAYERS`, unified-memory cards, lane batching and `bench_prefill`. A speculative request that reaches the mesh with anything but greedy native MTP (or with eviction or a resume) is refused with a validation error before any state mutation.
  - **Qualify a box.** `scripts/fn-ep-gate.sh --mode pp` (options `--pp-layers COUNTS`, `--transport auto|host`, `--ref-ranks R` for a PP-R reference when one card would need more pinned RAM than the host has, and `--mtp` for the native-MTP exactness arm under the fixed policy `HIPFIRE_MTP_AR_FLOOR=0`, `HIPFIRE_MTP_INCREMENTAL=0`, `HIPFIRE_MTP_NGRAM=off`, `--spec mtp --temp 0 --ngram off`) runs `fn_ep_oracle --pp N --canonical-state` against the reference, byte-compares tokens, logits and state, and writes a receipt with pp, bands, transport, each rank's PCI id, arch and link, and host RAM. `fn_ep_oracle` gains `--pp N` (the daemon's `params.pp`); its PP arm records the same `window`/`tokens`/`state` records as Single with the MTP head digests (`mtp.<name>`) in the canonical union, and `meta.json` adds `numerical_policy` and `placement`.
  - **Qualified so far.** Three R9700 (gfx1201), packed `mq4`, bands 16/16/16, host-staged edges, one binary for every arm: PP3 is byte-identical to one card and to the cut-safe one-card schedule in tokens, every logits row and the canonical state, for AR decode after a pipelined three-chunk prefill with an exact 276-row tail and for greedy native MTP (including the MTP head state). Through the daemon, four committed requests with a 7,659-token prompt give identical text on PP3 and one card, and both reuse 4,096 cached tokens on the repeated prefix. No gfx1100 cell and no performance claim yet.
  - **Docs.** `docs/multi-gpu.md` has the new Flash-Next pipeline parallelism section and corrects the generic Qwen3.5/3.6 PP text: that route moves the residual with a peer memcpy (`boundary_copy`) and needs peer access; the driver fallback its source comment mentions is not a hipfire host-staged path, and only Flash-Next PP has an admitted host-staged edge service. `HIPFIRE_PP_PFLASH` / `HIPFIRE_PP_DFLASH` are documented as generic-route flags that do not change Flash-Next PP.
- **Flash-Next expert-slab builds (`mq3-xts`, `mq2-xts`) load under pipeline parallelism (`topology.pp` 2..=8).** Each card loads only its own band's slab arenas, fully in VRAM, and the MTP head's experts sit on the output card. R9700 (gfx1201) runs `mq3-xts` and `mq2-xts`; 7900 XTX (gfx1100) runs `mq2-xts` only, because the MQ3 codec is not available on gfx1100, as on one card. `mq2-xts` (about 47 GB) fits fewer cards than the packed `mq4` trunk (about 68 GB): roughly the file size over N per card, before the runtime terms. The refusal for slab artifacts under `topology.pp` is gone; host-mapped experts, the hotset and expert staging stay refused. `scripts/fn-ep-gate.sh --mode pp` takes a slab container as its model file. See [docs/multi-gpu.md](docs/multi-gpu.md#expert-slab-builds-mq3-xts-mq2-xts).
  - **Qualified so far.** R9700 (gfx1201), host-staged edges, one binary for every arm, on pre-release exports of both builds (same expert codecs as the published files, not those files): `mq3-xts` (W3 and MQ4 slabs) at PP3, bands 16/16/16, and `mq2-xts` (E8P and MQ4 slabs) at PP2, bands 24/24, are byte-identical to one card and to the cut-safe one-card schedule in tokens, every logits row and the canonical state, for AR decode after a pipelined three-chunk prefill with an exact 276-row tail and for greedy native MTP (including the MTP head state). The one-card reference host-maps the slab layers that do not fit: 29 of 48 for `mq3-xts` (about 31 GiB pinned) and 23 of 48 for `mq2-xts` (about 19 GiB). Measured per-card VRAM peaks: `mq3-xts` PP3 21–23 GB, `mq2-xts` PP2 25–27 GB. No gfx1100 cell and no performance claim yet.
- **Flash-Next native MTP: the AR floor no longer prices AR from the process's first decode token.** A singleton request's floor prices AR by its first decode token, and on a fresh process that token pays the decode route's one-time kernel binds (Strix Halo: 55.6 ms against the next request's 30.0 ms in the same process, about 140 ms in an agent-transcript run, 9.35 s once). AR priced that high kept a request whose speculation loses from ever retiring to AR, and priced each extra draft at several real rows (the cost fit's prior is 0.27 AR steps per row), so a request that fell to one draft in a low-acceptance stretch stayed there (Halo n-gram copy-lane transcript: 625 native windows at one draft, 72% accepted). The drafter's first AR token now prices nothing, as its first window at each depth already did, and the next window calibrates again: one extra AR token per drafter. Output is unchanged (an AR token either way). CPU, through the drafter with Halo costs and a first token at 4.7 AR tokens: a 0.2-acceptance request retires (beta pricing drafts to its end), and after a 200-window 0.45-acceptance dip the one-draft share is 0.1% (beta pricing 64% at budget 7, 88% at 3).
- **Native Qwen4 singleton MTP re-arms after thinking retires it, and a fresh adaptive request starts at depth `min(3, cap)`.** A Strix Halo thinking request retired the AR floor during its reasoning and then decoded the answer, about 2300 tokens, head-free at 32.8 tok/s against about 48 tok/s with MTP (about 26 s); on R1 the first K7 request's 308 windows accepted 29% (34.7 tok/s) against 53.9 tok/s for its sibling. Now, once per newly emitted tokenizer think-close (`</think>`) token after retirement within the same request, the floor resets to the request-start thresholds and config, the head catches up on its owed rows first, AR is recalibrated and MTP is probed again; no sampler or target state is mutated. A request with no measured depth history now starts at `min(3, cap)`; the cap is unchanged (`auto` on gfx1151 stays 7) and measured evidence still grows the depth to it. Forced diagnostic routes are unchanged. Verifier contract unchanged: greedy and naive output stays AR-exact, Leviathan stays exact in distribution. Docs: `HIPFIRE_MTP_K`, `HIPFIRE_MTP_AR_FLOOR`, `HIPFIRE_MTP_FLOOR_MIN_WINDOWS` ([`env-vars.md`](docs/env-vars.md)), `mtp_k` ([`CONFIG.md`](docs/CONFIG.md)).
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) developer schedule `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_CUT_LAYERS` (default off): the "cut-safe Single" of the pipeline-parallel parity gate.** It runs the single-card trunk program as separate interpreter runs split before each listed layer, so no `HyperWrite`→`HyperRead` fusion, gate quarters or HC fusion state crosses a future pipeline band boundary (eager only; refuses diagnostic taps, EP and the NPU pair route; unset changes nothing). Gate result, same binary, `fn_ep_oracle` one card, cuts `9,17,25,33,41` and `2,24,47` against the uncut program: tokens, every logits record and raw dump and every state digest byte-identical on gfx1201 (R9700) and gfx1100 (7900 XTX) for 3×256-token AR decode, native MTP verify windows and a 4,396-token prompt; kernel traces confirm each cut replaces the fused `hyper_write_norm_f32` / rotated read with the separate write, norm and gate launches.
- **gfx1151: Muse Glimmer prefill 5x faster and DFlash decode ~3x faster, bitwise identical.** The single-wave HFQ4-G256 WMMA GEMMs (`gemm_hfq4g256_residual_wmma_k2` / `_k2x32` / `_k4`) ran at their VGPR-limited 16 waves/SIMD. Each wave re-reads one 128-byte line per weight row over 8 K-tile pairs, so at large grids the resident working set overflowed the caches and the kernels fell to ~15 GB/s: Glimmer gate/up (M=19968, K=6656) took 4.4 ms at 4 rows and 50 ms at 192 rows. On gfx1151, grids of 640+ blocks now reserve 512 B of dynamic LDS per weight row, which only caps occupancy (gate/up: 0.52 ms at 4 rows). Full 96-column batches route `gemm_hfq4g256_batched_lmhead` to the Muse RM2/BV6 kernel (same per-accumulator K2 order; gate/up 5.5 ms at 192 rows), and Q8 prefill widths (`M >= 4096`, `M % 64 == 0`, `N % 64 == 0`) route `gemm_q8_0_batched_chunked` to `gemm_q8_0_wmma_4w` (same per-accumulator dequant and K order). Output bytes are unchanged on every route: Glimmer prefill logits match beta bit for bit at 384 and 576 tokens on `.mq4` and `.mq4r`, and serve battery transcripts (AR and DFlash) are byte-identical. Strix Halo, `hipfire bench --matrix`, beta → this change: `.mq4` pp512 30.5 → 151.1 tok/s, pp2560 30.5 → 148.5; `.mq4r` pp512 30.6 → 155.0, pp2560 30.2 → 155.4; tg64 unchanged. DFlash serve battery (greedy, profit guard off), same tau: `.mq4` 7.4 → 21.3 tok/s, `.mq4r` 6.7 → 19.7. Other gfx1151 callers of these routes (Qwen3.5 MQ4 residual prefill below 128 rows, MQ4 DFlash `lm_head` at M=248K, which is 3.2x faster at 16 rows) get the same bitwise-identical speedup. gfx1100 and gfx12 routing is unchanged.
- **PeaceMaker CPU test fixtures account for the RDNA code-end guard.** Refresh the lift F2 bundle payload size and the RIP QSA assembly baselines after binary bisection isolated the image refresh (`18909b331`) and emitter change (`906c75705`), respectively. Strict old/new object comparison proves identical kernel instructions, symbols and descriptors, with only the expected alignment/guard tail and derived ELF/container layout fields changed.
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) on gfx1201: the default fp8 QSA K/V state now has a KLD gate and GPU tests (no behavior change).** `kv_cache = auto` has been fp8 on exact gfx1201 since 0.4.0: E4M3 codes with one f16 scale per KV head and token, and BF16 index keys. That default was validated by parity and greedy agreement only, because no Flash-Next KLD reference existed then. The new `crates/rdna-compute/tests/qsa_fp8_state.rs` (exact gfx1201, `lab`, ignored by default) runs three checks:
  - The production append writes E4M3 rows byte-identical to a CPU model of the encoder.
  - Single-row, batched (1–8 rows) and gathered WMMA attention over the fp8 state match an f64 reference over the decoded bytes.
  - The fp8-state output stays within the derived E4M3 bound of the F32 state's; relative L2 is 2.5–2.7 % on every route and length.
  - **KLD:** R9700, canonical `qwen3.8-flash-next-gptq3.mq4` with q4 PLE rows, one binary for every arm, against the HF BF16 teacher refs (24 sequences, 95 % paired bootstrap).
    - Code 24 × 512: fp8 0.082302 vs the F32 state (`kv_cache = "bf16"`) 0.080320 (+0.0020 [−0.0012, +0.0053]) and q8 0.080855 (+0.0014).
    - WikiText-2 24 × 2048: fp8 0.078071 vs F32 0.080890 (−0.0028 [−0.0072, +0.0005]) and q8 0.075610 (+0.0025).
  - **Speed:** same card, `max_seq` 262,144, ABBA with 2 runs per arm.
    - Decode ITL: fp8 27.2 / 27.1 / 28.5 / 30.9 ms vs F32 32.1 / 32.9 / 36.4 ms at 8K / 32K / 128K / 256K.
    - Prefill: fp8 4,410 / 4,246 / 3,586 / 2,986 tok/s vs F32 3,646 (warm run) / 3,437 / 2,702 tok/s; the 128K and 256K prefills are incremental over the previous prompt.
    - F32 does not finish the 256K prompt on a 32 GB card: mapping the QSA context runs out of memory at 253,952 tokens, and the request is rolled back.
  - **Memory:** at 262,144 tokens the QSA context is 4,056 MiB for fp8 vs 14,208 MiB for F32, so 12.9 GiB of experts stay in VRAM instead of 4.1 GiB. Most of the decode gap comes from that placement.
  - **MTP and serve:** greedy native MTP equals AR under fp8 in all four MTP arms (256 and 1,200 ids). On the serve route, battery, chain and an 8,552-token session snapshot save → restore → live prefix reuse pass. The coding session's literal `dedupe` recall check misses because the model writes "deduplication".
- **Flash-Next router non-finite rows fail closed.** A NaN or infinity in a router row invalidates that row's expert slots instead of letting an `INT_MAX` candidate reach an expert-table index. Routed expert consumers check expert bounds before indexing. A device-side router error is reported at the host synchronization boundary with its layer and row, failing the request rather than faulting the GPU or returning partial output. Finite routing retains the existing arithmetic and ordering.
- **Slab and expert-parallel PeaceMaker consumers range-check expert ids.** `mq_i4_moe_gemv` (gfx1151 and gfx1201 images re-emitted, M7 obligation-free) takes a trailing `n_experts@88` (kernarg 88 → 96 bytes with a zero word at 92; the dispatch `MoeGemvKernargs` and the byte oracle follow) and returns before indexing `expert_weight_ptrs` for an id at or past it. The EP2 `ep_gather_grouped_rows_by_tile_owner_pm` (gfx1201 and gfx1100 images re-emitted) no longer pulls from the peer for an owner outside `{0, 1}`, as N8 already did for `0..8`. The hipcc `ep_gather_rows_by_owner` takes a trailing `n_experts` (`Gpu::ep_gather_rows_by_owner` and `EpSlotOwners::ExpertModulo` carry it) so an id outside `[0, n_experts)` owns nothing instead of an `e % ranks` owner. `qwen4_slab_tile_mask`, `ep_tile_mask`, `qwen4_ep_owner_assign_pm` already range-checked and are unchanged.
- **Slab K1/K2 range-check extends to the gfx1100 and E8P images (current ABI).** The gfx1100 MQ4-only and both archs' E8P `e8p_i4_moe_gemv` K1 kernargs grow 88 → 96 bytes (`n_experts@88`, zero `reserved@92`) and the gfx1100 MQ4/E8P and gfx1201 E8P NT1 K2 kernargs 60 → 64 bytes (`n_experts@60`), matching the shared gfx1151/gfx1201 MQ4/W3 images. A workgroup whose expert id is `>= n_experts` (one unsigned compare, so negative ids too) exits before the pointer-table index, any weight prefetch and the first barrier, storing nothing; finite-id arithmetic is unchanged. CPU descriptor tests pin the 96/64-byte kernarg layouts of every served K1/K2 image; earlier 88/60-byte receipts keep their qualified scope.
- **`moe_nan_guard_regress` proves the MoE non-finite guard on a real GPU against the old kernels (harness only, no product path).** The example compiles the `origin/beta` sources (`git show` of the pinned baseline commit `f1a457b`, or `--old-dir`; sha256 and the baseline commit are printed) as `<symbol>__beta` next to the new kernels, and the two PM images from `git show` next to the new embedded ones. Finite input must match bitwise: router incumbent and fast, stable and fused scatter, unscatter+SiLU, Q8/MQ4G128V2 indexed and grouped down, both combines (f32 and BF16-input), the full router → scatter → down → combine chain, the PM `mq_i4_moe_gemv_mq4sym_*` K1 pair (88 → 96 B kernarg) and the grouped IU4 sym gate/up and down images (60 → 64 B). Rows with NaN, `±Inf`, BF16-overflowing logits and raw ids `-1`/`512`/`INT_MAX`/`INT_MIN` must fail closed, record the right `(layer, row)`, fault nothing and leave every other row bitwise unchanged; a negative control runs the old router on a NaN row and requires it to violate the contract. Each case runs in its own child process under a 600 s supervisor budget. Build with `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 cargo build -p hipfire-runtime --release --features lab --example moe_nan_guard_regress` and run `target/release/examples/moe_nan_guard_regress --expect-arch gfx1201`; CPU contract tests (fault encoding and error text, the scatter model, a family-wide expert-bound scan, guard markers present now and absent at the old ref) run with `cargo test -p hipfire-runtime --release --features lab --example moe_nan_guard_regress`. About 150 MiB of device memory.
- **`ep_transport_oracle` proves host-staged multi-GPU transport on cards without peer access (feature `lab`, harness only).** `--devices 0,1[,..]` runs one rank per device and host thread over shared mapped-pinned host banks: owned rows/tiles are published into the bank, every producer is host-synchronized (or stream-waited) before the existing gather kernels read it, and a bank is reused only after every reader finished. It checks every byte, coherency across reuse and a read-before-publish negative control, and times EP exchange shapes and pipeline boundary hops against P2P. `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EP_TRANSPORT=auto|peer|host` selects the transport when `--transport` is absent; `host` never enables peer access. Measured on two R9700 (Gen5 x16): 356/356 byte cases pass; a 10-row EP decode exchange takes 47.0 µs host-staged vs 55.5 µs over P2P (host-waited), and a one-row 40 KB boundary hop 48.6 µs vs 49.1 µs. No EP route uses host staging; the Flash-Next pipeline-parallel route above has its own host-staged edge service.
- **Qwen thinking history preserves each assistant turn's generated tokens.** The turn-splice cache distinguishes normalized content and tool calls by producer reasoning text, so consecutive reasoning-only turns no longer overwrite each other. Clients that omit `reasoning_content` recover a cached turn only when its content/tool key is unambiguous; otherwise that turn renders normally. Completed open-think stops now replay the unclosed generated body verbatim, without inserting a synthetic `</think>`. Length terminals with a complete call-less body are stored too (next entry); truncated or malformed tool output, suppressed hidden calls, stop-sequence, abort and fail-closed terminals remain unstored. The existing prompt-cache cap (default 32 turns) is unchanged.
- **Qwen splice cache stores `length`-terminated turns (AR, native MTP, DFlash), including open-think length.** A `length` terminal whose body is complete and call-less stores the emitted token body under the unchanged content/tool fingerprint plus producer reasoning text, so the next turn's template re-render splices it instead of re-tokenizing. The template's per-turn `im_end` framing is retained and no synthetic think close is inserted. A `length` terminal with truncated or malformed tool output, or with completed calls that are suppressed (hidden calls cannot be described in the echo key, and no calls are released at `length`), stays unstored; an open-think stop follows the same guard, and stop-sequence, abort and fail-closed terminals remain unstored. Measured issue (R2, Strix Halo, Flash-Next): 3 of 16 turns ended `length`; one, with emitted think tokens, re-rendered divergently at row 68,711, so the next turn fell back to the 44,992 resident rows and prefilled 38,701 rows in total, with TTFT 21.7 s instead of ~5 s. The fix caches the body; the wire output is unchanged.
- **Registry: split-base PLE sidecars are a generic `ple` map.** A registry entry now names its PLE row files as `"ple": {"q4": {…}, "q8": {…}}`, keyed by format token (lowercase letters and digits), replacing the fixed `ple_q4` / `ple_q8` fields (the bundled `qwen3.8:flash-next-mq3-xts` entry is converted and `registry/v1.json` regenerated). Every key is validated the same way: the entry's `file` must be a split base, the sidecar is `<file>.ple-<key>` or, for the Flash-Next family only, the shared `qwen3.8-flash-next.ple-<key>` (pinned identically wherever it is named), and `registry_gen.py` pins each from the live tree (LFS sha256 required). An unknown key such as a future `q2` parses and validates; a client plans only the formats it can load (`q4`, `q8`) and ignores the rest with a note. `q8` is the exact reference: it is the fallback when a lossy format a client wants is unpublished, and an explicit `--ple q8` never falls back. `plan_pull`, the on-demand download, `--ple all`, `rm` and listings follow the map.
- **A verified local Flash-Next monolithic keeps serving the split MQ4 XTS tags.** A pin compiled into the client (`GRANDFATHERED_MONOLITHICS`: split base `eafaff94…`, 70,888,270,360 B ↔ monolithic `8b15b6fe…`, 125,288,544,792 B, canonical and `-gptq3.mq4` names) lets a SHA-verified monolithic serve a registry entry that carries the split-base identity: `hipfire pull` prints `Already satisfied (monolithic): <path> (serves <tag> without the split base)` and downloads no base, skips the q8 rows the monolithic embeds, links a planned q4 beside it, and still re-fetches the monolith-bound overlay and expert hot set when missing; `rm`, listings and the path resolvers know both spellings. The split base's own trunk-overlay and expert-hot-set pins (`e3e352ca…`, `91143074…`) are added next to the monolithic's. The four stock MQ4 tags carry that identity.
- **Resolving a pinned monolithic no longer hashes 125 GB on every load.** Verification is cached in `<HIPFIRE_HOME>/cache/verified-artifacts.json` (one record per path: device, inode, size, mtime seconds and nanoseconds, SHA-256, verified-at). An unchanged file with a record for the same pin skips the hash; a changed mtime, size or inode, or a record for another SHA-256, hashes again and rewrites the record atomically. A corrupt or unwritable cache file is ignored, never fatal.
