- **`hipfire pull --ple auto` on a mixed-GPU host fetches the union of what every GPU arch defaults to.** A gfx1100 + gfx1151 host plans q4 and q8 (it used to follow whichever arch the sysfs listing returned first); no GPU still plans q8, and a verified grandfathered monolithic trims the plan to q4 because it embeds q8. The interactive summary preselects the same union. The load-time on-demand download resolves `memory.ple_format = auto` with the arch of the card the load targets (`hardware.devices`, else `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, else the first ROCr agent), falling back to the first detected arch when the CLI cannot tell.
- **Unified-memory host sizing no longer counts free CMA pages as available, and the session cache keeps a larger unified-memory headroom.** `MemAvailable` includes free pages of CMA pageblocks (`CmaFree` in `/proc/meminfo`), which only movable allocations can use; pinned GTT and kernel allocations cannot. A host reporting `MemAvailable` 81,450,396 kB and `CmaFree` 13,858,816 kB (even with `CmaTotal` 0) therefore had ~13 GiB less available to a GTT allocation than every sizing site assumed, so a load or a session-cache capture sized to the larger figure could still reach the global OOM killer. One shared accounting in `rdna_compute::uma_memory` now subtracts it: host bytes available to unmovable allocations = `MemAvailable − CmaFree`, saturating at 0, with a missing `CmaFree` counted as 0 (a kernel without CMA is unchanged); the figure is unavailable only when `MemAvailable` is unreadable. New exported helpers `meminfo_available_bytes` (from `/proc/meminfo` text), `mem_available_bytes` (live) and `host_total_bytes` (`MemTotal`) replace the per-crate `MemAvailable` parsers, and every direct host sizing site reads them: the free-device-memory clamp on a GTT-backed APU (`Gpu::device_mem_info` and `Gpu::device_mem_info_for`, which share it), the OOM guard's host headroom check, host-mapped expert and offload placement, PLE prewarm, hot-row store and load-fill budgets, and the load-time JIT worker count. The TTM page-pool estimate (freed GTT pages the next GTT allocation takes first) is unchanged and is still added on top where it applied: `MemAvailable − CmaFree + TTM pool estimate`. Discrete GPUs and carve-out APUs keep `hipMemGetInfo`'s figure. The session cache (`memory.session_cache_bytes`, `HIPFIRE_SESSION_CACHE_BYTES`) keeps free device memory untouched for the live state's context growth and the allocation in flight; that headroom on a unified-memory APU is now `clamp(MemTotal / 16, 2 GiB, 8 GiB)` (was a fixed 1 GiB), so 32 GiB hosts keep 2 GiB and 128 GiB hosts 8 GiB; a discrete GPU keeps 256 MiB. Every allocation path of the cache, including disk staging, applies it, so a capture or a staged restore never takes the room the live context still needs to grow. The cache's byte budget (default 8 GiB) and the TTM pool addition are unchanged.
- **Unified-memory host sizing subtracts the whole CMA region, so Kexec HandOver (KHO) scratch no longer counts as available; model loads and `hipfire diag` warn about it.** Kernels with KHO enabled by default (Ubuntu 7.0 generic: `CONFIG_KEXEC_HANDOVER_ENABLE_DEFAULT=y`) release their boot-time scratch memory as `MIGRATE_CMA` pageblocks without counting it in `CmaTotal`; only movable allocations can use them, and page cache that fills them still counts in `MemAvailable`, so `MemAvailable − CmaFree` still over-reported by up to the whole region once the cache filled it. The shared rule in `rdna_compute::uma_memory` is now host bytes available to unmovable allocations = `MemAvailable − max(CmaFree, cma_region)`, saturating at 0, where `cma_region` is the larger of `CmaTotal` and the sum of the `/proc/zoneinfo` `cma` pages × 4 KiB (the per-zone `cma` line, not `nr_free_cma`; unreadable zoneinfo falls back to `CmaTotal`). Every sizing site that reads `meminfo_available_bytes` / `mem_available_bytes` / `host_available_from` / `host_available_bytes` gets it, and `meminfo_available_bytes` / `host_available_from` / `compile_jobs::available_memory` take the zoneinfo text. New `kho_scratch_from` / `kho_scratch_bytes` return the CMA pageblocks outside any registered CMA area (zoneinfo `cma` sum minus `CmaTotal`). A model load on a unified-memory GPU prints `KHO scratch reserves N GiB unusable by the GPU; boot with kho=off to reclaim it` once per process when that is at least 1 GiB, and `hipfire diag` (text and `--json` key `kho_scratch`) reports a `pass`, or a `warn` (never a failure) with the same text; the TUI doctor lists it as a `KHO scratch` check. Measured on hipx (Strix Halo, 128 GB, kernel 7.3.0-rc7-perfopt+ from Ubuntu's config): `CmaTotal` 0, `CmaFree` 13.2 GiB after boot (0.45 GiB once page cache fills it), zoneinfo `cma` 3,465,216 pages = 13,536 MiB = the KHO scratch (760 + 8,476 + 4,300 MiB). Fix: boot with `kho=off`; see `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`.
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) row-exact wide verify, default off (both per-arch caps stay 8, every wide switch off).** An MTP/n-gram verify forward of n rows equals n sequential `forward_token` steps byte for byte only while every few-row route (`route_rows <= 8`, the per-row twins of the decode GEMVs) serves it; above 8 rows the verify falls to prefill routes (Halo nat-8k: max |Δlogit| 1.7–2.3 at n ≥ 9, argmax agreed). The few-row gates now read `Gpu::few_row_limit`: inside an eager verify forward it is the arch's proven row count `qwen4_row_exact_verify_rows` (`QWEN4_ROW_EXACT_VERIFY_ROWS_GFX1151` / `_GFX1201`, both 8, so no route changes; developer override `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_WIDE_VERIFY_ROWS`, clamped to 8..=32, for oracle runs); recording and graph capture keep 8, and so does a verify whose AR runs recorded with a QSA decode attention policy that differs from eager (`guarded_wide_verify_rows`; both conditions have recording-inventory rows). Above 8 rows, S1 loops every few-row launcher's existing <=8-row launch over 8-row groups (`few_row_groups`); S2 adds wide twins behind `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_WIDE_TWIN_{MQ4,MQ6,BF16,Q8,K1}` and QSA rows-32 score/filter candidates behind `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_{SCORE,FILTER_FEW}_ROWS32` (all default off). HIP modules that gained wide kernels (`gemm_mq6g256v2_f32_rows`, `qwen4_gemv_bf16_xf32`, `qwen4_gemv_q8_0`, `qsa_bf16_scores`) change source hash with their narrow kernels' source unchanged; `qwen4_slab_union_plan` takes up to 320 slots (32 lanes) in one 512-thread workgroup and writes each output word from exactly one thread (same words; its scratch grows 1,928 → 7,688 B). Oracles: `qwen4_wide_verify` (feature `reference-parity`; production `verify_block_rows` vs sequential AR, per-row logits bitwise, post-commit state digests) and the per-family `mq4_rows_oracle`, `mq6_wide_rows_oracle`, `q8_wide_rows_oracle`, `bf16_rows_oracle`, `bf16_rows_pm_oracle`, `lane_rows_pm_oracle --wide-cap`, `mq6_lm_head_rows` (feature `lab`). At rows 1..32 with every switch on, the per-family GEMV and QSA oracles pass on gfx1201, and the gfx1151 GEMV oracles differ in 0 bytes; on gfx1151 the full-model oracle is bitwise with S1 groups at n = 1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 16 and 32 (8185- and 752-token prompts). Each cap rises only with its full-model oracle receipt. `Qwen4Bundle::row_exact_verify_rows` exposes the cap to the n-gram copy lane.
  - **Current 1..64-row source work is not a qualification or default promotion.** The global shipping qualifications remain GPU 8 rows / CPU-owned experts 4 rows. Actual allocated executor/storage capacity is at most 64 total rows (seed + 63 drafts), not a forced K=63 or an algorithmic tuning cap; feasible offers and transaction costs still govern depth. Explicit lab CPU64 reserve uses the common D1/D2 capacity/census, not a new CPU64 qualification. Scratch/logit/capture allocation may narrow the feasible window.
  - Dedicated **legacy aggregate** qt44 GU `[512,1280,2560]` / qt53 down `[512,2560,640]` source targets R=1..64 with fixed eight-token tiles (C1 GU ROWS8 means eight output rows). GU keeps its original 52-byte prefix in a 56-byte ABI, adding total R at offset 52 (M=1280); down retains its original 52-byte ABI and uses N at offset 40 for total R (M=2560, K=640). The source defines two distinct same-image exports per gfx1151/gfx1201 architecture: GU block 256/static LDS 10,240 B, down block 32/LDS 0. This is not Slab K1 or descriptor reinterpretation; weights, arithmetic, codec and precision are unchanged.
  - The real-model G1 consumer holds the model alive, borrows immutable weights and compares original C1 against the candidate wordwise through GU/activation/down/combine at all 64 widths on real inputs plus two pathologies (192 cells), failing missing cells or mismatches. Canonical gfx1151/gfx1201 legacy images are emitted with byte-exact M7 checks; the 12 original CPU oracle cases passed as nine retained cases and three affected rechecks, not a fresh all-12 run. These component proofs and the frozen Slab 1928/96 native all-row proofs do not qualify full-model G1–G4 or promote a route/default. Retained/eager AR, every kept prefix/abort/continuation, 1,200 greedy IDs, copy/native paths, retirement/budget behavior, native capture COMMIT-TICKET/state coverage and paired ABBA full-transaction costs remain mandatory; eager projection eligibility is not HIP recording/graph-capture qualification.
  - Launch-ABI coverage follows delegated calls and returned kernel descriptors through live, explicit source edges to successfully ABI-checked terminal launchers, covering every originating symbol. Pure image/export factories remain non-launching; stale inventory entries are removed without adding candidates, weakening unknown-symbol refusals or repinning source goldens.
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) native MTP: the VRAM census charges the GDN capture ring at its real row count.** The runtime ring holds the wider of the window (`max_k + 1`, or a copy lane's `proposal_capacity + 1`) and the arch's row-exact verify rows (`qwen4_row_exact_verify_rows`), but the loader placement, the MTP request census (`native_mtp_request_bytes` / `native_mtp_device_bytes`, the PP band census) and the unified-memory admission charged the window alone. All of them now size the ring through `mtp_spec::native_mtp_capture_rows` / `native_mtp_capture` (GDN format and ring rows), the same helper the runtime uses. Q8 GDN state (the Flash-Next default) costs about 61 MB per ring row: about 0.49 GB at 8 rows and 1.96 GB at 32. No cap changes: both per-arch row-exact verify caps stay 8.
- **K1 expert GEMV wide twins `_c16` / `_c32` (gfx1151 and gfx1201 PeaceMaker images, not yet routed).** The `mq_i4_moe_gemv_pm_<arch>` modules gain eight symbols, `mq_i4_moe_gemv_{mq3i4,mq4sym}_{r256_gate_up,r128_down}_c{16,32}`: the same guarded 96-byte kernarg ABI as the narrow entries (`n_experts@88`, zero padding at 92), grid `[ceil(M/8), U, 1]`, block 256, one wave per output row over every slot of the expert, slot X staged through 4096/8192 B of static LDS eight slots at a time, weights reconstructed once per group. Every (slot, row) keeps the narrow entry's arithmetic chain, so a union of up to 32 token lanes is bitwise `C` singleton decode launches; the four narrow entries retain their arithmetic and now share the expert-bound guard (emitted-text sha256 pins refreshed in `tests/mq_i4_moe_gemv.rs`). `mq_i4_moe_gemv_byte_oracle --wide [--wide-c 1-32]` compares the twins with the CPU oracle and C singleton GPU launches, and `tests/mq_i4_moe_gemv_wide_emu.rs` does the same on the peacemaker CPU interpreter (which gained `s_cselect_b64`, `v_add_lshl_u32`, global SADDR accesses and a few opcode rows). Images regenerated; their sha256 pins are `MQ_I4_MOE_GEMV_PM_GFX{1151,1201}_SHA256`.
- **Flash-Next gfx1151 wide GEMV objects:** `qwen4_lane_rows_pm` adds separate R16/R32 MQ6 single/x4 and Q8 single-chain, four-chain, x2 and HC k8 exports, retaining the original four narrow emitted-text hashes. Wide entries share bounded F32 activation tiles in LDS while keeping decode's independent row chains, reduction trees and HC epilogue. `lane_rows_pm_oracle --wide-cap 16|32` compares against independent shape-selected singleton launches. These object/ABI additions do not themselves certify GPU byte equality, end-to-end state equality or performance, and do not raise architecture admission.
- **Strix Halo NPU trunk: arming no longer logs a burst of `amdxdna … Failed insert pages, ret -22` kernel errors.** Linux 7.1 removed mmap support from amdxdna's user-pointer buffers ("accel/amdxdna: Remove mmap and export support for ubuf"). railgun still tried to mmap each of the trunk's 12 user-pointer arenas (6 per bank) when the route armed, and the driver refused each one with `-EINVAL`, logging `amdxdna_insert_pages: Failed to mmap dma buf -22` and `amdxdna_gem_obj_mmap: Failed insert pages, ret -22`. The errors were harmless: the driver cleaned up the failed mapping, and railgun already used the process's own mapping of the same pinned pages, which is the address the NPU reaches under SVA. railgun now skips the mmap and uses that mapping directly, on every kernel.
- **Strix Halo (gfx1151) MQ3 expert-slab prefill: the grouped W3 kernels unpack each 8-code chunk in 8 VALU instead of 9.** The 3-bit codes were spread to nibbles with three shift + bit-field-insert stages, then a fourth shift, a bit-field insert against `0x11111111` and the `0x88888888` rebias XOR (9 VALU per chunk, and a `0x11111111` register). The last stages now merge into one shift, one shift-or (`(y << 2) | 0x11111111`) and one bit-field insert that already yield the clean nibble `2c + 1`, followed by the unchanged rebias XOR; the chain, the WMMA operands and the fold are untouched. The old and new unpack agree on all 2^32 code dwords, so every output byte is the incumbent's. Hot-loop VALU slots per two K128 epochs (PeaceMaker audit) 387 → 355 for the NT4 entries (VGPRs 216 → 208: the unpack temporaries fill the two free registers between `d` and X) and 630 → 566 (gate/up) / 315 → 283 (down) for the NT1 entries (VGPRs 208 → 200 / 176 → 168); `qwen4_moe_iu4_sym_w3_nt4_pm_gfx1151.hxaco` and `qwen4_moe_iu4_sym_w3_pm_gfx1151.hxaco` are re-emitted. Measured gains pending.
- **Strix Halo (gfx1151) sealed expert-slab one-lane decode runs the new K1-C1 kernels, on by default (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SLAB_K1_C1=0` is the kill switch).** The slab K1 GEMVs (`mq_i4_moe_gemv_*`) ran a union-plan launch plus one launch per codec bucket with one wave per row and each wave re-reading X; for one decode lane (AR and one-row forwards, not MTP verify) the new PeaceMaker module `mq_i4_moe_gemv_c1_pm_gfx1151` takes the MQ4 rows8 schedule (8 rows per 256-thread workgroup, X staged once in LDS, all weight loads of a row issued up front) and serves both codecs in one launch per projection straight from the routed ids, with no union plan. Its 80-byte kernarg ABI ends with `n_experts@72` (the host passes 512, the K1 launcher's value, and refuses a pointer table under 512 entries or a codec table under 512 bytes) and a zero `reserved@76`; every routed id is compared unsigned against `n_experts` right after it is loaded, and a workgroup with an invalid id (including the router's `-1`) exits before any pointer-table, codec-table, weight or X access, barrier or store. C1 serves layers whose cold codec is MQ4-only or W3; E8P layers keep the K1 bucket kernels. Per-lane arithmetic, chain order and reduction are K1's, so outputs are bitwise K1's; measured gains pending. Other architectures and lane counts are unchanged.
- **Strix Halo (gfx1151) sealed expert-slab multi-lane decode (MTP verify, 2..8 lanes) runs the new K1-Cn kernels, on by default (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_SLAB_K1_CN=0` is the kill switch).** The new PeaceMaker module `mq_i4_moe_gemv_cn_pm_gfx1151` replaces the per-codec-bucket K1 GEMVs for 2..8 lanes over the same union plan: 8 rows per 256-thread workgroup, each expert's slots' X staged in LDS once per workgroup, every weight load of a row issued up front and each weight group dequantized once for all of the expert's slots. Its four symbols take the guarded K1 96-byte kernarg ABI (`n_experts@88`, zero `reserved@92`, all 17 arguments on the kernelParams path) and exit a workgroup whose expert id is at or past `n_experts` (unsigned, so negative ids too) before any pointer-table, codec-table, weight or X access, barrier or store. Per-slot arithmetic, chain order and reduction are K1's, so outputs are bitwise K1's; measured gains pending. Cn serves layers whose cold codec is MQ4-only or W3; E8P layers keep the K1 bucket kernels. One-lane decode (K1-C1) and other architectures are unchanged.
- **Multi-slot serve exports engine state on `/metrics`.** Every multi-slot `done` event carries `engine_stats` (`admitted`, `rejected`, `evictions`, `restores`, `prefix_hits`, `reused_tokens`, `pool_free_pages`, `pool_total_pages`, `active_slots`, `total_slots`), and serve exports the latest snapshot as `hipfire_kv_pages_free`/`_total`, `hipfire_slots_active`/`_total`, `hipfire_evictions_total`, `hipfire_restores_total`, `hipfire_prefix_hits_total` and `hipfire_prefix_reused_tokens_total`. The series are absent on the standard route, and they update when a request finishes, not during a generation. The TUI "Live metrics" card adds a slots / KV pages / evictions row when serve exports them.
- **Flash-Next MQ4 XTS split-base artifacts get their own walked route plan on gfx1201.** The split header is the canonical monolithic header minus the 128 PLE `ngram_embedding.shard_N.weight` tensors (1,197 tensors against 1,325; layout `65811e8a…597c5c`). `route_plans/qwen3.8-flash-next-base.mq4-xts.gfx1201.tsv` is walked on it and selected by header layout next to the monolithic plan, so each layout resolves to its own plan, every planned HIP module is served from the release kernel pack with zero compiles, and a header matching neither layout still has no walked route. `fn_route_plan` now exercises both layouts for walked-kernel, pack and policy coverage and checks that an unknown layout is refused. The plan is walked on the current source (the walk daemon and kernel pack are built from the same commit), because any kernel-source change after a walk changes the planned image hashes: the earlier walk on an older source was stale against the current kernel corpus, which the `fn_route_plan` guard caught, so the plan was rewalked and regenerated.
- **Performance receipts record Flash-Next startup configuration.** `scripts/perf_config_receipt.py` extracts PLE rows, expert hotset, trunk overlay, NPU and route evidence, memlock, environment pins and model identity into receipt JSON, then checks it against the current per-architecture default pull (the split base plus the shared PLE sidecar: q4 on gfx1151, q8 on gfx1201) and labels whether the log came from the split base or a grandfathered monolithic install. Unknown evidence stays unknown. The validation policy now requires public performance claims to state their configuration and whether it equals a default pull; historical q4 measurements are not relabelled as product-default results.
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) developer switch `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_EXTENT_CHECK` (default off): checks every QSA kernel's byte extent against the VMM mapped prefix or the allocation size before launch.** `1` aborts on the first extent that overflows `usize` or ends past its limit, naming the arena, the limit, the required end, the QSA depth and the launch site; `2` also synchronizes the device after each checked launch to attribute a fault to its site. Every other value is off, the disabled path only tests a flag, and the diagnostic changes no launch, mapping policy or numerics. It is fault-localization instrumentation, not a serving setting. The extent arithmetic and mapped-prefix decision are pure functions with CPU unit tests; the developer-only `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_NPU_PAIR_SYNC` switch is removed.
- **Developer loaded-code snapshot `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_CODE_CHECK` (default off):** verifies genuine CPU aliases at module load and compares immutable loaded bytes once after the first host-side HIP error 700, without GPU copies or synchronization; the `qsa_code_check_selftest` example checks startup eligibility without consuming the fault snapshot. Unavailable mappings are explicit, and equality is not evidence about fault-time bytes, instruction-cache/PTE/translation defects, transient corruption or a bad PC.
- **Daemon GPU-fault reporting:** the first HIP error 700 during load or a request logs a single-line kernel/ROCm/MES evidence-collection hint and points to `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`, independently of developer switches.
- **Opt-in (`HIPFIRE_MTP_NGRAM_COPY=on` / `speculation.mtp_ngram_copy`, default `auto` = off on every GPU for now): Flash-Next native MTP n-gram copy lane — a verbatim-copy matcher, an adaptive take length of up to 7 candidates, row-0 confirmation only until the copy source is established, the copy lane kept on retired requests, and no pool clear on low acceptance.** With the switch off nothing changes: the 5/3/3 `MtpNgramContext` pool, the head's row-0 confirmation on every takeover, the yield gate, the five-low-window pool clear, takeovers ending with the floor's retirement and beta's admission sizing, with no `ngram_plan` / `ngram_confirm` trace events. `on`/`1` arms the lane wherever the native Qwen4 n-gram source is armed, as described below. Before the lane, the takeover drafted at most 3 candidates (triple 5/3/3) chained through a 5-token hash table, needed the MTP head's row-0 argmax to equal the first candidate, passed a yield gate with a fixed prior, and died with the floor's retirement; a long verbatim copy therefore advanced 4 tokens per window. With the lane on the proposal source is `MtpCopyContext`: keys of 32, 16, 8 and `n_match` tokens (longest first), each mapping to the position past its most recent occurrence in the request's history, the match checked token for token, and the proposal copying `history[pos..]` (up to `n_max` = 63 tokens, triple 5/1/63 on gfx1151 and gfx1201); its tables are never cleared and a stale slot can never propose. On a CPU proxy of the agentic code-edit chain (`release-0.4.3/ngram-copy-research`; a proxy, not a hardware measurement) conditional per-depth acceptance was 0.991-0.997 against 0.90-0.96 for the 5-token chain. A window with a proposal takes the length `d` in `1..7` maximizing the expected emitted tokens per cost, from the request's own shadow-measured per-depth n-gram acceptance (the proposal compared with the tokens the window committed, whichever source ran it) and its measured takeover window costs (nearest measured candidate count or the native cost model before a count is measured; a drafter's first takeover of a row count is observed unpriced), when that is at least the native chooser's rate. The cap is `min(n_max, row-exact verify rows - 1)` = 7 today: a verify forward is row-exact against single-row decode only up to the per-GPU `rdna_compute::prefill_invariant::qwen4_row_exact_verify_rows` (8 on every GPU: `decode_copy`, K1 MoE, rows_x4 GEMV, k4 HC, QSA prologue); more rows run prefill kernels and break greedy byte-identity, so raising that one per-GPU value raises the cap. The head's row-0 confirmation is skipped for a take of at least 5 candidates once depth-1 acceptance is at least 0.9 over at least 4 windows of evidence (checked against agentic-chain replays) and the last window's first candidate was accepted, so a divergence costs at most one blind window. **A request the floor retired keeps the copy lane:** retirement says native drafting loses to AR, not that the copy source does (on R9700 at the agentic chain's sampling the floor retired every request during the thinking prose, and the answer's verbatim code copy ran as AR). Only the floor's AR calibration bars the pool; on a retired request a take must beat AR itself, the head is caught up (the rows the retired AR tokens owe, appended teacher-forced as a forced advance does) before each takeover and confirms the first candidate unless the source is established (falling back to the AR step on a mismatch), and the floor keeps pricing takeovers after retirement and disarms the lane only when they cost at least AR per token; the request stays retired and counts its takeovers in the `ngram_mod_*` stats. The request-local pool is not cleared by a low-acceptance rule in the copy lane (it wiped the seeded prompt, up to 200K tokens, for the rest of the request); Qwen3.5 is unchanged. The row capture and verify scratch grow to the armed take cap and load admission sizes the verify rows and GDN row capture by it (`native_mtp_proposal_drafts`). The `qwen4 native MTP n-gram` load line is unchanged; with the lane armed one extra line, `qwen4 native MTP n-gram copy lane: on (take_cap=N)`, prints. With the lane on, `HIPFIRE_MTP_TRACE=1` adds `ngram_plan` (with a `retired` field) and `ngram_confirm` events. CPU coverage (Halo prices, simulated 0.9 native acceptance): a 500-token verbatim copy takes the cap and accepts long runs, prose with no matches plans identically to n-gram off, a copy that diverges after each 5-token key backs off and recovers, a retired request keeps copy takeovers at more than twice the AR-only rate, and retired takeovers that lose to AR stop. No hardware measurement yet.
- **Flash-Next native MTP: the depth chooser prices the margin prune, and windows are timed without a per-window device sync.** A batched depth was priced as if every window drafted it in full, so a cap whose weak windows the margin prune cuts short looked dearer than it is and prose requests stayed at depth 2 (on Halo, forced K=4 with the prune beat the chooser by +8.4% on prose). A cap is now priced by its windows' mean wall time over the agreement-predicted tokens of the depths they actually drafted; a neighbouring cap counts for the evidence it holds beyond this one, shifted by one row on its full-cap windows, and every cap's evidence ages with every window, so a cap measured only during a poor start is re-priced from the one that runs. Each floor-observed window is priced from its start to the next window's plan instead of ending in a device sync. Retirement still reads measured options only; `HIPFIRE_MTP_FLOOR_TRACE` lists `capN` candidates.
  - Strix Halo, mq4-xts + q4 PLE rows, 9 prompts, sampled (T0.7, presence 1.5), 3 fresh processes per arm interleaved in one hold: all 58.02 → 59.88 tok/s (+3.2%), prose prompts +11.5%, code −0.6% (spread); forced K=4 in the same hold +4.2% all (code +5.0%, prose +17.1%). Greedy ids identical on 9/9 prompts.
  - R9700 (default K=3): all 42.35 → 43.07 tok/s (+1.7%), greedy ids identical on 9/9 prompts.
- **PeaceMaker code objects now end with the shader-prefetch guard used by LLVM.** The certified builder stopped `.text` at the last kernel's `s_endpgm`, leaving instruction prefetch safety dependent on spare bytes in the mapped page. It now aligns the code tail to 128 bytes and appends 96 `s_code_end` dwords (384 bytes). Only the code tail and the ELF layout fields needed to contain it change; kernel instructions, symbol sizes and descriptors are unchanged.
- **Flash-Next native MTP: the adaptive draft-depth chooser explores deeper depths, and `speculation.mtp_k = auto` drafts up to 7 on gfx1151 (was 4).** After its three probe windows the AR floor ran only depths it had measured on the request, and those were the depths the probes happened to draft (early rejections and the margin prune held them at 2–3), so a code request on Halo ran depth 2–3 at a budget of 4 or 5 (code_edit accepted all 3 drafts in 63 of 65 windows and never tried 4). Once a measured option beats AR the window now runs the cheapest candidate: the measured depths plus each unmeasured depth next to one, priced by the request's own window-cost fit, whose slope is the measured cost of one more verify row on this GPU (0.27 AR steps assumed until two depths are priced). Depths no window compared drift toward the next-shallower depth's agreement instead of a fixed 0.8, and the first window at each drafted depth in a process (one-time row-count kernel binds, +8–15 ms at 5–8 rows) is not priced. The AR verdict and retirement still read measured options only. The Qwen4 lanes use the same floor; no other MTP producer uses it. gfx1201 keeps `auto` = 3 (its walked route plan is at K=3; forced K=5/7 lost 10–16% there).
  - Strix Halo, mq4-xts + q4 PLE rows, 9 prompts × 256 tokens, sampled (T0.7, presence 1.5), 3 fresh processes per arm: code 67.20 → 70.25 tok/s (+4.5%), prose 50.42 → 52.33 (+3.8%), all 56.10 → 58.23 (+3.8%); greedy ids identical on 9/9 prompts. The forced-depth ceiling with the margin prune on (product setting, floor bypassed): K=4 code +4.8% / all +7.9%, K=5 code +5.8% / all +5.9%, K=6 code −3.5%, K=7 code −13.2%.
  - R9700 (default K=3 both arms): all 41.59 → 42.48 tok/s (+2.1%), greedy ids identical on 9/9 prompts; with `HIPFIRE_MTP_K=7` the new chooser holds 42.57 (+2.3%). Qwen3.5-class MTP (Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B, unchanged code path): 125.47 → 125.78 tok/s, identical windows.
- **`POST /v1/systemone` choice options now always show their key; a `null` description no longer renders as the literal text `null`.** Each option line was `{code}. {description}`, so `{"a": null, "b": "desc"}` printed `A. null` and the key was never shown. Choice options now render `{code}. {key}` when the description is `null`, and `{code}. {key}: {description}` when one is present (`A. a` / `B. b: desc`). A `null` score level prints its own code, and a `null` noul `true`/`false` value is accepted and prints `yes` / `no`. The option codes and the logit readout tokens are unchanged. Prompt text for choice questions with descriptions changes (the key is now included), so previously cached or calibrated outputs for those prompts can differ.
- **Strix Halo NPU trunk: an NPU fault no longer fails every later request; the route turns off for the process and the faulted request finishes GPU-only, byte-identical to npu_trunk=off.** Before, a chain watchdog, submit error, ERT failure or relay exit mid-prefill failed the request and left the runtime failed for good, so every later request that planned an NPU pair also failed until the model was reloaded. A host-side wait timeout also left the GPU's wait on the NPU in place until the relay finished. Now every pair fault aborts the runtime at once, which publishes the terminal signal of every pending bank, so no GPU wait hangs. Under `auto` an NPU runtime fault latches the route off for the rest of the process with one `WARN npu-trunk: NPU pair fault, the route is off ... (NPU runtime: <reason>); host kernel=.. iommu=gpu:..,npu:.. amdxdna=.. npu_fw=..` line. The faulted request (an AR prefill, a native-MTP prefill or a reset spec advance) then restarts from its session start (the committed snapshot, or row 0) on the exact `off` schedule and logs `npu-trunk: the faulted request restarts GPU-only from row N of M`. Later requests run GPU-only. A GPU HIP error inside a pair (a sticky context, so a rerun could only fail) latches the route off too but is neither rerun nor logged as contained: the request fails with its original error. `npu_trunk=on` still fails the request closed but no longer hangs, and a forced advance mid-turn fails closed with the route latched off. Relay teardown is bounded at 3 s: a stuck relay is detached and its banks quarantined. The armed load line now ends with `host=[kernel=.. iommu=gpu:..,npu:.. amdxdna=.. npu_fw=..]`. The developer variable `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_NPU_TRUNK_FAULT_CHAIN=<n>` forces the chain watchdog of the nth relay chain to 1 ns to exercise this path.
- **New `hipfire doctor --npu`: checks a Strix Halo host for the NPU trunk route, measures `auto` against the GPU-only route, and checks that `on` and `emulate` agree.** Eleven GPU-free checks run first, and nothing is opened on the GPU or the NPU: a gfx1151 GPU, an `amdxdna` XDNA2 NPU, a read-write `accel0` node, NPU firmware, a memlock limit that covers what the trunk pins, a ROCm runtime, the daemon, a local Flash-Next model that a calibration record admits, no running `hipfire serve` or GPU reservation, and the effective `npu_trunk` and fabric clock as information. A failed check blocks with a fix line and exits 1. The host is then placed in a tier: `reference` when it equals a validated profile (kernel, IOMMU domains, amdxdna, NPU firmware, model index SHA-256 and kernel set), `compatible-unvalidated` with the differing fields listed otherwise, `blocked` on a failed check; a kernel set (`pack:<tag>@<commit12>` or `jit:<commit12>`) that no profile row lists is a difference by itself. The one validated row, `hipx` (7.3.0-rc7-perfopt+, identity IOMMU), is pinned to the v0.4.3 release kernel pack by tag: `pack:v0.4.3` matches that pack at any commit, since the release commit cannot name its own hash. After a `y` at the prompt, or with `--yes`, one `npu_trunk=auto` daemon alternates the GPU-only route and `auto` on cold 16K and 32K-row prompts (2 reps each, alternating order, no prompt-cache hits), then `npu_trunk=on` and `npu_trunk=emulate` daemons each generate 16 greedy tokens from the same 9319-row prompt and the outputs must be identical; the run takes about 6–7 minutes. Per size it reports medians, saved % and the spread of the two arms, and calls the size a gain, a loss or no measurable gain (a gain or loss must exceed the spread). A recommendation follows: keep `auto`, set `off` (a loss and no gain, or an exactness mismatch, which asks for a bug report with the `--json` report), set `auto` when `npu_trunk` is off and `auto` wins, or none. Without a terminal and without `--yes` the calibration is refused with exit 2. `--json` prints one `hipfire-doctor-npu-1` report with no hostname, user, path or PCI address. `--apply` only ever sets `npu_trunk off`, and only on a measured loss or an exactness mismatch. `--soak [--hours H] [--out DIR]` runs a long (default 4 h) NPU and GPU stability soak instead: it stops at the first fatal kernel log line, request hang, daemon exit or `MemAvailable` below 4 GiB, counts the benign `amdxdna … -22` mmap lines without stopping, writes an fsync'd heartbeat every 10 s, writes only into the output directory (`summary.txt`, `summary.json` and the logs), and `--soak-report DIR` summarizes it with the previous boot's kernel log after a freeze. Linux only. Reference: [docs/CLI.md](docs/CLI.md#hipfire-doctor---npu).
- **Daemon and kernel-pack surfaces behind `hipfire doctor --npu`: a diagnostic GPU-only route message, `hipfire-daemon --version`, and an installed-pack manifest record.** The daemon accepts `{"type":"npu_trunk_route","route":"gpu"|"auto"}` (Linux only; diagnostic, not a config key or environment variable). The route is read once at the next request's begin; a request on `gpu` takes the path of a tripped fault latch, so it runs exactly the `npu_trunk=off` schedule, plans no NPU pair, leaves the fault latch and the rate estimator untouched, and logs `npu-trunk: rows=<n> route=gpu (diagnostic)`. `hipfire-daemon --version` prints `hipfire-daemon <version> <commit>` before any config, protocol or GPU work. `hipfire kernel-pack install` now records the verified pack manifest as `<arch>.manifest.json` beside the installed `kernels/compiled/<arch>` directory (temporary file and rename), so the doctor can name the installed kernel set; an install made before this change has no record and is named by the daemon commit instead.
- **Strix Halo (gfx1151) and 7900 XTX (gfx1100) Flash-Next (qwen4): q8 QSA K/V is the default, with split-KV decode attention for q8 K/V.** `memory.kv_cache` `auto`/unset now resolves to `q8` on exact gfx1151 and gfx1100 (Q8_0 K/V, 1,408 B per token and QSA layer instead of 4,736 B; BF16-valued index keys, so selection is unchanged); other architectures are unchanged (gfx1201 `fp8`, everything else `bf16`). `kv_cache = "bf16"` restores the exact F32 state. An `auto` request with unsupported head geometry (head_dim other than 256) falls back to F32; explicit `q8` is still refused there.
  - Under `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_DECODE_SPLITK` (default on for q8 on exact gfx1151 and gfx1100, `=0` disables), q8 decode launches (head_dim 256, 24 query heads over 2 KV heads, 1..=`few_row_limit` rows, eager only) run `qsa_decode_splitkv_partial_q8` + `qsa_decode_splitkv_merge_f32` (`qsa_decode_splitkv_q8.hip`). One workgroup per (KV head, split, row) dequantizes each Q8_0 K/V tile once into shared F32 LDS for all 12 query heads, with 32 splits merged by the dense product-LSE combine. The F32 state keeps its existing kernels: F32 split-K (`qsa_decode_splitk.hip`) remains gfx1151-only. The q8 route is KLD-gated, **not bit-exact** against the per-head kernel.
  - **Halo:** mq4 Flash-Next, same binary, decode KLD against the BF16 reference: q8 0.082833 (code24) / 0.080197 (WT2) versus F32 split-K 0.084828 / 0.083067. Paired AR runs (ABBA, n=2 per arm, 128 tokens, 128K/256K prefill incremental over the previous prompt), F32 -> q8: decode ITL 29.69 -> 30.57 ms (8K), 29.12 -> 29.74 (32K), 29.82 -> 30.09 (128K), 30.21 -> 30.87 (256K); prefill 1,997 -> 2,008 tok/s (8K), 1,992 -> 2,250 (32K), 1,756 -> 1,818 (128K), 1,506 -> 1,825 (256K). QSA context at 262,144 tokens is 14,400 -> 4,224 MiB (admission commit 14,912 -> 4,736 MiB). Decode costs 0.3-0.9 ms per token (1-3%); long-context prefill and memory gain.
  - **XTX KLD:** code24, decode route, all 24 sequences / 6,120 scored tokens per arm: q8 0.080915 versus F32 0.077988 (+0.002927). WT2, approved matched 20 of 24 sequences / 20,460 scored tokens per arm, cold-prefill route: q8 0.062506 versus F32 0.064818 (-0.002312). Both are inside the +0.010 cap. WT2 uses numeric `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_VRAM_LAYERS=10` identically in both arms, graph 0, normalize 0 and q4 PLE; the initial setting 11 exhausted VRAM in both arms before scoring any chunk. F32 alone sets `HIPFIRE_KV_MODE=bf16`. This is not a claim that the product-default expert placement behaves the same.
  - **XTX timing not measured: offload-bound fixture.** Logged legacy QSA context targets at 135,168 tokens are 7,326 -> 2,178 MiB (F32 -> q8), not peak total VRAM measurements. Historical 32K prefill rows are not comparable: daemon logs show F32 reused 0 / prefilled 32,010 tokens, while q8 reused 7,680 / prefilled 24,330 because F32 snapshots were skipped under the memory guard. No equal-work prefill speedup is claimed.
  - This QSA default is **not a fix** for the separate rare gfx1151 GPU memory fault in [docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md](docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md); its root cause is unresolved, and `kv_cache = "bf16"` still runs the kernel it was seen in.
  - **Session save/restore with the q8 default needs the F32 GDN WY T inverse (`02bb0521b`, `fix/gdn-wy-t-f32`; not in this change).** Without it a repetitive ~8.5K-token prompt fails closed on the gfx1151 F16 WY inverse (MoE router non-finite logits, request rolled back), q8 or not. On the q8 binary plus that fix (Strix Halo, Flash-Next mq4, native MTP K=7, fresh kernel cache), save (8,552-token context) / unrelated / restore / live all finish `stop` and the save, restore and live answers are the same string; the restore reuses the saved snapshot (8,192 cached tokens, `source=snapshot`) and the follow-up turn reuses the live prefix (8,595 tokens, `source=live`). This is string identity plus prefix reuse, not an internal-state byte comparison, and not an all-turns-stop claim: the corrected-fixture run passes retrieval 3/3 but its first turn ends on the 2,048-token length cap.
- **DeepSeek-V4 capture-safe verify no longer panics at the first per-row compressor window (`tensor sub-view exceeds accessible buffer prefix`).** The capture-safe verify body (DSpark verify graph / PM4 / AQL routes and the Redline DSpark shadow, all developer opt-in) runs every compressed layer through the per-row compressor with device-side commit slots, which reads the global ratio-4 / ratio-128 commit slots 10 / 11 of the attention-state array. The batched array had only 10 slots per row, so slot 10 / 11 lay outside the row's stripe. Decode and the batched stripes now fill one 12-slot layout (`attn_state_slots`), and the batched stripes also map commit slots through the compressor cache placement as decode does (identical on single-GPU replicated placement). On gfx1151 with `deepseek-v4-flash-0731.mq2r` (2,300-token prefill, 40 verify windows of 1-8 rows): the direct verify path is bit-identical to beta (2,289 digests), and the capture-safe body is bit-identical to the direct body when both run the per-row compressor. With defaults the direct body still takes the batched compressor on window-aligned chunks, which rounds differently, so the two routes drift after the first such commit (163 of 169 greedy ids agree).
- **Flash-Next: a symlinked model finds the PLE sidecars published beside the link, and a load no longer silently derives a ~29 GB `.ple-q4`.** `hipfire serve`/`run` canonicalized a model path before the loader saw it, so for `models/x.mq4-xts` → `/elsewhere/x.mq4-xts` the loader looked for `/elsewhere/x.mq4-xts.ple-q4`, missed the published `models/x.mq4-xts.ple-q4`, and (with `memory.ple_format = "q4"`) derived a fresh copy from the q8 rows. `find_model_path` now returns the selected path made absolute with its symlinks intact, and every `<model>.ple-q4`/`.ple-q8` lookup probes that path first and its canonical target second (the on-demand sidecar download check and the DFlash, MTP, vision and NPU sidecar lookups follow the same order; `hipfire rm` still acts on the canonical file). A load never derives: `memory.ple_format = "q4"` with no `.ple-q4` at either location is refused with both searched paths, `hipfire pull <tag> --ple q4` and `hipfire ple derive --format q4 <model>` (the explicit step, which writes beside the path as given). **Behavior change:** a `q4` load that used to derive from a present `.ple-q8` on first start now needs `hipfire ple derive --format q4 <model>` first; `auto` is unchanged (it never derived).
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) `auto` expert placement keeps the long-prefill stage buffers, the kernels' lazy workspaces and a safety margin free (beta28bfc4ece ran out of device memory on a 32 GB card at a 763-token prompt).** `auto` sized the resident expert layers from the reserve alone, but a slab load also allocates two dedicated long-prefill stage buffers of `2 × (largest layer payload + 4096 B)` at load (it scales with the artifact's largest layer: 2,120 MiB for the 1,060 MiB-per-layer mq3-xts artifact on the failing card), and the kernels' lazily sized workspaces grow at the first long prefill. On the failing card (32,550 MiB free, 5,115 MiB non-expert weights, 1,060 MiB per layer, 7,927 MiB reserve) that placed 18 layers resident and left 428 MiB for 2,120 MiB of stage; `auto_vram_reserve` now also charges the engine's 1 GiB lazy-workspace headroom, and whole-layer placement additionally charges the 512 MiB hot-set safety margin and, only where the slab stage allocates (stage on, slab recipe, not expert-parallel), the stage buffers, so the same card places 14. The unset fallback that decides fully-resident, expert-parallel splits and the placement log use the same terms, itemised; when even zero resident layers cannot hold the weights and the charged reserve the load is refused before allocating. The hot set path keeps its own margin and tier-plan stage budget, uncharged twice.
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) `auto` expert placement charges what a full-context request and the long-prefill stage actually take (beta28bfc4ece ran out of device memory on a 32 GB card at a 763-token prompt, and mq2 on an R9700 at a 16K prompt).** `auto` sized the resident expert layers from a historical measured reserve alone, which charges QSA context growth as zero past 32,768 legacy tokens and nothing for the lazy F16 weight shadows, the kernels' pool workspaces or the QSA selector scratch; a slab load also allocates two dedicated long-prefill stage buffers of `2 × (largest layer payload + 4096 B)` at load (it scales with the artifact's largest layer: 2,120 MiB for the 1,060 MiB-per-layer mq3-xts artifact on the failing card), and the first long prefill grows the rest. On the failing card (32,550 MiB free, 5,115 MiB non-expert weights, 1,060 MiB per layer, 7,927 MiB reserve) that placed 18 layers resident and left 428 MiB for 2,120 MiB of stage. The reserve is now the larger of the historical formula and a bottom-up census of the first full-context request, itemised term by term on the `qwen4 auto expert placement` line (the QSA context at the admitted `max_seq` as the actual backend maps it, the rest of the request state, the chunk forward, the F16 weight shadows queried from the manifest, the pool workspace, the QSA selector, native MTP and QSA gather); whole-layer placement then adds the 512 MiB hot-set safety margin and, only where the slab stage allocates (stage on, slab recipe, not expert-parallel), the stage buffers. The unset fallback that decides fully-resident, expert-parallel splits and the hot set budget read the same reserve; when even zero resident layers cannot hold the weights and the charged reserve the load is refused before allocating. A request that still runs out of memory returns a `gpu` error with `rolled_back: true` (the pool drains its free buffers and retries once first), and the daemon keeps serving the next request.
  - Strix Halo (gfx1151, unified memory) is unchanged: on the shipped admission (VMM F32 QSA, Q8 GDN, BF16 pooled mirror, 8192-row chunk, 16384 context, no MTP) the historical reserve (12,150 MiB) exceeds the census (9,854 MiB), so the historical floor wins and both Halo artifacts still fit fully resident (a unit test pins both figures and the decision).
  - **R9700 placement cost:** the published mq4-xts default, the per-expert hot set, loses **0 bytes and 0 hot experts**. Comparing beta `28bfc4ece` with this fix using the same published sidecar (`7f6760e1…`), the hot-set reserve is byte-identical. Across the logged free-memory interval `[32550, 32551)` MiB, AR keeps a 17,887,947,008–17,888,995,583 B budget and 6,850 hot experts; native MTP K3 keeps 16,920,046,824–16,921,095,399 B and 6,479/6,480 hot experts. Plans are identical before and after; no GPU rerun was needed for the unchanged default. Whole-layer `auto` with the hot set off costs one XTS layer (15 → 14; 33.65 → 33.25 decode tok/s, −1.19%, three fresh processes per build on the same card). mq3-xts goes from OOM to 15 resident layers and 35.70 decode tok/s. CPU budget evidence: `rcpt/placefix.hotset.json`; whole-layer timing evidence: `rcpt/placefix.speed.json`.
- **DeepSeek V4 Flash greedy DSpark is reproducible across processes (HIPF-78).** The DSpark draft-block controller picked each window's block from a cost curve fitted to live window wall time, and kept that fit across requests. On warm gfx1151 processes the fitted `dt / t_ar` landed between 0.390 and 0.423, so fresh processes drafted different block schedules; the verify width follows the block, and batched verify logits depend on the width, so greedy text and τ changed from run to run. DeepSeek V4 now passes a fixed ratio (`WindowCost::Fixed { ratio: 0.40 }`, the median of those fits) and the block schedule depends only on the request's acceptance history. Qwen3/3.5 DSpark keeps the live fit (`WindowCost::Measured`). On Strix Halo, `deepseek-v4-flash-0731.mq2r`, serve battery with greedy DSpark and 160 tokens: 4 fresh beta processes gave 2 τ sequences, 4 fixed processes gave identical text and τ, with the same decode speed (19.4-20.0 tok/s mean, beta 19.5-19.9).
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) cache-quality oracle: hit arms can measure the live continuation (`"cache_mode": "live"`).** A hit arm committed every prior turn with `session_commit`, which drops the live record, so the oracle never measured what serve resumes: below one 8192-row prefill chunk its hit arms re-prefilled cold. A `live` hit arm commits each prior turn with `session_commit_live(stream[..consumed_end])`, as serve's `commit_qwen4_session` does, and fails unless the final `selected_start` equals the last turn's `consumed_end`. A live arm needs at least one prior turn; `"default"`/omitted arms are unchanged, and the result reports `cache_mode: "live"`.
- **Exact-gfx1100 long-context DFlash now defaults to the existing FA2 split-KV verifier envelope.** This is a policy-only promotion: admission remains dense Qwen H24/KV4/HD256, Q8/Q8 VMM KV, sequential B4..32, live context above 4,096, with the existing capture and Redline guards. `HIPFIRE_GFX1100_FA2_SPLIT_VERIFY=0` restores the incumbent verifier and `HIPFIRE_VERIFY_ATTN=0` remains the parent opt-out. On one W7900 with the canonical Qwen3.8-27B XTS target and the committed long-code prompt (21,582 engine tokens), fresh-process DFlash median improved 43.5 -> 49.4 tok/s (+13.6%) with tau unchanged at 1.97; plain AR was 36.2 tok/s. Promotion evidence also recorded mean logit KLD 1.812338e-5 (mean cosine 0.999999156, top-1 agreement 383/384; the one flip had a 0.004265 reference margin) and a 9/30 vs 9/30 LongBench-v2 hard30 task tie with zero task flips. This route uses a different split partial/merge reduction order and is not promised byte-identical to the incumbent.
- **Muse Glimmer: the unwired continuous-batch decode core is removed (#891, HIPF-90, @fivetide).** `hipfire-arch-muse-glimmer` `batch.rs` (`GlimmerDecodeBatchState`) and `forward_batch.rs` (`forward_decode_batch_glimmer`), added in `e367dee01`, had no caller: the daemon never routes arch 14 into a batch driver, the layer skipped the per-head Q norm, and its residual copies were blocking `memcpy_dtod`. Measured on Strix Halo (gfx1151) with the Q norm fixed, lane batching does not pay with today's batched MQ4 GEMM: at ctx 2048 on `muse-glimmer-30b.mq4r`, 4 lanes decode 6.1 tok/s in aggregate against 13.3 tok/s for one singleton request (0.46x), 8 lanes 11.4 tok/s (0.86x). `gemm_hfq4g256_residual_wmma_k2` takes 88% of a 4-lane step (577 of 654 ms), against 75 ms for a whole singleton decode token; the batched verify block runs at the same per-row cost, so a port onto `pipeline::sandwich` hits the same cap. A later port can start from `e367dee01`. No served route changes.
- **Flash-Next native MTP speculates again on thinking-off requests (beta regression: every window committed one token, τ 0, below AR speed).** The window-repair change clamps each native Qwen4 window to the think budget's `window_cap()`. Outside a think span that cap was the whole budget, and thinking off reaches the engine as `max_think_tokens: 1` (the CLI, `serve`, `bench` and the daemon's legacy encoding), so every answer window was capped at one token on every GPU. `ThinkBudget::window_cap` now returns `None` outside a span. The in-span cap (`max - count`) and the queued close-token cap are unchanged, so a force-close inside a span still lands on a window's last token. A span the answer opens and trips inside one window takes the existing window repair, or Realign where repair is unavailable, as it did before the clamp. Greedy output is identical to AR. Measured on one R9700 with the 2026-09-28 nine-prompt method (thinking off, greedy, mtp_k 3), best-of geomean: pre-clamp 7feb452c2 53.74 tok/s τ 1.56; window-repair 2f3f10ea1 41.83 τ 0.00; beta c5c7f9b8a 41.77 τ 0.00; fixed 54.50 τ 1.83 (AR 45.39). nat-8K: 41.51 τ 0.79 fixed vs 37.80 τ 0 on beta.
- **Flash-Next expert parallelism no longer crashes a peer rank in a prefill chunk (`thread 'hipfire-qwen4-ep-rank1' has overflowed its stack`).** The chunk forward kept its step list in a 384-entry inline `SmallVec` (~567 KiB) that a closure moved, so one frame held three copies (~1.7 MiB). Rank 0 runs on the 8 MiB main thread, but peer ranks run on 2 MiB worker threads and overflowed on EP2 R9700 with a 498-token prompt (reproduced on beta a6f241ce2). The list is now a heap `Vec` (one ~567 KiB allocation per chunk forward), and the worker's peak stack drops to about 0.4 MiB; the Strix Halo NPU trunk bank program had the same inline list and moves to the heap too. Output is unchanged.
- **R9700 (gfx1201) Flash-Next long-context decode: exact BF16 split QSA score/filter-select route, on by default; 256K decode token latency -6.2%.** Selected indices, the final-row mirror, logits and greedy ids are unchanged. On exact gfx1201 with BF16 pooled index keys, selection past a measured crossover (2048 pooled blocks for calls of at most 256 rows, 8192 above) runs the exact hipcc BF16 rows8/rows16 score kernels (`kernels/src/qsa_bf16_scores.hip`, scores bit-identical to the fused per-block score) followed by the exact sampled filter trio instead of the fused `indexed_attention_select_bf16_batched`. `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_BF16_SPLIT=0` is the kill switch (only `0` disables; other architectures are unchanged, and `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_FILTER_SELECT=0` also keeps the fused selector).
  - Selection identity at model level: `qwen4_qsa_ctx` capture of nat-128k at 65,536 tokens (prefill past 8,192 blocks, decode at 16,380-16,384 blocks, route engaged with 3,264 BF16 score launches): 1,152 selection/mirror hash pairs, 0 mismatches against the fused selector.
  - Greedy identity: token ids identical off vs on on nat 8K / 32K / 128K / 256K x 3 paired reps and on all 8 lane prompts.
  - Measured (one R9700, Flash-Next, natural-text prefixes, 3 paired reps per depth, trimmed-mean decode inter-token latency, `=0` vs default):

    | depth | off (ms) | on (ms) | change |
    |---|---:|---:|---:|
    | 8K | 31.58 | 30.87 | -2.2% |
    | 32K | 32.04 | 30.98 | -3.3% |
    | 128K | 35.00 | 33.89 | -3.2% |
    | 256K | 37.88 | 35.53 | -6.2% |

    All three 256K pairs improved by 1.7 to 3.3 ms; 256K decode 26.4 -> 28.2 tok/s.

- **Flash-Next (qwen4) singleton native MTP on the R9700 expert hot set: the AR floor no longer retires requests where MTP still wins (humaneval_0 49 → 53 tok/s, records_parser_1k 38.7 → 49 tok/s in the processes that retired, bare_factual 37 → 42, fiction_lighthouse 40 → 45; aggregate 47.1–49.2 → 50.5–50.8).** Route-only: greedy ids are identical at every route and a sampled request stays distribution-exact. With the hot set on, the single calibration token that priced AR was 7–26% off the request's mean AR token (humaneval_0 19.6 ms against 23.7 ms mean and 24–28 ms for the AR tokens that followed; bare_factual 23.2 against 29.5; fiction_lighthouse 22.5 against 25.3; records_parser_1k 31.4 ms in one hold and 21.1–21.5 ms in the next, so it retired in 2 of 3 fresh processes), because one token's cost is a property of its routed experts (VRAM hot set against host-mapped). A losing verdict past the retirement grace is now confirmed before it is sticky: the floor first spends 6 real AR tokens (the calibration step again, head kept synced; retirement would run them anyway), re-prices AR by their mean (26.0–26.2 ms humaneval_0 and 27.8 ms records_parser_1k in every fresh process, 27.6–29.2 ms bare_factual), at most once per 16 windows, and also needs the ~25-window realized cost of all its windows (the 8-window memories dip on any streak of rejected drafts) to lose to that price. Continuous-batching lanes are unchanged. `HIPFIRE_MTP_FLOOR_AR_PROBE=0` is the kill switch (single-token floor); `HIPFIRE_MTP_FLOOR_TRACE=1` prints one `QWEN4_FLOOR_TRACE` JSON line per window / AR token (developer vars in `docs/env-vars.md`).
  - Measured on one R9700 (gfx1201), Flash-Next mq4-xts, hot set on (6479 experts in VRAM, 18097 host-mapped, `ple rows: q4`), l2 prompt set, MTP greedy, 3 interleaved fresh processes per arm after one pre-warmed kcache, decode tok/s: records_parser_1k beta 49.9 / 38.9 / 38.7 (retired in 2 of 3, tau 0.12) against fix 49.3 / 48.4 / 49.6 (0 of 3 retired); humaneval_0 48.9–49.2 (retired after 9 native windows, tau 0.59, all 3) against 52.9–53.1 (tau 2.05); fiction_lighthouse 39.5–40.0 against 45.2–45.4; bare_factual 37.4–37.7 against 41.6–42.2; every other prompt within spread (glimmer_coding 64.5–66.6 / 64.8–64.9, lru_cache 63.6–64.6 / 64.0–64.4, code_edit 47.4–47.5 / 47.4–47.5, agentic_user_read 44.0–44.2 / 42.4–45.4, glimmer_prefill_1024 56.7–57.4 / 56.8–57.5, records_parser_4k 49.4–50.7 / 50.0–50.2). Aggregate beta 49.16 / 47.14 / 47.22, fix 50.72 / 50.47 / 50.77. Greedy id md5 identical across all 6 processes, the no-hot-set cells and the kill-switch cell. No hot set (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_HOTSET=0`, one process per arm): aggregate 39.57 → 41.29, records_parser_1k 32.9 (retired) → 41.5, bare_factual 36.4 → 41.1, every other prompt within 3%, except agentic_user_read 35.6 → 33.3 (a 45-token request where MTP and AR both cost ~29–30 ms per token: the fix retires after its probes, beta did not). Kill-switch cell (`HIPFIRE_MTP_FLOOR_AR_PROBE=0`) retires exactly like beta (humaneval_0 83 AR windows, fiction_lighthouse 219, bare_factual 92). Receipts: `qcal/release-0.4.3/fn-floor-hotset-r9700/runs/dec-b-*` and `GATE.txt`, traces `dec-a-*`.
- **Flash-Next on gfx1201 loads its whole kernel route before ready, from a plan generated by walking the dispatch.** The planned route has 57 modules for native MTP and 51 for AR: 54 HIP modules from the release kernel pack plus 3 embedded PeaceMaker images. With an installed pack, every one is loaded before the `loaded` acknowledgment and no kernel is loaded mid-request. Without a pack, the plan compiles during the weight load (`HIPFIRE_JIT_JOBS`). Unlike the Qwen3.6-27B plan, the route is not sealed. A kernel the walks missed still loads lazily with one stderr line, `kernels: WARNING unplanned kernel <symbol> (module <module>) loaded lazily on the Flash-Next <arch> <route> route plan [<n> unplanned this load]`, and is counted (`Gpu::unplanned_route_kernels`).
  - **How the plan is generated:** `scripts/route_plan_walk.py` drives the real dispatch under `HIPFIRE_MODULE_LOAD_AUDIT`:
    - every prompt row count to 300, then stepped counts and the chunk and staging tails;
    - decode contexts to 131000;
    - greedy and nine sampling variants;
    - n-gram copies and session resumes;
    - 20K–128K-token QSA prompts, plus short and medium thinking-on greedy and sampled requests.

    It walks both the expert-hot-set/PLE-q4 and plain configurations, each as AR and as native MTP. `scripts/route_plan_build.py` writes the result to `crates/rdna-compute/src/route_plans/qwen3.8-flash-next.gfx1201.tsv`.
  - **Stale plans:** every row records the effective source or image SHA-256. A row that no longer matches the registry refuses the plan, and the load falls back to lazy loading. `cargo test -p rdna-compute --test fn_route_plan` checks that every walked kernel is planned and that every planned HIP module is a release-pack entry.
  - **What stays lazy:** another header layout, `max_seq` above 131072, a QSA/GDN/KV-backend setting outside the walks, non-default MTP K or feature flags, EP, a trunk overlay and the retained Redline route. All of these log `no closed route plan` and keep lazy loading. Staging fn-lanes (`serve.vmm_batch`) returns a planned load to lazy loading.
  - **Walk coverage**, all on the canonical GPTQ3 header with expert hot set + PLE q4 and with the plain pull, each as AR and as native MTP (1734 requests, plus four prompt-sizing probes), on beta `5e4a9b752`:
    - **Prompt rows:** AR prefill for every row count to 300, rows to 1100 in steps of 7, every multiple of 128 to 4224 ±2, then 2047–2049, 3000, 5000, 6143–6145, 8191–8200, 12289, 16385, 33000, 125000 and 131000. MTP prompt fill from 1 to about 1100 words, plus 2K/4K/8K tails. All four loads use `max_seq = 131072`.
    - **Decode contexts:** 1 to 131000, including 125000 and 131000.
    - **QSA at depth:** generates with 20.7K-, 31K-, 100K- and measured 127454-token prompts, including prefill near the 131072 ceiling.
    - **Sampling:** greedy and nine sampled variants (top-p, top-k with seed, min-p, repeat/presence/frequency penalties, logprobs, logit bias), plus sampled code, copy and short top-k requests on the MTP route.
    - **n-gram windows:** verbatim-copy prompts, greedy and sampled.
    - **Session resumes:** three-turn chains.
    - **Thinking:** thinking-off (`max_think_tokens = 1`) and thinking-on greedy and sampled requests, with uncapped and 24-token think budgets, on both routes. These walks include beta's corrected thinking-off MTP windows (`1ee6815c5`) and default gfx1201 QSA BF16 split select (`c5c7f9b8a`).
    - **fn-lanes:** not walked.

    Any kernel an unwalked configuration needs loads lazily with the warning above.
  - **Developer changes:** `HIPFIRE_ROUTE_PLAN=0` is a new developer kill switch, which the walk uses. `ensure_embedded_kernel` loads now print their `HIPFIRE_MODULE_LOAD_AUDIT` line.
  - **Measured:** on an R9700 (Flash-Next GPTQ3, hot set, PLE q4, native MTP; 11 prompts; fresh `HIPFIRE_HOME`, empty kernel cache, current-registry gfx1201 release pack in the install layout), 3 fresh processes gave a first token in 210.9 / 213.3 / 209.8 ms, against a warm control at 209.5 ms. All four logged 0 unplanned-kernel lines, 0 JIT compiles and 0 pack loads during requests. Plan-on re-walks (867 requests) also finished with 0 unplanned-kernel lines. The current release pack includes `qsa_bf16_scores`, which the older comparison pack lacked; acceptance used `scripts/build-kernel-pack.sh`, not runtime writeback.
  - Installed users were never hit by the 19–21 s cold first request: the release pack already carries every Flash-Next gfx1201 and gfx1151 module. The cold first request only happened on a bare dev binary without the pack.
  - gfx1151 has no walked plan yet and keeps lazy loading.
- **Qwen4 maps the QSA context ahead for the decode budget: the Strix Halo decode growth stall is gone (256K run stall 636 / 376 ms -> 51 / 0 ms).** After prefill and before the first decode forward (and any decode capture or record), the target QSA context (plus the attached MTP head's when the request drafts) is mapped once through `min(position + remaining max_tokens + draft rows, admitted capacity)`, so per-token growth checks never remap; VMM growth also sets access on the newly mapped range only instead of the whole prefix. Mapping failure falls back to on-demand growth; token positions, valid lengths and memory admission are unchanged. Halo, Flash-Next, natural text 8K/32K/128K/256K in one process, 128 AR tokens each, 3 paired runs against beta 9d5eb9203, greedy ids identical:

  | depth | stall per run, base (ms) | stall per run, map-ahead (ms) | steady ITL base -> map-ahead (ms) |
  |---|---|---|---:|
  | 8K | 0 / 358 / 58 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 29.99 -> 29.98 |
  | 32K | 0 / 205 / 48 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 30.48 -> 30.02 |
  | 128K | 0 / 236 / 0 | 0 / 66 / 0 | 30.28 -> 30.48 |
  | 256K | 0 / 636 / 376 | 0 / 51 / 0 | 31.31 -> 31.40 |

  256K decode 29.7 -> 31.0 tok/s. Cost: the whole `max_tokens` window is mapped at the first token. 8K prompt, fresh process per cell, 2 runs per arm, TTFT change (median) by `max_tokens`: 128 -4 ms, 4096 (the default) -16 ms, 32768 +23 ms, 250000 +167 ms (+84 / +251 ms, about 4% of the 3.85 s TTFT). Prefill tok/s at 8K/32K reads about 1% lower in all three runs (follow-up open).
- **Flash-Next expert parallelism now admits 2 to 8 cards of one exact arch, gfx1100 (7900 XTX) or gfx1201 (R9700); `topology.ep` (`HIPFIRE_TOPOLOGY_EP`) is allowed `1..=8` (was 1, 2 or 4).** Still opt-in and experimental, and still eager. The load refuses `ep` above 8, an arch other than gfx1100 or gfx1201, a mixed set (`requires the same architecture on every rank`), too few visible devices and any directed card pair without peer access; there is no host-staged fallback.
  - **Uneven expert ownership.** Routed expert `e` lives on rank `e % N` at slot `e / N`, and N no longer has to divide 512 (512 over 6 ranks is 86/86/85/85/85/85). Every rank budgets the largest share when it sizes how many MoE layers stay in VRAM, so a layer is resident on all ranks or on none; pinned host bytes are charged per rank at its own share. `multi-gpu.md` has the per-rank counts and the arithmetic for 24 GB gfx1100 cards at 32K context (19 of 49 routed layers resident at N = 2, 39 at N = 4, all 49 from N = 5); it is arithmetic from single-card load figures, not a measurement.
  - **Transport to eight ranks.** The decode row gather and the owner-routed tile pull take up to eight sources (the pull has certified PeaceMaker kernels for gfx1100 and gfx1201); the EP2 launches are unchanged.
  - **Owner-routed prefill (S1) for N = 2..=8 on both arches; the `EP4 owner-routed prefill not yet gated` refusal is removed.** gfx1201 keeps the symmetric IU4 route. gfx1100 runs it on the F16 WMMA grouped MoE route (BF16-out gate/up with the SwiGLU epilogue, BF16-out down, `moe_down_combine_grouped_top10_bf16in`): each rank masks the tiles of other ranks' experts to `-1` (the grouped kernels return on it before any load), computes only its own, and pulls every peer-owned live tile's BF16 grouped rows before the unchanged combine. No symmetric headers are needed there; the per-layer verdict is the QT44/QT53 expert formats and every rank must agree. The route takes the stable grouping (`moe_scatter_stable_top10`, now admitted on gfx1100) because the fused scatter's atomic bucket order is not reproducible across ranks.
  - **Balanced owners (W1) are gfx1201-only at 2..=4 ranks, and expert staging (S2) is gfx1201-only.** On gfx1100 each rank logs `balanced ownership not admitted (needs gfx1201); static split`, and on gfx1201 at 5..=8 ranks `balanced ownership not admitted (needs at most 4 ranks); static split` (the certified owner-assign kernel covers 2..=4 ranks); both run the static split, which is exact. On gfx1100 `expert staging not admitted (needs gfx1201)` builds nothing. Single card and the `HIPFIRE_EP_*=0` kill switches are unchanged.
  - **Logical emulation covers Qwen4 EP (developer-only).** With `HIPFIRE_EMULATE_GPUS` set, rank `r` runs on physical device `r % count`, one visible device is enough, each rank's free VRAM is its device's free VRAM divided by the ranks aliased onto it, and same-device peer checks are skipped. It does not prove interconnect behavior or throughput.
  - **A rank no longer holds a file descriptor per weight range.** Every tensor or span range of an HFQ model took its own duplicate of the model file's descriptor, and a Flash-Next EP rank keeps about 130 of them for its lifetime: 8 ranks held 1,044 descriptors on the model file (1,171 while a rank loaded), so under the common 1,024 soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` the eighth rank's load failed with `Too many open files (os error 24)`. Ranges now share the container's one descriptor (reads are positional, so nothing else changes).
  - **Community gate.** `scripts/fn-ep-gate.sh` runs one card and N cards over the same prompts, `scripts/fn_ep_compare.py` compares them byte for byte (tokens, logits, every rank's mirror and state digests), and a receipt records the environment, per-card PCIe links, P2P topology, speed cells and the verdict. `ep_transport_oracle` (feature `lab`) is a one-device synthetic oracle for the transport launchers at N = 2..=8. `--ref-ranks R` runs the reference arm as EP-R on the first R cards (for hosts without the ~50 GiB of pinned RAM a 24 GB card needs, e.g. `--ref-ranks 4` on four 24 GB cards) and checks that reference against itself as well as the EP-N arm against it.
  - Exactness, on 4x R9700 (gfx1201), Flash-Next mq4-xts, greedy `fn_ep_oracle` runs against one card on the same build. Tokens, rank-0 logits sha256, every peer rank's logits mirror and every rank's state digests are byte-identical for EP2 (MTP windows included), EP3 on three real cards (171/171/170 experts), EP4, `HIPFIRE_EMULATE_GPUS=6` over three cards and `HIPFIRE_EMULATE_GPUS=8` over four. The runs used 3 short prompts × 256 steps, a 4,396-token prompt (a 300-row S1 tail) × 64 and, except at 8 ranks, a 9,319-token prompt × 64. On one 7900 XTX (gfx1100), two emulated ranks (47 of 49 expert layers host-mapped) are byte-identical to the card alone: 3 short prompts × 256 steps, plus 3,372- and 4,396-token prompts × 64 on the F16 WMMA owner-routed route (1,536-row chunks). With the fixes above, the 6-rank load holds 24 descriptors at most under a 1,024 soft limit. The one-device transport oracle is byte-exact 245/245 on a 7900 XTX and on an R9700 at N = 2..=8. No measurement on multiple real gfx1100 cards is part of this entry.
- **Strix Halo NPU trunk: `auto` plans each request from rate scales learned live in the process, and the built-in calibration matches on hard fields only.** No calibration file is required: the built-in Halo record (measured on one kernel, NPU firmware and GPU PCI address) binds on arch, build, model index, epilogue and trunk route, and takes the host's kernel release, NPU firmware and GPU PCI address at margin 0.0. The 5% advisory margin (`ADVISORY_MARGIN`) is removed; the host speed difference is now measured instead. The calibration file and `hipfire calibrate-npu-trunk` remain as a strict override.
  - Live rates: the process keeps two scales against the built-in model, a GPU-window scale and an NPU-chain scale, each an EWMA (0.25) of measured/model per executed pair, clamped to 0.5-2.0. The snapshot is applied when it moves more than 1%, frozen after 6 samples once the last 4 each move less than 1%, and reopened after 3 consecutive deviations over 5% in the same direction. The first long request of a process runs the built-in prior. `on` and `emulate` never use the estimator, so they plan from the static calibration and stay the bit-exact comparable pair.
  - Per-request families: all four families are packed at load under `auto`; each request picks its fastest family subset and pair plan at request start from the current scales, and a subset runs a contiguous panel range of the packed chains. Developer variable `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_NPU_TRUNK_FAMILIES` (comma list of `qkv,zab,q,kvidx`, or `all`) forces the subset in every mode.
  - Guard: after each pair, if the GPU's measured waits on the NPU exceed what pairing saves it (the moved families' GPU projection time minus the pair's GPU glue and DRAM contention, under the current scales), the rest of that request runs GPU-only and the load logs one `npu-trunk: guard: ...` line. Request planning and family selection use only executable pair geometries (`plan_executable`: no single-chunk split or re-banked plan). Output differs only between the NPU and GPU projection routes, both within the accepted KLD cap.
  - `device.pci_bdf` in the calibration key is the selected GPU's PCI address (HIP's PCI bus ID), not an NPU slot; the docs and the v0.4.2.1 entry below now say so.
  - Measured on Strix Halo (gfx1151 + XDNA2, 7.3-rc7 PerfOpt, Flash-Next gptq3 + zab overlay, `hipfire serve`, fresh process per cell, 5 per arm, arms rotated within each fabric hold; each process sends 57,552- and 128,086-token prompts twice). TTFT median auto vs off: 26.7 vs 29.6 s and 72.1 vs 76.0 s on the first pass, 28.3 vs 31.2 s and 70.5 vs 74.8 s on the second; per-rep auto/off 0.905 / 0.952 / 0.905 / 0.913. Against the previous beta's auto, the per-rep ratio medians are 1.025 / 1.008 / 0.979 / 0.986, i.e. no change beyond process noise. The pair counters show the estimator learn the NPU chain at x0.73-0.87 of the built-in model and the GPU window at x1.01-1.09 (the model's QSA growth runs low at depth), freezing by the fourth request; all four families stay selected on this host, and the measured GPU wait on the NPU is 3-10 ms per request. `on` == `emulate` greedy output is byte-identical for five forced subsets that cover every per-shape panel range, at 9.7K, 16K and 57K tokens. With the serve pinned to 4 CPUs under 12 or 24 busy loops, the GPU's NPU waits rose to 1.7-4.0 s per 128K request but stayed under the 9.4 s modelled saving, so the guard did not trip.
- **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4): tail lineage residents — a prompt that extends the same final user/tool message restores the tail before the last `<|im_end|>` instead of re-prefilling the whole last turn (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_TAIL_SNAPSHOT`, default on; `=0` is the kill switch).** A cold or snapshot-restored (capture) prefill, other than one restored from a tail snapshot, now splits at the token index `p` before the last `<|im_end|>` and captures a session-cache tail snapshot there; a later prompt that extends that same final user or tool message (not a new message) restores that tail. The split is skipped when any chunk multiple lies in `(p, prompt.len()]`, when `p` is already a normal snapshot boundary, when `p - max(reused, floor(p / chunk) * chunk)` is below `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_TAIL_SNAPSHOT_MIN_GAP` rows (default 1024), i.e. the gap is measured from the later of the restored/live start and the preceding chunk boundary, or for prompts under `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_TAIL_SNAPSHOT_MIN_PROMPT` tokens (default 16384). On a Strix Halo NPU pipe pair the split row ends its pair group (the NPU request is planned through `p`), so the prime keeps its pipe pairs and only the template rows past `p` run as a GPU tile. The tail snapshots are **session-exact, not cold-exact**: the last template rows of the prime run as their own small tile after the split, so the forward schedule (and therefore the bytes) differ from one cold pass over the same tokens. Live agent turns (strict extension of the previous committed history) are unchanged and capture no tail split, and snapshots taken after a tail restore never enter the snapshot pool. `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_TAIL_SNAPSHOT=0` restores the previous prefill schedule. See `docs/env-vars.md` (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_TAIL_SNAPSHOT`, `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_TAIL_SNAPSHOT_MIN_GAP`, `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_TAIL_SNAPSHOT_MIN_PROMPT`).
  - Measured on Strix Halo (Flash-Next GPTQ3, q4 PLE, NPU trunk auto, one fresh `hipfire serve` per cell, one binary with `=0` vs default; a document prime, then the same last message extended): append TTFT at +512 @ 256K 2.57 → 1.16 s (median of 3 cells per arm; 2,555 → 521 rows prefilled) and at +4096 @ 32K 5.57 → 2.67 s (mean of 4 cells per arm; 11,530 → 4,105 rows). Cold prime at 256K in alternating order: 163.0 / 169.9 s off vs 159.9 / 171.5 s on (means 166.4 vs 165.7 s). Cold prime at 32K: 13.85 / 13.82 / 14.26 / 13.98 s off vs 15.09 / 13.95 / 15.06 / 14.15 s on; the two 15.1 s cells each ran first after the 256K cells in their hold. The 32K prime keeps its pipe pairs (`16384..24192 + 24192..32001` and a 9-row tile, against `16384..24256 + 24256..32010` off).
- **Flash-Next expert-slab wiring:** admit E8P-I4 cold experts plus an MQ4 hot set on gfx1100 and gfx1201 through the codec-generic two-bucket K1/K2/K3 route; use the MQ4-only K1 serving bundle on gfx1100, preserve gfx1201 W3/MQ4 kernel bytes, and refuse W2 on every architecture. gfx1100 E8P K2 is CPU-prepared with GPU qualification separately gated. The CPU admission checker reports all four codec counts per layer and in total, including E8P (codec 3). The shared admission matrix also serves gfx1151 (Strix Halo) with MQ4 and W3 only: its W3 K2 keeps the NT4 launcher (block 128, down row repeat 1/2/4), its tile mask stays the hipcc twin, E8P and W2 are refused there, and its slab kernel preload (planner, mask, all four K1 symbols) stays unconditional even for an MQ4-only layer, unlike gfx1100/gfx1201 whose MQ4-only layers preload no cold kernels.
- **Flash-Next expert-slab: gfx1151 (Strix Halo) admits E8P-I4 cold experts (mq2-xts) through PeaceMaker ports of the rc5 gfx1100 kernels.** The single `SLAB_ROUTE_GFX1151_E8P_RECEIPTS_LANDED` switch is true; MQ4/W3 behavior and every other architecture's admission are unchanged. K1 `e8p_i4_moe_gemv_pm_gfx1151` uses the bounded 96-byte ABI (`n_experts@88`, reserved zero at 92; 17 parameters); K2 `qwen4_moe_iu4_sym_e8p_pm_gfx1151` uses the bounded 64-byte ABI (`n_experts@60`). Both reject invalid expert IDs with an unsigned uniform guard before pointer reads, prefetches or barriers and preserve rc5 E8P NaN containment. Only target/name and the gfx1100-only VALU trans-use hazard waits differ from the gfx1100 arms; gfx1100/gfx1201 images re-emit byte-identical. Earlier Halo byte-oracle and KLD receipts qualified pre-rc5 images, not these regenerated bounded images; fresh GPU qualification is separate.
- **`qwen4_kld s11ref --sequence-range START:END` scores a contiguous slice of the S11 corpus in one process.** It writes only those sequences' canonical rows (each sequence is one cold window, so every row equals the full run's) and an `OUT.npy.json` of the distinct schema `hipfire.qwen4.s11ref_klrows.partition.v1` (sequence/row range, totals, sha fields, route), which is never a full-gate receipt; the range is validated against the corpus before the GPU load and is refused with `--smoke-seqs` or outside `s11ref`. The default full mode and its receipt are unchanged. Diagnostic example only; serve is unchanged.
- **`fn_lane_oracle` now loads the PLE rows through the same attach policy as `qwen4_kld`, `qwen4_greedy_ids` and `qwen4_g2_replay_gate`.** It honours `HIPFIRE_PLE_FORMAT` (an explicit `q4` binds `<model>.ple-q4`, `auto` is q4 on gfx1151 when the sidecar exists), prints the actual `fn_lane_oracle: ple rows: <q4|q8> from <path|embedded model file>` line, and refuses an explicit q4 whose sidecar is missing (it never derives one) and any sidecar that does not open and bind to the base, instead of silently measuring the embedded q8 rows. Artifacts with embedded rows and no sidecar load exactly as before. Diagnostic example only; serve is unchanged.
- **`fn_lane_oracle --lane-capacity N` stages the lane store with N lanes (and N row budget) independent of the selected `--ks`.** The singleton references, active lanes, controls and `--g0` run exactly as before (their lane count is still the `--ks` maximum, raised to 8 by `--g0` and 2 by `--controls`); only the staged capacity changes, so a per-k cell (e.g. `--ks 1 --lane-capacity 8`) steps the same 8-slot plans, with idle slots, as the full `--ks 1,2,4,8` run. N below the lanes the run drives or above the lane store's 64 is refused before the GPU load. `summary.json` records the resolved value as `args.lane_capacity` (every run, both `--spec` modes); without the flag the capacity is the old value, so existing runs are unchanged. Diagnostic example only; serve is unchanged.
- **`hipfire pull <model>` asks instead of requiring flags.** On a terminal it walks through only what the registry leaves open: the tier (other tags `<model>-<suffix>` with the same `arch_id`, e.g. `qwen3.8:flash-next` / `-mq3-xts` / `-mq2-xts`, each with size, a one-line note from `desc`, and whether it fits the detected VRAM or VRAM+RAM), the PLE rows of a split entry (q4 preselected on gfx1151 or when RAM cannot hold base + q8, else what `--ple auto` fetches), the registry's draft/MTP sidecars, then a summary with the total download and a free-disk check before it downloads anything. The choices only feed the existing pull plan (`plan_pull`, the registry entry). Flags skip their question (`--ple`, the tier's own tag, new `--draft` / `--no-draft`); a single-variant model with nothing to ask never prompts. `-y` / `--yes`, a non-terminal stdin, and the automatic pulls of `run` / `bench` / `serve` take the previous defaults with no prompts, so scripts and CI are unchanged.
- **Dense Qwen TP2 whole-token HIP graphs are now default on for exact homogeneous gfx1100 and gfx1201 pairs.** Each of the 128 per-token reductions is one graph-resident kernel (bounded device signal barrier plus the rank-ordered `x + (p0 + p1)` add), replacing 257 graph-segment launches, 258 kernel launches and 512 event record/wait pairs per token. Arithmetic and kernels are unchanged; a mixed gfx1100/gfx1201 pair is not admitted. `HIPFIRE_TP_FULL_GRAPH=0` restores the segmented route on either architecture.
