  - Measured on 2x W7900 (gfx1100), Qwen3.8-27B mq4-xts, Q8 VMM KV, pure AR, greedy, 512 generated tokens, 3 fresh processes per arm in A,B,B,A,A,B order: segmented 48.0/47.8/47.8 tok/s (median 47.8), whole-token 53.4/53.2/53.1 tok/s (median 53.2), **+11.30%**. The cross-device oracle passed 100/100 exact replays; six product-path prompts generated 3,072 tokens per arm with byte-identical transcripts.
  - Measured on 2x R9700, Qwen3.8-27B mq4-xts, greedy decode of 64 tokens, 3 fresh processes per arm, median after the first token: one card 29.86 / 26.82 ms, TP2 segmented 19.99 / 20.59 ms, TP2 whole-token 18.55 / 18.97 ms (ctx 128 / 8K). Rank-0 logits were byte-identical between the two TP2 routes on every token of every process; the TP2-vs-one-card route oracle passes with the same per-position logit differences; the first captured token takes about 25 ms instead of 39–46 ms for the segmented capture.
- **Strix Halo (gfx1151) Flash-Next long-context decode: exact QSA filter select and pooled BF16 mirror, on by default; 256K decode token latency -5%.** Selected indices, attention, state bytes, logits and greedy ids are unchanged. Both are on by default on exact gfx1151, where they were measured; `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_FILTER_SELECT=0` / `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_POOLED_BF16=0` are the kill switches. Elsewhere: the filter route serves only F32 QSA states on gfx11+ (`=1` forces it; gfx1201's default fp8 state selects through the fused BF16 selector, which this route does not replace), and the mirror is gfx1151-only (gfx1201 stores BF16 index keys natively).
  - `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_FILTER_SELECT=1` replaces the single-workgroup select-from-scores pass of large eager score/select calls with a deterministic 2048-sample threshold, tiled candidate compaction and an exact finish (`kernels/src/qsa_filter_select.hip`); underfilled or overflowing rows repair exactly in-kernel. It is admitted only past the measured crossover of the select it replaces: 4096 pooled blocks against the hipcc select; against the gfx1151 PM select 24576 blocks for calls of at most 16 rows and 49152 otherwise (Halo per call: 1 row PM 18.6 / 50.7 / 160 us vs filter 37 / 39 / 39 us at 8192 / 32768 / 65536 blocks; 256 rows PM 0.26 / 1.15 ms vs 0.35 / 0.80 ms at 32768 / 65536).
  - `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_POOLED_BF16=1` keeps a derived BF16 mirror of each QSA layer's pooled index keys (lossless: `qsa_pool_rope` stores BF16-rounded values), synced past a block watermark after pooling, never snapshotted, clamped/invalidated at every F16-arena lifecycle site and charged in admission (16 MiB per layer at 256K); mirror-covered select calls run the PM BF16 rows16 score instead of the F32 one.
  - Exactness: `tests/qsa_filter_select.rs` on gfx1151 and gfx1201 (6,048 from-scores and 864 full-route cases equal to the incumbents, forced underfill/overflow repair); `qsa_select_pm_check --filter` 17,280 cases with 0 mismatches on both architectures (depth/tie/tail/budget families, an 8192-row chunk at position 245,760); 63 real natural-text captures (layers 0/6/11 at 8K-256K plus 8K prefill chunks) replay byte-exactly through the incumbent hipcc and PM pairs and the filter route; `qwen4_qsa_arena_check` four arms identical through prefill, rollback, branch and restore with 990,372 mirror blocks checked. The oracle gains `--filter` and the `QSA_DUMP_LAYERS` / `QSA_DUMP_LAST_FULL_DECODE` / `QSA_DUMP_SELECTOR_ONLY` capture filters.
  - Measured (Halo, Flash-Next GPTQ3, natural-text prefixes; one fresh process per arm running nat-8k, nat-32k, nat-128k, nat-256k with 128 AR tokens each; 2 interleaved processes per arm; trimmed-mean inter-token latency): base 29.92 / 30.73 / 31.21 / 33.11 ms vs both switches 29.90 / 29.88 / 30.48 / 31.43 ms; 32K -> 256K growth +7.7% -> +5.2%.

    | depth | base rep 1 | base rep 2 | both on rep 1 | both on rep 2 | change |
    |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
    | 8K | 29.84 | 29.99 | 29.89 | 29.91 | -0.1% |
    | 32K | 31.32 | 30.14 | 29.87 | 29.88 | -2.8% |
    | 128K | 31.31 | 31.11 | 30.59 | 30.37 | -2.3% |
    | 256K | 33.15 | 33.07 | 31.16 | 31.69 | -5.1% |

    (ms per token; at 32K, 128K and 256K both candidate reps beat both base reps; 8K is a tie.) Greedy ids are identical on all four depths and on the 8-prompt lane AR cell. Prefill is unchanged within the process-to-process variance of these cells. A one-off 0.4-0.9 s stall when the QSA context maps its next 8192-token granule at 256K is excluded from the latency figures and is not QSA work.
- **CPU-only mesh splitting contract.** Dispatch now describes programs with stable `StepGraph` operation/resource IDs and explicit split rules; runtime's pure `split_program` binds TP reductions and PP transfers exactly once to manifest schedules. Weight placements retain their declared shard policy and logical shape. Single-device plans preserve operation order without collectives, and admission refusals allocate nothing. This is a planning API only: existing forward, loader and executor paths do not consume it.
- **SKU application-capacity emulation (`HIPFIRE_EMU`, `hipfire bench --emu`, `hipfire emu list|validate|estimate`), opt-in and capacity-only; no CU-count emulation on RDNA.** `HIPFIRE_EMU=<id>` (ten registry profiles: `rx9070xt`, `rx9070`, `rx9060xt`, `rx9060xt-8g`, `rx7900xt`, `rx7800xt`, `rx7700xt`, `rx7600`, `strix-point`, `krackan`; process start only) caps this process's managed application allocation (device, pinned-host, VMM and ROCr kernarg backing, charged by a ledger before the raw allocation) to the target's memory capacity, and routes the sizing and admission queries through the same budget. The host still executes at full speed on all its CUs with its own gfx, clocks and cache: it is "R9700 execution at 16-GiB application capacity", never a measured RX 9070 XT. CU masks are not used: they hung an R9700's MES on 2026-10-14 and are refused at runtime init, no safe method is approved, and clocks and power cannot be emulated without root. A target-performance figure is only ever an *estimate*: `hipfire emu estimate <id> --input <derating-input.json>` is CPU-only (starts no daemon, never touches HIP) and applies the disjoint-bucket derating model to measured kernel observations and host/target rates, reporting `unavailable` instead of a scalar when time closure, rates or run identity are missing. `hipfire emu validate <id>` starts a fresh model-free daemon with the profile installed and prints a schema-v1 receipt that keeps physical (raw hardware), emulated (budgeted ledger) and estimated fields apart; it exits nonzero on a capacity, host-topology or graph failure. `hipfire bench <model> --emu <id|off>` passes the profile to every spawned bench daemon arm, overrides `HIPFIRE_EMU` (including `off`), validates the id before anything spawns and logs the effective value. UMA profiles (`strix-point`, `krackan`) use a scenario (32 GiB host, 1 GiB carve-out, 4 GiB reserve, 16 GiB GTT; override with `HIPFIRE_EMU_HOST_BYTES`, `HIPFIRE_EMU_CARVEOUT_BYTES`, `HIPFIRE_EMU_HOST_RESERVE_BYTES`, `HIPFIRE_EMU_GTT_BYTES`), not an AMD limit. With a profile active the daemon's `diag` line gains an `emu` object (budgeted free/total and ledger) next to the unchanged physical `vram_free_mb`/`vram_total_mb`; with no profile every output is unchanged. A bandwidth-contention limiter is a proposal only and is not shipped. Measured sizing finding, documented in [docs/EMU.md](docs/EMU.md) and [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md): an RX 9070 XT (16 GB) host with 64 GB RAM (TTM cap 31 GiB) cannot load Qwen3.8 Flash-Next, whose 38–61 GB of host-mapped routed experts exceed it; Flash-Next on a 16 GB card needs at least 128 GB of host RAM. Env rows: [docs/env-vars.md](docs/env-vars.md).
- **Flash-Next native MTP: a turn the AR floor retired now continues live in the next turn.** After the AR floor retires a request, its AR tokens advance the target alone. The MTP head used to stay where retirement found it, so the turn ended with the head behind the target. The session commit then dropped the live state, because live continuation needs head and target at the same position. The conversation's next turn restored the newest chunk snapshot (a multiple of 8192 tokens) and re-prefilled everything above it: on Strix Halo in a 32K agent conversation, a turn that stopped on `max_tokens` after retiring cost the next request 9,613 re-prefilled rows (4.8 s) instead of 55. Length stops themselves never needed a repair (an MTP window is capped at the remaining `max_tokens`); retirement was the cause. Now each retired AR token's target hidden row is copied into the spec hidden capture, and the head appends the owed rows teacher-forced, as an n-gram takeover appends its kept rows (one batched decode fill where it runs, else one Append per row). It does so every 1024 tokens and before every teacher-forced advance, the terminal pending-seed flush included, so the turn ends with head and target together and commits live. Retired windows stay head-free apart from that one row copy per token. Greedy output is unchanged (native MTP emits AR's greedy tokens).
- **Flash-Next native MTP: a think-budget force-close no longer re-prefills the conversation, and a stop sequence or other mid-window stop repairs the window instead of dropping live state.** A native MTP window commits up to k+1 tokens before the emitter observes any of them, so a think-budget force-close that fired on an interior token used to take the full-history Realign (reset, then re-prefill every prompt and decoded token), and a stop sequence or think-cap stop strictly inside a window used to invalidate the conversation cache so the next turn restored the newest chunk snapshot. The serve decode loop now clamps each native Qwen4 window to the emitter's `window_cap()`, so a think-budget force-close or think-cap stop only ever lands on a window's last token and the intervention needs no repair. For a stop inside a window (which cannot be predicted), the loop first calls the speculator's `repair_terminal_prefix`, before any reset, forced advance or prefill: native Qwen4 restores its retained pre-window target and head and replays only the consumed prefix, so the turn ends live (`HIPFIRE_QWEN_CACHE_TRACE=1` logs `[qwen-cache window-repair] … repaired=true`), and only an unrepairable window falls back to the existing reset. Requests that carry stop sequences now say so to the drafter through `SpecRequestConfig::stop_sequences`. Other speculators are unchanged (the cap applies to native Qwen4 MTP only); greedy output is byte-identical where no intervention lands inside a window, and `serve_harness --stop TEXT` sends stop sequences for chain checks.
- **CU masking is refused on RDNA (gfx10/gfx11/gfx12), at runtime init and at every mask entry point; `HIPFIRE_GFX1151_REDLINE_CU_COUNT` is refused and deprecated (CDNA unchanged).** On 2026-10-14 a CU-masked queue probe hung the R9700 (gfx1201) MES scheduler, forced mode1 resets and took the host down. `hipfire-config` now refuses a non-blank `HSA_CU_MASK` / `ROC_GLOBAL_CU_MASK` in the real process environment before ROCr (`Runtime::initialize`) or HIP (`HipRuntime::load`) loads whenever any KFD GPU node is RDNA, or the topology cannot prove otherwise; all-gfx9 hosts pass. In `redline-rocr`, `AqlQueue::create_with_cu_mask`, `QueueSet::create_with_cu_masks` and the queue/PM4 set-mask paths return `CuMaskRefusedOnRdna` on RDNA devices before any HSA call (the API itself stays). `diagnostic.replay.gfx1151_cu_count` / `HIPFIRE_GFX1151_REDLINE_CU_COUNT` can no longer build a mask: any value other than `all` fails PM4 replay preparation on any arch, and the key is deprecated (0.4.0, removal 0.5.0). The earlier "200× under `ROC_GLOBAL_CU_MASK=0x1`" stress recipes are withdrawn and are now refused at runtime init on RDNA.
- **Device spin waits are bounded at 500 ms; a stalled peer GPU or rendezvous now fails the request instead of leaving waves spinning.** Several kernels spin on a flag that another GPU or workgroup writes, and none of those waits had a device-side bound: the gfx1201 TP3/TP4 graph barrier `tp_graph_signal_wait2/3_gfx1201` (default-on for DeepSeek-V4 MQ2R on 3–4 R9700s), the gfx1100 TP2 barrier/reduce (`HIPFIRE_TP_FULL_GRAPH`), the gfx1100 RMSNorm wavegrid kernels (`HIPFIRE_RDNA3_RMSNORM_WAVEGRID`, `HIPFIRE_AWQ_NORM_WAVEGRID`) and the gfx1151 `hc_compute_control` `rsqrt_once` handoff, which was a pure spin with no `s_sleep`. If the producer stalled, the waiter spun until teardown, and a reset on any card suspends every GPU process on the host. Each wait now reads the realtime counter (`wall_clock64`). After 500 ms, well inside the ~2.1 s MES hang window, it records its site in a per-device host-mapped error block (`kernels/src/device_wait_deadline.h`, `rdna_compute::device_wait`) and stops. TP barriers exit the wave. Rendezvous kernels finish their epilogue, so their self-restoring scratch stays consistent. Later waits on that device stop within about 100 µs. The host reads the block after the step: `Gpu::download_*` and `Gpu::take_device_wait_error`, `Gpus::take_device_wait_errors` after the DS4 TP graph sync and the dense TP2 logits, and every bounded-wait launch for a timeout left unread. A timeout fails the request with `device wait timeout on GPU <n>: <kernel> waited 500 ms for … (<epoch|workgroup> N)`, and after a TP timeout the TP graph signals are re-zeroed. The polls keep their `s_sleep(1)`, `rsqrt_once` gains one, and a healthy wait reads neither the counter nor host memory. On one R9700 (gfx1201) the normal-path outputs are byte-identical to the pre-change kernels: wavegrid, AWQ wavegrid at K 2048/4096/5120, `hc_compute_control_vec4_finalize` t256/t1024 with and without `rsqrt_once`, and the TP4 waits, 3 seeds × 20 launches each. Forced timeouts (an unpublished peer signal, poisoned rendezvous scratch) stop at 500.1 ms with the right site and detail and restore the scratch, and the next launch matches the old kernel bit for bit. In interleaved A/B launches, the bounded kernels measured 0.998–1.003× the old ones over 3 runs. A second harness measured up to 1.02×, but an old-kernel-plus-unused-kernarg control moved −1.1% to +0.5% (A/A floor 0.1%), so the remaining spread is code placement rather than wait cost. Gate: `cargo run --release -p rdna-compute --features lab --example device_wait_deadline` (one gfx1201 card).
- **`hipfire serve` optional bearer authentication; a key is recommended on a non-loopback bind.** New `serve.api_key_file` (env `HIPFIRE_SERVE_API_KEY_FILE`, flag `--api-key-file <absolute-path>`) names a UTF-8 key file of at least 32 bytes; on unix a group- or other-readable file is refused with a `chmod 600` hint, and only the path is ever stored or printed. With a key, every route (including UI assets and CORS preflight) needs `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and otherwise gets an empty `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`; unauthenticated `GET /health` returns only `status` and `version`. The key is optional on every bind: without one, behavior is unchanged, and a non-loopback bind logs one recommendation line suggesting a key. Windows never auto-generates a key. Local CLI/TUI clients read the configured key automatically through the new `hipfire_client::ServiceEndpoint` (http/https only, verified TLS, no insecure mode). docs/SERVE.md has a tailnet-only Tailscale Serve recipe.
- **Native Windows `hipfire stop`, `ps` and home discovery.** On Windows every serve binds a second loopback listener on an OS-assigned port with a per-process 32-byte random credential; `POST /api/v1/shutdown` with that bearer runs the existing bounded drain, and the route is not on the inference listener. A Windows `serve.pid` also records `manage_port`/`manage_token` (written by exclusive create and rename) and `hipfire ps --json` shows `manage_token_present` instead of the token. Windows `hipfire stop` uses the management route after proving the PID's image, creation time and listen port (kernel32/iphlpapi); Windows `hipfire update` refuses with the `install.ps1` re-run command. The Windows hipfire home is `HIPFIRE_HOME`, then `%USERPROFILE%\.hipfire`, then `%HOME%\.hipfire`, and never the current directory. Unix serves bind no management listener; their `serve.pid`, `ps` output, `stop` (SIGTERM) and home are unchanged.
- **`hipfire diag` reports host memory and, on Windows, per-adapter DXGI budgets.** `diag --json` gains an additive `host_memory` object (`/proc/meminfo` on Linux, `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` on Windows); Linux text output is unchanged. Windows adds a "GPU memory budget (DXGI, this process)" section: `QueryVideoMemoryInfo` local/non-local budget and usage for node 0 of each adapter. These are calling-process views, not engine admission budgets. On Windows the GPU-less OOM guard's swap test uses the pagefile approximation (commit limit minus physical memory).
- **Native Windows builds: the CLI and daemon cross-compile and link for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; Unix-only engine paths now fail with explicit errors there.** POSIX-FD VMM export/import is compiled out on Windows; PLE conversion, the PLE hot-row store/pack writer and prewarm return "unsupported on Windows" errors (run on Linux). Linux behavior is unchanged. A new advisory `Windows MSVC (advisory, no GPU)` CI job builds both binaries, tests hipfire-config/registry/client, smoke-checks `hipfire --version` and `hipfire diag --json` without HIP, and uploads an unsigned developer ZIP (`scripts/package-windows.ps1`, with `manifest.json` and SHA-256). This is compile/package coverage, not Windows GPU certification.
- **Windows: ROCm roots derived from a compiler path are plain `C:\…` paths.** The root that `hipfire-config` derives from the selected `hipcc`/`amdclang++` (exported as `ROCM_PATH`) came from `std::fs::canonicalize`, which on Windows returns verbatim `\\?\C:\…` paths. Verbatim drive paths are now rewritten to the plain form when it names the same file (under MAX_PATH, no reserved device names or trailing dots/spaces). Linux is unchanged. The Windows CI job's hipfire-config tests no longer assume Linux library names (`install_guidance`) or the Debian multiarch layout.
- **Flash-Next (qwen4) fn-lanes: a request promoted from the native-MTP singleton into an AR lane now continues the AR singleton's text byte for byte.** With `serve.batch_spec = false` beside a loaded MTP head, the first request runs alone on the native-MTP singleton; when a peer queued, its promotion into an AR lane was refused after the lane had been admitted, so the stream went on from a fresh trunk state and its text differed from running alone (exactly one stream per process at C2/C4/C8). An AR lane now takes the request's trunk state and drops the resident head. `fn_lane_oracle --spec ar --promote P` checks the promoted stream against the AR singleton ids (at P=0 also every logits row and trunk state). Halo, 3 processes each at C2/C4/C8: every stream is identical to its alone run on AR lanes and on MTP lanes.
- **Strix Halo (gfx1151) Flash-Next: agent-turn appends under 512 rows run on the >= 512-row kernels by default (401 rows 900 → 434 ms at 32K; KLD within +0.005).** Below 512 rows a prefill tile used to run every family on F32 SIMT routes, at about 2 ms per row. A 401-row tool result appended at 32K depth took 900 ms (446 rows/s), while a whole 529-row append took 461 ms. Now, on exact gfx1151, a prefill tile of 48 to 511 rows engages the canonical routing switch for that tile only. That switch, `Gpu::prefill_invariant_scope`, is the one the `HIPFIRE_PREFILL_PM_INVARIANT` profile uses. Every row-count routing predicate sees the canonical chunk while launches keep the real row count. So the tile runs:
  - F16 WMMA for the dense and MQ6 projections;
  - WMMA QSA;
  - BF16 HC streams;
  - the WY GDN recurrence;
  - the F16 WMMA grouped MoE, with the symmetric IU4 arm suppressed for the tile (`Gpu::qwen4_append_f16_moe_scope`).

- **Sub-4-bit G2 run carrier: `scripts/subq4_g2_carrier.py` (lab tooling, no engine change).** One scheduler submission (class correct, card C, 30 GB device, 44 GB pinned host, hostmem lock, P1, 7200 s) through `/home/kaden/qcal/locks/fabric/fabric-run.sh` runs `fn_lane_oracle` (AR and native-MTP lanes with controls, ks 1,2,4,8), `qwen4_parity --mode state` and `qwen4_g2_replay_gate` serially on the ctl3-hot artifact and writes `g2.json` with per-check rc, command, hashes, card identity, mismatch counts and the first mismatch's repro. `--expert-vram-layers N` (integer, default 16; 15 only if 16 still runs out of device memory) sets `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_VRAM_LAYERS` for the lane and parity checks and the replay gate's CLI flag, is required in the replay report's params, and is recorded in `g2.json`. The scheduler is mandatory: `fabric.py` silently falls back to in-process admission when fabricd is down, so the carrier refuses unless a live fabricd answers `--status --json`, refuses when `FABRIC_NO_DAEMON`/`FABRIC_SANDBOX` is set, and inside the job requires fabricd to list the wrapper as a running `jN` job with the declared card, memory, lock, priority and owner, before any GPU child starts. It also refuses to start without an explicit real-artifact PASS smoke receipt, a `--code-sha` that matches the G2 worktree's HEAD, and a card whose UUID/BDF match the known map, the KFD topology and the scheduler. An MTP run that never drafts, accepts and rejects a window is a FAIL.
- **Real-model expert-slab retained-replay gate: `qwen4_g2_replay_gate` (lab example, no engine change).** On a ctl3-hot slab artifact it captures the decode body through the production lifecycle, checks that the production route, the prepared plan and the recorded-HIP oracle reproduce ordinary HIP byte for byte (logits, GDN, QSA, PLE state, lengths, position) at consecutive positions while proving each arm actually replayed, then frees and rebuilds the bundle between capture and replay and requires all three executors to refuse the changed binding with the route-identity error before any retained submit. Output is JSON with an exact mismatch count and error per check; the exit status is non-zero on any failed or unevaluable check.
- **`qwen4_g2_replay_gate` runs only where Redline is the product default; elsewhere it reports SKIP (lab example, no engine change).** The gate used to force `configure_model_default(true)`, so a non-default model (for example a Strix Halo MQ3 artifact) failed a route the product never takes. After the load it now passes the loaded model's facts (GPU arch, `qwen4`, file path, one rank, no drafter installed, `qwen4_ep`, platform refusal) to the daemon's own `hipfire_runtime::config::retained_redline_default`, and runs the full capture, positive and changed-binding phases, unchanged, only on a default route (`.mq4r` on gfx1100/gfx1151/gfx1201, or Qwen4 on exact gfx1201 with no drafter). Otherwise it frees the bundle and exits 0 with `{"ok": true, "status": "skip", "skipped": true, "reason": "Redline not on the default route (config.rs:15–22)", "checks": []}` plus the route facts. A SKIP has no check rows, so it never reads as a PASS, and a forced-route result is not evidence about a default one. `scripts/subq4_g2_carrier.py` accepts exactly that report as a `SKIP` child verdict (not a failure, not a PASS; any inconsistent skip report fails as `report_invalid`), and writes a `g2.json` status of `SKIP` and exits 0 when no check failed and the replay check skipped.

An absent or unusable sidecar, or an artifact the hot set cannot back, falls back to the unchanged whole-layer placement instead of refusing the load. The VRAM budget is the same as `auto` (free − non-expert − reserve − tier tables − long-prefill stage buffers) minus a 512 MiB safety margin. It is filled with the experts ranked highest by a decode-routing sidecar, in one device owner plus one host-mapped owner, and reached through the existing per-layer absolute expert pointer tables. Kernels, slot order and combine order are unchanged. Long-prefill staging copies only a layer's host-tier experts into two VRAM stage buffers. EP, stock FP8, slab arenas, unified memory and an explicit `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_VRAM_LAYERS` are not eligible and keep whole-layer placement.

The sidecar `hotset-decode-v1` (sha256 `7f6760e1…`) was ranked on 25 prompts disjoint from the bench set and is the same one that ships. Both arms use the same binary. MTP is the median of 3 interleaved fresh processes per arm and AR is 1 process per arm. Greedy ids are identical on all 11 prompts, AR and MTP. It is not a blanket gain on every prompt: `records_parser_1k` regressed (43.1 → 39.4 tok/s, −8.6%) and `code_edit` is flat (47.7 → 47.6). Receipts: `/home/kaden/qcal/release-0.4.3/lever1-r9700/runs/{dec,cmd}-l2-*` (scheduler job j723).

    The MTP aggregate rises +14.6% and the AR aggregate +20.8%, but per prompt the change ranges from −8.6% (`records_parser_1k`) to +41.8% (`glimmer_coding`). p16k prefill is flat. With the margin the hot set holds 6,479 experts under MTP and 6,850 under AR (daemon log); the whole-layer arm holds 14 (MTP) and 15 (AR) layers of 512 experts, 7,168 and 7,680. Peak VRAM is the maximum `peak_vram_mib` in each run's `vram-peak.txt`: the decode row is the max over the 4 decode runs per arm (3 MTP and 1 AR; the whole-layer maximum is the AR run at 31,662, the hot-set maximum the AR run at 31,517), the prefill row the single p16k run per arm. These are VRAM-poller samples, not an allocator high-water mark, and decode and prefill are separate measurements. In decode the hot set peaks 145 MiB lower than whole-layer placement; at p16k prefill both arms peak at the same 31,841 MiB.

On gfx1201 only, `whole-first` keeps the same baseline whole layers as the hot-set-off placement, materialization and route, with no partial or tiered layers and no mixed experts (hot experts = 0), and does not consult the sidecar (even an explicit `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_EXPERT_HOTSET` path). On by default, `qsa_decode_splitk_partial_f32` cuts every (row, KV group) list into 32 slices that run as separate workgroups, each scoring its 12 query heads from a single K/V read (32-way KV-group shared scoring), and `qsa_decode_splitk_combine_f32` merges the per-slice softmax partials, held in the QSA per-launch scratch, in slice order (new `qsa_decode_splitk.hip`; existing kernel sources are untouched). A no-shared recipe now rotates the routed input with the routed gate/up's per-layer AWQ scale (and the opt-in down scale), as MiniMax's packed experts carry them. - **Strix Halo (gfx1151) Flash-Next decode: the per-token PLE row fetch no longer stalls the GPU, and 120 fewer launches per token (exact; AR +2.6%).** A decode token used to spawn 16 reader threads to fetch its 16 PLE rows; the GPU finished layer 0 and then waited for them (0.94 ms per token at 1.4K context, 1.80 ms at 32K). Small fetches (at most 64 reads) are now read inline from the page cache with `preadv2(RWF_NOWAIT)`. Only reads that would block go to readers, and never more readers than reads. The greedy token id is copied to pinned memory right behind the argmax, so the host waits once instead of twice. On exact gfx1151 single-token decode, two launch merges reuse the incumbent arithmetic verbatim: router plus shared gate/up in one launch, and GDN z/b/a in one launch. Few-row QSA score/select now takes the certified PeaceMaker gfx1151 pair that prefill already uses. Every lever has its own kill switch: `HIPFIRE_PLE_INLINE_FETCH`, `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_TOKEN_READBACK_EARLY`, `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_DECODE_HEAD_FUSE`, `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_DECODE_ZBA_X3`, `HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_SELECT_PM_DECODE`.

A golden fixture generated from the teacher (254 finite codes × 49 scales) is bit-identical. Layout and the FNUZ fold are in [docs/quant-formats/fp8-e4m3.md](docs/quant-formats/fp8-e4m3.md).

MI300X, stock-fp8 Flash-Next, against the landed P2 receipts: greedy ids identical on the 18 short battery prompts and both ~16.5K long-context prompts (3 fresh processes each), `qwen4_kld s11ref` KL rows byte-equal on wt2/code24/assistant, Tier C hc 7/0 and hyper 5/0. 16,635-token prefill, 3 fresh processes per arm interleaved against beta 434b99f65: 20.494 / 20.536 / 20.545 s → 12.369 / 12.371 / 12.374 s (median 1.66×, ranges disjoint). Decode is unchanged (one row was already three launches).
- **PeaceMaker CDNA arm (gfx942 / MI300X): new `peacemaker-cdna` crate and `peacemaker_isa::cdna`, opt-in and not selected by any serving path.** `peacemaker-cdna` is the wave64 CDNA3 instruction model: an `Arch` variant with a capability table, typed encoders/decoders with `llvm-mc`-compatible printers (SOP, DS, MUBUF/SMEM/FLAT, VOP1/2/C/3, VOP3P and MFMA), FNUZ/OCP FP8/BF8, F16 and BF16 conversions, the gfx90a+ kernel descriptor, and a CPU wave64 emulator. `peacemaker-isa` gains `Arch::Gfx942` (its RDNA text paths refuse it), the CDNA3 wait-ledger rules, a checked wave64 `cdna::builder`, a wait-state hazard pass and native code-object emission. Three first kernels (`fp8_act_producer`, `fp8_moe_gate_up`, `qsa_fp8_kv`) ship with HIP twins under `kernels/src/pm_cdna/` and run Tier C in emulation, plus a `cdna_card_tierc` MI300X card harness (runbook in `crates/peacemaker-isa/tools/`, receipts under `docs/pm-cdna/card/`). Default-off at run time: `peacemaker-isa` now depends on `peacemaker-cdna` unconditionally and `rdna-compute` depends on `peacemaker-isa`, so the new crate is a transitive compile-time dependency of runtime builds, but no dispatch table, callsite selection or kernel set references the arm or the kernels, so run-time behavior on every arch is unchanged; no throughput claim. `docs/pm-cdna/route/` and `ROUTE-MIRROR.md` are design inventory for the gfx942 route mirror, not shipped routes. Crate maps for `peacemaker-cdna`, `peacemaker-isa` and `hip-bridge` regenerated.
  - **gfx942 GDN: decode rows take the batched persistent route, and the recurrence runs the register-resident `gated_delta_step_pipe128_f32` (exact; decode +5.5 % at 145 tokens of context and +5.3 % at 16.6K, 16.6K-token prefill −0.8 %).** A one-row GDN step (decode) ran the sequential `gated_delta_step_f32`, 204 µs per layer (7.4 of the 128 ms per token); `gdn_persistent_batch` now admits one row on gfx942, whose persistent recurrence is pinned to the sequential kernel's arithmetic. gfx1201's `gated_delta_step_pipe128_f32` (one thread per value column, register-resident state, one barrier per row) now also builds for gfx942 with persistent256's `__fmul_rn` / `__fmaf_rn` / `__fsub_rn` pins and is the gfx942 F32 route (`HIPFIRE_QWEN4_GDN_PIPE=0` keeps persistent256); Q8 pipe128 stays gfx1201-only, and the gfx1100/gfx1151/gfx1201 `tensor_ops` objects are byte-identical to the base. MI300X, stock-fp8 Flash-Next: `gdn_pipe128_is_bytewise_the_persistent256_kernel` passes on gfx942 (F32, rows 1–1536); Tier C gated 6 pass / 1 known fail (`qwen4_gated_delta_step_norm128_q8_gated`, unchanged since P1, Q8 state not on the gfx942 route); greedy ids identical to the P2 receipts on 18 short and both ~16.5K long-context prompts (3 fresh processes each); `qwen4_kld s11ref` KL rows byte-equal on wt2/code24/assistant. 3 fresh processes per arm against the L1 build: decode 7.98 → 8.42 tok/s (145-token prompt) and 7.75 → 8.16 tok/s (16,635-token prompt); 16,635-token prefill 12.37 → 12.27 s; every range disjoint.
- **Qwen4 UMA context admission counts arena-inclusive QSA growth, and the context takes precedence over the reclaimable PLE page cache.** Admission counts the opt-in F16 arena at full capacity and partial contexts with pooled-index and four-token F16-arena row rounding (2 KiB/token/layer at 2 KV heads), plus the gather workspace, native MTP request buffers and the existing headroom. The PLE prewarm/load-fill budget is not a hard reservation: it is admitted up to what free memory leaves after the context, shrunk to 0 if need be (one `qwen4 ple budget: …` log line reports the shrunk budget), and the carrier caps the prewarm budgets it sets at that value. `card_cap` is the largest context that fits with PLE at 0 and moves with free host memory only. Oversized explicit `max_seq` values refuse under the default auto OOM guard with byte charges and the largest fitting `card_cap`; discrete GPUs are unchanged. Strix Halo receipt: Flash-Next at `max_seq` 262144 with native MTP on needed 33,660 MiB against 33,068 MiB free and was refused; it now admits with PLE 14,336 → 13,743 MiB, and `auto` resolves to 262,144 again. CPU Halo regression tests cover the 256K serve receipt, the exact-cap refusal, a full-PLE fit, arena/mirror growth and discrete behavior.
- **EmbeddingGemma 2 (`google/embeddinggemma-2`, arch 18): a single-vector embedding encoder served end to end on the non-chat `embed` verb — text, images, audio and video — with the checkpoint's vision and audio towers riding one `.vl` sidecar.** 24 bidirectional Gemma-4-family layers (sliding ±512 : full = 5:1, per-layer head_dim/KV overrides, half-split RoPE, projection-only PLE, sandwich norms, `layer_scalar`), mean pooling + L2 into the 768-d `embedding_projection`, Matryoshka 768/512/256/128 via the request's `dims`. Reached through `hipfire embed` and `POST /v1/embeddings` only — no LM head exists, so no generation route. The quantizer writes the checkpoint's 963 tower tensors (`vision_tower.*`, `audio_tower.*`, `embed_vision.*`, `embed_audio.*`) into a `<trunk>.vl` pack beside the tower-less trunk; tower VRAM is paid only when the load's `vision_mode` ladder resolves it (`off`, the schema default, is text-only and refuses media per modality with a pointing error).
  - **Media input.** Images arrive as `images_base64` (`--image` / `image_url` content parts) and clips as `audios_base64` WAV (`--audio` / `input_audio` with `data`/`format`); video is its own bullet below. The text carries one `<|image|>` (id 258880) or `<|audio|>` (id 258881) marker per medium; zero markers appends before EOS, a mismatch is refused naming both counts. Each marker expands to `boi + <token>×N + eoi`, where `N` is the pooled patch count (≤ 280 by the processor's resize rule) and, for audio, `M` is the mel mask-subsample count, **uncapped**: `audio_seq_length: 280` is metadata, not a cap (a 15 s clip is `M` = 375, and the waveform is never truncated). Every medium is one batched forward with the text rows; the arch-17-shaped slot engine serves mixed media in one batch.
  - **Video (the third modality, same `.vl` tower pack).** A clip arrives as `videos_base64` — one entry per video, each a list of that clip's decoded FRAMES (PNG/JPEG, display order; `--video f0,f1,…` per clip on the CLI, `input_video` content parts on the HTTP route). The daemon applies HF's own sampler (`EmbeddingGemma2VideoProcessor.sample_frames`: a decoded frame list carries no capture rate, so the `fps` pass is skipped exactly as HF skips it and the `max_frames` 32 budget governs — ≤32 frames all kept, more strided by `np.linspace(0, total-1, 32, dtype=int)`), so a caller hands a clip at its native rate and gets the checkpoint's sampling, not its own. One `<|video|>` (id 258884) per VIDEO expands to one `boi(255999) + video_token×S + eoi(258882)` block PER FRAME (HF `replace_video_token` with `add_timestamps=false` — no `mm:ss ` text, no separators), each frame resized against the VIDEO processor's own budget (`video_processor.max_soft_tokens = 140` → 1 260 patches, not the image leg's 280/2 520) and run through the SAME vision tower as one independent sequence (HF's tower batches frames with `attention_mask = ~padding_positions`, so frames never attend each other). No new tower weights, no new tower code: `vision.rs` unchanged, `video.rs` owns the sampler + the frame container rule (a non-PNG/JPEG blob is refused by name with the `ffmpeg` extraction to run, mirroring the audio leg's WAV-only rule), and `carrier.rs` emits one `MediaSpan` per frame. Frames of one clip must share a size — HF stacks them into one array — and are refused by name otherwise; `add_timestamps=true`, a `num_frames` key, a non-uniform `overflow_strategy` or a `max_soft_tokens` outside HF's supported set are refused at load rather than silently changing the frames. Parity: five video fixtures (a 4-frame clip, an exactly-32-frame clip, a 77-frame clip that forces the uniform sampler, a tall 480×144 aspect, and a marker mid-text) at rel-L2 3.1e-4…4.9e-3 against the float32 reference with every `n_input_tokens` equal to it, plus the marker-count mismatch and the non-image-frame refusals.
  - **Parity against a float32 CPU `transformers` 5.19.0 reference** (`scripts/check_embeddinggemma2_parity.py`, band 2e-2 rel-L2, `scripts/make_embeddinggemma2_reference.py` regenerates it): nine text fixtures 2.2e-4…1.0e-3 (including 8192 tokens), six image fixtures 2.7e-4…3.1e-3, six clips 2.4e-4…2.6e-3 and five video clips (3, 4, 5, 32 frames and a 77-frame clip that forces the sampler) 3.1e-4…4.9e-3, every `n_input_tokens` equal to the reference tokenization — which requires the merge-rank SP-BPE path (`Tokenizer::enable_sp_bpe_merges`); the default greedy SentencePiece tokenizer is longest-literal and diverges from HF `tokenizers` on ordinary text. The same script's edge-case contract covers marker-count mismatch per modality, tower-less media refusal, `dims`/kind/length validation, a non-image video frame and the 8192-token truncation.
  - **Quantization matrix** (`scripts/check_embeddinggemma2_quant.py`, band from each artifact's own HFQ index): q8f16 worst 2.0e-2 against a 3e-2 band, mq4v2 worst 2.8e-1 against 5e-1 — each including an image leg, because the towers ride F16 in the pack for every tier and the trunk's own band must therefore govern the image embedding too.
  - **Multi-slot is bit-exact**: eight text inputs plus an image, a clip and a 4-frame video in the same batched forward reproduce the sequential daemon's vectors bit for bit (`scripts/check_embeddinggemma2_multislot.py --slots 4`), the same exactness contract arch 17 carries.
  - **Three formula bugs the float32 reference caught, all in the new towers** (each is now pinned by a unit test and documented where it bites): HF's audio attention **inverts** its 5-D mask — its `masked_fill(attention_mask.logical_not(), −1e9)` sees an *additive* mask because eager mode's `eager_mask` converts the boolean one first, so the surviving keys are the complement of the causal window, and the whole subsampled sequence must be run rather than just the `M` valid rows (~15 % rel-L2 otherwise); the vision tower's axial RoPE pairs are `(j, j + head_dim/4)` *inside* each half, not `(j, j + head_dim/2)` (the old permutation sheared the rotation); and the image resize must be torchvision's ATen uint8 bicubic kernel — the `image` crate's CatmullRom and Pillow's bilinear both miss.
  - **Two integration bugs found by running the oracle, fixed here:** an HFQ `.vl` pack read as tower-less because `HfqFile`'s `ModelSource::tensor_info` is a documented stub (`None`) while the arch crate asked through it — the trunk path never calls it, which is why text passed and every media load failed; and the slot route ignored the load's `vision_mode` ladder entirely (a carrier-delegated preflight peeked at the process config instead), so a `serve.multi_slot` load asking for `auto` came back text-only and an explicit `off` could be defeated by a config-file `auto`.
  - **And one on the shipped client, found by driving the CLI end to end: `hipfire embed` never forwarded `vision.mode`.** It loaded the daemon with an empty params object instead of the `load_params` projection `run`/`serve` use, so a configured `vision_mode=auto` still came back "text-only (no sidecar)" and every `--image`/`--audio`/`--video` request was refused — while the same model served all three through the daemon protocol (which is how the harnesses passed). `embed` now projects the encoder's own key set — the vision ladder plus an authored `max_seq`, deliberately not the generation-only policy — and a unit test pins both the projection and that restriction.
  - **An arch-18 checkpoint whose weights are a format this decoder cannot read now fails closed, by name, instead of panicking the daemon.** `hipfire-quantize --format q4k` writes Q4K (HFQ quant_type 4, a GGUF/Maple-side container outside the dense HFQ decode set) for any dense arch; the arches whose kernels decode Q4K load it, but this encoder decodes on the host and the shared `dequantize_to_f32` has no arm for it — its answer used to be a `panic!` mid-load, which took the daemon and any model resident beside it down. `weights::refuse_unsupported_quant_types` screens both the trunk and the `.vl` pack before any GPU work and returns a load error naming the tensor, the quant type and a loadable tier; `weight_backend::dequant_f32_supported` is the single predicate.
  - **`hipfire quantize --install` carries the artifacts the quantizer writes BESIDE the trunk** — today the arch-18 `.vl` tower pack. It copied the trunk alone, which left a 1 GB pack in the caller's working directory and produced a *text-only* install (media refused with no tower) for the documented bring-your-own flow. Install and `--upload` now walk the same `derived_packs()` helper, which locates the pack with the loader's own probe so an install and a later load cannot disagree about which file it is; the CWD copies stay behind, as before.
  - **Two `embeddinggemma-2:` registry rows, local-only (empty `repo`), so all of this works with no Hugging Face publish.** `embeddinggemma-2:q8f16` (0.33 GB, the default tier; also the `embeddinggemma-2` alias) and `embeddinggemma-2:mq4v2` (0.25 GB) each declare their `<trunk>.vl` tower pack in the registry's `vision` slot with real digests. `hipfire pull` refuses them by design ("place \<file\> in \<models dir\>") instead of 404ing, and `hipfire embed <tag>`/`list` resolve them from the models directory — verified end to end, media included, from the single `hipfire quantize … --install --register` command. `scripts/registry_gen.py` gained the arch-18 family mapping; the generator has supported empty-`repo` entries since the staged Flash-Next ZAB row.
- **Strix Halo NPU trunk: the HIP interop now loads the HIP runtime the way the GPU runtime does, so it works on hosts without a system ROCm.** `railgun::npu` opened a bare `libamdhip64.so` through ldconfig, which fails on a host whose ROCm lives under a configured or bundled root (no `/usr/lib` copy), so the NPU trunk could not start there even though the GPU runtime loaded fine. It now reuses a HIP runtime the process already mapped (an `RTLD_NOLOAD` probe of each HIP soname), then tries `hipfire_config::rocm::library_candidates` in order, the same list and order as `hip-bridge`; it never falls back to a bare soname. A unit test pins that order without a GPU.
- Flash-Next load refusals now name the offending option.
- **Model-load refusals now say what happened and which setting or flag to change.** Every refusal a normal user can reach while loading a model in `hipfire-loader`, `hipfire-runtime` and `hipfire-cli` was inventoried and the jargon-only ones rewritten: the pipeline-parallel refusals (`<family>: pipeline-parallel (pp>1) unsupported`, `safetensors + pp>1 unsupported`, `pp>1 unsupported via registry`) now read `<family>: this model family cannot be split across GPUs in pipeline mode (topology.pp = N). Set topology.pp = 1 …`; the `pp`/`tp` geometry refusals and the `HipError(0): init_uniform …` strings no longer quote internal function names (`Gpus::init_uniform`, `multi_gpu.rs`) and name `topology.pp` / `hardware.devices`; the expert-parallel, explicit `--kv-backend vmm` (VMM reasons such as `no VMM layout` / `no certified VMM KV path`), partial-offload, Qwen4 MTP/Redline, DFlash-draft, Gemma 4 / Muse Glimmer drafter, DeltaNet `state_quant`, vision-sidecar and kernel-compile refusals say what is incompatible and what to set; truncated or corrupt model files, unknown HFQ versions and unsupported weight formats (HFQ, GGUF, tokenizer, fixed-layout blob sizes) tell you to run `hipfire pull <model>` or update hipfire instead of quoting `qt=` ids and developer symbols; mixed-GPU and uneven-VRAM refusals name `hardware.allow_mixed_arch` and `hardware.uniform_vram_tolerance_gb`; the `hipfire` host-RAM preflight points at `hipfire stop`. The `load refused:` prefix, the `pp=N` / `tp=N` / `num_experts=N` tokens, the `truncated` wording and `refusing to load Qwen2` are unchanged, and no refusal changes meaning: the same loads are refused or admitted. The inventory is `docs/load-refusal-wording.md`.
- **`test_kernelsQA` Qwen4 attention-batch case checks the route an open verify gate takes (test only, no kernel or runtime change).** `qwen4_indexed_attention_attention_batch` and `…_geometry` still expected the gfx942-era hg4 / hg12 arms and CPU F32_ACCUM agreement for decode batches of 2..=32 rows, and failed on gfx1151 with the wide-verify gate open, where an admitted decode call is ONE implementation (split-K on eager gfx1151 F32 hd256 group-12 layouts, the per-head kernels elsewhere; never hg4/hg12). Open-gate decode rows now label the arm from the decode policy and assert raw F32 bits equal to the n one-row public calls on every architecture (36 new checks, all bitwise on Halo gfx1151, fabric j1603); gate-closed calls (1 row, 33 rows, prefill scope) keep the previous CPU and serial-HIP checks. The legacy gfx1151 `prefill_scope` hg12 tolerance failures are unchanged. The helpers live in `examples/qwen4_tierc/qsa/attn_open_gate.rs`; `wide_attention_f32` reuses them. `qsa.rs` also takes a rustfmt-only commit so the changed-file format gate passes.
- **Device-mesh `g5-production-sealed-moe-run` no longer caps `hipfire run` at 64 tokens (harness-only; no production change).** `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-mq4r` reasons by default and `hipfire run` prints only answer tokens, so a 64- or 512-token budget ended inside hidden reasoning, stdout was a bare newline, and `run_reload_equal` failed `min_chars` on every host. Both runs now use the fitted default budget and must still print identical non-empty text.
- G4.8 vision/OCR lifecycle matrices now finish on gfx1151: the child watchdog kills only after 1800 s without output (not 1800 s total), the test committer waits for the whole turn instead of 60 s, and the `g4-vision-lifecycle` row budget is 6000 s (each matrix takes ~32-34 min there).
- The GPU buffer pool reuses the smallest fitting buffer in a size bucket instead of the newest. Before, rebuilding a scratch with the same sizes could hand a small request the large pooled buffer, drop the remaining undersized one and allocate a new buffer (Qwen3.5 prefill scratch after a failed construction: 60 allocations vs 59 warm).
- **LFM2.5 stop tokens resolve to the real `<|im_end|>` / `<|endoftext|>` ids.** `encode()` prepends BOS on LFM tokenizers, so the single-id probe never matched and `eos_tok` fell back to id 1 (BOS on 1.2B, a 9-newline content token on 8B-A1B, which ended turns early). Stop ids now come from the special-token table in the AR, continuous-batch and VL decode loops and in `SpecTarget::eos_token()`.
- **LFM2 decode runs as typed dispatch steps (#666 G10).** Single-lane LFM2.5 decode (dense and the 8B-A1B MoE) is one `hipfire_dispatch` step program per layer: the LIV short convolution is the model-neutral `Step::GatedShortConv`, and MoE layers run the shared sealed MoE executor through its new biased sigmoid router (`MoeParams::selection_bias`: select on `sigmoid + expert_bias`, weight unbiased, normalize, scale; runtime top-k on MQ4/MQ6 experts). The hand loop and the #397 super-op path are gone, so `HIPFIRE_FORWARD_LOWERED` no longer affects LFM. Tokens, logits, convolution state and KV bytes are bitwise identical to beta at every position on `lfm2.5-350m.{q8,mq4}`, `lfm2.5-1.2b.mq4`, `lfm2.5-8b-a1b.mq4` and LFM2.5-VL-3B MQ4V2 (gfx1151); VL image turns are token-identical. LFM2 MoE files with mixed expert formats or expert AWQ sidecars are now refused at load. The continuous-batching decode is unchanged.
- **Developer tooling: `scripts/qwen2-reset-gate.sh` now drives the daemon attempt/commit protocol, so every reset+generate cycle is a committed turn.** Each reset and generate carries a distinct nonzero `attempt_id`, each turn answers the daemon's `commit_ready` with the matching `commit` before `done`, and the gate requires all cycles committed: a rolled-back turn rewinds `next_pos` by itself and would hide a reset no-op as a false pass. Developer regression gate only; engine behavior and defaults are unchanged.
- **Row-exact emitter source fixes (peacemaker-isa, source only; no M7-numeric/GPU proof yet):** Halo BF16 rowtile COUNT is now a single definition (TMP/min same-integer clamp under the existing predicate pass, not a new SCC feature), and the same single-COUNT clamp is applied independently on gfx1100 as its own source fix; gfx1100 BF16 computed LDS offsets route through the lit formatter; Q8 gfx1100 private body labels are non-reserved, separate from the `emit.rs:129` auto-footer. Parent verifies new compiler 010 only after all source owners land.

- **Fixed:** fused SwiGLU IU4 launchers now honor explicit reference-eight candidate selection, including AWQ. The compiled quantization mode remains the default.
- **Fixed: Qwen4 expert placement charges the distinct stage tables once and keeps whole-layer AUTO conditional.** The base owns the gate/up and down pointer tables plus the 1-byte-per-expert codec (17/expert); the stage allocates only two F32 address tables per staged layer (16/expert) and borrows the codec, and the shipped hotset fixed point reserved only the base table plus stage payload bytes, so a staged host-mapped placement could admit a packed owner that crossed capacity once the separate stage pointer tables (and optional kept-expert masks) were counted. The hotset solve now carries those bytes in the same fixed point with a fresh recheck and charges no stage payload or tail pads without a host owner, matching the stage constructor. Whole-layer AUTO retains the existing reserve: it solves without EXTRA stage tables first, pays no EXTRA stage charge when fully resident, and re-solves with the extra owned stage charge only when the placement needs a stage. Guards, margins, caps, K/native MTP reserve, UMA/S1 policy and serving defaults are unchanged; one CPU regression exercises the disjoint budget and the real whole-first solver's fully resident boundary.
- **Muse Glimmer decode runs on the shared sandwich-norm operations, and Glimmer refuses every parallel topology (#666 G11).** Single-lane decode (`decode_step` and the DFlash hidden-capture decode) declares each layer as `Step::SandwichAttention` + `Step::SandwichMlp` (`crates/hipfire-arch-muse-glimmer/src/program.rs`), the operations Gemma 4 runs; the hand layer loop is removed. `pipeline::sandwich` gains the fields Glimmer needs instead of new steps: an attention output gate (`AttnGate`), a separate post-norm eps, NoPE layers (`RopeKind::NoPe`), `Activation::Silu` with the FWHT-rotated SwiGLU product (`RotationFamily` `WithSwiGLU`), the absolute-position windowed Q8 attention (`KvRoute::WindowedQ8`, tiled from 1,280 positions), an output stream that replaces the residual copies, and `SandwichRoute::Steps`, which runs decode projections as generic `Gemv` steps so the fusion table groups them. Every sandwich stream carries one explicit `pipeline::RowsRoute` (`Decode`, `Prefill`, `Verify`; lifted out of `sandwich`): the route, never the row count, picks decode or batched kernels, so `SandwichRoute` is only the ladder and fusion choice (Gemma 4 binds `Decode` exactly at one row). `SandwichAttentionOp` and `SandwichMlpOp` are validated before launch: a decode route with more than one row, batched rows without positions, windowed Q8 KV / draft KV / an output gate off the steps route, rows past the position-indexed cache (`position + rows <= physical_cap`), and the tiled / flash / rotation / BF16 scratch. `Step::RmsnormAutomatic` gains `rows`, so batched row norms are the row-complete norm op rather than `QkNorm`; Gemma 4's batched final norm runs on it too. Prerotated MQ4 gate/up (and the `.mq4r` q/k/v/gate) take the fused multi-output launch on every arch, not only on gfx1100. Design and semantic checkpoint: `docs/design/glimmer-declarative-program.md`.
  - gfx1151, on `muse-glimmer-30b.mq4` and `.mq4r` (route oracle against beta `09540d8c4`; serve and decode against `f826e2197`): tokens, full logits, the residual stream and all KV bytes are bitwise identical at every one of 2,148 committed positions (past the 2,048 sliding window and the tiled-attention threshold), as is the DFlash hidden capture; serve battery and chain transcripts are byte-identical. Decode (`hipfire bench --matrix --tg 64`, A/B/A/B): `.mq4` 11.82 → 11.98 tok/s at ctx 128 and 11.31 → 11.52 at 2048; `.mq4r` 13.48 → 13.86 and 12.84 → 13.25.
  - Loading a Glimmer source now fails closed when its config declares semantics the decoder does not implement: a non-SiLU `hidden_activation`, `attention_bias`, or a layer whose `layer_types` entry and RoPE theta disagree (full layers must be NoPE, sliding layers must rotate).
  - Admission refuses arch 14 with `pp > 1`, `tp > 1` or `topology.ep > 1` before teardown or allocation, with one message. Before, `tp > 1` hit the generic EP refusal, `pp > 1` the carrier refusal, and `topology.ep` was ignored for Glimmer.
  - Removed developer switches: `HIPFIRE_GLIMMER_NO_{EMBED_NORM,QK_NORM,QK_SCALE,ATTN_GATE,OUTMUL,SOFTCAP}`, `HIPFIRE_GLIMMER_ROPE_{ALL,INTERLEAVED}` (bring-up ablations), `HIPFIRE_GLIMMER_FUSED_POSTNORM`, `HIPFIRE_GLIMMER_FUSED_QK_ROPE` and `HIPFIRE_GLIMMER_FLASH_DECODE`.
- **Muse Glimmer prefill, DFlash verify and the drafter run on the shared sandwich-norm operations (#666 G11 slice 2).** The slice-1 layer program also serves batched rows (`LayerIo::route`: a prefill or verify `RowsRoute`, whose batched kernels apply at any row count): batched prefill (`prefill_chunk_batched`), batched DFlash verify (`verify_block_capture_impl`) and the shared draft/verify LM head (`glimmer_lm_head_picks`) run it. The DFlash drafter declares each layer as the same two operations without post-norms, its attention on `KvRoute::Draft` (context rows projected, cached, copied with a recorded `copy_f32_buffer` launch and rotated; scalar `AttnFullF32` tile pinned through `AttentionFamily::run_full_attention_on`). The arch crate keeps staging, embedding and hidden capture; the hand layer loops and their projection helpers are gone (about 3,000 lines). `sandwich::gemm_rows` is the one rows projection of sandwich models: its `Ladder` is `Wide` (Gemma 4) or a `RowsRoute` (Q8 chunked GEMM; gfx12 residual, Muse residual and fused QKVZA prefill GEMMs). Once the next DFlash verify window would cross `max_seq`, the request finishes on AR decode, so DFlash requests that fit the context complete as AR ones do; behind that, rows past the KV cache are refused by the sandwich cache bound before any launch (`tests/kv_cap_gpu.rs`, `dense_rollback_gpu::glimmer_dflash_request_that_fits_max_seq_completes`), never written.
  - gfx1151, `muse-glimmer-30b.mq4` and `.mq4r` against beta `28d70996c`: the route oracle (2,251-token prompt in 192-row chunks through the 1,280 and 2,048 boundaries, greedy decode, 1-row and 300-row turns, verify blocks of 16/16/1/7 with partial accepts, verify blocks at 300/1,270/2,040, a device-capture prefill/verify/commit, and five drafter windows with delta rows, a rollback and an empty context) is bitwise identical on all 130 digests per fixture: every logit, captured hidden row, KV byte, pick and drafter output.
  - A verify block now maps the VMM KV pages it writes. BF16 verify projections (calibration teachers, gfx942) take the staged MFMA GEMM prefill takes, and the BF16 LM-head picks no longer apply the output multiplier and soft cap twice. On gfx12 the MQ4/HFQ4 members of a mixed-format projection group take the residual GEMM like every other prefill projection.
  - Drafter: the MQ4 `fc` input rotates into a scratch sized to its K. The old view was `hidden` wide, so each rotation wrote five times its view and, near the context limit, past the end of its buffer. The unused `kv_input` scratch is gone.
  - Removed developer switches: `HIPFIRE_GLIMMER_NO_FLASH`, `HIPFIRE_GLIMMER_FLASH_FULL`, `HIPFIRE_GLIMMER_O_RESIDUAL`, `HIPFIRE_GLIMMER_MUSE_GEMM`, and the verify timing line of `HIPFIRE_GLIMMER_TIMING`.
- **DeepSeek4 decode runs as typed dispatch steps (#666 G9).** Single-lane decode (`decode_step_body`, shared by the eager, hipGraph and Redline capture routes) is one `hipfire_dispatch` step program per layer (`crates/hipfire-arch-deepseek4/src/program.rs`), and the EP sublayer handlers run the same step builders. The operations moved into `hipfire_dispatch::pipeline::mla`: manifold hyper-connection pre/mix/head (`HcPre`, `HcPost`, `HcHead`), Q-LoRA, joint latent KV and tail YaRN RoPE (`QLoraPrepare`, `QLoraProject`, `KvJoint`, `ApplyTailRope`, gfx1201 `PackedProjections`), the strided KV compressor (`CompressorProject` for its projections, then `KvCompress`), the sparse indexer (`SparseIndex`), the attention as one operation per kernel chain (`SwaRingWrite`, `IdentityGather`, `SwaAttention` / `SparseAttention`, the inverse `ApplyTailRope`, `OLora`; the operations batched rows run too, so decode and prefill of a layer expose the same steps), the shared + routed expert FFN with its serial / overlap / retained-split schedules (`ExpertFfn`) and the lm_head projection (`PreparedProjection`). Removed: the hand layer loop and the #397 super-op single-lane path (`HIPFIRE_FORWARD_LOWERED` no longer affects DeepSeek4). Design: `docs/design/deepseek4-declarative-program.md`.
  - gfx1151, `deepseek-v4-flash-0731.mq2r` against beta `8d1801c77`: tokens, full logits and HC residual streams at all 2,300 committed positions, and every layer's SWA ring, compressor and indexer caches and rings, are bitwise identical, eager and hipGraph; serve battery and chain transcripts are byte-identical. Decode (`hipfire bench --matrix --tg 64`, A/B/A/B) 26.39 → 26.35 tok/s at ctx 128 and 23.28 → 23.23 at 2048 (power-limited, within run-to-run spread).
  - Not covered on gfx1151: the gfx1201, gfx942 and heterogeneous gfx1100+gfx1151 routes, physical EP and the MTP sidecar. Batched prefill / verify, MTP, DSpark and the heterogeneous schedule keep their own sequencing over the moved operations.
- **DeepSeek4 batched prefill, verify, MTP layer, DSpark drafter and TP prefill run as typed dispatch steps (#666 G9, slice 2).** The hand-sequenced batched layer (`attention_block_batched_swa_only` / `_mixed`, `ffn_batched`, `compressor_forward_batched`, the batched HC / Q-LoRA / KV / RoPE helpers, the per-row compressor state swaps) is gone. Each layer over a window of rows is one step program (`crates/hipfire-arch-deepseek4/src/rows_program.rs`) of typed `hipfire_dispatch::pipeline::mla` steps, one `Step` variant per operation: the eighteen that also run at decode (including the compressor projections and the attention's ring write, gather, attention and O-LoRA) take a `Decode` or `Batched` route with `rows` beside it and refuse a decode route with other than one row, and five are rows-only (embedding, DSpark stream capture, the drafter's ring KV and block staging, SWA staging). They cover embedding, HC pre / mix, Q-LoRA with the gfx1151 B3 pack, joint KV, tail RoPE, SWA staging and attention, compressor projections and windowed commit (or one slice-1 `KvCompress` per row), sparse indexer and gather, sparse attention, O-LoRA, ring write, expert FFN, DSpark stream capture, batched heads. The batched GEMM router moved into dispatch (`project_prepared_rows`). The MTP layer block, the DSpark drafter stages, the gfx1201 TP3/TP4 prefill and the batched / lazy / sampled heads compose the same builders. `hipfire-arch-deepseek4` no longer reaches `Gpu::gemv_*` / `gemm_*` / `fused_*` directly (dispatch-bypass 26 → 0).
  - gfx1151, `deepseek-v4-flash-0731.mq2r` + DSpark sidecar against beta `fbcdb362b`: every row's logits, HC streams and every layer's SWA / compressor / indexer caches at each 512-row prefill chunk boundary over 2,300 positions; the 1,024-row production prefill plus 48 decode steps; 40 verify windows of 1–8 rows (also with `HIPFIRE_DEEPSEEK4_BATCH_HEAD=0`); DSpark capture, drafted blocks, `x_head` and stage rings; all 554 calibration activation dumps — bitwise identical. Prefill 4,096 tokens (A/B/A/B): 102.05 / 102.63 → 99.20 / 102.38 tok/s; verify windows at depth 2,048: B=3 36.2 → 36.7, B=8 46.8 → 47.1, B=64 67.8 → 68.1 tok/s; AR 24.7 → 24.5 tok/s — within halo's run-to-run spread.
  - Not covered: the capture-safe verify body (on beta and here its per-row compressor fallback reads attention-state slots 10/11 from a 10-slot batched stripe and panics on the first window), the MTP sidecar (fixture missing), gfx1201 / gfx942, the TP3/TP4 prefill and the heterogeneous route (hardware). The one-row MTP draft, the DSpark head prologue / epilogue and the heterogeneous gfx1100+gfx1151 schedule keep their own sequencing.

- Qwen dense uniform MQ4G256V2 targets can use the experimental Exact VMM continuous-batching AR route on gfx1100. Each lane runs the complete singleton layer program, retaining fused projection and attention-epilogue state; KV and DeltaNet state remain private per request. Multi-request DFlash/MTP verification stays unadmitted on this new route. Q8 recurrent state requires default-on error feedback; EF-off retains the singleton route. Enable with `serve.vmm_batch`; the default remains off.

- **LFM2.5 (arch 11): think-channel and tool-call wire shapes now match the model's trained format.** LFM2.5 is a pure reasoning model: its chat template ends the generation prompt with a literal `<think>` opener, so generated tokens begin inside the block and only `</think>` is generated. The arch-11 generate paths (`generate_lfm2moe`, `generate_lfm2_vl`) detect that opener and re-emit `<think>` as display-only text — `serve` then splits `reasoning_content`/`content` correctly (vLLM deepseek_r1-class semantics) and `finish_reason` reports `length` when a still-thinking turn hits `max_tokens`. Tool calls arrive inside dedicated special tokens wrapping a Pythonic `[f(k=v, ...)]` call list: the decode loop suppresses the whole span from the client stream at the token level, parses the body on span close via `emit_text::parse_lfm_tool_call_body` (mirroring vLLM's `pythonic` tool parser: kwargs → JSON object, positional args dropped, malformed body → no calls), and emits a `{"type":"tool_calls"}` event + `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. An unclosed span at EOS/`max_tokens` is re-emitted as raw text and never fabricates a call. `extract_lfm_tool_calls` provides the same parse for text that still carries markers. Verified on gfx1100 (RX 7900 XTX, HIP 7.15): `serve` non-streaming returns `reasoning_content` + a parsed `get_weather` call with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`; streaming emits `reasoning_content` deltas; `hipfire run` prints `<think>…</think>` then the answer on both the 24B-A2B (under `HIPFIRE_MOE_EXPERT_BUDGET=auto`, 17 layers' routed experts host-placed) and the registry 8B-A1B.
- **Fix: the atomic-free expanded MoE down GEMV was hardcoded to K=512.** `gemv_hfq4g256_moe_down_k8_indexed_batched_expanded` hoisted `x` reads only for the first two 256-weight groups and summed exactly two groups per row; any consumer with `moe_inter != 512` dropped the rest of each expert's down projection. That was the standing "LFM2.5 MoE emits degenerate text" blocker (registry `lfm2.5:8b-a1b`, `moe_inter` 1792 → only 2/7 of each dot product) and the same latent defect in MiniMax-M2 (`moe_inter` 1536). The kernel now keeps the K=512 unrolled fast path bitwise-identical and runs a sequential group loop otherwise; the gfx1151 row1/row2/row8/buffer variants stay `k == 512`-gated. Verified on gfx1100: per-stage MoE dumps match a NumPy replay of the HFQ bytes at cos=1.0000 on both K=256 and K=512 tiny oracles, `lfm2.5-8b-a1b` generates coherent text through `hipfire run` and the `serve_harness` battery (~97 tok/s decode), and the lfm2moe offload parity tests are byte-identical across resident/layer-spill/expert-spill. New developer knob `HIPFIRE_LFM2_MOE_DUMP=<dir>` dumps every MoE intermediate per layer/position for this kind of bisection.

- **LFM2 decode runs as typed dispatch steps (#666 G10).** Single-lane LFM2.5 decode (dense and the 8B-A1B MoE) is one `hipfire_dispatch` step program per layer: the LIV short convolution is the model-neutral `Step::GatedShortConv`, and MoE layers run the shared sealed MoE executor through its new biased sigmoid router (`MoeParams::selection_bias`: select on `sigmoid + expert_bias`, weight unbiased, normalize, scale; runtime top-k on MQ4/MQ6 experts). The hand loop and the #397 super-op path are gone, so `HIPFIRE_FORWARD_LOWERED` no longer affects LFM. Tokens, logits, convolution state and KV bytes are bitwise identical to beta at every position on `lfm2.5-350m.{q8,mq4}`, `lfm2.5-1.2b.mq4`, `lfm2.5-8b-a1b.mq4` and LFM2.5-VL-3B MQ4V2 (gfx1151); VL image turns are token-identical. LFM2 MoE files with mixed expert formats or expert AWQ sidecars are now refused at load. The continuous-batching decode is unchanged.

## v0.4.2 — 2026-10-14

- **Strix Halo NPU trunk: the fused HC kernels now also run under the NPU pair route (16K Flash-Next TTFT −298 ms, exact).** The pair executor runs each bank layer as prepare, an NPU-fed Core and the output projection, and the interpreter dropped its HC pairing state between those windows. So under the NPU route the attention HC read never handed its gates to the HC write, the `hcw` output-projection epilogue never fired, and the MoE HC row fold was skipped. The GPU-only route took all three. `HcFusionCursor` now carries each bank's pairings across its windows, and `hc_gates` is bank-private (+16 B/row) because those gates now cross the bank switch. The fused kernels are the GPU-only route's byte-exact twins.
  - Halo, Flash-Next p16k, bounded memlock, 3 fresh processes × 3 measured per arm, interleaved against 1be80ed54. The all-9 median dropped from 7,194 to 6,896 ms (2,274 → 2,372 tok/s), with per-process medians of 6,882 / 6,892 / 6,907 ms against 7,709 / 7,086 / 7,194 ms. Every candidate TTFT was lower than every base TTFT.
  - Greedy p16k, p16k plus a cached-prefix suffix, and short prompts: NPU `on`, `emulate` and `off` bytes match beta.
- **Strix Halo NPU trunk: the memlock limit it needs is now exact, bounded and reported loudly.** Under an 8 MiB `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` (Tailscale SSH, many default logins) the Flash-Next NPU trunk turned itself off with a one-line `npu-trunk: off (mmap heap: errno=11 (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK?))`.
  - railgun and hipfire-xdna no longer map amdxdna BOs with `MAP_LOCKED` or `mlock` them. The driver already pins those pages (VM_PFNMAP), so the flags locked nothing (`VmLck` 0 kB). They only tested 3.1 GiB of mappings against the limit.
  - The memory the trunk really pins is its userptr A/C arenas: 1,053,843,456 B for the shipped two-bank 8192-row layout. The driver charges it to `VmPin`. At open the trunk computes that figure. When the hard limit allows, it raises the soft limit to exactly `VmPin` + need. Otherwise it fails closed with a message naming the bytes and a bounded fix: `LimitMEMLOCK=1318060032` / `ulimit -l 1287168`, which is the need × 1.25 rounded up to the MiB. No `infinity`. See [host memlock limit](docs/npu/npu-trunk.md#host-memlock-limit).
  - With `npu_trunk=auto`, a qualifying load whose NPU fails to arm now logs `WARN npu-trunk: off (...)` and serves GPU-only. With `npu_trunk=on` it is a load error. An ineligible model keeps the plain `npu-trunk: off (...)` line.
  - Output is unchanged once armed: greedy 16K bytes match beta.
- **Strix Halo NPU trunk: bank B's PLE rows are fetched ahead, and the trunk arenas ask for transparent huge pages (exact; no kill switch).** In a paired prefill, bank A now adopts the PLE row fetch started at admission instead of dropping it, and bank B's rows are enqueued as soon as bank A's fetch owns the epoch, so bank B's initialization adopts a fetch already in flight. The userptr A/C arenas are mapped on a 2 MiB boundary and marked `MADV_HUGEPAGE` before first touch, so under `transparent_hugepage=madvise` they can fault as 2 MiB pages and the NPU DMA and GPU arena reads need fewer translations. Arena lengths are unchanged, so the memlock need is the same 1,053,843,456 B; without THP support the arenas keep 4 KiB pages.
  - Exactness on gfx1151 + XDNA2: greedy output is byte-identical across NPU trunk `on`, `emulate` and `off`.
  - Measured (Strix Halo, Flash-Next 16K, NPU trunk on, interleaved against the base, 3 fresh processes × 3 requests per arm, median of per-process medians): TTFT 7,054 ms against 7,111 ms on the base. That is measured not slower than the base; the gain is not resolved beyond run-to-run noise.
  - On a loaded host THP backed only about 44 % of the arenas; the rest stayed on 4 KiB pages.
- **Opt-in `POST /v1/systemone` decide endpoint (#790 by @nwoolmer).** Answers single- or multi-question classification requests (choice, score, yes/no-or-unclear) from one prefill of label logits instead of generating text, with optional per-model temperature calibration (`decide.calibration.choice|score|noul`, default `1.0` = raw readout). Session mode reuses the chat prompt cache. Chat completions and the default serve path are unchanged; the route only runs when a client calls it. Evaluation harness in `scripts/jev_eval/`; published results in `bench/jev/` carry hipfire's own numbers on licence-clear datasets only (BoolQ-derived data was removed as CC BY-SA 3.0; see `bench/jev/DATA-LICENSES.md`).
- **Redline tapes now record the Lloyd2/Lloyd4 V-cache decode write.** `kv_cache_write_v256_{2,4}bit_vec` launched outside the recorder, so a retained Redline PM4 tape with `--kv-v lloyd2`/`lloyd4` replayed without the V write (Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B MQ4R: 623 launches instead of 633). On gfx1100 the VMM arm page-faulted and dropped the card off the bus. Both writers, and the same-shape Givens 2/3/4-bit and FWHT3 head-dim-512 K writers, now launch through the recorder. `redline_daemon_harness.py` gains `--kv-v` and `--kv-backend`.
- **Strix Halo (gfx1151): PeaceMaker barriers now retire in-flight LDS loads of the slots they free.** The A4 gate/up epilogue (27B dense prefill, default on) and the Qwen4 QSA select kernel could read an LDS row another wave had already overwritten when the GPU was shared, so greedy output changed under concurrent GPU load (any second process; on an APU, any GPU client). Same bytes when the GPU is not shared; deterministic under co-tenancy.
- **gfx1100 DFlash draft: reuse shared MQ4V2 input rotations (#838 by @HUSRCF).** Noise Q/K/V, FFN gate/up and incremental context K/V rotate their common input once per group instead of once per projection. Each group keeps its existing GEMMs, weights and scratch. Default on exact gfx1100 only; `kernel.draft_shared_qkv_rotation`, `kernel.draft_shared_ffn_rotation` and `kernel.draft_shared_ctx_kv_rotation` set to `false` (or the corresponding `HIPFIRE_DRAFT_SHARED_QKV_ROTATION`, `HIPFIRE_DRAFT_SHARED_FFN_ROTATION`, `HIPFIRE_DRAFT_SHARED_CTX_KV_ROTATION` set to `0`) independently restore per-projection rotations.
  - Admission stays eager-only, 2..=16 token rows, compatible MQ4G256V2 weights with identical K divisible by 256, sufficient existing scratch, no AWQ or GEMM dump. Recorded/captured calls and every other architecture keep their original per-projection dispatch. The already-default stream-ordered draft copies remain unchanged.
  - Maintainer evidence on gfx1100 (7900 XTX), pinned Qwen3.8-27B XTS plus MQ4V2 draft: default-on, all-switches-off and beta greedy batteries match text, token counts, acceptance τ and cycle counts (5/5); on/off chains match (5/5), VMM throughout. gfx1201 beta versus explicitly-all-switches-on battery also matches (5/5), and the no-GPU flag-default test excludes gfx1201/gfx1151. Sharing removes redundant rotations, not a new numerical GEMM route.
  - Stock `hipfire bench`, three fresh processes per arm (five measured requests each), greedy DFlash: beta → shared-on decode remains 290.7 → 290.7 tok/s on `humaneval_0_has_close_elements` and 60.8 → 60.8 tok/s on `fiction_lighthouse`; acceptance τ is unchanged. These short-prompt measurements do not establish a significant serving throughput gain. The gfx1100 dense-trunk `redline_daemon_harness.py --pm4` also passes on beta and the candidate (659 dispatches, eight shadow positions, HIP/blob/PM4 logits, KV and recurrent state bit-exact); this is not certification of gfx1100 DFlash-cycle recording invariance.
- **DFlash on gfx1201: the exact-F16 projection producers, the GDN pre/tape fusion and the batched FA prep + paired Q8 K/V write (S3/S5/S6 of #759, by HUSRCF) now run on the R9700 too; byte-identical, decode unchanged within noise.** All three were exact-gfx1100 only. `ArchCaps::supports_dflash_f16_projection_fusions`, `supports_dflash_gdn_pre_fusions` and `supports_dflash_fa_batch_fusions` admit exact gfx1100 and exact gfx1201; gfx1151 and every other arch keep the pre-fusion launches.
  - On gfx1201 the F16 QKVZA/QKV/gate-up consumers launch under the module names the F32 entries use (`gemm_*_hfq4g256_wmma_gfx12_mq4v2`, the ldsstage arm under `HIPFIRE_HFQ4G256_LDSSTAGE=1`), and the F16 projection route stays off inside the gfx1201 IU4 verify scope, where every projection already takes the A4 producer + IU4 GEMM.
  - The AWQ F16 producer now reduces with the live F32 AWQ symbol's two-level wave-shuffle tree instead of the retired LDS tree, which could move `rms` by one ULP and cross an F16 rounding boundary on gfx1201.
  - Fix: the S5 GDN pre conv now matches the reference's operation order on every arch, spelling the first step as `fmaf(w2, s0, w3*x)`. The old `fmaf(w3, x, w2*s0)` rounded `w2*s0` instead of `w3*x`, a 1-ULP change on `q_raw`, so `test_dflash_gdn_pre_gfx1100` failed on a 7900 XTX (gfx1100, beta) and on an R9700. It now passes on both, and greedy output is unchanged.
  - The S3, S5 and S6 parity oracles (`test_mq_f16_projection_producers_gfx1100`, also with the ldsstage arm, `test_dflash_gdn_pre_gfx1100`, `test_qwen35_fa_batch_fusion_gfx1100`) pass bit-exact on gfx1201.
  - Qwen3.8-27B MQ4-XTS + mq4v2 DFlash draft on an R9700, `hipfire bench`, fresh process per cell, 3 per arm, rotated order: every committed text is byte-identical across beta, fused and all-off (code 27/27, 8K prose 9/9, 21.6K code 9/9). Medians beta → fused: 21.6K TTFT 4,670 → 4,665 ms, decode 50.6 → 50.9 tok/s; 8K TTFT 1,647 → 1,646 ms, decode 83.8 → 84.3 tok/s; code decode 311.9 → 312.2 tok/s. Seeded serve battery transcripts are byte-identical to beta.
  - On a 7900 XTX (gfx1100), same fixture and protocol: all three oracles pass and every committed text is byte-identical across beta, fused and all-off (27/27, 9/9, 9/9). Medians beta → fused: 21.6K TTFT 8,410 → 8,418 ms (beta spread 8,409–8,418), decode 56.7 → 56.7 tok/s; 8K TTFT 3,070 → 3,068 ms, decode 87.6 → 88.4 tok/s; code decode 307.9 → 308.0 tok/s.
